Set just off the trail through the tall grass is a gently flowing creek.  Crystal clear water barely ankle deep flows along the creek bed.  The trail heads to the northeast, descending into the creek by way of a small path.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: The heavy mist that fills the pass condenses to form small rain drops.  The sound of running water carries through the night air from the north.
The heavy mist that fills the pass condenses to form small rain drops.  The sound of running water carries through the pass from the north.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: A layer of heavy mist floats above the grass, sparkling in the moonlight.  The mist tumbles away from travellers in the area.  The distant cry of a bird of prey announces the beginning of a hunt.
A layer of heavy mist floats above the grass, sparkling in the sunlight.  The mist tumbles away from travellers in the area.  The distant cry of a bird of prey announces the beginning of a hunt.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: A stone outcropping canopies the darkened trail to the west.  A heavy mist shrouds the northeast path as it disappears down the verdant mountainside.
A stone outcropping canopies the trail to the west.  A heavy mist shrouds the northeast path as it disappears down the verdant mountainside.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Outcropping]
description: The trail passes under a small rock outcropping.  The grass fades to gravel under the outcropping where the night breeze drops the temperature further.  A small niche has been carved into the rock wall.
The trail passes under a small rock outcropping.  The grass fades to gravel under the outcropping where shadow turns the air even colder.  A small niche has been carved into the rock wall.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: The field of tall grass continues to flank the wildly wandering trail.  Moon and starlight spreads across the paths of matted grass that mark the passing of adventurous trailblazers.
The field of tall grass continues to flank the wildly wandering trail.  Paths of matted grass mark the passing of adventurous trailblazers.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: The moonlit trail meanders through a field of grass slightly taller than the average halfling.  Gusts of wind create waves in the grass, causing the blades to bow low onto the trail at the wave's terminus.
The trail meanders through a field of grass slightly taller than the average halfling.  Gusts of wind create waves in the grass, causing the blades to bow low onto the trail at the wave's terminus.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: Tall yellow grasses mix with the shorter green grass in the darkened fields surrounding the trail.  A few boulders are scattered in the field while some bushes with red berries lend color to the field.
Tall yellow grasses mix with the shorter green grass in the fields surrounding the trail.  A few boulders are scattered in the field while some bushes with red berries lend color to the field.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: Gravel covers the path, a snake of white swimming through a dark sea of green grass.  A giant maoral stretches towards the sky near the path.
Gravel covers the path, a snake of white swimming through a sea of green grass.  A giant maoral stretches towards the sky near the path.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Field]
description: The trail becomes exceedingly rocky as it continues down the mountainside.  Pebbles cover the trail, interspersed with larger stones, hidden in the dark of night.  A halfling-sized boulder rests near the trail, seemingly the perfect place to stop and rest sore feet.

The trail becomes exceedingly rocky as it continues down the mountainside.  Pebbles cover the trail, interspersed with larger stones.  A halfling-sized boulder rests near the trail, seemingly the perfect place to stop and rest sore feet.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: A small tree lies where it fell across the trail, its foliage still a dark green in the darkness, fighting decay.  A brown vine snakes its way around the tree trunk like a snake crushing its prey.  The chill of the higher regions fades as the field descends to the north.

A small tree lies where it fell across the trail, its foliage still emerald green, fighting decay.  A brown vine snakes its way around the tree trunk like a snake crushing its prey.  The chill of the higher regions fades as the field descends to the north.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: The trail swings wide to avoid a large boulder covered with moss, glistening in the moonlight.  Moonlight breaks through the thin veil of mist hovering near the treetops.  Songbirds whistle a merry tune somewhere in the trees above.

The trail swings wide to avoid a large boulder covered with moss.  Sunlight breaks through the thin veil of mist hovering near the treetops.  Songbirds whistle a merry tune somewhere in the trees above.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: Incredibly, the fog thickens further down the trail.  Marked by moisture from the fog's passing, a few patches of tall grasses can just barely be seen off the trail, their wet blades sparkling like stars in the darkness.  The grade of the trail levels out more with its descent.

Incredibly, the fog thickens further down the trail.  Marked by moisture from the fog's passing, a few patches of tall grasses can just barely be seen off the trail.  The grade of the trail levels out more with its descent.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: The mist turns to a dense fog here, obscuring the trail in the glow of reflected moonlight as it eddies throughout the area.  Thankfully, the trail is clear and somewhat straight as it continues its journey.  Linden trees line the path, their upper branches arching over the path itself.

The mist turns to a dense fog here, obscuring the trail as it eddies throughout the area.  Thankfully, the trail is clear and somewhat straight as it continues its journey.  Linden trees line the path, their upper branches arching over the path itself.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: The giant conifers begin to thin as the trail continues its descent.  An owl's call can be heard in the distance.  Patches of grass spill across the mountainside, interrupted only by a mound of small stones just off the trail.  Slight breezes blow puffs of rolling mist through the trail.

The giant conifers begin to thin as the trail continues its descent.  Patches of grass spill across the mountainside, interrupted only by a mound of small stones just off the trail.  Slight breezes blow puffs of rolling mist through the trail.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Grassy Field]
description: Stray clumps of green grass struggle up from the rocky soil, overcoming the incredible odds presented by the bitterly cold and thin air.  Patches of moss stretch to consume the surface of several nearby rocks illuminated by moonlight.  To the northeast the trail begins a slow wind down the mountain.

Stray clumps of green grass struggle up from the rocky soil, overcoming the incredible odds presented by the bitterly cold and thin air.  Patches of moss stretch to consume the surface of several nearby rocks.  To the northeast the trail begins a slow wind down the mountain.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: The craggy alpine peak nestles against a cloud blanketing the ledge with soft, downy fog.  The wind pushes through the mist, creating a legion of ghostly forms that charge your position only to shatter harmlessly against you and the mountainside.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: A low flying cloud covers this portion of the ledge, covering the stone with a thin patina of dew.  The visibility drops to an inch and the footing becomes uncertain--perhaps crawling would be a wiser mode of travel?

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: You would not need a running start to fly a kite in the steady winds that buffet the mountains.  The exposed and vegetation-free ledge offers no break or shelter whatsoever.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: Damaged by the impact of a boulder thrown loose from the very top of the mountain, a section of the ledge is slowly crumbling along fault lines running from the edge toward the center of the slab.  The trail yaws toward the wall in order to avoid the danger.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: A basaltic outcropping juts out of the peak as if reaching across the yawning chasm toward the neighboring summits.  A hawk plummets between the twin peaks, its cry echoing between their sheer walls of stone.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The tunnel opens out to a large antechamber lit by a triangular beam of moonlight that glimmers through a distinctively-shaped entryway.  The chamber appears to have begun as a small cave, but was later widened to provide room for travelers to take shelter at night or during inclement weather.

The tunnel opens out to a large antechamber lit by a triangular beam of light that streams through a distinctively-shaped entryway.  The chamber appears to have begun as a cave, but was later widened to provide room for travelers to take shelter at night or during inclement weather.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The tunnel takes another sharp turn, cutting off the sources of light at either end.  Many travelers find the movement from light to dark unsettling, as the imagination fills the empty spaces with strange and terrible forms.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A thick vein of clear quartz crystal runs the length of one wall, flooding the room with sharply refracted moonlight carried from the surface to the center of the peak.  Any night vision you had developed in the tunnel instantly disappears.

A thick vein of clear quartz crystal runs the length of one wall, flooding the room with sharp white light carried from the surface to the heart of the mountain.  Any night vision you had developed in the tunnel instantly disappears.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: No change in light or air signals the sharp turn in this section of tunnel.  Most travelers discover the turn only by bonking their noses against the cold, stone wall.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The darkened tunnels twist, turn, and double back upon themselves, leaving you unsure whether you are making progress through the mountain or merely returning to where you began.  This labyrinthine structure has obviously been created deliberately, perhaps to frustrate an invasion through the pass.  Each of the seemingly infinite corners represents an ideal location for ambush.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: You stub your toe on a raised vein of mithril that runs diagonally across the floor of the tunnel.  Rather than exploiting the find, the tunnelers simply exposed the metal so that its beauty might be admired.  Thick ropy coils of mithril reflect the negligible ambient light with a faint silvery tinge.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Some light spills through the entrance, but the tunnel quickly turns as dark and chill as krolvin dreams.  The smooth surfaces of floor and walls suggest that the passage was not created by nature.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: The sheet of stone comes to a sudden end by swerving to rejoin the mountain.  Just at the terminus of the ledge, a tunnel has been carved into the face of the peak, providing access to the shelter within.  The sharp alpine wind rushes across the entrance, creating a harsh and ominous whistle.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: The ledge narrows through this area, forcing you to edge closer to the sheltering mountainside.  Some wispy clouds drift through the valley below, temporarily shrouding the opposite peaks with a misty veil.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: A dead branch falls from a tree far below, the cracking sound filling the gap between the mountains with a sharp, staccato echo.  A night hawk patrols the sky beneath the ledge, barely visible as it turns sleepy ovals amidst the moonlit peaks.

A dead branch falls from a tree far below, the cracking sound filling the gap between the mountains with a sharp, staccato echo.  A hawk patrols the sky beneath the ledge, turning sleepy ovals as it searches for appropriate prey.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: This rocky ledge might just be the loneliest place in the world.  The commanding location provides a feeling of mastery and control--as if you were an intrepid explorer, perhaps the very first to reach these heights.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Ledge]
description: A narrow shelf high near the summit offers a fabulous view of the surrounding peaks, which huddle as if for warmth in the thin alpine air.  A small break in the ledge forms a steep chute leading to the craggy slope below.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Icy Crags]
description: A row of ice-laden crags forms a precarious staircase on the side of the mountain leading to the rocky ledge above.  The view from the steps is breathtaking, the distant peaks of the DragonSpine glistening in the moonlight, though your attention is better placed at your feet.

A row of ice-laden crags forms a precarious staircase on the side of the mountain leading to the rocky ledge above.  The view from the steps is breathtaking, the distant peaks of the DragonSpine shining in the distance, though your attention is better placed at your feet.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Icy Crags]
description: A large crag high on the slope cuts off the light from moon and star, cloaking the icy trail in deep darkness.  Clear ice over black stone dimly mirrors the image of those careful travelers who glance down to watch their footfalls on the slick surface.

A large crag high on the slope shades the icy trail, creating a gloomy contrast with the bright sunshine beyond.  Clear ice over dark stone mirrors the images of those careful travelers who glance down to watch their footfalls on the slick surface.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Icy Crags]
description: The ice beneath your feet has a layer of reddish brown deep within the icepack, bespeaking some act of terrible violence on this rugged promontory.  The slippery conditions do not provide a good place to fight, and so perhaps an accident caused the bleeding--but would that explain the deep gashes and chipped surface of the surrounding stone?

title: [Whistler's Pass, Icy Crags]
description: The jagged rocks rising from the icy mountainside resemble a chain of volcanic islands--or the business end of a morning star.  Wise travelers choose their steps with care, as sliding down the mountainside seems as unattractive a fate as the alternative: impaling oneself on an icy crag.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Icy Crags]
description: This portion of the trail challenges even the most experienced mountaineer.  Thick ice covers stone outcroppings, leaving the trail simultaneously rough and slick.  The rough crags that jut out of the peak offer some purchase, should you manage to grab onto one before losing your footing.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Ridge]
description: A radically steep incline ascends from ridge to ice-covered peak.  A few ragged fir trees cling precariously to the rocky, snow-covered soil beside the trail.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Ridge]
description: A dip in the ridge threatens to cause shinsplints as the traveler negotiates the steep decline and incline.  The one benefit you derive from the arduous climb is a temporary break from the winds that buffet the exposed areas of the ridge.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Ridge]
description: The trail wraps around a curious pillar of basalt that rises up out of the ridge line.  A nest of woven fir branches sits atop the pillar, though from the base it is impossible to tell whether its builders are at home.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Ridge]
description: Some rare edelweiss grows on the side of the trail, the gravelly soil ideally suited to the hardy plant.  Thick, wooly bracts surround the yellow and white flowers in a star shape above the lance-shaped downy leaves.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Ridge]
description: The trail follows the rocky ridge from the subalpine meadow to a dizzying height.  Some low flying clouds wreath the neighboring peaks in mystery, while the route over the nearest peak to the east is all too clear.  Its rocky crags, snow, and ice portend an arduous climb.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The temperature changes dramatically as the trail passes a snowline.  Travelers looking up have to squint to see from the brilliant glare thrown off the snowcapped peaks.  Some cord-hardy pines cling desperately to the thin soil of the alpine ridge.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: A pool of rock-cress surrounds some thinly spaced fir trees on the sloping mountainside.  Years of travel have worn a path through the grass and hardened the rocky soil beneath.  With only the testimony of your footfalls to judge by, you might imagine yourself walking across a flagstone-paved street.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The trail moves down the side of a ridge and across a rounded meadow covered in deep green grasses.  The sky stretches out in an enormous sea of black framed by the ghostly forms of the moonlit, snow-capped peaks.

The trail moves down the side of a ridge and across a rounded meadow covered in deep green grasses.  The sky stretches out in an enormous sea of blue framed by the craggy peaks that surround the pass.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The climb along the ridge requires exquisite care lest the traveler plummet down the sheer rocky slope, though the field of wildflowers on each side of the ridge looks soft enough to cushion a fall.  The stars gleam brightly through the thin mountain air, bathing the few clouds in the sky with an ethereal glow.

The climb along the ridge requires exquisite care lest the traveler plummet down the sheer rocky slope, though the field of wildflowers on each side of the ridge looks soft enough to cushion a fall.  Two eagles patrol the mountain skies, seemingly immobile as they ride a rising thermal.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The arduous route along a steep mountain ridge exposes you to strong gusting winds, cold enough to penetrate the warmest clothing.  To either side of the rocky trail, flag trees wave in the gale as if saluting the traveler who braves these conditions.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail climbs along the mountain's spine, the ridge top providing a breathtaking view of the climb that awaits the traveler to the north.  To the south the trail descends into thick forest.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail climbs sharply through the montane forest in the direction of the peak to the north.  A stand of fire-damaged pine, likely resulting from a lightning strike, covers the slope to the east.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail winds down the sharp incline to the northeast, crossing a maelstrom-torn landscape only to disappear beneath a large pile of arboreal wreckage.  A small arch-shaped opening is wreathed by a flowering trumpet vine.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The faint light filtering through the debris creates a spectral mottling effect, blending foreground and background and effectively camoflaging everything inside the tunnel.  A breath of clear air enters from the arched entrance, creating a sharp contrast against the warmer, loamy atmosphere within.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: A squirrel chitters as if mocking your struggle to pass through the tunnel of trees.  Emboldened by the darkness, it scurries across your foot and disappears into a pile of leaves.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: A darkened tunnel leads through a thick brake of tangled trees and other plant matter.  The smell of pine needles overwhelms a faint odor of rotting leaves, yet the combination makes most travelers eager to seek fresher air.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: A dense stand of pine trees has been woven into an impenetrable snarl by the passage of a maelstrom through the area.  The trail leads directly into the thicket through a dark opening at its base.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail passes through an intense swath of maelstrom damage.  Intense, swirling winds uprooted ancient oak trees and snapped tall pines like twigs.  Enormous hail pelted the ground, leaving it pockmarked and nearly void of grass.  A faint ammoniac smell rises from the mass of dead and decaying vegetation that litters the ground in the twister's wake.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: A bluejay chases a squirrel around some large canyon oaks, its angry squawk drowning out the panicked chitter of its prey.  A powerful gust of wind carries the bird out of range just long enough for the frightened rodent to find shelter in a hollow bole.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: A large red cedar lies across your path, a dry rot slowly returning it to the soil from which it grew.  A spotted salamander scurries at your approach and disappears beneath the log.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: Only a few rugged cedars grow in the rocky soil as the trail passes over a low ridge.  A faint smell of gin rises through the frigid air from the aromatic needles that litter the ground beneath the trees.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: Enormous pine trees stand in perfectly straight wind rows, like sentries guarding the mountainside.  The trail follows a serpentine path between some hillocks, seeking flat ground for easier passage through the forest.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail passes through a small clearing where a dense grove of spruce yields to more thinly-spaced, towering pines.  Whispery starlight pours into the area, bathing onion and catchfly plants with a pale silver glow.

The trail passes through a small clearing where a dense grove of spruce yields to more thinly-spaced, towering pines.  Intense sunlight pours into the area, bathing onion and catchfly plants with a bright golden glow.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: You hear soft footfalls crunching through the thin layer of snow, but the tightly knotted spruce grove guards the identity of the stalker.  The only tracks on the trail are bootprints, but it's hard to imagine a humanoid negotiating these woods.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: A small cart lies on its back where it spilled into a ditch beside the trail.  One wheel is smashed beyond repair, leaving you to wonder what similar fate met its passengers.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: A low and hollow roar fills the dense wood.  A heavy mist in the air confirms the presence of a waterfall somewhere behind the treeline.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: Very little moonlight filters through the dense thicket of spruce.  Your steps crackle over the thin, icy snowcap covering a layer of needle and cone.
Very little light filters through the dense thicket of spruce.  Your steps crackle over the thin, icy snowcap covering a layer of needle and cone.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: A dense wood of bigcone spruce shades both sides of the trail.  Just south of the trail, a large rack of antlers sits beside a pile of bones, silently warning that the forest is not entirely safe.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The rocky bald spot on top of the ridge is fringed with buckwheat and mousetail.  Grass and flowers join in a frenzied dance, with the mountain winds calling the tune.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: At the top of the ridge, the trail crosses a bald--a distinctive geographical feature of the montane forest.  Covered with finely broken-up rocks and exposed to the harsh effects of wind and weather, the bald supports only a few odd-looking cushion plants.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail runs from the edge of a snow melt gully up a rise toward a ridge to the east.  Hoary-barked cedar trees stand in silent protest against the frigid wind that whips at your clothing.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The eastern edge of the snow melt gully is home to currant and gooseberry bushes that thrive in the moist soil.  Golden potentilla flowers beckon you up the slope to the northeast with a promise of untold fortunes.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail continues through the snow melt gully, passing walls of columbine and paintbrush.  Several willows shade a slender stream that courses through the middle of the gully.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail descends into a large snow melt gully.  The nearly vertical slope left by the rushing water blooms with a profusion of bright red monkeyflower and golden yellow sneezeweed.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: An enormous thicket of winterberry bushes crowds the trail.  Some birds chirp pleasantly from inside the thicket as if resting, satiated, from a feast.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: The trail passes through a stand of ancient canyon oaks, some towering eighty feet in the air.  Several squirrels dash up a nearby trunk, startled by the sound of your passing.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Montane Forest]
description: Tall pines grow in a tight thicket, as if huddling for warmth.  Your steps are punctuated with the crunch of fallen needles or cones, which thickly cover the rocky soil of the mountainside.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The trail, a narrow path of rocky mud coursing through a grassy field afire with snapdragons, continues to trace the slope of the mountain.  The aspen and birch of the subalpine forest begin to mingle with canyon oak and cedar, signaling a transition to the montane region below.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: A large bristlecone pine has fallen across the trail just where it turns to cross a burbling stream that drains a small lake to the west.  A variety of small mushrooms grow in the cool, damp shade beneath a stone footbridge.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The trail circles the lake, then crosses a large stream that carries its water south down the mountain.  A rough-hewn stone footbridge allows you to cross without getting wet, which might be dangerous in the chill mountain air.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The forest opens up at the edge of a small mountain lake.  Fed by the streams that carry melting snow down the mountain, the waters are beautifully clear but far too cold for swimming.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: A circle of charred stones to one side of the trail indicates that some recent travelers stopped here for the night.  Densely packed firs provide some break against the wind, though their shade prevents the snowpack from melting.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The trail passes through a thicket of wild snowberry bushes, their waxy berries not yet ripe for picking.  Several birds scold you from a nearby spruce as you stop to admire the shrubs.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: Quaking aspen shiver in the damp and chilly breeze that courses through the mountain pass.  The trail is framed by densely packed cinquefoil shrubs that keep even the least attentive traveler moving in the right direction.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: A great snowy owl is perched on a branch halfway up a bristlecone pine tree just beside the trail.  The owl's head swivels as it tracks your movement and weighs your value as food.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: Mixed fir and spruce trees line the trail as it continues to follow the contour of the land on the lower portion of the mountain.  Thin grasses and meadow rue ripple in the chilly breeze that winnows through the trees.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The trail passes over a portion of the mountainside where a small rise lifts the treetops into the wind.  The wind has shaped the crowns of the trees to resemble a line of fluttering flags.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Subalpine]
description: The trail passes through a thin birch forest.  The air is cool and damp from the densely packed snow that remains unmelted in the shade of the trees.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: A dense patch of greenleaf bluebells marks the border between alpine tundra and subalpine forest.  Tall birch trees sway in the wind that batters the mountainside with frequent, savage gusts.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: The trail descends sharply from south to north.  To the south and west immense mountains block the sky, while to the east a dense forest stretches to the horizon.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: A shooting star blazes briefly across the night sky, then seems to fall to the ground an immeasurable distance to the east.  The thin night air carries a chill into even the warmest of clothing.

A flock of small, black birds arranged in strict military precision crosses one corner of the sky.  Their movement is observed by a solitary hawk turning circles as it hides in the direction of the sun.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: The trail passes across a rocky streambed that leads toward a pond to the southwest.  At present, the water descends in a thin and lazy stream, though the depth of the cut suggests the occurrence of seasonal torrents.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: A small, shallow pond of crystal clear water lies to one side of the trail.  A plain stone bench provides a comfortable spot to look into the water, though all that can be seen is a scintillating reflection of the starry night sky.

A small, shallow pond of crystal clear water lies to one side of the trail.  A plain stone bench provides a comfortable spot to look into the water, though all that can be seen is a dazzling reflection of the clear blue sky.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: The trail bends from north to east as it passes through some fairy primrose.  Small delicate petals of lilac and pink tower above the deep green, hairy leaves.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: The trail continues to climb from north to south along the contour of the mountain.  The air grows thinner and noticeably colder as you pass a patch of deep blue alpine forget-me-nots.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: The trail winds through a field covered in mountain dryad, yellow and white blossoms peeking above a carpet of woolly evergreen leaves.  The gusting wind sends ripples through the field like waves across a body of water.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: The trail continues on its way following the slope of the mountain as it rises to the south.  The stars shine through the thin mountain air in a dazzling display of celestial light.

The trail continues on its way following the slope of the mountain as it rises to the south.  Some hearty butterflyweed attracts a variety of insects, which float in a chaotic dance above a rising thermal.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Tundra]
description: The gentle gurgle of a nearby mountain stream does little to distract you from the rigor of the climb along this stretch of tundra.  The pollen from a small field of goldenrod, devalued to silver in the moonlight, tickles at your nose.
The bright sunlight reflecting off a nearby mountain stream blinds your eyes but does little to warm your bones.  A small field of mountain goldenrod beckons like the wealth of kings.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Talus Slope]
description: The cascade of basalt shallows, then ends, meeting a beautiful meadow of alpine tundra.  Dwarf bilberry and alpine bearberry dominate a landscape profuse with floral shrubbery.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Talus Slope]
description: Animal bones, including many a broken leg, litter the talus slope.  The complete skeleton of a giant roc lies amidst the charnel debris, perhaps indicating that its attack on some wounded prey went awry.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Talus Slope]
description: Navigating along the talus field is treacherous.  The rocks are angular and rendered unstable by the trickle of frigid alpine water that seeps between them.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Stone Steps]
description: Basaltic debris, from large boulders to the finest silt, has accumulated at the foot of a massive stone staircase.  The talus slope narrows from a broad fan to a narrow channel of crushed rock as it follows the contour of the mountainside to the north.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Stone Steps]
description: The easiest path down the stairway is clearly marked where travelers' feet have scoured the stones free of lichen.  If you pause a moment to catch your breath, you'll catch the pleasant scent rising from a nearby meadow of crimson clover.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Stone Steps]
description: Wide basalt pillars, some spaced for tiny halfling steps and some for the widest giantkin stride, form an impressive causeway against the side of the mountain.  The windblown alpine tundra blooms with wildflowers on either side of the stairs, which are covered with a variety of mosses and lichens.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Stone Steps]
description: A natural formation of stone steps comes to an end high atop the mountain.  At the very top of the stairway, years of travel have carved a shoe-shaped depression just in the spot where your foot wants to go to bring you to a narrow ledge.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Crevasse]
description: The gap between the walls of the crevasse widens from the weight of the stone into a small antechamber leading back out to the open air of the mountainside.  A small pile of torches lies to one side of the opening.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Crevasse]
description: Icy cold water cascades down one wall and drains along a shallow channel in the floor.  The dark black stone becomes shiny when wet, reflecting the dim moonlight that penetrates the narrow walls of the crevasse.

Icy cold water cascades down one wall and drains along a shallow channel in the floor.  The dark black stone becomes shiny when wet, reflecting the dim light that penetrates the narrow walls of the crevasse.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Crevasse]
description: The skitter of clawed feet echoes through the narrow cleft, announcing the presence of some unseen beast.  The half-eaten carcass of a bird suggests you disturbed a scavenger's meal.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Crevasse]
description: It is hard to keep a thought in one's head, with the distraction of a high-pitched whistle that rises from the wind blowing across the mouth of the crevasse.  The high walls created by some massive rupture of the stone remain open to the night sky, though the trail itself is plunged into the deepest darkness.

It is hard to keep a thought in one's head, with the distraction of a high-pitched whistle that rises from the wind blowing across the mouth of the crevasse.  The high walls created by some massive rupture of the stone remain open to the sky, though the trail itself is deeply shadowed.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Mountain Ledge]
description: The rocky ledge comes to a sudden end at a dropoff apparently caused by the collapse of the ledge some time ago.  The wind whistles across the mouth of a deep crevasse that cuts the stone wall in two.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Mountain Ledge]
description: The trail bends from north to southwest, following the contour of the mountain.  Some flattened, shrub-like black spruces provide a comforting margin between the trail and the cliffside.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Mountain Ledge]
description: The stone ledge slopes gently upward from the rocky wall to its edge, forcing you out of kilter as you pass along the trail.  The slope holds a shallow pool of rainwater against the wall, its surface covered with a faint layer of ice.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Mountain Ledge]
description: A concave hollow in the wall provides an additional bit of shelter from the whistling wind.  Several pitons have been driven into the rocky floor of the ledge, where they slowly rust in shallow pools of water that has run off the melting snows above.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Mountain Ledge]
description: The trail hugs closer to the looming wall as the mountain ledge narrows to the merest shelf.  Over the brink, a vast and limitless darkness yawns beneath the starry sky.

The trail hugs closer to the looming wall as the mountain ledge narrows to the merest shelf.  Over the brink, a thick forest runs like a verdant carpet to the horizon--though most travelers prefer to keep their eyes on the ground beneath their feet.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Mountain Ledge]
description: A wall of stone leans over the trail, half sheltering and half threatening those who pass beneath.  High up on the wall, a bowl-shaped protrusion holds a cluster of alpine violets that lend the only color to the stark, windswept ledge.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: After a strenuous climb, the rocky shelf levels off high on the mountainside.  The opposite wall of the canyon falls away, following the incline of the mountain to the north, opening up a breathtaking vista.  A series of snowcapped peaks are visible in the distance, standing silent vigil in the frigid winds of the DragonSpine.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: The path continues to climb, travel growing more difficult as large boulders and broken shale clog the pass.  The most stable footing can be found against the southern wall of the canyon, where a sharp incline rises above the debris on the canyon floor.  The trail ascends the rocky shelf, climbing out of the canyon and onto the mountainside.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A chill breeze gusts through the pass, bringing with it the sharp, fresh scent of pine.  To the north, a full-grown pine tree, standing some twenty feet or more above the rocky floor, rises from a mound of broken shale and several layers of decaying pine needles.  Its trunk bent at an odd angle to catch any stray rays from the rarely seen sun, the old pine appears to have flourished in a realm where few large plants have a chance for survival.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: The path begins a slight incline to the north, forcing already weary travelers to exert more energy and willpower to continue onward.  The normal debris of the pass appears to have been physically moved in this area, forming small piles along the base of the stone walls.  Although a few larger fragments of stone remain on the canyon floor, the path seems to be easier to navigate.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Heavy clouds of various shape drift across the night sky, their presence dimming the pale light of the moon.  A chill wind whips through the pass, sending the gnarled branches of small shrubs and bushes into a flurry of commotion.  In a moment, they settle, returning to their grim and silent existence.

Heavy clouds of various shape drift across the grey sky, their presence sending long shadows across the canyon floor.  A chill wind whips through the pass, sending the gnarled branches of small shrubs and bushes into a flurry of commotion.  In a moment, they settle, returning to their grim and silent existence.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A long fissure cuts across the pass in a diagonal slant, from wall to wall.  Although no greater than half a foot in length, the fissure appears to be quite deep, its interior lost in darkness.  Easily bypassed by a simple lengthy stride, the fissure may attest to the unstable nature of the mountain.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: High on the stone walls, small clumps of dried grass and broken twigs mark the spots where nests have been built by the avian inhabitants of the pass.  Although little movement seems to come from them, the nests appear quite sturdy, designed to withstand the heavy gusts of wind and chill, mountain temperatures of the area.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: The rock-strewn floor of the canyon is cluttered with broken shale, small pieces of gravel, and larger, man-sized stones.  Although many of the smaller stones have long ago been blown away by the raging winds, some pockets of collected dust and sand lie trapped amid the larger rocks.  These few, infrequent deposits are home to small clusters of grass and tiny shrubs, which eke out a living in this sparse region.  The seemingly ill-placed sound of trickling water can be heard from the south.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A gentle gurgling sound dances between the narrow walls of the pass, its source a natural spring lying near the base of one of them.  Moss-coated and entangled with small, but lush vegetation, the narrow fissure in the rock issues forth a steady trickle of fresh water, which flows into a small pool.  The area around the trapped water is spotted with small animal tracks, as if this place were a favorite watering hole for the denizens of the pass.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: The bleak, grey landscape stretches onward, as the high-walled pass curves along the mountain.  The sound of trickling water drifts from the north, its metallic tones overshadowing the low howls of cold wind.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Overhead, the edge of one of the high rock walls has crumbled, sending a large pile of boulders down into the pass.  Contrasting round and jagged edges protrude from the conglomeration of rock, effectively barring the pass from further movement to the south.  Strangely, a few shallow indentations have been cut into the rock, perhaps as an aid to those who might wish to climb them.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A pile of large boulders, the remnants of a partial collapse of the canyon wall, seem to block further passage through the cleft in the mountainside.  Flecked with a few clusters of orange and pale green lichen, the boulders appear to have lain in this position for some time.  Oddly, some of the large stones have been etched with what appear to be shallow hand and footholds.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Occasionally, black-winged owls can be seen gliding overhead, their ominous forms circling the pass and its occupants.  With an infrequent shriek or piercing cry, the owls descend slightly, perhaps to get a better view of their prey below.

Occasionally, black-winged birds of prey can be seen gliding overhead, their sleek forms circling the pass and its occupants.  With an infrequent shriek or piercing cry, the birds descend slightly, perhaps to get a better view of their prey below.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A swift breeze blows through the pass, its movement accompanied by a shrill, high-pitched whistling.  Besides the chill caress of mountain air, the breeze carries the fresh scent of pine.  Gazing upward, a few tall pine trees can be seen growing along the uppermost ridge of the pass, their slender shapes blocking out thin slivers of the night sky.

A swift breeze blows through the pass, its movement accompanied by a shrill, high-pitched whistling.  Besides the chill caress of mountain air, the breeze carries the fresh scent of pine.  Gazing upward, a few tall pine trees can be seen growing along the uppermost ridge of the pass, their slender shapes casting long shadows down the canyon walls.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Hidden within the darkness of night, a small creature, perhaps a squirrel or chipmunk, berates the travelers below.  Its high-pitched screeching echoing off of the high walls, the tiny voice appears to be highly offended at this intrusion into its territory.  Although the chittering continues, its originator seems to be less than apt to back up its threats with physical force.

Hidden amongst the thick shadows and scattered foliage of the canyon walls, a small creature, perhaps a squirrel or chipmunk, berates the travelers below.  Its high-pitched screeching echoing off of the high walls, the tiny voice appears to be highly offended at this intrusion into its territory.  Although the chittering continues, its originator seems to be less than apt to back up its threats with physical force.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A few scraggly pine trees dot the landscape, their thin trunks rising from mounds of broken shale and windblown dust.  Each branch droops slightly, its surface sprouting small clusters of yellowing pine needles and its bark thin and wrinkled.  The base of each tree is surrounded by a shadow of drying needles.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Clusters of low-growing bushes and grasses cling to niches in the stone walls, their foliage ranging from shades of pale yellow to dark green.  Hearty and tenacious in this inhospitable environment, the rugged plant-life obstinately defies the harsh, mountain winds and chill temperatures of the canyon.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A chill wind howls through the pass, its dull echo akin to the sound of lonesome wailing.  Bordered on both sides by high walls of stone, the atmosphere of the pass appears both bleak and sheltered, as if those who travel through its confines are somehow isolated from the rest of the world.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Rocky debris has fallen from the sides of the sheer cliffs in this region, littering the pass with clusters of stone and shale.  Although maneuvering around the constantly shifting rock proves time-consuming, passage is possible.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A pair of green-tinged shrubberies stand beside a dark opening in the sheer cliff face in the face of a sheer cliff, almost like squat, silent guards.  High stone walls rise up on either side of the pass, limiting the view to a rectangular patch of star-dotted sky, its bespeckled surface masked by thin, tattered clouds.  The narrow cleft through the mountain continues northward.

A pair of green-tinged shrubberies stand beside a dark opening in the sheer cliff face in the face of a sheer cliff, almost like squat, silent guards.  High stone walls rise up on either side of the pass, limiting the view to a rectangular patch of grey sky, its serene surface masked with thin, tattered clouds.  The narrow cleft through the mountain continues northward.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Pale moonlight filters in from a roughly oval opening in the tunnel wall.  Gusts of chill, mountain air and the fresh scent of forest growth enter through the tunnel opening, quickly dissipating in the stale air of the interior.  Over twelve feet in height, the opening appears large enough for use by even the largest of giantkin.

Hazy sunlight filters in from a roughly oval opening in the tunnel wall.  Gusts of chill, mountain air and the fresh scent of forest growth enter through the tunnel opening, quickly dissipating in the stale air of the interior.  Over twelve feet in height, the opening appears large enough for use by even the largest of giantkin.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A set of precisely-cut, squared steps has been crafted into the tunnel here, perhaps to allow for an easier ascension as the tunnel continues its incline to the north.  Half a dozen in number, the steps have been carved out of the rocky floor itself, their straight edges and well-defined lines the marks of true stonesmiths.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The dim tunnel continues to twist and turn through the heart of the mountain, its serpentine path set long ago by the flow of ancient waters.  A slight, yet discernable incline leads upward to the north, as if the passage were rising slowly toward the surface.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Long, finger-like strands of webbing drift from the walls of the tunnel, their gossamer touch reaching out to those who seek passage.  Anchored to the stone by fraying tatters, the drifting, veil-like webs pose no real danger, their adhesive nature long since lost to dust and time.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Bits of gravel and small stones have been cleared to the sides of the tunnel in a nonsensical fashion, their origin unknown.  Although uneven, the walls of the tunnel are mainly smooth, with a small protrusion or shallow pock in some places.  A few old, yellowed bones, perhaps from a large rat, lie amidst the rocky debris.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Although somewhat stale, the air in the passage is dry and cold, lacking the dank, stagnant quality of some underground areas.  Slight, infrequent gusts flow through the tunnel, their crisp scent calling to mind the chilly atmosphere of snowy, mountain slopes.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: This narrow section of tunnel appears to dead-end at a large crevasse in the rock wall.  The crevasse extends from floor to ceiling, its width no greater than three feet at its widest area.  To the north, the system of tunnels continues onward into darkness.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Crevasse]
description: Studded with protrusions and deep indentations, the irregular walls of the crevasse are difficult to navigate.  The screeching sound of metallic armor, iron buckles, and slung shields against the small outcroppings of rock are not uncommon, as travelers make the slow, methodic trek through the tight space.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Crevasse]
description: The tight confines of the crevasse allow for very little extraneous movement beyond the sideways shuffling required to continue forward.  The stale, cramped air seems too thin to adequately feed the lungs, and the narrow walls of the fissure impede normal breathing.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The tunnel narrows considerably at this point, nearly ending at the narrow mouth of a large crevasse in the rock wall.  Its outer edges scraped and chipped by the passage of many travelers, the crevasse appears to be a rather tight fit for halfling and giant alike.  Although the fissure reaches all the way to the tunnel ceiling, it varies in width and seems riddled with jagged protrusions, making for slow and painstaking movement.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A low, tentative howling permeates the tunnel, its apparent source a narrow, gash-like fissure in the tunnel ceiling.  Accompanied by chill blasts of mountain air, the howling changes tone from a deep growl to a high shriek according to the force of the wind passing through the opening.  Fed by the fresh, icy air of the surface, the fissure provides ventilation to the underground passages.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A cold gust of wind passes through the tunnel, a barely audible groaning following in its wake.  Motes of dust whirl with its passing, and then return to their places amid the rough sediment of the stone floor.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The walls of the tunnel wind smoothly through the dark rock of the mountain, their rough edges and protrusions worn off long ago by the flow of water that created them.  In some places, a sharp edge or corner appears to have been rounded, perhaps by less natural means.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The few pebbles and finger-sized stone chips scattered across the stone floor do little to deter your passage through the tunnel.  A low, deep sound emanates from somewhere in the area and moves along the floor in rhythmic waves.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Propped against one wall, a pile of arm-length, cut wooden logs waits patiently for some unknown use.  Bound together with thick twine, the dozen or so pieces of wood might serve as stout torches, although their exact purpose remains unclear.  The dull hum of falling water moves through the tunnel, its presence noticeable, but not overwhelming.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A trio of tiny black beetles, their shiny carapaces glistening in the dim light, flee down the tunnel, their scurrying forms quickly becoming lost amid the heavy shadows.  The loud hum of flowing water permeates the passage, sending vibrations through the stone walls and floor.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The rumbling of swiftly flowing water bathes the passage in a loud hum, its nearby source causing a build-up of moisture in the cramped air of the tunnel.  As the condensation builds, tiny rivulets of water cascade down the stone walls and form small pools on the damp floor.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The powerful sound of falling water is loud in this section of tunnel, its booming rhythm engulfing the subterranean passage.  Heavy and dank, the air seems to be laden with moisture and the odor of soggy climes.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The omnipresent sound of falling water fills the tunnel, silencing all other noises.  To the south, the tunnel opens into what appears to be a vast, underground cavern and the source of the nearly visible sonic vibrations.  To the north, the tunnel continues onward, fading into darkness.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: The thunderous roar of the waterfall seems deafening, its descent into the darkness of the cavern sending up thick clouds of vapor.  A narrow, stone ledge works its way around the eastern side of the large cavern, opposite the tumult of falling water.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: Running tightly along the edge of the rugged, pocked walls of the large cavern, the stone ledge makes for uneven footing in its best places.  Glazed with condensation from the careening water on the other side of the pit, the surface of the ledge must be meticulously navigated, each footstep carefully placed to avoid slipping into the wet abyss below.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: Although obscured by darkness and wisp-like clouds of vapor, the surface of the underground lake, oily and capped with shallow, foam-tipped waves, can still be glimpsed from the height of the ledge.  Along its rocky shores, where the dark water laps against the rugged stone of the cavern, a pale, yellowish phosphorescence glows dimly in the darkness.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: The thin, stone ledge is marred by deep cracks and chips in its surface, the result of untold years of exposure to the thick mists of the underground falls and the heavy passage of unnumbered travelers.  Occasionally, a sliver of stone is knocked free from the ledge and tumbles down into the calm, gently lapping waters below.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: The air in the cavern is thick and heavy, its mixture of trapped odors almost overpowering.  The sharp, lively scent of swiftly flowing water has combined with the dank odor of deep, unexplored grottos to produce a fragrance that is both invigorating, as well as repulsive.  Those who are alien to these vast, dark regions do not take long to yearn for the light of the surface.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: At this distance, the roar of the waterfall is dulled slightly, allowing other sounds of this subterranean world to be heard.  In the darkness above, hidden within the vast, shadowed heights of the enormous cavern, a high-pitched squealing and the minute sounds of tiny claws scraping against stone, have become audible.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: The rising vapor mists seem thinner here, revealing an unhindered view of the waterfall on the other side of the dark cavern.  Descending like deafening shafts of silver, the water falls some one hundred feet below the ledge, ending in a tumultuous, foaming pool of oily black water which stretches like a monstrous lake across the cavern floor.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: The wet stone of the thin ledge is slick and unsteady, its edges showing signs of crumbling and decay.  Below, heavy clouds of vapor rise upward from the falling water, obscuring a clear view of the depths of the cavern.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Cavern]
description: Away from the rumble of the cascading waterfall, a thin rocky ledge follows the eastern wall of the great cavern, its edge overlooking the vast darkness of the pit below.  Moist with clinging water vapor, the uneven walls of the cavern provide few safe handholds for cautious travelers attempting to reach its nether side.  Nearby, a tunnel branches off to the south.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The twisting tunnel opens up into a huge cavern, its ultimate height lost in the darkness above.  An awe-inspiring waterfall, the roar of its passage emitting a thunderous wave of sound through the tunnels, cascades into a shadowy pit at the bottom of the cavern.  Thick clouds of water vapor reach upward from the pit, their curling, snake-like forms dissipating into the cold air.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: All other sounds succumb to the deafening roar of the underground river, its sheer force shaking the stone walls and floor of the tunnel.  A dank odor drifts in the air, which has become thick with moisture.  The walls of the passage glisten slightly with the sheen of water that clings to their rocky surfaces.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A thin shelf, no wider than the length of a hand, juts outward from one of the walls of the passage.  Atop its narrow surface squats the frozen remains of a candle, its remaining wax pooled into a blob-like mound.  The thunderous roar of the unseen river is deafening here, its passage causing the stone floor and lower parts of the walls to quiver.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Small, scattered mineral deposits sparkle in the dark tunnel, their tiny facets glinting like the miniscule eyes of bats against the greyish stone.  All around, the noise of violently surging water engulfs the passage, drowning out all other sounds.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The tunnel twists, following a course determined centuries ago by the flow of water.  Although sound within the passage seems muffled, the muted thunder of an underground river, its source hidden within the mountain itself, rolls across the stone, sending a discernible shudder through the tunnel system.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A shimmering band of crystal glints in the dim light of the tunnel.  Milky white with flecks of gold, the mineral vein might be a rare form of quartz, although its exact nature remains mysterious.  The low rumble of flowing water can be felt beneath the stone floor.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Nearly invisible patches of mortar fill small cracks and seams in the tunnel walls, as if this section had begun to succumb to the enormous weight of the mountain atop it.  Carefully applied and flush with the dark stone, the repairs appear to have accomplished their task, as no new fractures mar the stone surface.  The steady hum of the underground river is audible here, its force vibrating through the passage.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Cool and dry, the tunnel worms its way through the heart of the mountain, the heavy rock insulating its interior and seeming to absorb all sound, except for the low rumble of the unseen river trapped in the depths of the stone.  Even the occasional footfall or the clank of a hard-soled boot on the tunnel floor seem to lose their echo within the all-encompassing rock.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A series of old charcoal marks adorn one of the stone walls of the tunnel, although their purpose is unclear.  Faded by time, the marks may have at one time been a tally of some sort, or they may simply have been the designated spot for extinguishing torches.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The tunnel twists slightly, following the natural course of water which originally formed it.  Any protrusions or jagged corners in the stone walls have long since been worn smooth, either by the water itself or by the will of intelligent hands.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A massive, wooden arch has been erected in the tunnel here, its limbs and supports covering a ten-foot span of the irregular ceiling.  Formed from stout felwood timber and banded with thick mithril straps, the arch appears to be quite sturdy.  Minute, vein-like cracks in the stone ceiling and walls may have initiated the need for its construction in this area.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Although a thin layer of dust coats much of the stone floor, very little debris clutters the passage, attesting to both its strength and frequent use.  Occasionally, the burnt stub of a torch can be found lying in the darkness along one of the twisting walls, its usefulness at an end.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The dry, chill air in the tunnel contains a hint of the dankness associated with wet, underground caverns, although a slight breeze occasionally moves through the dim passage, bringing with it the sharp, living scent of the surface.  A high whistle or eerie howl accompanies these infrequent gusts, as the cold wind blows through some opening or crevasse in the mountain.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The wispy tendrils of pale-grey cobwebs cling to the uppermost corners and crevasses in the twisting tunnels, their weavers apparently absent or hidden within the deep pockets of shadow surrounding them.  Although much of the tunnel system appears to have been created by the normal flow of water through the mountain, small chiseled supports and the rounding of certain corners remain as evidence of intelligent construction within the otherwise natural passage.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: A dull thunder emanates from the walls of the dark tunnel, its source originating from beneath the dirt-strewn floor.  The low, muffled sound of rushing water, perhaps from an underground river, vibrates through the stone, engulfing the passage in an audible hum.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: Dusty, pale moonlight filters into the tunnel from an opening to the south, its dim illumination outlining the crags and crevices in the uneven rock walls.  The tunnel floor is coated with a thick layer of dust and fine sediment which has formed into small piles along the base of the walls.  The glint of smooth stone shows through in many places where the dust has been disturbed by frequent passage through the tunnel.  Somewhere deep below the tunnel floor, a low humming sound vibrates through the rock.

Dusty, pale sunlight filters into the tunnel from an opening to the south, its dim illumination outlining the crags and crevices in the uneven rock walls.  The tunnel floor is coated with a thick layer of dust and fine sediment which has formed into small piles along the base of the walls.  The glint of smooth stone shows through in many places where the dust has been disturbed by frequent passage through the tunnel.  Somewhere deep below the tunnel floor, a low humming sound vibrates through the rock.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Tunnel]
description: The tunnel opens up suddenly as the ground drops away into a deep gorge below.  Rushing water rumbles down the gorge, the sound thundering in the tunnel's mouth and bouncing off the stone walls endlessly.  A rope bridge extends across the gorge, to a ledge just visible at the bridge's far end.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rope Bridge]
description: Anchored to a rocky ledge jutting outward from a smooth wall of stone, this end of the rope bridge ends before a dark opening.  Nearly twice the height of the average human and just as wide, the gaping black maw yawns open, its center appearing dark in the faint glow of the pale moonlight.  The frequent creaks and groans of the old bridge, as well as the muted thunder in the gorge below, seem to urge cautious travelers toward the opening with their methodic song.

Anchored to a rocky ledge jutting outward from a smooth wall of stone, this end of the rope bridge ends before a dark opening.  Nearly twice the height of the average human and just as wide, the gaping black maw yawns open, exposing only darkness within.  The frequent creaks and groans of the old bridge, as well as the muted thunder in the gorge below, seem to urge cautious travelers toward the opening with their methodic song.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rope Bridge]
description: A blast of damp air wells up from the unseen gorge, shaking the weathered knots of the rope bridge and its occupants.  As the gust dissipates into the crisp mountain air, it leaves behind the heavy, mineral-tainted odor of damp climes and submerged grottos.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rope Bridge]
description: Worn smooth by the passage of many grasping hands, the heavily-bound ropes of the bridge have withstood the rigors of time.  A low vibration moves through the woven cords, lending them the illusion of life.  However, it is the dull hum of the rushing water below and quick gusts of inconstant wind which truly send a shudder through the stretched and fraying twine.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rope Bridge]
description: Swaying over the unseen depths of the mist-enshrouded gorge, the rope bridge appears to be at the mercy of the chill, mountain winds.  Although the thick, woven cords seem to endure the wrath of the tumultuous air, sharp creaks and high-pitched squeals from the ropes attest to their burden.  Beneath the bridge, darkness hides what must be a rushing waterfall, the sound of its passage echoing like dull thunder from the gorge below.

Swaying over the unseen depths of the mist-enshrouded gorge, the rope bridge appears to be at the mercy of the chill, mountain winds.  Although the thick, woven cords seem to endure the wrath of the tumultuous air, sharp creaks and high-pitched squeals from the ropes attest to their burden.  Beneath the bridge, a heavy, greyish mist hides what must be a rushing waterfall, the sound of its passage echoing like dull thunder from the gorge below.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rope Bridge]
description: Stout, carved wooden posts secure this end of the old bridge to the secure, stone surface of the pass.  Fraying and unraveling over time, the thick woven ropes of the bridge remain tautly stretched across the chasm, their loose hair-like threads quivering in the frequent gusts of cold air.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: The trail ends abruptly at the edge of a deep gorge.  The sound of rushing water echoes up the rock face from far below, as the water itself tumbles furiously on its way down the mountainside.  An old rope bridge extends across the gorge, disappearing at the far end into a dark opening in the sheer rocky cliff.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A crumbling pile of stone chips and loose gravel leans against one of the stone walls, attesting to the transitory nature of some portions of the pass.  Bits of rock and loose debris clog the passage as they trickle down the sides of the man-sized pile, making forward movement a tedious endeavor.  In the distance, a muffled sound seems to vibrate through the stone walls.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A chill wind whistles through the night-cloaked pass, its cold fingers prying through even the most heavily bundled clothing.  Seemingly alive with ill-intent, the icy tendrils crave warmth.   Stealing heat from their hapless victims, they howl off with their quickly fading prize into the dark environs of the mountain slopes.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Some slabs of loose shale and crumbling rocks of the canyon floor appear to have been arranged here, forming small teetering stacks and squat piles.  Near a small, dwarf-sized niche in the rock wall, a semi-circle of stones has been constructed, its interior sheltering a single, partially-burnt branch from the ravaging wind.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Towering overhead, the stone walls of the pass reveal only a narrow band of dimly-lit, night sky and veil-like clouds above.  Lower on one wall, perhaps at the height of a human midsection, a vague pattern of crude marks scars the otherwise smooth stone.  Etched into the hard surface with a dagger or spike, the diagonal pattern resembles a trio of claw marks.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Something small and unseen skitters across the rock wall, its miniature form masked by a thick blanket of darkness.  All around, chaotic wind gusts blow lightweight debris across the narrow canyon floor.

A small, grey-backed lizard skitters across the shallow grooves in the rock wall, only pausing for mere seconds to sense the air before scampering on its way.  All around, chaotic wind gusts blow slivers of wood and other light debris across the narrow canyon floor.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Trapped within a thin, needle-shaped crevice in the rock wall, a tattered length of leather dangles limply, its thread-like ends undulating slightly in the breeze, like the strands of a horse tail.  Perhaps at one time a belt or harness strap, the leather strip has been harshly weathered, its original purpose unknown.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A few shriveled, scrub bushes and tufts of dying grass cling to small crevices in the rock wall, their effort to survive hampered by the chill winds and dry conditions of this desolate region.  Their bony limbs bare of fruit or leaves, the small plants have been picked clean by the foraging inhabitants of the mountain.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A distant peal of thunder, or perhaps a trick of the wind as it howls through some unknown cavern, echoes with a deep, resounding tone.  The sound, trapped by the high walls of the pass, reverberates for a few moments and then fades to silence.  The stone walls remain motionless and stoic, as if accustomed to these frequent, audible outbursts of the dark heavens.

The sound, trapped by the high walls of the pass, reverberates for a few moments and then fades to silence. title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Scattered shale and loose gravel confound movement through the rocky cleft, making footing uneasy and at times treacherous.  Stones seem to shift with each step, and the frequent gusts of chill mountain air only add to the difficulty of the trek.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Partially obscured by the darkness, a beleaguered thorn bush squats amidst a pile of broken shale.  Its tentacle-like branches are bare of fruit, their precious bounty having been stolen by the stealthy denizens of the pass.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Crooked fractures and vein-like lines, the result of constant weathering and the stress of time, split the facade of smooth stone, creating jigsaw patterns on the rock walls.  Sparse grass and other small clusters of vegetation cling to the creases, their hungry roots pulling a meager existence from the tiny patches of sand and sediment trapped in the irregular surface.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Nearly twenty feet above the rock-strewn floor of the pass, a tangled nest of broken twigs, dried grasses, and other foraged debris clings to a small, jagged cleft in the stone wall.  The pale, tell-tale streaks just below the nest indicate the nature of its inhabitant, as well as the tiny splintered bones scattered about the rocks below.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Fragments of stone and scattered gravel litter the narrow pass, making movement difficult and sometimes tedious.  Lying amidst the rocks, grape-sized animal droppings, desiccated by the dry mountain winds, bear testament to the presence of other creatures in this windswept world.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A dull night sky gazes down with little emotion, its blank complexion scarred slightly by the tattered vestiges of forlorn clouds and the faint glimmer of tiny stars.  A chill wind dances about the pass, its force, from a bare whisper to a harsh gust, ever-changing.

A dull grey sky gazes down with little emotion, its blank complexion scarred slightly by the tattered vestiges of forlorn clouds.  A chill wind dances about the pass, its force, from a bare whisper to a harsh gust, ever-changing.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Stray twigs and torn bits of dried grass cling to the rocks in this area, their tiny frames blown about by frequent chill blasts from the mountain winds.  A barely audible scuttling can be heard as the gusts subside, perhaps from the subtle movements of small animals hidden within the blanket of night.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: A faint scratching and rustling sound emanates from within some of the many small, grass-filled nests dotting the high stone walls.  Although the sound's exact source remains lost within the darkness of night, it is obvious that many small yet unseen creatures survive in this dry, cold environment.

Although the sound's exact source remains lost amidst the long shadows cast by the tight enclosure of the pass, it is obvious that many small yet unseen creatures survive in this dry, cold environment.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Small crevices and pockmarks mar the otherwise smooth surface of the stone walls, providing no more than a few inches of sparse shelter to the small denizens of the pass.  Carefully chosen twigs and strands of dry grass fill some of the tiny nests, although the diminutive engineers that built them remain hidden within the blanket of the night.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Chill to the touch, the high stone walls of the cleft tower overhead, nearly shutting out the pale rays of the moon.  Although easily discernable, the narrow trail is strewn with a dangerous assortment of crumbling rocks and shards of stone, their sharp edges and shifting positions seemingly intent on slowing progress through the pass.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: The ear-splitting shriek of an unseen bird of prey echoes through the pass, the crooked beak from which it must have originated hidden among the dim stars above.  As the shrill cry slowly fades, the rocky cleft is once again masked in an eerie stillness.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Skull-sized stones and gravel litter the passage, making movement through the tight cleft especially difficult.  As travelers carefully pick their way across the shifting ground beneath their feet, the grating sound of stone grinding against stone echoes through the pass.  A pile of large boulders blocks movement to the south.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: High stone walls reach toward the dim lights of the starry sky, their smooth facades punctuated by small clusters of lichen and withered clumps of pale grass.  A pile of large boulders has fallen here, blocking further passage to the north.  Oddly, the towering stone walls do not appear to have crumbled or been damaged, cloaking the origin of the tumbled boulders in mystery.

A pile of large boulders has fallen here, blocking further passage to the north.  Oddly, the towering stone walls do not appear to have crumbled or been damaged, cloaking the origin of the tumbled boulders in mystery.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Vein-like cracks scar the surfaces of the otherwise smooth walls of the pass, evidence of  the tremendous toll placed upon them by the harsh elements of the region.  Although travelers are partially sheltered from frequent gusts of icy wind, the silent stone walls seem to emit a bone-numbing chill of their own.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Harsh winds howl through the narrow pass, their hollow moans dissipating in the chill night air.  Scattered stones and jagged bits of rock clutter the passage, making movement through the cleft both hazardous and slow.  In some places, the mountainous walls have deteriorated, dropping sharp stone slivers and fist-sized rocks to the ground below.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: The rocky cleft narrows and twists, a massive shard of stone partially blocking the already tight passage.  Apparently having dislodged from one of the walls, the enormous shard leans precariously across the cleft, its fractured base surrounded by a small field of broken and slivered rocks which crunch and grate underfoot.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Minute cacti, their bulbous stalks armed with an array of needle-like spines, sprout from jagged cracks in the stone.  Their spiny profiles lend texture to the otherwise smooth walls of the bleak pass.

Minute cacti, their bulbous stalks armed with an array of needle-like spines, sprout from jagged cracks in the stone.  Dark hues, from deep greens to brilliant purples, adorn their flesh, lending some color to the otherwise bleak pass.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Rank weeds and yellowed grasses cling to tiny niches in the stone walls of the cleft, eking a subsistence from the sparse soil in which they grow.  Walls of rock, worn smooth from years of blasting wind and occasional rain, tower overhead.

title: [Whistler's Pass]
description: Only faint quivering rays of moonlight filter through this narrow cleft in the rocky cliff.  Gray clouds mask the sky overhead, further distilling the feeble pale light from above.  The massive stone walls of the pass are chill to the touch, seeming to drain the very life from those who would make their way through the tight passage.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: Narrow streams of melting snow trickle down the hillside, coalescing into small pools around the rough trail.  A high cliff face rises from the rocky earth, its countenance impeding further progress into the valley below.  Near the center of the massive wall of rock, a jagged fissure scars the stony surface, revealing a narrow passage.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: A rock-strewn trail descends into the valley, its edges bordered by sparse patches of melting snow which send finger-like rivulets of icy water running down the hillside.  Overhead, a chill wind whistles among unseen crags and caverns, emitting high-pitched squeals and dull moans as reminders of its passage.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: A thick forest of pine and fir hugs the edge of the plateau.  The trees are heavily draped with fallen snow, and drifts are piled up against the large trunks.  The well-marked trail moves off into the forest to the southwest while to the northeast it slowly descends into the Khalerineth Valley.  Looking east, the waters of Mreanith Lake sparkle in the moonlight, and to the north the DragonSpine Mountains thrust their cloud-shrouded, snowcapped peaks high into the sky.
