title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: An occasional clump of snow from an overburdened tree branch falls onto the trail with a loud 'plop!'  The forest is quiet all around except for the moaning of the wind as it courses relentlessly through the conifers.  The trail is easy to follow, appearing to have recently had something wide and heavy dragged through it to uproot the encroaching sawgrass.  It would all be rather idyllic were it not for the frigid, numbing cold.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: Rabbit tracks emerge from the pines to circle several small bushes then dart away into the depths of the forest.  The small impressions in the snow show no sign of pursuit by a predator.  The road bends slightly, moving off to the south and northeast.  Although covered in snow, the road is flat and passage is easy.  Just to the north, a huge blue spruce stands out among the darker pines and firs.  The spruce's fragrant aroma fills the air.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: Tall pines, cedars and firs compete for space in the surrounding forest.  The tree branches spread wide, shading the forest floor and creating circles of bare earth across the snowy field.  Many of the trees are old, large specimens with thick trunks good for hewing into structural lumber.  Here and there, in places where the light is particularly good, holly bushes have taken root.  Their jagged, sharp leaves protect an abundance of small berries.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: The forest passes near the edge of the plateau giving a breathtaking view of Mreanith Lake spreading out below to the east.  Unfortunately, the pristine view of the lake and surrounding valley is marred by the presence of a rather foul odor.  Wagon tracks lead directly to the edge of the precipice, and pieces of refuse are scattered on the ground near the dropoff.  It is evident where much of the garbage produced in Zhindel's Hold gets deposited.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: Much of the forest has been cut away leaving a patchwork of thick stumps.  Drag marks in the ground indicate that the logs were pulled to the roadway, and deep grooves in the road indicate that heavily laden carts moved off to the southwest.  Although no one is cutting trees now, several axes, saws and hatchets in pristine condition rest against a few uncut trees a slight distance away.  Perhaps the lumberjacks have gone home for the night.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Trail]
description: A herd of domesticated roltons occupies the field to the east.  The beasts huddle against the cold, some bleating loudly and moving about while others lie in the snow, apparently sleeping.  Loud sawing sounds seem to come from somewhere to the west, though the wind and blowing snow mix the sounds up and make it difficult to discern a direction.  The road bends here, moving off to the northwest and northeast.

A herd of domesticated roltons occupies the field to the east.  The beasts root about through the snow, bleating loudly and searching for edible grass blades as a pair of young dwarven lads keep watch over them.  Loud sawing sounds seem to come from somewhere to the west, though the wind and blowing snow mix the sounds up and make it difficult to discern a direction.  The road bends here, moving off to the northwest and northeast.

title: [Zhindel's Post]
description: The roadway skirts a section of the forest, passing just to the southwest of the stand of pines and firs.  Several wooden cabins huddle under the protective branches of the trees.  Smoke wafts lazily from some of the chimneys, bringing the smells of burning pine and savory stew to your nostrils.  Neat, rock-lined paths lead to the front door of each house.  The area has a serene feel to it, and the wind is filtered to a soft breeze by the trees, although at times hard gusts blow through.

title: [Zhindel's Post]
description: Tidy homes nestle together on either side of the roadway with candlelight peering out cheerily from several windows.  The road is wide and appears well traveled with the dirt packed down tightly.  The clouds pass overhead quickly, allowing patches of bright moonlight to illuminate the field to the west.  A snow fort, probably built by dwarven children during the day, is situated in the center of the field behind a large wooden structure.

Tidy homes nestle together on either side of the roadway, their brightly colored doors and whitewashed fronts speaking of neat, meticulous ownership.  The road is wide and appears well traveled with the dirt packed down tightly.  A group of dwarven children appear to be constructing a snow fort in a field off to the west behind a large wooden structure.  Their laughter rings out musically in the interludes when the wind dies down to a sufficient level.

title: [Zhindel's Post]
description: A number of dwarves hurry by, some in groups, some alone, always bundled up heavily against the elements and moving with determination as if to stop would mean instant freezing.  Several businesses butt up to the roadway to offer their services to passersby.  Not far overhead, clouds move quickly across the sky, driven onward by the constant wind, and occasionally one is low enough to drag a chilling fog through the area as it scurries past.

title: [Zhindel's Post, Crossroads]
description: Three roads converge to flow in a donut shape around a large stone well.  On the outside edges of the roads, small commercial structures huddle closely together as if trying to keep warm against the constant frigid wind.  Lights glowing from upper windows indicate that these buildings are used as residences as well as places for conducting business.  An occasional lone house interrupts the rows of shops, but it is apparent that this is the heart of the commercial district.

On the outside edges of the roads, small commercial structures huddle closely together as if trying to keep warm against the constant frigid wind.  The businesses are well maintained and, for the most part, gaily painted in various shades of blue and green.  An occasional lone house interrupts the rows of shops, but it is apparent that this is the heart of the commercial district.

title: [Zhindel's Post]
description: Loud voices haggling in both dwarven and elven accents emanate from a nearby warehouse.  Cartloads of fresh vegetables, slightly frozen in the wind, sit in front of the warehouse, collecting snow on top of their foodstuffs.  Several more warehouses line the roadway.  From the words written on their neatly lettered signs and the goods piled out front, many deal in foodstuffs, lumber, ore, clothing and salt.  The entire area has the look of a freight transit center.

title: [Zhindel's Post]
description: Pens filled with bleating roltons occupy the east side of the roadway.  Rolton carcasses, stripped of their fur, heads and extremities, hang on racks outside the slaughterhouse.  There is no worry of spoilage as the frigid air keeps the carcasses in a frozen state.  Unused rolton parts are piled unceremoniously behind the slaughterhouse, and, despite the frozen condition of the parts, rats scurry through the pile, dragging claimed pieces away to devour elsewhere.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau]
description: A small stand of trees protruding out from the main forest forms a place of refuge from the constant wind.  The tree trunks are scarred and gouged from their bases to a height of about ten feet.  A soft layer of pine needles blankets the ground, and the snow tends to pile up outside the stand, leaving the layer of needles relatively dry and providing a good place for travelers to bed down for the night.  Someone has even set up a small fire pit under the trees.

title: [Zhindel's Plateau, Slope's Edge]
description: The trail switches back and forth across this squat hill that separates the DragonSpine Mountains from Zhindel's Post.  Aside from where travelers have passed, the snow is an unbroken white field.  There is one place, though, where the snow seems to be badly disturbed.  Directly upslope several trails have been plowed straight down through the powdery accumulation.  Nothing could have made such a trail moving uphill, so whatever made them must have come downhill...fast.

title: [Eastern DragonSpine, Slope]
description: A steep climb up the mountainside leads to a large cavern far above while a less strenuous path winds down to the town below.  Although both directions look well trod, the constant reforming of ice from the passing mists makes footing unsure.  The wind howls off the mountainside, and, every so often, the heavy load of ice cracks and rumbles noisily high in the peaks.  Looking up, the extensive snow on the towering mountainside seems poised to come rumbling down at any moment.

title: [Eastern DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The wind gusts, mounding clouds up against the mountainside, obscuring vision and making movement difficult.  Then, in the next gust, the clouds are driven away and the moon shines down brightly on the path, creating blinding reflections off the ice and, in its own way, making the path once again difficult to traverse.  It is hard to decide which is preferable, clouds or moonlight.  The wind makes its own decisions, however.

title: [Eastern DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The trail is extremely icy, steep and treacherous.  Below, the homes and businesses of Zhindel's Post cluster near the face of the DragonSpine Mountains.  The well-kept buildings with their candlelit windows give the Post the look of a toy town, but a few figures moving on the streets and between the buildings belies this impression.  Farther to the east the conifer forest spreads out in a rolling carpet of green.

Farther to the east the conifer forest spreads out in a rolling carpet of green.

title: [Cavern Mouth]
description: A large, well-lit cavern extends back into the mountain face.  Wagonloads of freight move slowly out of the cavern, stopping at the precipice's edge to await daylight and the use of the freight pulley.  The pulley appears to be closed and locked for the night.  Several large bags of salt are piled near the freight pulley.  The footing is icy, and the dwarves moving the wagons wear heavy-soled boots to provide better traction.

Once emptied, the dwarves load the wagons up again with inbound freight and make their way back into the cavern.  Several large bags of salt are piled near the freight pulley.  The footing is icy, and the dwarves working the pulley wear heavy-soled boots to provide better traction.

title: [Kharag 'doth Dzulthu, Tunnels]
description: The tunnel narrows as it approaches a set of metal rails.  An endless procession of mining carts rotate along the rails, flying past at an exceptional rate of speed, and occasionally stopping to take on passengers.  Several burly dwarves stand by, directing traffic and ensuring the carts move along.

title: [Kharag 'doth Dzulthu, Tunnels]
description: Mica sparkles in the fissured granite walls of this small cavern.  A single metal lantern hangs from an iron bracket mounted on one wall, barely illuminating the area.  A carved stone arch funnels passengers out into Zul Logoth.

title: [Zul Logoth, Marcasite Tunnel]
description: Solid timbers butt up against solid granite walls in this long, relatively narrow tunnel.  Standing only a foot apart, the timbers are a good foot thick and ten feet long.  They rise from the scuffed granite floor to the impenetrable rock ceiling overhead, supporting cross timbers equally as long and thick.  To hear them creak and groan, one would think that only these pieces of wood keep the weight of the entire mountain range from crushing everything in the tunnel.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Marcasite Tunnel]
description: Gigantic toadstools rest in stone pots every twenty feet or so.  The trunks of the toadstools are a bright opaque white and quite thick, reaching up to support a flaring cap.  It is the cap that is of use in the dark mine.  The underside of the cap glows a luminescent white, casting its light to the tunnel floor in a white circle.  The topside of the cap, however, casts a light silver illumination and gives the ceiling a silvery sheen all along the tunnel.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Sapphire Tunnel]
description: Rather heavy traffic proceeds northeast and southwest as dwarven laborers move burdens along the tunnel.  Sacks and boxes marked "Clothing" and "Food" as well as long pieces of lumber are transported southwest, while containers marked "Salt," "Ore," and "Gems" move the other direction.  Occasionally the workers move aside to let a long line of domesticated roltons or other meat-on-the-hoof move southwest, but for the most part the labor seems endless.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Sapphire Tunnel]
description: A breeze courses down the tunnel from northeast to southwest, bringing a bit of fresh air to the hazy, claustrophobic environs of the narrow tunnel.  The sound of footsteps echoes loudly from both directions, intermingling to make it sound as if hordes of dwarves are converging on this very section from both ends.  Gigantic toadstools, their caps glowing a luminescent blue, light the tunnel at twenty-foot intervals.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Sapphire Tunnel]
description: Water trickles out of a clay pipe set high up on the north wall.  The water falls into a long, deep, metal trough.  Dwarven men and women arrive from the south and west carrying various types of containers.  They dip the containers in the trough, filling them with water, and then return in the direction from whence they came. The action of filling the containers slops a great deal of water on the stone floor, creating a slippery, slightly treacherous surface.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Sapphire Tunnel]
description: Traffic steadily moves north, east, and southwest through this tunnel junction.  A small brown door nestles unobtrusively into the west wall next to a wide glass window, and a red door stands along the southern wall.  Dwarves, particularly children, move up to press their noses against the window's glass and stare in at the displays.  Then they either happily enter the shop, or they move along, usually with a sigh and a wistful expression, and go about their business.

title: [Zul Logoth, Sapphire Tunnel]
description: The sweet scent of composted wood pervades the tunnel, though the source of the odor is not readily apparent.  A steel door occupies a portion of the west wall, and a burnished brass sign flanks the door.  A crude stone arch along the eastern wall provides entrance to a small shop.  Dwarves carrying packages and dry goods wander in and out of the shop.  Some seem happy and gregarious, while others are aloof and serious.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Sapphire Tunnel]
description: An overpowering odor of fresh meat mingled with a hint of decaying flesh fills this bend in the tunnel.  A dark red swinging door set into the northeast corner of the tunnel springs open every so often, and a dwarf pushing a cart loaded with a variety of cut meats hustles her way to the west.  When she returns, the cart is empty save for bits of flesh and a bloodstain or two.  A burnished steel sign affixed to the wall to the right of the door announces the ownership of the premises.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Sapphire Tunnel]
description: The tunnel turns ever so slightly as it makes its way through this portion of the business district.  A wrought iron pole protrudes several feet out of the south wall, and a silvery metal key hangs from the pole.  Below the key, a heavy black door with several deadbolt locks allows entrance into the building.  A wide, unpainted, metal rollup door occupies the north wall.  The sound of many roltons bleating pathetically emanates from behind the door.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Crystalline Cavern]
description: Crystalline formations glitter and gleam across the inside of the cavern's dome, as if one were standing in the center of a giant geode.  The crystals reflect and refract the light cast by the luminescent toadstools below.  The light plays off stone streets, shifting from color to color as one moves in relation to the facets of the crystals.  Large pots, each sporting one massive toadstool, line the thoroughfare in all directions.

title: [Zul Logoth, Crystalline Cavern]
description: The stone avenues give way to a mixture of humus and dirt.  Narrow, well-trod lanes wind among gigantic toadstools and spreading mushrooms.  Boulders and decaying logs, seemingly placed at random among the dense growth, provide places for lichens, mosses and fungal growth to grow abundantly.  A moist coolness pervades the area, and the reflected light from the crystalline dome is filtered and muted by the many varieties of non-luminescent toadstools that tower overhead.
paths: Obvious exits: north, east, south, west
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Crystalline Cavern]
description: A huge monument dominates the center of this donut-shaped confluence of avenues.  Several dwarven warriors, rendered in gleaming white marble, battle a dozen orcs, depicted in black obsidian.  Several stone benches rest around the monument, facing outward in a circular pattern, while other benches sit on the outer edges of the circle, facing the monument.  Wide streets lead in from the north, south, east and west, and each thoroughfare is lined with luminescent toadstools in wide stone pots.
paths: Obvious exits: north, east, south, west
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Crystalline Cavern]
description: A spacious gem dome stretches out to the northeast, east and southeast, unsupported by pillars or beams.  The curvature is accented by the placement of hundreds of thousands of clear crystals across the stone sky.  The crystals catch the light from the luminescent toadstools beneath, reflecting and refracting the light in brilliant white as well as all the colors of the rainbow.  As one shifts position, the varying bands of light shift and play colorfully along the stone floor.
paths: Obvious exits: northeast, east, southeast, southwest
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Emerald Tunnel]
description: Emerald light plays across the tunnel ceiling in circular patches as each toadstool projects its glow upward through its green cap.  A gentle, constant breeze courses through the tunnel, but the toadstools remain unmoving due to the sheer weight and solidity of their stalks and lack of variance in the wind's speed.  The lower glow from the toadstools also creates pools of light and areas of darkness.  This is not a travel problem, though, for the floor is smooth and clear of hidden obstructions.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Ruby Tunnel]
description: Colorful depictions of outdoor homes have been painted upon the walls in realistic detail.  Only the doors are real, though.  A white marble mansion looms on the north wall, complete with black wrought ironwork along its curtained windows.  The south wall displays a cute pink bungalow nestled within a stand of birch trees.  In the split between the northeast tunnel and the southeast tunnel, the bottom floor of a circular stone tower looms with candle-lit windows.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Ruby Tunnel]
description: The few dwarves that pass this way seem somewhat perturbed by the presence of adventurers in their midst, particularly adventurers that are not dwarven.  Some dwarves stare outright.  Others gaze more with mixture of incredulity and awe.  Small dwarven children, frightened by the larger beings, hide behind a toadstool pot or behind their mother's skirt and stare, speechlessly, at these new ones who have been allowed to invade their city.

Overhead, the solid rock of the ceiling is broken by a steep chute.  The few dwarves that pass along the stretch of tunnel seem perturbed by the presence of visitors, particularly those not of dwarven heritage.  Some of the natives stare outright, while others greet intruders with a mixture of incredulity and awe.  Small dwarven children hide behind a toadstool pot or behind their mothers' skirts and stare, speechless, at the travelers invading their city.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Ruby Tunnel]
description: Large pots spaced at twenty-foot intervals house one giant toadstool each.  The toadstools provide light for the mine shafts, projecting a bright crimson light toward the ceiling and a soft white light toward the floor.  The illumination is not complete, with pools of light punctuated by intervals of darkness that march off into the distance.  The toadstools are nearly the perfect lighting devices, causing no smoke, no fire hazard, and merely needing a bit of water and nutrition.
paths: Obvious exits: east, southeast, southwest, northwest
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Ruby Tunnel]
description: If mining could be called an art, this tunnel may be as close as it gets.  A perfectly flat granite floor, its surface roughened just a little for traction, leads off to the southeast.  The walls follow, their sides unerringly vertical and neither moving together nor widening out.  The ceiling is a flat, smoothly chiseled expanse of grey granite.  Thick beams set the same exact distance apart all the way down the tunnel support the walls and ceiling.
location: the tunnels and caverns of Zul Logoth

title: [Zul Logoth, Ruby Tunnel]
description: The smooth walls of the tunnel give way to a small cavern utilized as an entrance to the vast network of mining tunnels under the DragonSpine.  Carts ricochet past on a double-railed metal track, stopping occasionally for brief instances to pick up passengers.  Several dwarves busily work the area, ensuring the carts travel rapidly towards their destination.

title: [DragonSpine Mountains, Crevasse]
description: The pass dwindles and disappears into a large crevasse.  Nearly black inside as compared to the bright light of day, dwarves and travellers hasten into the crevasse, from which odd grinding and squealing sounds can occasionally be heard.

title: [Pass, Entrance]
description: A small pass winds around the mountain to the east.  Groups led by dwarven guides appear and disappear around the corner of the pass towards Ta'Illistim and other eastern cities.  Travelers gather around preparing for the trek, while others are resting after a long trip.

title: [Khazar's Hold, Grotto]
description: The center of the village lies just to the west.  Two buildings and several ratty tents have been constructed on this artificial ledge.  Beyond the settlement, the deep blue sky contrasts with the bland greys of the mountainous landscape.  White clouds, constantly reshaped by the wind pushing them across the jagged summits, gather around the peaks of the mountain ranges on all sides of the valley.

title: [Khazar's Hold, Grotto]
description: Sheltered from the stiff breeze out on the ledge, a large, sturdy building stands against the stone wall created by this artificial cavern.  A hand-painted sign is nailed above the door of the structure.  The rough wall and ground are uneven, and marks from the picks used to carve the cave out of the mountainside are slightly smoothed by erosion, but still apparent.  Occasionally, dust rains down from above, loosened by the winds.

title: [Khazar's Hold, Central]
description: A dwarven outpost is located on this shelf carved into the rock mountain face.  Ragged tents line the edges of the outpost along the cliff and rock face.  A ramshackle tavern that sits just to the north has a faded wooden sign hanging unsteadily above its door.  The wind whips around the sides of the mountain, kicking up dirt and adding quite a chill to the air.  Diverse groups of travelers wander past, most likely just passing through on their way to another town.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Cliff]
description: A rough precipice juts out from the mountainside, creating a ledge above.  Tufts of sturdy grasses grow out of dirt that has collected in the crevices of the rock.  The moonlight glows softly on the sea of mist in the valley below.

A rough precipice juts out from the mountainside, creating a ledge above.  Tufts of sturdy grasses grow out of dirt that has collected in the crevices of the rock.  A sea of white mist floats near the floor of the valley below, tendrils of the mist whirling and dissipating above the surface.
tags: meta:mapname:Elven Nations - Trail (Locksmehr River/West of Dragonspine)

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The air is bitterly cold and dry.  The edges of the dull grey clouds above shimmer bright silver, reflecting the moonlight.  Grass taking root in patches of dirt rustles softly as the strong breeze constantly blows around the mountain.  The uneven rock face and small ledge are noticeably smoothed by the sand and dirt that ride the unrelenting wind.

Clouds created by the high peaks of the mountain range drift slowly through the sky.  The uneven rock face and small ledge are noticeably smoothed by the sand and dirt that ride the unrelenting wind.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The mist below glows white from the moonlight.  The stars are filtered out by the bright moons, but are still visible.  The dark ledge is smoothed somewhat, and traces of moss line the small indentions of the rock.  The stiff breeze adds a chill to the air.  A rocky crevice leads upwards, and the ledge expands towards the northwest.

A few small, puffy white clouds float in the air around the peaks of the mountain range above.  The deep blue sky shimmers beyond the mountains and clouds.  The stiff breeze adds a chill to the air.  A rocky crevice leads upwards, and the ledge expands towards the northwest.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The ledge is one of many small, flat areas scattered across the slope of the mountains.  The ominous peaks of the mountain ranges protecting the valley open up towards the southwest.  Beyond the Dead Plateau, the moonlight sparkles weakly on the distant Locksmehr River.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The immense mountain range wraps around to the north, west and south to form a large bowl.  The mist in the valley below floats closely to the ground, undisturbed by the heavier winds aloft.  A few treetops protrude from the fog in the northern area of the valley and tops of boulders rise above the mist to the south.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The dry dirt and dusty rocks are signs of the arid climate.  The air is crisp, lacking the moisture of the mist-covered valley below.  The sea of fog strangely and abruptly stops just a few feet below this ledge, along with the calm and stillness surrounding it.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: A thick mist envelopes the mountainside just below this narrow ledge.  Wisps of the mist rise up on the steady breeze, drifting slowly through the air before dissipating.  The dry air pushes gritty, loose dirt across the now smooth, rocky mountainside.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The thin ledge slowly disappears against the mountain towards the northwest, leaving the ledge to the southeast or the sheer rock cliff leading upward the only directions of travel.  The damp, cold air creates a raw atmosphere, its heavy mist blanketing the area.  Green and brown moss clings to many of the jagged rocks forming the ledge and wall of the mountain.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The ledge narrows here somewhat, but it is still passable.  A small flurry of dust, disturbed by passing footsteps, disappears into the mist below the ledge.  The mountainside is sharp and rigid with pointed rock protruding out and small, deep fissures leading into the mountain.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The heavy mist drowns out all background noises, leaving a creepy silence over the ledge.  A hefty rock lies on the ledge, not quite large enough to impede progress, but large enough to stir concern over similar-sized rocks falling down the mountain from above.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: A soft mat of dull-colored moss covers the rock underfoot, muffling footsteps.  Dim lights out in the mist glow for a few seconds, and then fade from existence.  Odd scratching sounds come from a deep fissure, the emanations few and quick before resting.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: The silence on the ledge combined with the heavy mist isolates the area.  The only features are a light grey wall of fog to the west and the solid dark grey of the mountain to the east.  A nearly imperceptible breeze floats past occasionally, adding to the eerie atmosphere.  The ledge leads off to the northwest, and the cliff below looks scalable.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: This short, narrow ledge runs along the side of the massive mountain.  Deep fissures along the face of the mountain are jagged and sharp, untouched by any form of erosion.  A jagged cliff leads upward, bearing natural handholds created by the cracks and crevices in the rock.  The damp air hangs heavily throughout the area, creating a cool, raw atmosphere.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Slope]
description: Mist clings to the grey rock face, the air calm and cool.  Patches of lichen and moss cover the rock, blending a darker grey into the rocky surroundings.  A narrow ledge leads to the southeast, while all other directions are blocked by the steep mountainside.  Below, the ground is barely visible through the mist.

Mist clings to the grey rock face, the air calm and cool.  Patches of lichen and moss cover the rock, adding some drab color to the otherwise grey surroundings.  A narrow ledge leads to the southeast, while all other directions are blocked by the steep mountainside.  Below, the ground is barely visible through the mist.

title: [Western DragonSpine, Base]
description: The whole of Glo'antern Moor stretches out to the west, although much of it is shrouded in a dense layer of fog.  Strange pinpoints of light appear to flicker and dance in the mists.  Where the fog is not present the moor is a dark grey interspersed with small, lighter grey blotches.  A tall range of snow-capped mountains looms to the north, east and southeast, while a broad forest extends along far to the northwest.  In the distance a rock plateau rises above the mists, its top perfectly flat.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The rocky ground supports little plant life.  Clumps of hardy grass cling to what soil is present, and stumpy conifers force their way up through cracks between the rocks.  The trail drops steeply to the southwest and ascends in the same manner to the northeast.  The mists swirl as a soft breeze pushes them around obstructions in the area, and chipmunks scamper over the bare rocks in search of pinecone seeds, insects, and other things to eat.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The trail drops gently to the southwest, descending into thick fog.  To the northeast it climbs steeply, rising out of the surrounding mists.  Long-bladed grass has taken root all over the area, but its attempts to cover the area are interrupted by boulders, the occasional odd tree stump, and patches of bare ground.  Even a few small pine trees make valiant attempts to combat the encroaching grass.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The presence of decomposing stumps interspersed throughout the grass indicates that this area might once have been a forest long ago lost to the woodsman's axe.  Some of the stumps measure several feet across, and the trees that topped them must have been impressive in height and spread.  Now, with the tops long gone, the stumps provide homes to robust colonies of ants that scurry up and down the sides to transport food into their homes.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The thick fog wraps the area in a stifling cloud of wet mist.  Sounds are deadened and breathing becomes more labored in the heavy air.  The grass drips water, running down the blades to pool on the trail.  At this point the trail changes direction slightly, proceeding levelly to the west but rising gently to the northeast.  Lights of various colors appear far off in the distance to the northwest and south, just barely visible in the fog.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The trail leads in a general direction to the east and west, veering around boulders but making steady progress through the tall grass.  The boulders all seem to be of the same type of rock.  Their dark grey facets glisten with moisture and their surfaces are smooth to the touch.  They protrude in various sizes from the grasslands, some round, some pointed, some erratically shaped, and some even suggesting the forms of different animals.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The trail continues steadily to the east and west.  A howling erupts from out on the moor somewhere, the mournful tones filling the air for a full minute before abruptly stopping.  To the south a thundering sound passes by as if many beasts of considerable size were rushing from east to west, and, as the noise recedes, the sound of something padding through the grasses approaches and stops.  Whatever it is remains concealed by the grass and fog.  It snorts twice, then retreats.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: A single white light slowly appears in front of you several yards into the thick fog accompanied by a barely audible buzzing.  It stays consistently just ahead of you, partially hidden by the mists.  The light moves up and down rhythmically, always keeping the same distance, stopping when you stop, moving faster away when you accelerate.  After a few minutes it suddenly winks out, the buzzing stops, and the area returns to its quiet solitude.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: Something has died very near the trail.  The sickly sweet aroma of rotting flesh hangs as thickly in the air as the surrounding mists, and the intermittent scraping movements of small animals somewhere out in the grass indicate that others are either searching for or have found the carcass.  Occasionally a small snarl or a high-pitched shriek cuts the air, but for the most part the area is as silent as whatever is slowly decomposing out in the fog.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The gloom produced by the thick mist is dark enough that fireflies have come out to play.  The small winged insects flit about, flashing in shades of red and yellow as they move among the tall grasses in search of mates or food.  The absence of a breeze makes it easy for the insects to maneuver, and occasionally a large cloud of them will spill across the path directly ahead as if daring anything to move through them.  Somehow they always seem to get out of the way before a confrontation occurs, though.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: Something has disturbed the grasses at this point in the trail, and although the way is obvious to the west, it is totally indiscernible in the other direction.  The heavy mists do not help matters, limiting vision to twenty yards at best, and the wet grass seems to be especially tall all around.  A dark obsidian boulder perhaps ten feet high sits nearby, its surface scarred and deeply gouged by implements unknown.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The moist cold slips inside clothing at every opportunity, uncomfortably wetting skin and miserably soaking anything not immune to its liquid touch.  Bright lights flicker on somewhere out in the mists to both sides of you, accompanied by a raucous fit of high-pitched laughter.  The lights move along with you as if held by something paralleling your course, not approaching nor receding.  Then, one by one the lights disappear in the matter of a few seconds leaving only the quiet, wet grassland and mist.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The thick mists drape heavily.  Long blades of wet grass overhang over the trail, soaking anything that has to move between them.  The soggy ground squishes underfoot, and the mashed grasses on the trail combine with mud from underneath to form a slick, treacherous surface.  One misstep could result in a soaked, dirty backside or, perhaps worse, a face full of muddy grass.  Keeping one's eye on the trail and trudging diligently forward might be the best plan.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Forest's Edge]
description: Lofty pines compete with billowing spruces for light and moisture in the extensive forest to the north.  The odor of pinesap combined with the scent of decaying needles wafts out from the serene forest's cool, shady confines.  To the southwest the trail lazily follows the edges of the forest, jogging here and there to avoid a particularly thick tree trunk.  To the southeast it rolls off into the moor, a barely perceptible path of matted grass, until a thick bank of fog swallows it entirely.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Forest's Edge]
description: The trail winds along just outside the conifer forest, a small line of demarcation between the encroaching trees and the grassy moor.  It is as if someone has drawn a ragged, wavy line in the earth and declared, "Trees on this side, grass on that side."  No grasses invade the needle-covered ground beneath the pines, and no saplings attempt to push up through the moor's tight blades of grass.  The moons shine down brightly from overhead, equally lighting both sides of the demarcation line.

A hawk slowly circles overhead, looking for a meal on either side of the demarcation line.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Forest's Edge]
description: A vast forest spreads out to the northwest, north and northeast.  Stately pines reach up high toward the sky with younger trees clumped around them.  The forest floor is littered with a thick carpet of dark grey and light grey needles as well as prickly, sticky pinecones.  In the distance, an owl calls out, its hooting breaking the silence of the trees.  The trail does not lead into the forest, but parallels it to the southeast and moves off into the moor to the southwest.

The forest floor is littered with a thick carpet of grey and yellow needles as well as prickly, sticky pinecones.  Squirrels scamper through the trees, chittering loudly at each other.  The trail does not lead into the forest, but parallels it to the southeast and moves off into the moor to the southwest.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: A herd of urghs grazes off to the southeast, their dark backs barely visible above the tall grasses.  Occasionally one raises its tusked head as if sniffing at the breeze then resumes foraging.  To the north the edge of a large forest looms on the horizon, and dark clouds gather further back, with flashes of lightning punctuating the dark, billowy mass.  The presence of only a slight wind in the area indicates that the storm does not seem to be headed this way.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The trail continues to move in a northeast/southwest direction through the monotonous sea of grass.  The wind barely stirs the tops of the blades, and, except for the infrequent flight of some small animal frightened by the footsteps, the view is a serene, untroubled landscape.  A few small clouds drift lazily overhead to block the moon at times, and pockets of mist swirl near some of the larger boulders, the edges of the mists coalescing and breaking apart as the breezes buffets them.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: Cicadas provide a low droning throughout the grassland.  The insects seem to be in perfect cadence, as if someone has orchestrated them all.  Their noises rise and fall together in intensity, ranging from extremely loud to a bare background tone.  All at once the buzzing ceases entirely, and the silence seems to be louder than the noise that preceded it.  Then, as if on cue, the cicadas pick up again where they left off.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: A long line of mounded dirt appears to the west, causing those who wish to move that direction to follow the trail to the southwest where the mound seems to gradually disappear.  The long line of mounded dirt proceeds miles to the northwest where, on the horizon, a huge mountain of dirt has been pushed up by some inexplicable force.  Grasses have reclaimed the dirt mounds to some extent, although patches of bare dirt are still very much evident.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: A furrow begins just to the northwest, becoming deeper as it moves northwest until the bottom is completely shrouded in darkness.  The trail skirts the furrow on both sides, tracking northeast and northwest.  Very little grows in the furrow, although some of the grasses have attempted to root in the beginnings.  The few stones that peek out from the sides of the furrow have a peculiar glazed look to them, not dissimilar to the stones one might find at the bottom of a blacksmith's forge.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: Any attempt at progress to the northeast is blocked by a large furrow, maybe fifty feet across, which runs in a general northwest/southeast direction.  Large amounts of dirt are piled up on either side of the furrow.  Although the sides of the furrow are crumbly and footing treacherous, it is possible to see that the furrow is quite deep, its bottom shrouded in darkness.  The trail moves off to the southwest in one direction, and veers to the southeast in the other.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: Moonlight beams down to illuminate the moor for miles all around.  Mists stir in pockets throughout the area, buffeted by a slight breeze.  Tall grasses spread out as far as the eye can see, punctuated by the presence of scattered boulders of different sizes that protrude up through the green carpet.  The breeze buffets the top of the grass, moving across it in slow waves to give the grass the appearance of a rolling, dark green sea.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Singing Woods]
description: A dense forest extends off to the southwest and west, its trees spaced unnaturally close.  Healthy bramble and holly growth covers the forest floor beneath the trees even though the upper canopy appears too thick to allow much nourishing sunlight to penetrate to the lower levels during the day.  Laughter and other sounds of revelry are audible, but it is difficult to discern from which direction they come.  The trail leads south, skirting the forest, and northeast, out into the open, treeless moor.

Laughter and other sounds of revelry are audible, but it is difficult to discern from which direction they come.  The trail leads south, skirting the forest, and northeast, out into the open, treeless moor.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Singing Woods]
description: Lights flicker and move to the west and southwest. Further investigation of this phenomenon is prevented by the tightly interwoven forest, in which poplars and birches stand sentinel before massive oaks and spreading maples.  Under the deciduous canopy, holly bushes happily entreat travelers to try to move through their razor-sharp leaves and offer bright, poisonous berries to the unwary.  The trail follows a north-south orientation here, with the forest to the west and the moor to the east.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Singing Woods]
description: The mouthwatering aroma of roast boar wafts in from the forest to the west accompanied by the inescapable sounds of merriment.  The lilting tones of musical instruments fill the air, and song voiced in a strange tongue rises and falls from deep within the forest.  Lights in varying soft colors flash suddenly among the trees, then wink out or move away with dizzying speed. The trail follows the curve of the forest from north to southwest.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Singing Woods]
description: A large pile of white bones stands between the trail and the forest.  The bones are devoid of any flesh, and most appear to be from animals such as boar, urgh and rolton.  The forest is impenetrable, but through the screen of vegetation numerous lights of varying colors flash, spin, and appear to advance and recede accompanied by raucous laughter and loud singing in an undecipherable tongue.  The trail continues to run between the forest and the moor.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Singing Woods]
description: Lights seem to flicker and waver deep in the forest to the north, occasionally accompanied by snatches of song or laughter.  The trail moves in a northeast/southwest direction, skirting the edge of the forest.  To the southeast the grassy moor extends into a bank of mist, the tall, tightly bunched, wet grasses looking terribly uninviting.  Neither forest nor grassland appears to be a particularly hospitable place for travelers.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Singing Woods]
description: A thick deciduous forest rises out of the fog to the north.  Birch and poplar trees, tightly interwoven, form a screen that prevents passage, shunting the trail off to the northeast.  As if the tree branches and trunks were not enough, a maze of holly bushes grows underneath the trees, their sharply serrated leaves waiting to rend and tear should anyone or anything be foolish enough to try to force its way into the forest.  To the southwest the trail moves out into the open moor.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: Boulders thrust up at odd angles through the grasses, protruding in dark shapes against the grey carpet.  The mist keeps everything covered in a watery layer, making passage through the grasslands wet, cold and uncomfortable.  No wind stirs the blades of grass that stand stiffly upright with only a slight lean at the tops, bunched thickly enough to prevent anything resembling a tree from gaining a foothold in this area.

Boulders thrust up at odd angles through the grasses, protruding in greys and blacks against the green carpet.  The mist keeps everything covered in a watery layer, making passage through the grasslands wet, cold and uncomfortable.  No wind stirs the blades of grass that stand stiffly upright with only a slight lean at the tops, bunched thickly enough to prevent anything resembling a tree from gaining a foothold in this area.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: Thick grass grows as far as the eye can see, which isn't very far in the gloomy mist.  The grass extends several feet high and is a dark grey broken here and there by small patches of lighter grey blades.  Brighter spots on the glowing mists overhead indicates the positions of the moons, and enough light filters down to make it easy to see the partially trampled path that serves as a trail across this moor.

Thick grass grows as far as the eye can see, which isn't very far in the gloomy mist.  The grass extends several feet high and is a deep green broken here and there by small patches of light green and yellow blades.  A brighter spot on the glowing mists overhead indicates the position of the sun, and enough light filters down to make it easy to see the partially trampled path that serves as a trail across this moor.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: A tall grey boulder stands to the south, blocking passage in the direction.  The bulk of its mass extends to the west, while the trail skirts around it to the southeast.  Fat white grubs as large as a giantman's finger feed along the edge of the boulder, underneath its sheltering side in the thick rich loam of decomposing grasses.  Their bodies ooze and pulsate as they move along in search of more digestible matter.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: Small tunnels no larger than a human's thigh lead underneath the massive boulder to the west.  The tunnels are certainly much too small for any person to use, as if one would really want to clamber down into the cold, moist earth here.  Occasionally a pointed, whiskered snout protrudes out from one of the tunnels, followed by a pair of squinting green eyes.  The animal pauses, surveying the area, then retreats into the tunnel again accompanied by a loud chittering.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The edges of the boulder define the direction of the trail: north and southwest.  The long, tall grass closes in against the boulder, but near the rock the grass is slightly matted down, perhaps by the travel of someone or something.  Overhead the mist glows a soft white hue in a gentle reminder that the moons still exist somewhere up there beyond the covering veil, but only a little light penetrates to the ground below.

The edges of the boulder define the direction of the trail: north and southwest.  The long, tall grass closes in against the boulder, but near the rock the grass is slightly matted down, perhaps by the travel of someone or something.  Overhead the mist glows a soft yellow hue in a gentle reminder that the sun still exists somewhere up there beyond the covering veil, but only a little light and heat penetrates to the ground below.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: A huge grey boulder juts up from the earth directly to the north, forcing those wishing to travel in that general direction to veer to the northeast.  The top of the boulder is shrouded in the mists, and one side extends at least a hundred yards to the west before disappearing in the gloom.  The boulder's sides are slick and shiny, almost gemlike, and no path of ascension presents itself.  Small rivulets of water trickle down the surface of the boulder to drip onto the grass.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The fog seems to be all around and overhead.  Chilly, damp tendrils reach down to moisten clothing, skin and hair with their clammy touch.  Although the fog is a thick, wet blanket, it still allows vision for perhaps a hundred yards.  If only there were more to look at other than a sea of tall grass extending motionlessly in all directions.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: An overgrown bramble bush clings to life against the side of the cliff just to the west, blocking further passage in that direction with its long thorns and tightly woven branches.  A sparse collection of leaves clings to the ends of the branches, and the bush does not look to be in a robust state of health.  Perhaps the lack of sunlight coupled with the cold, damp conditions have something to do with its predicament.

title: [Glo'antern Moor]
description: The trail follows the sheer cliff face to the west and southeast.  Extending up through the fog until it is lost from sight, the smooth basalt wall of the cliff displays no handholds for use in ascending.  Its surface undulates slightly as if it had been cast in molten form, the hot rock waving back and forth, before solidifying into place.  The thick grass ends just short of the cliff, allowing relatively dry and unimpeded movement in both directions.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Rope Ladder]
description: A thick rope ladder dangles down the side of the cliff, pooling a bit on the ground.  The top of the ladder is not distinguishable as it disappears quickly into the mists above.  A small barren spot has been worn in the matted grass just below the rope ladder, most likely from the passing of feet and the swaying of the ladder.  In all directions away from the cliff the damp, thick grass grows high enough to prevent movement, although it seems to be somewhat beaten down along the cliff to the northwest.

title: [Rope Ladder]
description: Thick mist fills your vision on three sides, while on the fourth the sheer basalt wall of the cliff looms vertical and close.  Sounds become muffled and distorted by the thick, damp air, preventing their location from being ascertained at all.  Nothing moves in the mist or on the cliff face, and the only thing to do is continue to climb, either up through the mist, or down through the mist.

title: [Rope Ladder]
description: The top of the mist blanket stretches out to the northwest, north, northeast and east from where you hang on the rope ladder.  Above, the starry sky is unbroken by any cloud formations, and the moon shines down brightly off the white surface of the mists.  The ladder continues many hundreds of feet above, swaying slowly back and forth, while below it disappears quickly into the mists.  A small nest of some bird, now abandoned, resides in a crack in the sheer cliff side.

The top of the mist blanket stretches out to the northwest, north, northeast and east from where you hang on the rope ladder.  Above, the blue sky is unbroken by any cloud formations, and the sun shines down brightly off the white surface of the mists.  The ladder continues many hundreds of feet above, swaying slowly back and forth, while below it disappears quickly into the mists.  A small nest of some bird, now abandoned, resides in a crack in the sheer cliff side.

title: [Rope Ladder]
description: The sheer side of the Dead Plateau looms in front of you, the surface smooth and devoid of plant life.  To the north and east the mists spread out below to blanket the area in a white, frothy covering.  The rope ladder extends several hundred feet above to the top of the plateau, while below it drops straight down into the concealing mists.  A slight wind buffets you, causing the rope ladder to rock back and forth.

title: [Dead Plateau, Rope Ladder]
description: The Dead Plateau stretches out as far as the eye can see to the west, southwest, south and southeast in a long, cold, perfectly level expanse of solid rock.  It would be easy to navigate by the moons and strike out in one of the directions except for the presence of yawning, jagged crevices running as untamed lightning across the plateau's interior.  One crevice extends to the plateau's edge, cutting off travel to the west and leaving the only passable direction along the edge to the southeast.

It would be easy to navigate by the sun and strike out in one of the directions except for the presence of yawning, jagged crevices running as untamed lightning across the plateau's interior. title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The wind howls across the high plateau in chill, dry gusts, trying desperately to suck the moisture out of everything it touches.  The plateau's surface is dustless, scoured clean by the wind's relentless journey and left to gleam with a grey dullness in the moonlight.  The interior's cracks rush toward the plateau's edge, only to close before reaching their goal, leaving the edge passable to both the northwest and southeast.

The wind howls across the high plateau in chill, dry gusts, trying desperately to suck the moisture out of everything it touches.  The plateau's surface is dustless, scoured clean by the wind's relentless journey and left to gleam with a grey dullness in the direct sunlight.  The interior's cracks rush toward the plateau's edge, only to close before reaching their goal, leaving the edge passable to both the northwest and southeast.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: Solid rock stretches out in a hard grey sheet to form the plateau's surface.  Stiff and unyielding in the slightest, it is like walking on tempered steel or polished marble.  The wind has buffed the stone to a dull sheen, and though it means there are no protrusions on which to stub one's toe, it also means that footing can be slick and treacherous.  The cold wind has allowed none of the day's sunlight warmth to be absorbed into the plateau, and the stone surface is very chilly to the touch.

Solid rock stretches out in a hard grey sheet to form the plateau's surface.  Stiff and unyielding in the slightest, it is like walking on tempered steel or polished marble.  The wind has buffed the stone to a dull sheen, and though it means there are no protrusions on which to stub one's toe, it also means that footing can be slick and treacherous.  Although the sun shines down brightly, the cold wind also removes heat before the plateau can absorb it, leaving the stone surface chilly to the touch.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: Nothing stirs on the plateau--not an insect, or rodent, or any living form.  Nothing creeps or crawls.  Nothing flies or buzzes.  The grey basalt stretches for miles, unbroken in color by anything green.  The absence of soil, anything smaller than a pebble long ago whisked away by the wind, and lack of rainfall combine to make this an inhospitable land for flora as well.  Only the wind exists here, and to listen to it, it's not very happy about being here, either.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: A sea of mist stretches out below to hide the landscape from view.  The cloudy covering extends north, northeast, east and southeast, reflecting the moonlight in a brilliant white blanket.  Here and there groups of trees push up through the mist, appearing as dark islands in the midst of the sea.  To the southeast and north the mists end at expansive forests, while to the northeast and east the confining factors are the tall spires of the DragonSpine Mountains.

A sea of mist stretches out below to hide the landscape from view.  The cloudy covering extends north, northeast, east and southeast, reflecting the sunlight in a brilliant white blanket.  Here and there groups of trees push up through the mist, appearing as green islands in the midst of the sea.  To the southeast and north the mists end at expansive forests, while to the northeast and east the confining factors are the tall spires of the DragonSpine Mountains.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: Not one cloud makes an attempt to block the moons here on the plateau.  Brightly, but without warmth, the moonlight beams down on the flat rock surface, reflecting harshly off the smooth basalt.  Below, the moonlight also bounces brilliantly off the white cloud layer that surrounds the plateau, shimmering intensely until it becomes too vivid to look at.  The starry sky provides a much easier resting place for the eyes, although eventually it, too, becomes much too monotonous.

Not one cloud makes an attempt to block the sun here on the plateau.  Brightly, but without warmth, the sun beats down on the flat rock surface, reflecting harshly off the smooth basalt.  Below, the sun also bounces brilliantly off the white cloud layer that surrounds the plateau, shimmering intensely until it becomes too vivid to look at.  The blue sky provides a much easier resting place for the eyes, although eventually it, too, becomes much too monotonous.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: A shriek pierces through the wind's howling, the source somewhere toward the interior of the plateau.  Moaning follows, rising in pitch, then subsiding again.  Then, as the wind suddenly picks up speed, another shriek, exactly the same as before, followed again by the low moaning as the wind slows its gusting.  Eventually the pattern becomes distinguishable, another effect of the wind's lonely journey through this desolate plateau.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The trail continues to follow the edge of the plateau to the northwest and south, skirting very close to the edge to avoid large crevices that race out of the interior only to turn and zigzag back into the endless wasteland.  The plateau's interior almost looks as if someone molded the entire area out of soft clay, scraped it flat, then sent lightning randomly coursing through to make the crevices before it all hardened in place.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: Some of the smaller crevices manage to fracture all the way to the edge in this area.  However, they are thin enough that the area can be traversed by hopping from basalt island to basalt island, careful to stay near the plateau's edge for orientation and to clear each crack well.  Words shouted into the crevices do not return echos, and items dropped do not send back the sound of hitting bottom.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: To the east, the thick blanket of fog traps the land under its white, unmoving canopy.  To the west, the Dead Plateau's interior stretches away in a maze of cracks and crevices across an unnaturally flat expanse.  Before you, the hard stone trail follows the plateau edge.  Behind you, the hard stone trail follows the plateau edge.  The sameness seems to stretch forever, and the cold, dry wind follows you, adding to the monotony with its constant rising and ebbing wail.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: Someone has etched something into the basalt rock.  A large, very distinct arrow points northward, and underneath a single word has been written.  A second arrow, somewhat less distinct and much smaller than the first, points toward the interior.  Whatever was written below it has been obliterated, although all around the arrow dance crudely drawn images of strange figures, six-armed animals and a single, huge gem.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: Small tremors shake the plateau as if something huge is moving along underneath the surface.  The tremors rise and fall a bit in intensity but are rather soft and inaudible in the howling wind.  The plateau does not visibly move, but you can feel the vibrations with the soles of your feet.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The trail glimmers and flickers as it moves southwest and northeast.  Minute particles of a gem-like substance, imbedded in the rock surface, catch the moonlight and reflect it in tiny bursts of grey and silver.  An old sign, tumbled from its shattered post, lies alongside the trail.  The main trail follows the plateau's edge northeast and southwest, but it also appears possible to move toward the plateau's interior in a northwest direction should one wish to do so.

The trail glimmers and flickers as it moves southwest and northeast.  Minute particles of a gem-like substance, imbedded in the rock surface, catch the sunlight and reflect it in tiny bursts of blue and aquamarine.  An old sign, tumbled from its shattered post, lies alongside the trail.  The main trail follows the plateau's edge northeast and southwest, but it also appears possible to move toward the plateau's interior in a northwest direction should one wish to do so.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: Below, two waves appear to meet and stand still.  To the northeast a blanket of fog hides the land under its heavy, billowy cloud cover.  To the southwest, a low range of mountains undulates across the landscape, barren and arid.  The two meet head-on in a line just below you that runs directly off to the southeast until it meets a third natural formation--a thick forest that neither the fog nor the mountains seem ready to assault.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The edge of the plateau undulates much like the fluted rim of a pie crust, causing the trail to snake back and forth.  The wind has managed to bore a fairly large hole through a lateral extension of the solid rock, presenting a sizeable ring of solid stone that hangs out over the sheer drop to the mountains below.  It might be interesting to investigate the ring except for the uncertainty of the ring's load-bearing qualities and the annoyingly shrill scream the wind makes as it races through the hole.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The cracks and crevices that dominate the interior scurry closer to the edge here, many of them yawning widely as if hoping for something to accidentally fall into their ever-agape maws.  In places two or more crevices cross, leaving strange-looking islands of rock to stand, giving the impression of rock platforms suspended in midair.  One particularly large crevice winds close, and something white flickers up from it every so often before disappearing quickly back down inside.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The sound of rushing water, its source possibly to the west, filters in over the moaning of the wind.  The plateau's edge moves off to the west and east, while below, in the distance, moonlight glints off the surface of a river that winds toward the southeast.  The river appears strangely out of place in such a barren land.

The sound of rushing water, its source possibly to the west, filters in over the moaning of the wind.  The plateau's edge moves off to the west and east, while below, in the distance, sunlight glints off the surface of a river that winds toward the southeast.  The river appears strangely out of place in such a barren land.

title: [Dead Plateau, River Chasm]
description: A torrent erupts from the face of the plateau several hundred feet below.  Clear, sparkling water pours out of a chasm and cascades to the low mountain range below, drifting off to the southeast as a silver ribbon.  Though the river appears to provide ample water, no trees dot the river's edge as far as the eye can see.  The chasm itself yawns before you a hundred feet wide, effectively blocking progress along the plateau's edge to the west.

A torrent erupts from the face of the plateau several hundred feet below.  Clear, sparkling water pours out of a chasm and cascades to the low mountain range below, drifting off to the southeast as a blue ribbon.  Though the river appears to provide ample water, no trees dot the river's edge as far as the eye can see.  The chasm itself yawns before you a hundred feet wide, effectively blocking progress along the plateau's edge to the west.

title: [Dead Plateau, River Chasm]
description: The river crevice runs straight and true in a northwest/southeast direction.  Neither rising nor falling, the path follows the crevice's edge closely.  The rock surface feels dry and solid, even at the edge of the chasm.  Even for stone, though, this surface is hard and unyielding.  The cracks that infest the interior move closer to the chasm's edge, squeezing the passage at many points and funneling travel into walkways that allow passage only one person wide.

title: [Dead Plateau, River Chasm]
description: The sparse trail follows the deep crevice to the west and southeast.  The roar of rushing water echoes up from the crevice's depths, but the torrent's view is lost in the inky blackness of the crevice.  The nearness of such a large volume of water does nothing to relieve the arid conditions as the wind, pouring out of the dry plateau's interior, carries away any hint of moisture.  The wind's continual howling mixed with the water's constant roar pounds dully at the auditory senses.

title: [Dead Plateau, Plank Bridge]
description: A sturdy plank bridge spans the river chasm, offering a westward crossing and a respite from following the chasm deeper into the Dead Plateau's interior.  In the other direction, the trail follows the chasm's edge to the east and the plateau's edge again.  It is fortunate that the crevice narrows to approximately thirty feet at this point, allowing construction of the bridge, for farther up the crevice the sides diverge widely again as far as the eye can see.

title: [Dead Plateau, River Chasm]
description: The roar of the rushing water within the parallel crevice combines with the howling wind to render conversation a difficult task, even if one is only talking to oneself.  The crevice turns sharply, defining the trail to be westward and southward.  Small crevices converge with the much larger one, either causing a moment's inconvenience in the form of a small jump or a large detour to find a safer crossing.

title: [Dead Plateau, River Chasm]
description: A crevice a hundred feet wide blocks passage along the plateau's edge to the east.  Several hundred feet below, a torrent of water gushes out of the crevice in a spectacular waterfall, crashing down to the hills below and winding away to the southeast.  The plateau is arid and inhospitable, indicating that rainfall is a rare occurrence, yet the sheer amount of water suggests a voluminous source.  The only travel options available are to follow the crevice to the north or the plateau's edge to the west.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: Eastward and westward the trail extends along the flat plateau, unbroken by the crevices that spread like jagged lightning across the Dead Plateau's interior.  The ground is hard, all soil blown away long ago by the ceaseless wind, and nothing attempts to live in this severe climate.  Without soil, without rain, nothing attracts plants or animals.  The sound of rushing water comes from the east, audible in small snatches when the wind chooses to abate momentarily.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The trek continues around the edge of the plateau with no sign of ending anytime soon.  The sky holds a black expanse filled with stars, but it is difficult to spend time examining them and not walk off the plateau's edge.  The Dead Plateau is uninteresting, displaying its flat, windswept surface with myriad cracks and crevices, and the hills below are a uniform shade of dull grey.  If one did not die here from the cold and lack of water, it is conceivable that one could die of boredom.

The trek continues around the edge of the plateau with no sign of ending anytime soon.  The sky holds nothing but a blue expanse and the sun's yellow orb.  The Dead Plateau is equally uninteresting, displaying its flat, windswept surface with myriad cracks and crevices, and the hills below are a uniform shade of dull yellow brown.  If one did not die here from the cold and lack of water, it is conceivable that one could die of boredom.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: A narrow crevice sweeps close to the edge of the plateau before running away in a zigzag fashion.  Down in the crevice, the body of a dwarf has lodged between the rock walls, the dwarf's clothing shredded by contact with the sharp protrusions along the close surfaces.  The dwarf's body has been nicely mummified by the arid conditions, with the skin pulled tight and slightly wrinkled by the dehydration.  The dwarf's head peers upward, mouth agape, as if still hoping for rescue.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The way is flat and solid around the plateau's edge, and the edge itself provides a familiar landmark by which to navigate.  A scuffed surface runs off to the northeast at this point, though, winding between two parallel crevices deep into the plateau's interior.  No signs, messages or carvings indicate why the path exists and, judging from the lack of fearsome creatures encountered thus far, exploring it might not prove particularly dangerous.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The trail turns, following the plateau's curve.  A small mountain range, barely more than scrub hills, unfolds below the plateau to the south.  The wind continues to sing its melancholy song, rising and falling as it dips in and out of the crevices on its way across the Dead Plateau.  The cloudless night sky adds to the chill as the day's heat stored in the grey basalt escapes quickly into the cold night air.

The trail turns, following the plateau's curve.  A small mountain range, barely more than scrub hills, unfolds below the plateau to the south.  The wind continues to sing its melancholy song, rising and falling as it dips in and out of the crevices on its way across the Dead Plateau.  The sun, beaming down from the cloudless sky, brings no warmth, only an uncomfortable brightness as it reflects off the grey basalt surface.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The way continues along the edge of the plateau.  The trail is not marked, and, in fact, there is no trail at all.  The solid rock displays no footprints, and no one has taken the time to leave anything that indicates what direction one should go.  The Dead Plateau's interior is so uninviting, though, that at the moment the only real route follows the plateau's edge.  The wind continues unabated, bringing an equal discomfort from both its coldness and dryness.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: A narrow causeway of basalt rock leads between the edge of the plateau to the southwest and a wide, parallel crevice to the northeast.  The fierce wind, whirling and gusting, threatens to push you off the plateau's edge should your balance fail.  The fall would not be pleasant.  Several hundred feet straight down from the edge, piles of jagged rocks gleam dully in the moonlight, grinning rows of sharp stone teeth that eagerly await a plummeting body.

A narrow causeway of basalt rock leads between the edge of the plateau to the southwest and a wide, parallel crevice to the northeast.  The fierce wind, whirling and gusting, threatens to push you off the plateau's edge should your balance fail.  The fall would not be pleasant.  Several hundred feet straight down from the edge, piles of jagged rocks gleam brightly in the sunlight, grinning rows of sharp stone teeth that eagerly await a plummeting body.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The Dead Plateau's interior spreads out to the northeast as far as the eye can see.  A flat expanse of wind-scoured rock, the plateau would be easily traversable except for the myriad crevices and cracks that run helter-skelter throughout the interior.  Some are small and easily crossed, while others yawn widely with no discernible bottom.  Only the edge of the plateau appears relatively intact, and it is this edge that the trail follows.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: A chill, gusty wind sweeps out from the barren interior of the Dead Plateau and off the edge toward the low mountains to the west.  The wind's howling makes hearing difficult except in those short times when it mercifully abates.  The edge of the plateau looms perilously close, and to the north a deep crevice blocks passage.  A switchback drops down the cliff side, leading to an inviting copse of trees and a small creek, while the discernable trail follows the edge of the plateau to the southwest.

title: [Dead Plateau, Cliff Side]
description: Above, the trail reaches the cliff's summit, while below it continues downward in a switchback to the low mountain range.  The cliff sides are hard and unyielding, as if this tower of rock had been thrust upward from the earth by some gigantic hand.  Sweat from the journey's exertion evaporates quickly in the dry conditions, making the climb more bearable in that respect, but the arid conditions counter this benefit by producing parched throats and rapid dehydration.  Nothing stirs along the trail.

title: [Dead Plateau, Cliff Side]
description: Small, dislodged rocks careen quickly down the side of the cliff, giving indication of what might happen should a misstep occur.  The night sky is filled with radiant moons and glittering stars in all except a few spots far to the west.  A few hardy weeds have taken up residence in the soil of a nearby crevice, but no insects clamber over or around them, and the silence is only disturbed by your own movements.

A few fluffy clouds drift in the blue sky far to the west, but otherwise the day is clear and bright. title: [Dead Plateau, Cliff Side]
description: The lack of vegetation and the dust on the trail conspire to create a dry, thirsty journey.  A gentle, warm wind blows through the area, just enough to raise the small amount of dust and swirl it around and away.  A hundred yards or so from the cliff, a dark creature glides in lazy circles, perhaps searching for a meal in the hills below.  Every so often it banks closer, as if keeping a wary eye on your movements, then soars away again to resume its slow circling.

title: [Dead Plateau, Cliff Side]
description: The moon shines down brightly off this weathered basalt rock formation.  The face of the cliff rises a couple hundred feet, ascended by a well-defined switchback.  In the distance below, a small copse of trees nestles near a creek, the trees being the only large area of vegetation in sight.  The rest of the area is rolling scrub hills rising to a small mountain range.  It looks as if someone has scratched something in the cliff side here, but the words have long weathered into illegibility.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: A huge basalt plateau looms just to the east.  It is an edifice of sheer rock pushing hundreds of feet into the air.  The trail climbs the side of the tower, somehow finding a path until it reaches the top.  Although it looks like a tough climb, it is the only marked trail leading to the east.  The trail continues northwest, approaching a group of trees and then up into the barren hills.  The route into the hills looks a bit easier than the plateau route, but not much.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: Deep rivulets cut in the surface of this small plain indicate the beginnings of a watercourse, converging to the northwest.  Patches of hardy weeds and small scrub bushes dot the plain, taking in what moisture they can find and surviving valiantly against the drying wind.  The wind varies in intensity, maintaining a mild, comfortably warm breeze but occasionally speeding up until it is hurling abrasive sand at anything foolish enough to stand in the way.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: A fallen branch has blocked the stream, causing it to spread out and create a small slough.  Several types of insects forage in the murky waters, and bullfrogs croak from the nearby tall grasses.  The slough is still enough to breed annoying mosquitoes that buzz about looking for a good source of blood.  To the west the trail moves into a large copse of maple and elm trees, while to the southeast it spills out into a flat, treeless plain just before the basalt plateau.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: The stream is barely a trickle, a couple feet wide at best in places, narrowing to a few inches at others.  It is no more than a few inches deep on the average.  However, it is enough to keep the grove of trees and the interspersed wildflowers alive and vibrant.  Lush grasses grow near the stream's bank, and the water appears clear and drinkable.  The soft grass and fragrant wildflowers provide a peaceful place in which to take a snooze, if one is so inclined.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: The presence of the trees modifies the dryness as the trees release moisture into the air.  The maples and elms appear quite healthy and fully covered with leaves.  Their trunks tell a slightly different story, though.  Twisting and stunting indicate that these trees have had to weather very dry years when the waters of the creek have dissipated totally, but right now they enjoy full health and the surrounding area benefits from their vigor.

The presence of the trees modifies the dryness as the trees release moisture into the air.  The maples and elms appear quite healthy and fully covered with green leaves.  Their trunks tell a slightly different story, though.
