title: [Overland Trail]
description: Just to the east a copse of trees stands with the sounds of a stream trickling through it.  The grove is an inviting sight in comparison to the dry, dusty scrub area around.  To the northwest, the stream disappears down a deep ravine with sides that defy climbing.  If one is to travel in that direction, one will have to ascend into the hills to the southwest.  The breeze blows warmly through the area, picking up all the moisture it can find.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: Crystalline veins in the surrounding rock catch the moonlight and reflect it in varying shades of grey on the stone surfaces.  The quartz deposits appear to be streaked with impurities, rendering them useless for gem cutting.  A buzzard complains loudly, guarding its nest from the approach of strangers.  The protest is needless.  The nest is firmly established on the underside of a long rock outcropping, and it would take special climbing gear just to reach the agitated buzzard.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: The flat hilltop extends to the northwest.  Down the hillside, to the north and northeast, a small creek runs through an inviting stand of maple and elm trees.  Further east, a grey rock plateau rises straight up several hundred feet, its top appearing perfectly flat from this vantage point.  A short series of switchbacks steeply climbs the side of the plateau, and the plateau looks to be even more barren than the hills around you.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: The flat hilltop extends to the southeast.  Something slithers across the gravel behind a rock a few yards away, and the ever-present lizards coolly keep watch over your movements.  A group of white wildflowers have taken root in a depression on this windswept hilltop, and they display their flowers as signs of their defiance to the elements.  The moonlight glints brightly off the scoured rock surfaces.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: The hillside rises to a small summit to the southeast.  Lizards skitter about the area, stopping to survey the interlopers that have invaded their area before zooming under the nearest rock.  The moons shine down from a cloudless sky, and a warm, stiff breeze sweeps across the hillside, raising dust in small tornadoes as it goes.  It is pleasantly warm here, albeit a bit dry.  The lizards seem to like it, though.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: This rocky shelf is narrow, dusty and dry.  It does have one amenity, though.  To the northwest the broad panorama of the upper Locksmehr River valley spreads out along the horizon.  The Locksmehr River, a glistening ribbon of water, snakes down through the darker patches of the Khohallatain Forest.  Closer to you the forest reveals small glimpses of a creek cascading away to eventually join the larger river.

Closer to you the forest reveals small glimpses of a creek cascading away to eventually join the larger river.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: The canyon's slope is strewn with loose stones, making the climb extremely perilous.  Very little grows in this desolate area.  Only a few brown lichens cling to the underside of the rocks, perhaps nourished by dew in the few mornings when the air is slightly humid.  Above the canyon ends at a thin shelf, while below it spills out into a rather woeful-looking forest.  Neither direction looks particularly appealing, but either is preferable to this spot.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: A sheer rock wall and a nasty drop prevent any movement to the north or east.  Clambering up a canyon farther into the scrub hills appears to be the only way to find passage in that direction.  The trail meanders northwest into more of the same sparse deciduous forest.  The trees here live on the edge of existence, perhaps sending their roots deep enough to tap the water from the creek that can be heard down below the drop-off.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: The trail abruptly arrives at the edge of a V-shaped ridge several yards high.  The sparse forest crowds the edge, but even with the exposed roots of the trees there seems no good way to descend to the forest below.  The gurgling sound of a creek seems to come from off in the distance to the north, and the trees appear to thicken in that direction.  Scattered elms hold their ground up here against the encroaching scrub grasses.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: Hills rise to the south with only a few pockets of yellow grass indicating any life on them at all.  A ridge begins at this point and runs northward, separating the land into a lower forest on the west side and a higher forest on the east side.  Dust rises easily from the parched trail, and the hills certainly look like they could use a good rain.  Erosion appears to be more the work of a steady wind that blows across this area than the result of rainfall.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: Only the slightest bit of forest is present.  A few hardy elms cling to the dry soil, looking rather stunted, and grassy weeds cover much of the available ground.  A crumbly cliff approximately twelve feet high runs north and south.  Its face presents no solid handholds for climbing.  To the southeast the land rises steeply onto some barren scrub hills, while to the northeast the forest becomes thicker.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: A small cliff, perhaps produced by an earthquake long ago, stretches along to the east.  The trail moves alongside this obstacle as if searching for a way over it or around it.  The forest is sparse and open to the sky in many places, allowing the moons to shine brightly through.  Patches of dandelions cover the ground in many areas, their light grey flowers clustered closely to produce the appearance of grey throw rugs tossed randomly throughout the woods.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: A creek drops over a short cliff side here, creating a small waterfall and pool before continuing on to the northwest.  Water striders rush across the pool pursued by tadpoles, and a few mosquitoes quietly flit around the area, apparently not concerned about your presence at all.  The cliff is high enough and crumbly enough that it blocks progress along the creek to the east.  The trail strikes out into the forest to the southeast and follows the creek to the northwest.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: Reeds and succulent water plants crowd the banks of the creek to drink in the flowing waters.  They combine with the encroaching trees to make progress more difficult.  The ground feels solid enough, if only one could see it through all the vegetation.  The reeds bend, snap and crush underfoot, and movement becomes slowed. The trail seems to be completely lost in the undergrowth, but the direction of the creek is an indication as to which way to proceed.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: A creek barely ten feet wide cascades down from the east and rushes off to the west, gurgling happily.  Sunlight filters through the trees on either side to sparkle off the flowing waters.  The creek is not more than a few inches deep and would be easy to ford if the trail decided to go that way.  Instead, the trail parallels the creek to the east and moves off into the forest to the southwest.  A slightly greenish tinge to the water suggests that it might not be potable.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: A brisk wind stirs the leaves in the treetops, but at ground level it is filtered into a pleasant warm breeze.  Night birds call to each other from the surrounding trees while small mammals dart through the thick leaf cover in search of food.  The trail is dry and level, providing good footing.  The occasional mosquito might cause an annoyance, but for the most part the forest is a tranquil, pleasant place to be this night.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: A massive maple tree stands just off the trail to one side.  Its trunk must be eight feet wide, and it clearly towers over all the nearby trees.  The position of stature has cost it severely, though, and it looks to be dying.  A long, jagged black mark begins at the top of the tree and rushes down the side all the way to the ground, and the branches near it are blackened stumps.  The other sides still have a complete set of branches, but only a few leaves cling to the far ends.

title: [Overland Trail]
description: The trees are well spaced and travel through the forest is relatively easy.  Small ferns and ivy occupy the areas beneath the trees that receive little light, while smaller versions of the maples, elms, birches and other deciduous trees compete for dominance in the better lit spots.  A thick carpet of dried leaves crunches underfoot, but the trail is well marked, the leaves flattened down by the passage of other travelers.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: To the northwest the Locksmehr River splits as it rushes around a large island, most of the water diverting into the western channel with the remainder slowly making its way past you down the eastern channel.  Someone has cleared a trail to the northeast, moving away from the river and into the surrounding deciduous forest.  To the south the trail follows the bank of the eastern channel of the river.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The trail attempts to follow the river as best it can, winding among the trees that grow close to the shore and avoiding the protruding boulders.  The ground squishes heavily underfoot in many areas where the trail comes very near to the river's slow-moving waters.  The temperate air causes a bit of humidity to rise from the moist soil, but a breeze that follows the river channel helps to keep it from becoming an oppressive wet heat.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The river passes by sluggishly, meandering shallowly among the boulders, logs and other debris strewn across the riverbed.  The main volume of water seems to be somewhere else.  If not for the difficulty of clambering over the blockages, and the possibility that a deep, treacherous section hides among the rubble, one could consider walking across the river at this point.  Easier, though, would be to use the sturdy bridge that spans the river just to the south.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: A plank bridge crosses the river.  The bridge appears weathered but extremely sturdy.  Whoever built it sunk the pilings deep into the river, then heaped up boulders against them to prevent the river from carrying the bridge downstream even in the highest water conditions.  The bridge sports steps on either end and a handrail on both the upstream and downstream sides.  Much farther to the south the river appears to join a second river.

title: [Locksmehr River, Plank Bridge]
description: The bridge spans the shallow river, its planks well above the level of the water.  The bridge is built from weather-resistant cedar, and it even looks as if someone has taken the time to apply a coat of varnish to the handrail.  Someone made this bridge to last.  Below, the river snakes through boulders, rocks and logs as it slowly flows southward.  Fish dart from shady area to shady area as they search for food but fear the light.

title: [Locksmehr River, Wiley Island]
description: A sturdy bridge rises above the river to the east.  Thick pilings extend up from the river's bottom to support a wide floor of heavy planks and a well-constructed handrail.  The bridge does not appear to be built from any local wood, as there are no stumps visible on either bank.  The maples, elms, walnuts and other deciduous woods do not seem to match the grain or texture of the bridge's lumber.

title: [Locksmehr River, Wiley Island]
description: The river has cut its way through the forest as its waters rush down from the northern mountains towards Wehnimer's Landing.  Smooth boulders sticking out of the water and rough rapids deter any thoughts of trying to swim across the swiftly moving waters.  A wide rope bridge stretches west, over the river, and is secured around massive trees on both sides.

The river has cut its way through the forest as its waters rush down from the northern mountains towards Wehnimer's Landing.  Smooth boulders sticking out of the water and rough rapids deter any thoughts of trying to swim across the swiftly moving waters.  An old wooden foundation of a bridge sits on the bank.  A tight rope stretches over the river, tied around trees on each side of the river.

title: [Locksmehr River, Rope Bridge]
description: The long, narrow island to the east is lush with small bushes and grasses, and a few fallen trees point down river.  A gentle breeze is created by the whitewater as it speeds downstream.  The rushing waters below look like they could sweep away even the strongest of swimmers.

title: [Locksmehr River, Rope Bridge]
description: The water below is moving swiftly along the current of the Locksmehr River.  The deep roar of the rapids echoes off of the smooth rocks poking out of the river and bluffs on the surrounding banks.  A twisted pile of wood and wire lies trapped between a couple of rocks on the bank downstream.

title: [Locksmehr River, Rope Bridge]
description: Water sprays up into the air in all directions as it pounds the large boulders of the river below the bridge.  To the north, the river bends slightly as it comes down out of the mountains.  To the south it flows quickly around to the west towards Wehnimer's Landing.  The river has cut a wide swath through the lush forest, creating bluffs above the banks on either side of the rough rapids.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The trail opens into a small clearing, where several old, rotting logs line the muddy banks of the Locksmehr River.  A wide rope bridge stretches east, across the river, toward a narrow island in the center of the swiftly moving current.  Resting off to one side of the trail is a neat stack of wood.

A small clearing opens up at the bank of the river.  Several old, rotting logs line the muddy banks of the Locksmehr River.  A long, narrow island sits in the center of the water, sheltered from the swift movement of the current.  A hefty amount of cracked and faded wood is stacked neatly off to the side of the trail.  A tight rope has been strung above the river to serve as a way to cross the raging current to the small island.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The top of the ridge provides a decent view of the Khohallatain Forest to the south.  The woods are a mass of dark grey growth, and the varied heights of the trees create a rippling effect.  The Locksmehr River winds southward until it disappears from sight, blocked by rows of trees that stand taller than your present position.  The trail delves into the forest to the east, becoming quickly obscured among the tightly clustered trees.  In the other direction it winds down the ridge to the southeast.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The trail follows the river to the southeast, bending with the water's flow as it moves downstream.  Northward, a rocky ridge twenty feet high or so blocks progress.  The river appears to have carved its own passage through the rock, rushing and splashing rapidly as the raised land stands sentinel on both sides of the flow.  The trail moves inland to the northwest where it finds a way to ascend the ridge.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: A tight curve of the river at this point has created a wide sandy spit.  Pieces of driftwood, a few large logs, and other forest debris are scattered across the edge of the area as the river regurgitates its contents onto the sand.  Nothing of any value seems to be present among the collection of wood, though.  No trees have been able to take root, and the moons shine down brightly on the sand, illuminating the spit and making it easy to see.

No trees have been able to take root, and the sun beats down brightly on the sand, causing it to be much warmer than the nearby forest floor.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: A second, somewhat smaller river surges from the northeast into the Locksmehr River.  The second river doesn't have nearly the volume of the Locksmehr, but the convergence produces a series of small rapids as the two flows collide.  The two rivers have created a large, long sandbar between them, and quite a bit of debris gathers there.  Several ravens pick through the debris, perhaps hoping to find something to eat or something shiny to collect.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The trail becomes a bit softer, and the footing is unsure.  The ground isn't any wetter, but small, raised cracks in a serpentine fashion crisscross the trail, signs of mole or gopher activity.  Fox paw prints are evident in the dirt, and perhaps the foxes come to feed upon the burrowers when they emerge.  The forest is still, with only a small background humming caused by flies and other winged insects flitting about in search of sustenance.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: A number of stumps, their tops hewn off, gather around the edges of this clearing.  Some of the surrounding trees also bear the mark of the axe, and several have been felled but not trimmed or dragged away.  A pile of boards sits off to the side with moss covering the tops of most of the boards.  None of them look in good enough shape to make anything useful out of them.  A small side trail goes only a few yards into the forest to the west before petering out entirely.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: A small tributary stream meanders slowly across the forest floor on its way eastward into the Locksmehr River.  The water is a dark color and exudes a metallic odor.  Small insects skitter across the surface of the stream, avoiding the large maple leaves that attempt to completely cover the trickling waters.  Although the ground is mushy at this point, someone has strategically placed stones to create a dry crossing.

Small insects skitter across the surface of the stream, avoiding the large maple leaves that attempt to completely cover the trickling waters.  Although the ground is mushy at this point, someone has strategically placed stones to create a dry crossing.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The river adjacent to the trail on the eastern side rages angrily as it winds through the woods and out of the mountain ranges to the north.  The river has carved its way through the soil, leaving large rocks stranded in the water and bluffs on either side of the gully.  The trail hugs the river to the northeast and shifts inland around a large, dense copse of trees to the south.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: Thick brambles and bushes have begun to intrude on the trail from both sides.  The leafy plants begin on the forest floor and soak up every ounce of light to the tops of the tallest trees.  The foliage is so dense that only a small area of the surrounding forest is visible.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail, Swamp]
description: A small, swampy clearing is surrounded by the dense forest on the northern and western sides.  The large branches of the trees along the perimeter create a canopy of leaves above with just patches of moonlight penetrating the foliage.  Hollow logs lie half covered by water and mud, moss and fungi growing from the decay.  Quiet bubbling sounds emanate from the water as frogs and other critters surface out of and dive into the swamp.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail, Swamp]
description: A reptilian creature resting on a small dry area hops quickly into the water, startled by the movement.  Salamanders and lizards dart around the edges of the swamp looking for an easy insect meal.  The pervasive smell of decay rises up from the mushy ground and hangs heavily in the stagnant air.  An occasional frog breaks the quiet background noise with a loud croak.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail, Swamp]
description: An ankle-deep swamp covers this low spot of the forest; the murky water ripples concentric circles away from every footstep.  Small gnats swarm through the heavy air, darting at anything that moves.  The soft buzzing of the bugs blends in with the constant singing of tree frogs in nature's ambient harmony.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail, Swamp]
description: A slight, widespread depression in the forest floor has gathered waters from previous floods.  The ridge along the riverbank blocks the drainage of water back into the river.  Clumps of long-bladed grass have popped up randomly in dry areas of the swamp.  Once mighty trees now lie rotten and moss-covered, victims of the soft ground's weakened support.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The muffled roar of the Locksmehr River drifts in from the east, blending with the chirping of birds and chitters of squirrels.  The ground slopes gently away from the riverbank towards a low spot in the forest to the northwest.  The thick forest hinders any breeze's attempts to stir the temperate yet humid air.  The path to the southeast continues towards the river.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The dusty trail along the bank of the river is trampled considerably, the constant footsteps stifling any grass or brush attempting to grow.  To the west, the impenetrable forest blocks any travel away from the river.  To the north, a thick copse of trees and underbrush clings to the bank of the river.  The only directions of travel are southward along the riverbank or northwestward into a mushy swamp.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: Bullfrogs croak deeply, unable or unwilling to keep a harmony in the reeds that line the bank of the slow-moving river.  Moonlight filtering through the trees dapples the ground along the path, illuminating the matted leaves and barren spots.  The trees are clustered together, and in many places the moonlight is almost totally blocked.  At these spots toadstools grow abundantly around the bases of the trees, and the rocks are covered with heavy moss.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The path rises to the southwest, climbing atop a bluff as the river is forced into a narrower channel.  Here, upstream from the funnel, the river placidly spreads out, small eddies and whirlpools playing at the edges of the water.  The sun sparkles off the river's pristine surface, reflecting warmly on the trees and bushes gathered at the shore.  To the north the trail winds in and out of the maples and elms.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The ground slopes downward toward the northeast as the trail descends to river level.  To the southwest the trail winds through the Khohallatain Forest, hugging the bluff edge.  The river is forced into narrower confines as it flows downstream from this point.  It rushes past swiftly, boiling with rapids and whitecaps, carrying debris into troughs and then flinging it high into the air as the water roils and churns over boulders and rocks.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: Directly across the river very few trees stand among the rolling maze of holly, raspberry, thistle and other assorted bushes and vines.  Those trees that do stand are blackened, although a few of them still have slight growths to indicate that they have weathered the passing conflagration.  Further in the distance the Khohallatain Forest rears up in a line, and perhaps the fire was stopped by the river or by a timely thunderstorm.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: On this side of the river the trees are healthy and vibrant.  On the other side of the river the scene is quite different.  Only a few tree trunks stand, and those are charred and stripped of branches as a result of a passing fire.  Shrubs and berry bushes dominate the area, and in places fast growing cottonwoods thrust up ten feet or so, indicating that the fire probably did not happen in the recent past.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: A large patch of wild raspberries stands just off the west side of the trail.  The plants cascade all over, and a wealth of berries are clustered on the extensive bushes.  Two things keep travelers from enjoying the succulent fruit.  First, the plants also sport sharp thorns that happily puncture and tear any flesh that tries to slide past them.  Second, all the berries don't seem to be quite ripe enough, and where ripe ones might have been there are none.  There are bear tracks here.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: An owl follows you for a while, hooting loudly as it flies from branch to branch, well out of reach.  Perhaps it is hoping you will scare up a rodent for it to devour.  For no apparent reason it turns and disappears back the way it came.  Other night birds call from far back among the trees. Their songs differ in volume, tone and pitch, with some being melodious warblings and others being grating caws.  Every so often one flies across the path or darts out from a bush upon your approach.

A blue jay follows you for a while, raucously shrieking at you as it flies from branch to branch, well out of reach.  Then it quietly turns and disappears back the way it came.  Other birds call from far back among the trees. Their songs differ in volume, tone and pitch, with some being melodious warblings and others being grating caws.  Every so often one flies across the path or darts out from a bush upon your approach.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The wind rustles through the trees to provide a soft, whispering sound.  Maples, walnuts, cottonwoods, birches and several other species of tree reach toward the sky.  Their different shapes and colorations contrast pleasantly, relieving the monotony that might occur should they all be of the same configuration.  The elms in the area look to be a bit blighted, though.  Several of them are yellowed and losing their leaves.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The thick stands of elm in this area look devastated.  Many of them have fallen over or split in two, their leaves gone, their branches withered and blackened.  The trunks display scores of holes as if many small things had bored into the trunks, or something had smashed holes in the trunks in search of something else.  Others are barely alive with only a few leaves still attached to the ends of branches.  Here and there healthy specimens still stand, but they are very few and far between.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: Whoo, whoo whoo, whooo, wooo-whooo!  The booming, and unmistably loud voice of an owl fills the night.  In the distance a reply can be heard, carried on the air.  The elms in this area provide a perch from which the owls can survey what appears to be a prime feeding ground.  A rustling near some low brush is followed by the heavy flapping of wings.  The screech of a small animal is cut short and silence fills the night air.

Ratta-tatta-tatta-tat!  A woodpecker's drilling echoes through the forest.  Several other woodpeckers pick up the sound, and soon the woods are filled with the staccato hammerings of woodpeckers looking for a meal.  The elms in this area appear to be prime feeding grounds.  Many have leaves that are mostly yellow or missing entirely, and their branches droop as if something, perhaps a borer or other insect, is attacking them.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: A large, flat rock sticks out at an angle in the middle of the river, diverting the waters around it.  A large weeping willow has grown out of a crevice in the rock, forcing its roots down through the stone and somehow finding enough nourishment to keep itself alive even with all the water around it.  The tree leans toward the south, bowing to the buffeting of the winds, and the tips of its long, leaf-covered branches trail in the river's water.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: Beavers have constructed a dam in a shallow spur of the river below.  The dam, in turn, has created a large pool behind it to facilitate the growth of pond weeds, a favorite beaver food.  A pair of beavers move about in the pool and on the shore, carrying sticks in their mouths to add to the dam, diving into the pool to feed, or dipping down to perhaps inspect the sturdiness of their efforts or enter their lair for a rest.  A box turtle sleeps on a nearby rock, oblivious to the splashing beavers.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The river makes a sharp turn, curving around to smash into the bluff just to the southwest.  The constant pounding has caused the bluff to plummet into the churning waters, creating a large strip of exposed rocks and boulders.  Above, where the trail should be, large trees cling to the edge of the bluff's side, and the undergrowth prevents passage through that area.  With no other place to go, the trail descends the face of the bluff.  To the northeast the trail resumes its movement along the bluff.

title: [Rock to Rock]
description: Slick rocks constantly moistened by the splashing river provide the only means of travel to the west.  Above, the bluff trail is impassable, the river's assault having torn it down into the rushing waters.  Below, the river is littered with stones and tree trunks of varying sizes.  The only things keeping the river from claiming more of the land are the thick forest roots and the sheer volume of rocky material.  It is likely that these will also eventually succumb to the river's territorial demands.

title: [Rock to Rock]
description: Rocks large enough for several people to stand on mix with smaller rocks, many of which are submerged below the cold, clear waters of the Locksmehr River.  Shadowy shapes dart underneath the water's surface, mostly in directions away from the sound of footsteps.  The cliff looms close by, and dirt, pebbles and even large rocks occasionally break loose to splash into the water.  As evidenced by the area heavily gouged out at the base, the cliff is losing the battle to the tenacious river.

title: [Rock to Rock]
description: The bluff trail above has tumbled down into the river and been washed away, leaving large rocks protruding up through the rushing waters near to the sheer dropoff.  Atop the bluff trees crowd the edge, denying passage, their roots extending out in a futile attempt to grasp the soil that is no longer there.  With great care it might be possible to move along the cliff from rock to rock, but a misstep could prove cold and wet if not outright fatal.  The river does not look to be in a forgiving mood.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The bluff to the east has dropped off into the river, and the thick forest is so close to the edge as to prevent movement along the bluff in that direction.  The trail winds down the side of the bluff in a narrow and treacherous manner until it reaches a large section of rubble strewn below.  Negligence could send one plummeting either into the rushing river or onto the sharp rocks.  Neither one would be pleasant.  To the northwest the trail easily follows the edge of the bluff.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: Several tall maples have tumbled down into the river, perhaps victims of a combination of the river's erosion and high winds.  The trunks are strewn helter-skelter down the bluff's side with some of them coming to rest in the river below.  From all appearances they have been down quite awhile, for most of the branches are shorn off leaving jagged protrusions from the trunks.  The exposed roots on the higher ones block the trail a bit, but not enough to cause a bothersome detour.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The bluff protrudes out from the forest causing the river to bend sharply around the outcropping.  From this vantage point the river stretches out for several miles each direction, winding between the forest sections.  In some places it churns and whirls, adding whitecaps to its surface only to calm down and become more peaceable in other sections.  Boulders dot the water in many areas, and often piles of rubble lie strewn in the water below the bluff's face.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The trail moves through a long section of wildflowers that have taken root between the edge of the bluff and the forest.  Fireflies flit about gaily among the flowers, their colorful lights winking on and off.  Owls add to the music of nature with their calls from nearby trees, and the river below ripples as a steady undercurrent in the harmony.  The wind completes the composition by intermittently rustling the higher leaves on the trees.

The trail moves through a long section of wildflowers that have taken root between the edge of the bluff and the forest.  Bees flit busily from flower to flower, collecting the important materials for their hives.  Birds add to the music of nature with their calls from nearby trees, and the river below ripples as a steady undercurrent in the harmony.  The wind completes the composition by intermittently rustling the higher leaves on the trees.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The moons shine down brightly, illuminating the trail and sparkling off the surface of the river below.  The river makes slow progress to the west, its surface smooth and unbroken by protruding rocks.  An occasional fish breaks the surface in pursuit of a winged insect only to fall back with a splash, watery ripples radiating out from the point where it landed.  The trail proceeds steadily in an east/west direction.

The sun shines down brightly, illuminating the trail and sparkling off the surface of the river below. The trail proceeds steadily in an east/west direction.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: A few sugar maples seem to be an abnormal shade of grey, perhaps stressed by lack of good soil or competition for nutrients from other nearby trees.  The normally dark leaves have slipped into various shades of light grey, making the trees appear as billowing ghostly cones against the dark backdrop of the rest of the forest.  A few scattered leaves lie under the trees, their appearance once again taking on a much darker color.

A few sugar maples have changed color, perhaps stressed by lack of good soil or competition for nutrients from other nearby trees.  The green leaves have slipped into shades of flaming red, deep orange and bright yellow, making the trees appear as billowing cones of flame against the deep green backdrop of the rest of the forest.  A few scattered leaves lie under the trees, their colors fading to a murky brown.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The river is funneled through a narrow chasm.  The blockage forces the waters to spread out behind the gorge's mouth, flooding the opposite bank.  Several large, healthy oaks protrude up through the water at the edge of the lake, indicating that the volume of water may be only temporary or seasonal.  An eagle rests in the upper branches of one of the oaks, apparently sleeping and blissfully ignorant of your progress along the trail.

Several large, healthy oaks protrude up through the water at the edge of the lake, indicating that the volume of water may be only temporary or seasonal.  An eagle rests in the upper branches of one of the oaks, surveying the river below it for signs of an easy fish meal and warily watching your progress along the trail.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The opposite bank rises to form a narrow channel between it and the bluff.  The river pours swiftly through the channel as a deep black ribbon.  Just below, the river must be eating away at the bluff, for it is not possible to see the point where the river meets the bluff no matter how far one tries to stretch out over the edge.  It is an ominous indication that the edge might not be as sturdy as one would like to believe.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The roar of the river grows louder, and the current makes a small bend here.  Its course changes from northwest to due west, and the waters spill out of a narrow gorge, pouring forth to create a series of swift rapids that whirl and foam around the riverbed's large boulders.  Small pieces of wood carried out of the gorge by the waters smash to splinters against the boulders, displaying the river's destructive force for all to see.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The wind ripples through the trees to create a wistful sighing sound.  The air is warm and dry, and the sky is full of stars and devoid of clouds.  No rain threatens this peaceful scene.  The river rushes by below, its roar muted by the face of the bluff.  Near the edge of the bluff, fragrant alyssum plants fill the air with a slightly sweet aroma.  The trail ahead is level and dry.  It is a perfect night for a journey to far off places.

The river rushes by below, its roar muted by the face of the bluff.  Near the edge of the bluff, fragrant alyssum plants fill the air with a slightly sweet aroma.  The trail ahead is level and dry.  It is a perfect day for a journey to far off places.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: Down on the river, a mother bear and her two cubs move through the small pools present at the edge of the river's flow.  The cubs frolic in the cool water, batting at each other and splashing about.  A bit further upstream, the mother hunts in the bright moonlight, reaching down into a pool to slap at a fish.  Occasionally her attempts are successful, and a fish flies up onto the shore where it lays wiggling and struggling until the cubs, called by their mother, pounce on it and devour it with relish.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: Tall birches and poplars compete with spreading maples, walnuts and elms for sunlight, water and nourishment.  In some places the birches and poplars seem to be winning, their long trunks extending narrowly up and their leaves clustered at the top to drink in the sunlight during the day.  In other places, though, it is apparent that the slower growing walnuts and elms eventually win out, as witnessed by the large number of rotting birch trunks beneath the wider trees' stately crowns.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: To the west the trail begins a downward slope, and to the east it follows a long bluff overlooking the river.  The bluff has fallen away in a few places, adding rubble to the larger rocks already present in the river's course.  The trail winds around these fallen places, squeezing narrowly between the forest and the crumbly edge of the bluff, only to widen out again with the expansion of the bluff's surface.

title: [Locksmehr River Trail]
description: The trail rises steeply to a bluff overlooking the river to the east and descends to a small ferry landing visible to the west.  The scent of burning wood mixed with the mouthwatering odor of stew reaches your nostrils, its source most likely the smoke issuing from the chimney below.  The forest presses close, keeping the trail near the river.  The trail is clearly delineated, a long line of ground worn bare by the passing of many feet.

title: [Khohallatain Forest's Edge]
description: The Locksmehr River runs wider, deeper and slower here, allowing a ferry service to take passengers across to the opposite shore.  A weathered wooden dock, firmly lashed to several large pilings, juts out into the river.  To the west and north a deciduous forest basks in the moonlight, and no trails appear through the undergrowth.  Eastward the forest recedes somewhat from the rushing river, allowing passage along the bank.  Smoke curls lazily from the chimney of a nearby rustic cabin.

title: [Locksmehr River, North Dock]
description: The wooden dock is heavily weathered but sturdy.  Several thick pilings descend into the river bottom, and the dock's planks are securely nailed to heavy wooden crossbeams secured to the pilings.  On the upstream side near the shore, two of the pilings jut higher into the air, providing posts to which the ferry guide rope attaches.  The dock stands considerably higher than the level of the river, although watermarks on the pilings show that the river is fickle in its choice of depth.

title: [Locksmehr River Ferry]
description: The ferryboat is a shallow draft boat with squared sides.  On the upstream side, two iron rings encircle the thick guide rope that keeps the ferry on its course from dock to dock.  A flat, narrow walkway is built into the downstream side.  The ferryman negotiates this narrow path, planting his pole into the river's bottom, walking backward to propel the ferry forward, then lifting the pole and moving back to the prow to repeat the action.

title: [Locksmehr River, South Dock]
description: The wooden dock is heavily weathered but sturdy.  Several thick pilings descend into the river bottom, and the dock's planks are securely nailed to heavy wooden crossbeams secured to the pilings.  On the upstream side near the shore, two of the pilings jut higher into the air, providing posts to which the ferry guide rope attaches.  The dock stands considerably higher than the level of the river, although watermarks on the pilings show that the river is fickle in its choice of depth.

title: [Vipershroud, Ferry Landing]
description: The Locksmehr River runs wider, deeper and slower here, allowing a ferry service to take passengers across to the opposite shore.  A weathered wooden dock, firmly lashed to several large pilings, juts out into the river.  To the south and east, the Vipershroud grows down to the water's edge, making travel in those directions impossible.

title: [Raging Thrak Inn, Dining Room]
description: Loud and abusive noises emanate from behind the swinging kitchen doors, much to the laughing delight of some of the customers, and to the chagrin of others.  Tapestries hanging from the walls depict soothing idyllic wildlife scenes.  Hard wooden tables and chairs are placed evenly, allowing enough space for the cook and wait servants to pass.

title: [Raging Thrak Inn, Barroom]
description: A long and polished wooden bar occupies the whole north wall of the tavern here in The Raging Thrak, which is named for the fiery proprietor.  Hard wooden chairs, tables and benches are spaced liberally throughout the room.  The tavern does good business, and seems to be at least half full, no matter what time of day.
paths: Obvious exits: north, south, west, out

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The trail grows even more rutted, if that's possible, as it curves from west to north.  Scrubby bushes press in close on both sides.  Dusty looking trees loom over the bushes, and the whole place looks like it could use a good rain.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The trail climbs higher as it turns northeast, approaching a range of rough hills covered with grey rocks and brown grass.  Thistles poke up out of the grass in places, their puffy purple flowers surrounded by wicked spines.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: A dead tree stands off to one side of the trail, its branches reaching up to the sky like the blackened fingers of a skeleton hand.  No trees or bushes grow near it, as though the other plants shun whatever killed it.  The soil around its roots is bare and dusty.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: Modwir pines rustle in the wind, and bluejays swoop back and forth among them, belittling you and each other in rough, raucous voices.  The main trail curves to the west and southeast, while a rougher trail heads up the side of the hill to the north.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The trail curves, following the contour of the large hill to the north.  Part of the hill has slumped onto the trail, forcing you to detour around a jumble of grey boulders and dirt.  You eye the top of the slope fearfully, and quicken your pace to pass swiftly by.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The trail widens, running along the top of a sheer, rocky cliff.  A few scraggly bushes cling to the side of the hill above the trail, a lone modwir towering over them like a shepherd tending his flock.  A small brown chipwit flutters back and forth between the modwir and the ground, carrying grasses and fallen needles to line its nest.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: A few scruffy bushes cling to the hillside here upslope of the trail.  Downslope, to the southeast, you see only a few clumps of tough, brown grass clinging wherever a pocket of soil has collected on the rocky slope.  Dirty white lichen grows in lacy patterns across the surface of the rocks, its delicacy contrasting with the dull, blunt stone.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: A bush alongside the trail crackles softly in the breeze, and suddenly spits forth a small, sleek grass-colored bird that hoots in fright.  Dry grasses rustle as a small predator slinks off, chittering angrily, doubtless complaining of his hunger.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The hillside is steep here, not quite vertical but close.  Dry, brownish grass covers the hillside both above and below the trail.  The trail is only a few inches wide here, but with care you manage to keep from falling over the side.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The trail curls around a steep, treeless hillside.  Tough brown grasses, pierced by an occasional thistle, cover the ground.  The trail to the south is only a few inches wide -- rain, wind and use have eroded it down to near non-existence.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The trail narrows here and the branches of the trees meet over your head, casting deep shadows all around.  You brush against a pine tree and pick up a smear of gluey black sap down your arm.  The sharp scent of the resin bites your nose and throat, and your attempts to clean the goop off only spreads it around.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The trail winds through the trees, lights and shadows dancing between the branches.  To the north, your path is blocked by the trunk of a huge fallen modwir.  Wicked looking black brambles climb over the trunk and wind through the branches, except for a patch right above the trail.  The exposed surface of the bark has been worn smooth.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: An ancient modwir pine came crashing down across the trail here long ago, at least a century past if the size of the trees grown up around it are any indication.  A clump of wicked looking black brambles has grown up across the fallen trunk, covering it completely except for a narrow patch directly above the trail.  The rough bark of the tree has been worn smooth where it's not covered with thorns.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: Gaps in the trees allow the prevailing winds to blow briskly through this area, carrying with them a sound that can best be described as a frenzied drumbeat.  If it is indeed the sound of a drum, the player is obviously agitated.

title: [Upper Trollfang, Winding Trees]
description: Tall modwirs dominate the area, pulling closer together along the path as it lazily winds its way eastward.  Looking up, the tops of the trees wind along with the path making it appear as a path carved in the sky.

title: [Upper Trollfang, Winding Trees]
description: The icy peak of Glatoph looms in the skyline to the north bringing to mind visions of frozen peril.  Fortunately, the path skirts its way around the base of the mountain, keeping a clear and relatively safe distance from more dangerous terrain.  You notice a patch of some unidentifiable grey moss growing along the northern base of trees.

title: [Upper Trollfang, Winding Trees]
description: Harsh gusts of wind cut through the trees causing you to shiver not only from the cold but from the shrill eerie music in the air.  Several stalwart modwirs seem to be the source of the songs for they stand against the fast moving air, vibrating in defiance.  Somewhere in the distance, you hear a bell clanking along with the singing trees.

title: [Upper Trollfang, Winding Trees]
description: The path curves sharply as it snakes through the trees.  Some of the area's firs sport needles with black tips, providing a stark contrast to the usual greenery.  Resting between two of the trees you see a large boulder covered with mud as if it had been recently moved.  A particularly low copse of trees juts out across the path at your ankles.

The path curves sharply as it snakes through the trees.  Some of the area's firs sport deep green needles with black and silver tips, providing a stark contrast to the usual greenery.  Resting between two of the trees you see a large boulder covered with mud as if it had been recently moved.  A particularly low copse of trees juts out across the path at your ankles.

title: [Upper Trollfang, Winding Trees]
description: Trees upon trees crisscross in front of your eyes making you feel a bit dizzy.  There is a faint scent of cothinar in the air but you cannot find any sign of the flower nearby.

title: [Upper Trollfang, Winding Trees]
description: You feel like ducking low as a branch from a nearby tree swings down into the path almost touching your head.  The wind is definitely stronger here and you can't help but listen to its eerie song as it plays along the leaves and branches of the forest.

title: [Upper Trollfang, Winding Trees]
description: Winding again to the east, the path takes you back and forth through the trees making you wonder if there might be a better path hidden deeper within the foliage.  Somewhere far from the path, you can hear something moving quickly through the forest.

title: [A Dark Forest Path]
description: Dense foliage moves into the small path as it disappears into the trees to the south.  With little light and plenty of places to hide, you suspect this could be an excellent spot for an ambush.

title: [Hidden Settlement]
description: The path suddenly opens up to reveal a small settlement set in the middle of a forest clearing.  You see an occasional elf dart in and out of the tents.  A strange quiet surrounds the area and you wonder why the elves would choose to hide this deep into the forest.

title: [Vipershroud, Edge of Settlement]
description: Cicadas and crickets fill the night air with insectile song.  Moonlight illuminates a small path meandering southwest through the blackberry bushes toward the Elven Settlement, civilization and safety.  To the northwest, the living wall of the Vipershroud forest presents an impenetrable blackness.

Sunlight pours into this clearing, nourishing the multicolored wildflowers intermixed with the thorny blackberry bushes.  An overgrown path meanders southwest toward the Elven Settlement, civilization and safety.  To the northwest, the living wall of the Vipershroud forest, heavily overgrown and choked with brambles, encroaches upon the bright meadow.

title: [Vipershroud, Mossy Trail]
description: Huge conifers mixed with spreading deciduous trees block out most of the moonlight.  Moss grows thickly on the tree trunks and carpets the barely discernible trail that pushes through the thorny undergrowth.  To the southeast, the Vipershroud appears to thin, revealing patches of starry sky.

title: [Vipershroud, Mossy Trail]
description: An unusual silence pervades the shadowy forest, and the trees press in tightly on either side. title: [Vipershroud, Mossy Trail]
description: The trees press in even tighter, their canopies intertwining to produce a darkening tunnel effect, with little moonlight appearing through the vegetation overhead. title: [Vipershroud, Precipice]
description: The trail, coming from the southwest, suddenly ends at a sheer dropoff, perhaps caused decades before by raging floodwaters or a sudden settling of the land.  Massive tree roots extend out from the cliff face, then curl back to reenter the soil, keeping the entire face from tumbling down into the murky darkness below.  A huge boulder shores up part of the cliff, and the choking growth prevents movement along the edge for more than a few yards in either direction.

description: Tendrils of steam rise slowly from the valley floor, more felt than seen in the darkness, to cling damply to everything. title: [Vipershroud, Murky Valley]
description: The moss hangs from the trees in long, blackish icicles, in some places dragging on the forest floor to mingle with the grayer moss there. title: [Vipershroud, Murky Valley]
description: Gnarled, twisted trees loom menacingly, their bark a sickly grayish brown. title: [Vipershroud, Bubbling Spring]
description: A small clearing appears here, giving a brief respite from the claustrophobic trail and allowing a dim bit of sunlight to penetrate to the ground. The sulfurous water bubbles up, only to flow a few yards and disappear noisily down a muddy, sucking hole.

title: [Vipershroud, Murky Valley]
description: Twigs snap, leaves rustle, and it becomes apparent that something is paralleling your course from deep in the underbrush.  The heavy tree branches above cut off the moonlight, making it impossible to see more than a few feet in any direction, while the rampant humidity and lack of wind lend a tense stillness to the misty air. title: [Vipershroud, Fallen Tree]
description: A huge tree, perhaps twenty-five feet in diameter, has fallen onto the path, blocking further progress.  The tree trunk is heavily covered with dark green moss and brownish yellow fungus, and the overhead canopy shows no sign of a break in the tightly woven umbrella, indicating the fallen tree has lain here for some time.  Brackish water pools underneath the trunk, adding to the steamy mist.  The narrow path continues off to the southwest.

title: [Vipershroud, Inside the Tree]
description: Pitch blackness eliminates vision, and progress must be made through the sense of touch.  The sound of small scurryings and scrapings echoes faintly in the tight confines of the log, and soft, wriggly bodies squish easily under hand and foot.  The odor of decay, rising from the damp, pressing walls adds to the discomfort from the steamy humidity.  No way forward is apparent in the darkness, although the way back out is readily remembered.

title: [Vipershroud, Murky Valley]
description: The scent of rotting vegetation and decaying animal life gives the mists a peculiar odor.  On one side of the trail, almost hidden by the brambles and the shadowy darkness, a stump has broken open revealing a large termite nest.  Transparent white, bulbous termites, standing out brightly against the blackness of the decomposed wood, scurry about, attempting to repair the damage.

title: [Vipershroud, Murky Valley]

To the northeast the trail slopes up, out of the valley, while to the southwest it plunges deeper into the damp mist.

title: [Vipershroud, Mossy Trail]
description: The area explodes in a frenzy of activity as numerous small slithering animals are disturbed by the arrival of footsteps.  The moss undulates outward, pushed up by the escaping creatures underneath, then settles back peacefully, and the area returns to its unnatural quiet.  To the southwest the path seems to take a sudden dip downward.

title: [Vipershroud, Brackish Stream]
description: A dark, brackish, slow-moving stream emerges from under some thick, dangerous-looking brambles and meanders off to the northeast.  Several stones, strategically placed, allow dry passage across the stream to the heavily shaded, moss-choked path running northwest and southwest.  Swarming insects, spawned from the standing pools, add a buzzing, biting layer of black fog to the already misty atmosphere.

title: [Vipershroud, Brackish Stream]
description: The stream widens here, forming a small swamp.  Biting flies latch onto anything remotely alive, sucking the life-giving blood out with gusto.  Although the trees are sparser in this area, those that have survived are huge, continuing to block the moonlight with their spreading upper branches.

title: [Vipershroud, Brackish Stream]
description: The stream continues its slow progress, meandering around towering firs and creeping under razor-sharp brambles while encouraging the swarms of voracious insects.  The conditions are intensified by the smothering humidity and lack of light.  One might be able to fend off the insects if one could only see them.  A lone boot, the top and a few laces visible, protrudes up through the mud.

title: [Vipershroud, Brackish Stream]
description: The air is thick with moisture, and water dripping from the trees delivers a hot, unsatisfying rain.  The moist moss squishes loudly underfoot, and clouds of biting insects buzz around hungrily, attempting to feast on some fresh blood.  The trail, coming from the northwest, ends abruptly at a shallow, brackish stream.  To the northeast, the stream disappears under a thick clump of brambles, but to the southwest it is passable, if one doesn't mind tromping through heavy mud.

title: [Vipershroud, Mossy Trail]
description: The trees push closer to the trail, competing for space with the moss and brambles.  Little light penetrates the area.  The heat, however, seems to have no problem penetrating the leafy canopy, helping the humidity to make travel miserable.  A large canine skeleton lies just off the path, half-buried by greenish moss and fungus.

title: [Vipershroud, Mossy Trail]
description: A thick canopy of tightly intertwined branches closes off most of the moonlight, making the area appear as if the night were heavily overcast.  Sharp brambles choke the trail, and thick moss underfoot makes the passage a slippery one.  To the northeast the trees appear to thin somewhat, and the sound of a rushing river can be heard.  The nearby river moderates the temperature, making it damp but cool.

title: [Vipershroud, Locksmehr River]
description: Moonlight sparkles off the Locksmehr River as it rushes toward the west.  The current is very fast here, and the flow is interrupted by several protruding rocks.  To the east, a ferry service for crossing the river operates from a sturdy wooden dock.  The Vipershroud, a near impenetrable forest, looms to the south and west.

title: [Moot Hall, Registrar's Office]
description: This cramped, dusty office displays all the standard appointments that mark it as serving an extremely important role in the bureaucracy of the town government.  Dilapidated, make-shift shelves are crammed full of books and papers that bear no evidence of being organized in any useful manner.  Everything is covered with a thick layer of dust, and the walls and ceiling are stained with black from the smoke that rises from the single, small lamp that rests on a high desk in the center of the room.

title: [Clerics' Shop, Salesroom]
description: The atmosphere in this shop is one of quiet contemplation.  The walls are covered with somber murals depicting the gods and heroes of Elanthia in their ongoing struggles against the forces of the Undead.  Racks along the walls hold gleaming weapons that seem almost to glow with an inner light of their own.  The shop's proprietor, Brother Wuldreth, attends to business with serene determination.

title: [Elaraeyn's Boutique]
description: Illumination from smoky oil lamps reflects off polished glaes walls etched with delicate runes, making pale shadows appear to dance in the flickering light.  To one side of the room sits an oak clothes rack with some stuff hanging on it.

Pale blue enamel frames various mirrors and paintings along the ivory-colored walls of the boutique, the color scheme matching the scalloped rugs beneath a lacquered linden armoire and a riveted tan leather trunk.  The subtle fragrance of vanilla-tinged lavender drifts upwards from a pair of blown glass censers hung along either side of a tall ribbon-entwined rack, the pale grey wisps dissipating as they curl against the linden-planked ceiling.
paths: Obvious exits: northeast, south, northwest, out

title: [River Tower East, Headquarters]
description: Papers are strewn over the desk that stands in the middle of the room.  On the wall behind the desk is a banner with the insignia of the guard regiment assigned to man the walls and watchtowers of Wehnimer's Landing.

title: [River Tower East, Barracks]
description: You enter a square room with cots pushed back against the walls and a trunk at the foot of each bed.  Everything in the room denotes order and readiness.  In times of emergency, the extra militia sleep here.  To the north a recessed alcove is partly obscured by spare uniforms hanging from hooks.

title: [River Tower East, Alcove]
description: Once in the alcove you are surprised to see a room of quite comfortable dimensions.  A window slit looks out on the log walls of the surrounding stockade and across the choppy waters of Darkstone Bay.  A hooded cloak and a floppy-brimmed felt hat are laid out on a dressing table, and beside them are scattered some notes in an unrecognizable cipher.

title: [Alchemist's House, Shop]
description: The front part of the small house serves as an alchemist's shop.  The cramped room is filled with various ramshackle furnishings holding all manner of amulets, wands, phials, and magical potions.  A locked glass-paned bookcase holds ancient volumes and magical scrolls.  A strong steel door is set into the back wall.

title: [Alchemist's House, Library]
description: The hushed silence of this dark, dusty library envelops you.  Though draped with plush curtains, the room is bathed in a soothing golden light.  Atop a reading table, an ancient alchemical treatise in an obscure script lies open, surrounded by quills, parchment and other tools of scholarly research.  A low arch leads east.

title: [A Rainbow-Colored Tent]
description: Light from a few scattered candles reflects from the gaily striped rainbow-colored walls of the tent, illuminating the bare interior with a faint multihued glow.  Bits of charred wood and fabric and what looks like a few fragments of bone are imbedded in the freshly packed dirt floor, and a vague scent of something burnt hangs in the air like a memory.

Light filters in through the gaily striped rainbow-colored walls of the tent, illuminating the bare interior with a faint multihued glow.  Bits of charred wood and fabric and what looks like a few fragments of bone are imbedded in the freshly packed dirt floor, and a vague scent of something burnt hangs in the air like a memory.

title: [Caverns, Twisting Tunnel]
description: The tunnel is barely large enough for a giantman to squeeze through, and smells strongly of clay and unwashed dwarf.  It winds down from the tent above, its twists and turns hiding whatever lies below from view.

title: [Reignbeau Caverns]
description: Many-hued clay forms the walls, ceiling, and floor of this low, twisting cavern.  Dozens of stalactites drip thick liquids in every color of the rainbow.  It takes a keen eye and a quick step to avoid an unintended change in hair color.  The clay that oozes from the walls and drops from above forms dozens of multihued puddles around you.  Grumbling, uncooperative dwarves loiter in every corner.
paths: Obvious exits: north, east, south, west, up

title: [Reignbeau Caverns, Tunnel]
description: Small tunnels branch out in every direction and it's hard to be sure which one you entered through, let alone which to leave through.  Colored footprints dot the floor, wandering in every direction.
paths: Obvious exits: north, south, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Reignbeau Caverns, Order Room]
description: A massive dye-stained stone counter dominates the muddy rock-walled chamber, overseen by a disgruntled-looking dwarven clerk who glares and mutters to himself at each customer's approach.  Behind the counter, a dwarf-sized tunnel leads into some mysterious back room from which sounds of splashing and cursing and grumbling can be heard.

title: [Lower Dragonsclaw, Hollow Tree]
description: The buzzing of ceaseless activity shows this fallen trunk is far from dead, rather it is teeming with life.  The flurry of activity centers around a beehive clinging to the tree's inner wall.  The warm, sweet smell of clover honey and gathered pollen, and the gentle, purposeful humming of the bees, lull you into a sense of security.

title: [Lower Dragonsclaw, Hollow Tree]
description: It is dark and snug inside this part of the tree trunk, with the rotting wood emitting a gentle warmth and sickly sweet smell.  Scant light enters through cracks in the curving wooden walls.  Muffled sounds echo to the north and south, though the way is barely visible through the murky dankness.

title: [Lower Dragonsclaw, Hollow Tree]
description: This is a dark crook of the rotted log, just high enough for you to stand upright.  You hear ominous grunts and whines, but you cannot venture any farther down the narrow, hollow branches.

title: [Raging Thrak Inn, Trophy Room]
[Raging Thrak, Trophy Room]
[Thrak Inn, Trophy Room]
description: The charred form of a fireplace occasionally billows small clouds of dust from a spot away from the crowd in the tavern.  Charred animal skins lie before the hearth, flanked on either side by clawed and raggedly ripped couches.  Broken and blackened trophies of forgotten hunts line the burnt and stained walls.

Tiny smudges of soot mar the fieldstones used to create the grand fireplace in this cozy room.  A collection of plaques hangs above an immense grey marble mantel cluttered with trophy cups and bowls.  Fashioned from a single stone slab, the hearth extends to an impressive black bear rug with its maw frozen in a silent roar.  Several overstuffed wingback chairs, each covered in deep jewel-tone chintz, are scattered about the room.  Against the back wall, a tall glass-front curio houses several ancient mementos and a thrak hide curtain hangs nearby.

A massive granite fireplace covers the back wall, proudly displaying a glass-paneled case upon its solid felwood mantel.  Two distressed leather sofas are pushed up against the side walls to allow plenty of room for weary patrons to rest.  Nearby, a blackened thrak hide curtain leads to a small alcove.  Sprawled across the wooden floors are several mismatched animal pelts.  You also see some leather sofas, a hide-wrapped wastebasket and a basket of sticks.

title: [Zul Logoth, Marcasite Tunnel]
description: Smooth granite walls taper into a narrow passageway.  Through the tunnel visible ahead, mining carts careen past upon a set of metal rails, screeching and whining their way under the DragonSpine.  Several dwarves move about the tunnel, efficiently getting passengers loaded and keeping the carts moving along.

title: [Kharag 'doth Dzulthu, Tunnels]
description: The opening of the tunnel has been widened to form a sort of lobby.  The rough-hewn walls are shored up by thick oiled timbers.  Several small lamps dangle from the beams above, casting a dim light across the cavern.

title: [Frith's Inn, Parlour]
description: This room is a bit quieter than the main saloon.  A fireplace of large river stones dominates the far wall, a fire within it crackling cheerfully.  Sturdy tables fill the room, awaiting paying customers.  Serving wenches bustle about, always ready with a smile and a foam-topped tankard of ale.
