title: [Frith's Inn, Main Saloon]
description: Drawn by the aroma of good food and strong drink, you enter the main saloon.  The innkeeper presides merrily, ensuring everyone gets a share of attention from the pretty serving wenches and the handsome lad behind the bar.  Long benches and rectangular tables seat high-spirited patrons.

title: [Frith's Inn, Front Desk]
description: The front room of this unassuming inn imparts a sense of warmth and comfort.  Serving wenches carrying trays of food and drink to rooms throughout the hostelry cast a welcoming glance at you as they pass.  Laughter and the sound of good fellowship reach your ears from the direction of some swinging doors.  At the mahogany front desk, the friendly proprietor stands ready to attend to your needs.

title: [Glo'antern Moor, Boulder]
description: The view from atop this boulder is not spectacular by any means.  The monotonous grassland spreads out all around.  After about thirty yards of this same scene, mists choke off the view entirely, encasing the area like a grey dome.  Pockets of water dot the surface of the boulder, and footing is a bit tricky on the slick surface.  The trail runs off straight and true to the west from below the boulder, and here, on the boulder's top, the trail in the other direction becomes readily apparent.

title: [Kharag 'doth Dzulthu, Tunnels]
description: Several small torches are mounted upon the walls of this large cavern, casting a dim light across the faces of the occupants.  Half a dozen dwarves scurry about, directing passengers aboard a series of mining carts that barely stop long enough to allow entrance.

wayto.1261:
;e fput "buy pass"
waitfor "You hastily exit the cart"
wayto.1267:
;e fput "buy ticket"
waitfor "You hastily exit the cart"

title: [Zul Logoth, Western Mines]
description: The smooth stone of the cavern walls is unblemished save the occasional errant chisel mark.  Glowing lanterns hang from iron brackets mounted along the walls.  A carved stone arch funnels passengers out into Zul Logoth.

title: [Dead Plateau]
description: The dryness borne on the wind attacks the eyes, throat, and anyplace else it can insinuate itself.  Sand carried by the gusts attempts to accumulate underneath the eyelids and make blinking feel like drawing a layer of gravel across one's eyeballs.  The wind talks, loudly, but what it says remains a mystery.  It shrieks incomprehensibly at times before lapsing into self-pitying moans.  Despite its ravings and abrasiveness, the wind might come to be a welcome companion...if it were not so cold.

title: [Dead Plateau, Plank Bridge]
description: The crevice narrows somewhat at this point, the sides converging to a separation of approximately thirty feet.  Some industrious soul has taken advantage of the conversion and erected a plank bridge to span the crevice.  The trail continues either across the bridge or follows the crevice eastward toward the plateau's edge again.  For those needing to get across, crossing on the bridge beats trying to jump the chasm...or walking farther into the plateau's interior.

title: [Marshtown, Surde's Pier]
description: The pier is long and wide, but is utilized primarily by small rowboats and skiffs used for shallow-water fishing.  The dock is packed with anglers who are busy trying to catch dinner or fish to sell at market.  Splatters and stains on the dock show that the fish caught here are often cleaned here.

This pier is long and wide, but is utilized only by small rowboats and skiffs used for shallow water fishing.  The dock is packed with anglers who are busy trying to catch dinner or fish to sell at market.  Splatters and stains on the dock show that the fish caught here are often cleaned here.

title: [Vornavian Coast, Pine Forest]
description: The path slopes down into a fog-filled valley and up toward the coast, where the crashing waves can be heard even at this distance.  Rock outcroppings dot the hill, dimly visible in the night.  Lizards and spiders move rapidly across the rocks, looking for food and warmth in the shadowy pine woods.

The path slopes down into a fog-filled valley and up toward the coast, where the crashing waves can be heard even at this distance.  Colorful rock outcroppings dot the hill, forming striking color combinations that please the eye.  Lizards and spiders move rapidly across the rocks, looking for food and warmth in the shadowy pine woods.

title: [Vornavian Coast, Pine Forest]
description: A thick carpet of fallen pine needles covers the ground here, muffling all sounds and creating an uneasy silence.  As the wind subsides, the calls of several nocturnal birds become audible.  Unseen creatures jump from tree to tree overhead, dislodging an occasional branch or pine cone.

A thick carpet of fallen pine needles covers the ground here, muffling all sounds and creating an uneasy silence.  As the wind subsides, the calls of many different kinds of birds become audible.  Squirrels jump from tree to tree overhead, dislodging an occasional branch or pine cone.

title: [Tall Tower]
description: A rough angled ceiling of thin iron plates arcs overhead, supported by thick poles of iron that continue down to the ground that is far below.  Planks of wood make up the sturdy albeit rough floor, and a few small notches are cut into the dark metal walls.  The countryside expands out beneath you, its terrain easily visible from this high vantage point, the moonlight gently illuminating the interior of the tower.

A rough angled ceiling of thin iron plates arcs overhead, supported by thick poles of iron that continue down to the ground that is far below.  Planks of wood make up the sturdy albeit rough floor, and a few small notches are cut into the dark metal walls.  The countryside expands out beneath you, its terrain easily visible from this high vantage point.

title: [Marshtown, Shoreline]
description: As the raised platform approaches the Cairnfang river, less and less stable soil is available to support the buildings and inhabitants of Marshtown.  Rafts of large barrels have been tied together and serve as flotation for the walkway and the squat wooden buildings that line either side.  A breathtaking and living display of color takes place in the waters to the southeast as the crystal waters of the Cairnfang mingle with the bluer waters of Solhaven Bay.

As the raised platform approaches the Cairnfang river, less and less stable soil is available to support the buildings and inhabitants of Marshtown.  Rafts of large barrels have been tied together and serve as flotation for the walkway and the squat wooden buildings that line either side.  A chiaroscuro mingling of hues takes place in the waters to the southeast as the Cairnfang mingles with Solhaven Bay.

title: [Ta'Illistim, Rocky Trail]
description: Here the weathered rocks provide many hand and footholds for easy climbing.  Cool patches of moss provide relief for sore hands.  The trail above grows steadily steeper as it winds its way up the mountain.  The soft hooting of an owl can be heard in the distance.

Here the weathered rocks provide many hand and footholds for easy climbing.  Cool patches of moss provide relief for sore hands.  The trail above grows steadily steeper as it winds its way up the mountain.

title: [The Tapestry Lounge]
description: In contrast with the niche to the south, this space appears both comfortable and pleasantly colorful, with its plush carpets and vividly embroidered tapestries.  A large, overstuffed couch adorned with silken pillows rests against one of the walls, while an elegantly set buffet table provides appetizing refreshments and further enhances the cozy atmosphere within.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: Several grey squirrels bark in protest as your presence has greatly disturbed their work.  Countless numbers of acorns litter the ground surrounding the many large oak trees that grow here.  Obviously, these squirrels will be busy for quite some time yet.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: A carpet of oak and maple leaves cover the trail in this part of the forest.  A stand of oak trees lies further to the north while the forest becomes mixed to the south.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The shrill "cyeeak!" of an unseen bird comes as a start as you continue to walk along the path.  Apparently you are too close to the nest, even though the nearest branch is clearly fifteen or more feet above the ground.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: This part of the forest is damp and moss covered.  The sound of running water can be heard to the south and the terrain of this area slopes down in that direction.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: You are standing on the northern bank of a wide and surprisingly deep stream.  The trail splits here as it follows the course of the water.  The main trail runs off to the southeast while a smaller trail heads northwest.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: A small rise in the terrain allows the path to dry slightly here, providing a welcome bit of relief.  The stream appears to be slowing as it moves to the southeast.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The stream enters this area from the northwest and then meanders back to the northeast.  The water moves fast enough to allow large numbers of trout to live in the cold depths.  The trail is very wet and the going is difficult.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The stream is wide and slow here.  While not very deep, the muddy bottom is too soft to allow you to cross.  The trail follows along the bank and heads to the southwest.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The chirping and croaking of a myriad of frogs fill the air here.  A large number of lily pads grow in the pond formed by the slowing of the water that enters the area as a stream to the southwest.  A smaller stream exits the pond to the east and carries the water further into the forest.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The stream tumbles quietly over moss covered rocks as it flows from the west to the east.  The trail is soft and wet.  A large willow tree grows between the trail and the stream casting a deep shadow on both the water and the ground.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The stream meanders considerably here but runs in a general southwest to northeast direction.  At a particularly narrow stretch, you notice a stone bridge crosses to the opposite bank.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: You are on the southern bank of a wide, slow moving stream.  Spanning the water is a stone bridge that arcs gracefully to the northern shore.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: Chest high ferns sway slowly as you pass along this stretch of shadowed roadway.  Tall fir trees stand like great red pillars against the deep blue sky and provide the cooling shade necessary for the ferns to thrive.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: This wide clearing serves as the intersection of several wide paths.  A deep blanket of brown fir needles covers the ground which muffles the tread of passing feet and wheels.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: The trees in this area are tall and the branches are well above the ground allowing you to glimpse some of the surrounding countryside.  To the south can be seen a bright area, perhaps a meadow.  To the northwest grows a stand of tall evergreen trees.

title: [Upper Trollfang]
description: You are on the eastern edge of a vast region of hills and forest.  To the east and south stretches a rolling plain of tall grasses.

title: [Foothills]
description: From these gently sloping hills you can see a vast plain of tall grasses that stretches as far as the eye can see when gazing northward.  To the south lies the eastern stretch of the Dragonsclaw Mountains, a range of rugged snow-capped peaks.  The tallest of these peaks, Zeltoph Mountain, rises to a height of nearly fifteen thousand feet above the level of the sea to the north.
paths: Obvious paths: east, southeast, south, west

title: [Foothills]
description: The hills become steeper to the south, dotted with patches of scrub, but between the hills the top of a log palisade is visible.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, south

title: [Northern Caravansary, Stockade]
description: Vertical, rough-hewn logs form a stockade, providing some margin of safety this far from the walls of Wehnimer's Landing.  A trail worn by the passage of hooves, wheels, and booted feet leads off to the southwest.

title: [Foothills]
description: To the south the trail heads straight towards the western shoulder of Zeltoph Mountain and the band of pine forest that shrouds the slope at its base.  The serried points of a log palisade rise above a hilltop to the northeast.

title: [Foothills]
description: Scattered pines stand above the hillside grasses, with brown needles blotting out the vegetation beneath their boughs.  To the south the trees close in and the grasslands give way to forest.

title: [Zeltoph's Base]
description: Patches of starlight on the forest floor are filled with green grasses, shrubs, and a small tree or two -- pockets of grassland amidst the silver trunks and brown-carpeted twilight of pineshadow.
Patches of sunlight on the forest floor are filled with green grasses, shrubs, and a small tree or two -- pockets of grassland amidst the silver trunks and brown-carpeted twilight of pineshadow.

title: [Zeltoph's Base]
description: The west wind soughs through the pinetops high over head.  In every direction, ancient pines stretch toward the heavens, and their trunks hide the path even a short distance ahead.  The only young plants in sight are those along the trail, sprouting where hooves and boots have disturbed the earth.

title: [Zeltoph's Base]
description: To the east the trail parallels the mountain's base, keeping the slope more gradual and less wearing for travelers, two- and four-legged alike.  To the north it heads directly downslope among the pines.

title: [Zeltoph's Base]
description: Unprotected by any rock formations, the trail above the treeline is windswept and cold.  Racing along the face of the mountain, vicious gusts tug at the scant gorse bushes growing tightly against the rocks.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: On a trailbed built from crushed rock and bone-aching labor, the caravan trail climbs the base of Zeltoph Mountain from northeast to southwest.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: Reaching an impassable rock wall, the trail doubles back, climbing to the east.  Deep ruts have formed in the steep trail, causing wheels to break on the caravan wagons.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: A trickle of water runs down the mountainside, dripping into a pool at the side of the trail.  The overflow runs down the trail muddying the path.  Moss grows up the rock wall, working its way into old cracks and causing new ones.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: Narrowing severely, the trail bends around a rock outcropping that appears to have grown from the side of the mountain.  You stay close to the western side of the trail after glancing cautiously over the edge and seeing that the bottom is several hundred feet below.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: Bits of cloth are stuck to the rock wall where others have boldly climbed up to a ledge that shadows the trail.  Huddling under the ledge would also provide protection from the occasional showers of rocks that rain down from above.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: Wildflowers blooming along the side of the track carpet the ever present grey rocks.  The flowers are quite resilient, coming back from many tramplings by passersby, both of the two-footed and four-footed kind.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: The trail makes a tight curve up the side of the mountain, no doubt creating problems for the larger caravans.  Some scrubby bushes cover the west side of the trail.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: The trail to the south is wider than the path leading westward.  Below, it snakes around the mountain with a ledge jutting out midway between here and the level below.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: Just below the peak of Zeltoph Mountain, the trail has been washed out by a recent avalanche.  The loose scree makes crossing difficult and potentially hazardous.

title: [Zeltoph Switchbacks]
description: The trail reaches a pass through the mountain range and although Zeltoph towers over the trail to the east and Wehntoph to the west, the air is thin enough to make breathing a bit difficult.  The glorious vista mesmerizes even the most hardened of travellers as they gaze upon the foothills to the north.

title: [Zeltoph Pass]
description: Northward, the land is a patchwork of dark green forests and golden fields, and beyond it the sea stretches like grey-green slate to the horizon.  In the opposite direction, a grass covered plateau is bordered to the south by a line of blunt, snow-covered peaks.  Crossing Zeltoph's flank, the trail begins its descent to the grassland.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: The peak of Zeltoph Mountain is directly to the north, while the plateau stretches southward.  In the distance, Flynth Lake shimmers, reflecting glistening moonlight in the crisp, clear air.
The peak of Zeltoph Mountain is directly to the north, while the plateau stretches southward.  In the distance, Flynth Lake shimmers, reflecting blinding glints of sunlight in the crisp, clear air.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: Many caravans have stopped here, taking advantage of the stream gurgling westward across the trail.  A blackened ring of stones is surrounded by a larger circle of flat rocks used as seats by the drivers and guards.  The ground where oxen have trampled the grass shows signs of recovery from its ill treatment, and the overgrown ruts of a long-abandoned road are just visible among the tall grasses leading eastward.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: Flowing from the northwest, the Flynth River is joined by the stream flowing across the trail in a turbulent junction.  A log, not able to float past some rocks, spins continuously in the churning water.

title: [Plateau, Flynth Lake]
description: The stars and moons are reflected in the still lake that is west of the trail.  The water is as dark as the sky, beautifully setting off the reflected clouds.  Sitting on a partially submerged rock, a bullfrog basks in the starlight.

Clouds scudding across the sky are reflected in the still lake that is west of the trail.  The water is the same brilliant shade of blue as the sky, set off beautifully by the intense white clouds.  Sitting on a partially submerged rock, a turtle basks in the sun.

title: [Plateau, Flynth Lake]
description: A cabin at the water's edge provides protection from the elements for those who travel the trail regularly.  Built more recently, a barn similarly shelters their animals.  Pulled up onto the shore and tied to a nearby tree, a dinghy looks big enough for two fishermen.

title: [Plateau, Flynth Lake]
description: The southern end of Flynth Lake has a number of cattails and other water plants growing around the edge of it.  Croaking bullfrogs compete in a rousing chorus, with harmony provided by crickets hiding in the tall grass.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: Fallen leaves covering the ground cavort in the breeze, resting again as the wind dies down.  The trees hide the north-south trail from the moons' gaze overhead, where the river gently curves towards the trail forming a wide bank.

Fallen leaves covering the ground cavort in the breeze, resting again as the wind dies down.  The trees shade the north-south trail from the fierce sun overhead, where the river gently curves towards the trail forming a wide bank.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: Game trails crisscross the area, most heading towards a copse of trees to the east.  A grouse, flushed from the tall grass, squawks loudly as it flies up and away.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: To the southwest, gravel lines the banks of the Flynth River where the trail crosses it.  A natural ford has been built up over time, widening the river, but making it shallow enough not to cause undue hardship for the caravans.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: Scattered along the trail is some gravel from the river ford, caught in wagon wheels and carried southward.  Tangled threads flutter from a thorny bush where previous travelers have draped their clothing to dry.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: Patches of burnt grass survive despite a spark that went astray from the fire to the south.  The ground is scorched, blackened by spidery patches of black grass ash.  Fortunately, the winds drove the fire towards the river or the entire grasslands would be gone.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: Scattered remains of a burned-out wagon litter the east side of the trail.  Although it appears the fire was extinguished before getting completely out of hand, a large area was destroyed.  A crow pecks through the debris looking for a tidbit that escaped the flames.

title: [Plateau, Flynth River]
description: The blackened and scorched ground of the north fades into the grassy plain of the south.  Only small burned areas show where the fire fed on the fertile growth.  The prevailing winds are northeast across the plateau, which drove the fire back towards the river.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: Without any trees to block the wind, a breeze blows the entire length of the grasslands.  The grass ripples in green and brown waves as far as the eye can see.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: Grasshoppers jump wildly across the trail in a bizarre dance only understood by others of their kind.  The air is filled with a buzzing that changes from loud to soft with the rhythm of the dance.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: The trail swings eastward around a hill, saving the legs of the oxen pulling the laden wagons from the extra strain the slope would provide.  Moonlight reflects off something on the top of the hill.
The trail swings eastward around a hill, saving the legs of the oxen pulling the laden wagons from the extra strain the slope would provide.  Sunlight reflects off something on the top of the hill.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: A single tree stands a lonely vigil on the plain.  Its outstretched limbs reach for the sky, straining to touch the clouds that pass overhead.  A bird, sitting in the tree, suddenly bursts into song, filling the air with music.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: A flock of birds flies overhead in a V-shaped formation heading northwest.  A couple of stragglers strive to catch up with the main group, casting their shadows on the dried grass beneath you.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: Grass valiantly tries to grow between the wheel tracks on the trail.  To the west, a herd of rolton grazes peacefully.  They spook at some imagined horror and run northward, only to stop and begin grazing again.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: A bush grows along the side of the trail, its ripening berries peeking out from under the brown leaves.  A pile of gravel has been dumped to the side of the track, likely to be used for filling in the wheel ruts.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: A chilly, moisture-laden breeze blows over the edge of the plateau to the west.  It continues across the plain, tumbling weeds in a bounding dance.  Further to the south, mountain peaks rise in the distance.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: A discarded wagon wheel lies partially buried in the ground.  A vine has grown through it, intertwining with the remaining spokes.  Some spokes of the wheel point north along the trail, while others point southward towards the gap between Tor Soranrahk and Tor Aganrahk.

title: [Plateau, Grasslands]
description: A hut nestles forlornly in the lee of a large rock outcropping.  Just beyond it, the trail veers southwest in the first of a series of switchbacks, climbing towards the pass between Tors Aganrahk and Soranrahk.

title: [Tor Aganrahk, Switchbacks]
description: Carved into the shoulder of the mountain, and broadened with the crushed rock, the trail descends to the northeast.  Further upslope the gravel is dusted with snow.

title: [Tor Aganrahk, Switchbacks]
description: Wind shifts the ever-present snow, covering the trail with a thin layer and filling the ruts and bootprints.  Upslope to the south, the trail enters the pass between Tor Soranrahk to the east and Tor Aganrahk to the west.

title: [The Saddle]
description: Sun-bleached bones and the rusted remains of weapons and armor poke through the windswept snow.  Cold winds blowing across the plateau from the north are funneled through the pass, and carry enough moisture to bear a bone-chilling bite.

title: [Tor Aganrahk, Ravine]
description: Following a shelf that keeps it above the deadfall and loose stones of the ravine bottom, the caravan trail hugs the mountainside as it climbs toward the pass to the north.

title: [Tor Aganrahk, Ravine]
description: Rising as steeply as caravan traffic will allow, the trail climbs within the shadow of the ravine's western wall.  The blunt peak of Tor Soranrahk is easily visible to the northeast.

title: [Tor Aganrahk, Ravine]
description: Lacking the room to go around a large outcropping, the trail dips abruptly to pass beneath it.

title: [Tor Aganrahk, Ravine]
description: Gazing northward, the trail climbs towards a gap between Tor Aganrahk and Tor Soranrahk, while stark against the southern sky a patterned silhouette of crenellations crowns an east-west ridge.  From here the caravan trail runs straight up the ridge and meets the battlements at a gap marked by the sharper outlines of new stonework.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Ramp]
description: Halfway up the north face of the ridge, the sheer size of the battlements to the south is evident.  Either they were built by Giantmen, or by hundreds of dwarves with more time and energy than they knew what to do with.  A ramp, displaying the crisp colors of freshly worked stone, begins here and rises to intersect the wall where the crenellations have been removed.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Highroad]
description: Following the ridge, this raised and fortified stone roadway stretches out of sight to the east and west.  A newly built ramp climbs the ridge from the north and meets the road at a gap in the battlements.  The ramp and the recent changes to the ancient roadway evidence the precision and craftsmanship that are hallmarks of dwarven stonecraft.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Highroad]
description: A faint glimmer draws your attention to a stone block in the northern parapet, where a wire-thin band of metallic ore has caught a hint of light.  Knowing that it wouldn't still be there if it was of any monetary value, you realize that the block was probably placed there specifically to do what it has just done and brighten a possibly dull journey.

A small flash draws your attention to a stone block in the northern parapet, where a wire-thin band of metallic ore has caught the light.  Knowing that it wouldn't still be there if it was of any monetary value, you realize that the block was probably placed there specifically to do what it has just done and brighten a possibly dull journey.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Highroad]
description: Blackened areas on the surface of the road mark where someone recently chose to build several campfires.  Arkati only know what they used for fuel, or what became of the ashes and unburnt fuel.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Wings]
description: Sheer rock formations rise abruptly on either side of the road, transforming the ridgeline into a ravine.  Battlements are of no use here, yet the crenellations persist, half-carved from the red granite walls.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Wings]
description: Hemmed in on both hands by the sheer rock walls, the roadway continues.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Wings]
description: The sound of birds in flight fills the night sky, as fork-tailed mountain swallows descend into the high rock formations to either hand, dropping into the more protected air above the roadway and darting into nests built high in the folds of the Wings.  The surface of the roadway is almost hidden beneath a layer of white droppings, and a faint chorus of sleepy chirping echoes between the rock walls.

Fork-tailed mountain swallows appear above the high rock formations to either hand, dropping into the more protected air above the roadway and darting into nests built high in the folds of the Wings.  The surface of the roadway is almost hidden beneath a layer of white droppings, and a constant chorus of shrill chirping echoes between the rock walls.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Wings]
description: The roadway's white granite melds into red granite where matching rock formations grow up to the north and south.  Rising slowly to the east, the formations close in, confining the highroad in an unnatural ravine where the wind moans constantly.

title: [Zortahg's Spine]
description: Arcing over a chasm to the north, a grey stone bridge connects the highroad with a cut stone archway set into the mountain's side.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Tail]
description: The white granite roadway descends gently as it bends to the southwest.  The barren rock of Tor Aganrahk's flank gives way to stunted modwirs and patches of mountain laurel.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Tail]
description: Wooded vales flank the highroad's ridge to the east and west.  To the south, the road ends in a fog-bound swale.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Tail]
description: Intact and impressive only a stone's throw above the grasses, the crenellated highroad appears to have decayed as soon as it touched the bog.  Rounded, white humps of stone and pockets of black water dot the green expanse of marsh grass to the south.

title: [Zortahg's Spine, Tail's End]
description: An ancient stone ramp rises from the tall grass and heads north, growing into a battlemented roadway as it reaches above the mist.  To the east, south, and west an expanse of black water stretches, uninterrupted by stone blocks or marsh grass.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: A white gravel roadway surfaces intermittently above the black water.  Evidently created by crushing some of the frequent granite blocks, the gravel must need constant replacement to make up for settling.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale, Roadway]
description: A gravel ramp reaches from the waters of the swale up to the top of this granite paving block, and another block abuts this one to the south.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale, Roadway]
description: Just visible to the east, an obelisk of black granite crowns a low, grass-covered mound.  A wide gap filled with black water separates the mound from the roadway.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale, Roadway]
description: Fog and stone, grass and water.  Not much of interest here.  This might be a good opportunity for some introspection.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale, Roadway]
description: Bordered on either hand by the interminable grasses and water, the huge paving blocks run north and south across the bog.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale, Roadway]
description: The end of the blocks must lie further to the north or south, since there's no sign of it here.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale, Roadway]
description: The ever-present fog reduces visibility to no more than a few paces in any direction.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale, Roadway]
description: Judging from the small gravel ramp that rises out of the bog to reach the top of this paving stone, caravaners rely on these blocks to safely cross the swale.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: A series of flat stone blocks protrudes above the marsh grass to the west.  Whether once a road, an elevated walk, or the top of a wall, it's impossible to tell.  At this point they look like they'll serve admirably as a road.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: Verdant tussocks, huge granite blocks, and black water -- different arrangements of the same three elements appear and reappear in the sea of mist.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: The time-rounded stumps of stone columns stand at regular intervals in an expanse of black water, perhaps once a reflecting pool and bordering colonnade.  With the water's rise the remains of the columns now stand within the pool, and marsh grasses mark the boundaries of the surrounding stonework.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: Aside from guaranteed wet feet, this place doesn't look too bad.  Then again, the constant fog, the opaqueness of the water, and the total absence of any living creature larger than a snail can't all be coincidences, can they?

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: Rising out of the grasses and black water to the north, a massive pile of white granite blocks marks the site of what must have been an impressive building.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: Within the small circle that the mists allow you to survey, black water fills the gaps between the tussocks of marsh grass.  A worn trail emerges from the bog just a few feet from a pair of shattered columns and passes between them as it heads south.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: Like giant teeth protruding from the tall grass, the jagged remains of a massive stone wall stretch into the mist on either hand.  The trail continues north between a pair of shattered columns that once formed a gateway in the ancient wall.

title: [Stoneharrow Swale]
description: The land drops to the north, forming a large mist-filled swale.  Pale, weatherworn boulders and black water can be glimpsed as vagrant breezes worry brief gaps in the blanket of vapors.

title: [Cairnfang Uplands]
description: From the vantage of the ridgetop the land opens to the north and south.  Appearing as almost a border between the wholesome and the unwholesome, the ridge separates an idyllic meadow to the south, filled with wildflowers and a pond, from a mist-shrouded bog, littered with boulders and standing water to the north.

title: [Cairnfang Uplands]
description: The trail reaches the edge of the marsh grass, then turns.  Running northwest, it climbs a grassy ridge and disappears over the top.  Scaling rockier ground to the east, the trail enters a stand of stunted modwirs.

title: [Cairnfang Uplands]
description: The forest ends, and to the west the land drops.  A wide upland meadow overrun with blooming grass widows fills the hollow between the hills with a flood of purple.  A small pond ringed with cattails and marsh grasses nestles in the center of the meadow.

title: [Cairnfang Uplands]
description: The trail forms a 'T' here, with the base of the 'T' stretching south.  One arm of the trail heads west, and the other heads east towards the river.  A dauntingly sheer face of rock rises just beyond the intersection, a shoulder of the mountain to the north shrugging itself free of trees and soil.

title: [Cairnfang Uplands]
description: The trail jogs to the west to avoid the head of a small gully.  Extending to the east, and likely harboring a tributary or backwater of the Cairnfang, the gully is filled with young willows, giant thrakwoods, and tall grasses.

title: [Cairnfang Uplands]
description: The clatter of claws on bark, and fleeting glimpses of a bushy tail proclaim this stand of modwirs as the home of a family of red squirrels.

title: [Cairnfang Uplands]
description: The fast running waters of the Cairnfang are more easily heard than seen through the trees to the east.  To the north, west, and south the needled limbs of the trees cast the thin soil of the uplands into deeper darkness.

The fast running waters of the Cairnfang are easily seen through the trees to the east.  To the north, west, and south the needled limbs of the trees cast a light shade on the thin soil of the uplands.

title: [Cairnfang Uplands]
description: Crossing a barren stretch of flat rock, the trail runs from the edge of a sparse forest of stunted modwirs to the rocky bank of the river.

title: [Cairnfang Falls, Top]
description: The river disappears over the brink of the cliff here, the dull roar of its fall rising through the mist and the pinetops below.  The caravan trail follows a narrow ledge of angled rock as it begins its descent to the cliff's base.

title: [Cairnfang Falls, Switchback]
description: This portion of the trail exists only with the help of rock retaining walls and crushed stone made from the boulders that once stood in its way.  The new level ground has also been discovered by seeds and runners, and the edges of the trail are crowded with tall grasses and brush.  Above and to the east the trail reaches the top of the cliff.

title: [Cairnfang Falls, Switchback]
description: The trail threads its way between outcroppings and boulders as it traverses the cliff.

title: [Cairnfang Falls, Switchback]
description: A broad shelf of rock forms a safe turning point for the trail, so the trail takes the opportunity to reverse itself again and continue to climb.

title: [Cairnfang Falls, Switchback]
description: The trail doubles back on itself.  Dropping sharply to the west and rising to the east, this section sacrifices distance for height.

title: [Cairnfang Falls, Switchback]
description: The trail is as narrow and as steep as caravan traffic will allow, seeking to reach the land above.  The bottommost leg of the switchbacks ends below.

title: [Cairnfang Falls]
description: Clouds of mist rise to the edge of the trail, the bottom of the falls being lost amid the rocks below.  Close to the cliff face the trail turns sharply west, beginning a series of switchbacks to reach the top of the cliff.

title: [Cairnfang Falls]
description: Avoiding the jumbled rocks and vast pool at the fall's base, the trail has circled to the west as it climbs towards the cliff.

title: [Cairnfang Rapids]
description: The trail rejoins the river, crossing smooth expanses of black granite to the water's edge.  The Cairnfang churns past, and the thunder of falling water is carried down the river to you.

title: [Cairnfang Pineforest]
description: Weaving between rock formations and twisted pines, the trail seems almost to have lost its way at times, while overhead a pine siskin calls to its mate.

title: [Cairnfang Pineforest]
description: The trees here are more sparse, finding fewer places to sink their roots amidst the outcroppings and boulders.  Underfoot, the black granite wears a thin layer of fallen pine needles, each rain sweeping the rock clean of any that have fallen before.

title: [Cairnfang Pineforest]
description: A layer of brown needles, decades deep beneath the towering pines, muffles any sounds of movement.  The going is easier and quieter, but the silence is almost sinister.  A log-and-plank bridge spans a gully to the southwest.

title: [Cairnfang Pineforest, Bridge]
description: In the gully below, a line of wrack and driftwood marks the upper reaches of the stream during floods.

title: [Cairnfang Pineforest]
description: Beneath the shadow of tall pines, a small log-and-plank bridge spans a tributary of the Cairnfang River.

title: [Cairnfang Pineforest]
description: Along a sandy stretch of trail unshadowed by trees, the ringed blossoms of crimson wreath flowers provide a contrast to the muted tones of sand and pineneedles.
Along a sandy stretch of trail unshadowed by trees, the ringed blossoms of crimson wreath flowers provide a bright contrast to the muted tones of sand and pineneedles.

title: [Cairnfang Pineforest]
description: A silvery mist and the roar of falling water drifts through the trees from the south, while to the north the pines close in along the trail.

title: [Cairnfang, Stepfalls Gorge]
description: The force of the water and the jumble of unyielding stone churns the water to a foaming white along this stretch of the river.  As the going becomes more difficult along the top of the gorge, the trail turns north for the safer footing of the forested slopes.

title: [Cairnfang, Stepfalls Gorge]
description: The roar of the river from the gorge below makes talking almost impossible here.  The black granite walls of the gorge reflect the river's thunder upward as the water tumbles over huge boulders and arcs from jagged ledges.

title: [Cairnfang, Stepfalls Gorge]
description: A silvery mist wells up from the gorge, dulling vision with a gossamer shroud and drowning out sounds with the constant roar of the churning waters below.

title: [Cairnfang, Stepfalls Gorge]
description: The caravan trail ascends a series of sandstone shelves alongside the river.  Having cut through the soft stone, the river fills the air with scintillating mist as it cascades over several small falls in the gorge below.  To the southwest the trail veers from the river and enters a large clearing.

The caravan trail ascends a series of sandstone shelves alongside the river.  Having cut through the soft stone, the river fills the air with rainbowed mist as it cascades over several small falls in the gorge below.  To the southwest the trail veers from the river and enters a large clearing.

title: [Cairnfang Forest, Clearing]
description: Obviously used by caravans as a campsite, this clearing is marred by the remains of firepits and the signs of recent trampling by shod hooves.  The river is just visible through the trees to the south.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: The caravan route passes beneath the arching branches of a giant thrakwood bush, growing close alongside the trail.  About head level on a giantman, the branches are too high to be a hindrance to anyone shorter.  Moonlight reaches down through the canopy and softly highlights a cluster of snowblossoms in a clearing to the northeast.

The caravan route passes beneath the arching branches of a giant thrakwood bush, growing close alongside the trail.  About head level on a Giantman, the branches are too high to be a hindrance to anyone shorter.  Sunlight reaches down through the canopy and highlights a cluster of snowblossoms in a clearing to the northeast.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: Marred only by the trail's pathway of trampled mud, a blanket of deep, green moss carpets the ground between the ancient trees.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: The prone trunk of a massive modwir lies to either side of the trail.  Easily thicker than the height of a tall Giantman, a large section of the rotted wood has been chopped away so the trail could avoid detouring around the fallen giant.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: The sharp hammering of a hungry woodpecker echoes amongst the trees, as the trail follows a valley northward between ridgelines to the east and west.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: The caravan trail parallels a small gully.  The fallen trunks of trees undercut by the collected rainwaters span the miniature chasm -- moss-covered foot bridges to nowhere in particular.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: Having reached the top of a small rise, the trail levels off for a bit before heading downhill again.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: A carpet of splayed monkapple leaves hides the forest floor to either side of the trail, broken only by the trunks of ancient oaks rising like pillars to the green canopy above.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
[Cairnfang Forest, Wagon's End]
description: The trail climbs a gentle slope as it continues to the northeast beneath the trees.  Southward, the moonlit expanse of ferns and tree trunks stretches downhill, only to be lost among the grey and black columns of the trees.

The trail climbs a gentle slope as it continues to the northeast beneath the trees.  Southward, the sun-dappled expanse of ferns and tree trunks stretches downhill, only to be lost among the grey and black columns of the trees.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: Pale beams of moonlight striking gold-and-black curls of peeling bark draw your eye to a stand of ragbark modwirs a few yards east of the trail.
The striking gold-and-black curls of peeling bark draw your eye to a stand of ragbark modwirs a few yards east of the trail.

title: [Cairnfang Forest]
description: Trees crowd in from either side, casting the trail into utter darkness, and briars and creepers weave a darkened tangle close alongside the path.
Trees crowd in from either side, casting the trail into constant shadow, and briars and creepers weave a tangle of green close alongside the path.

title: [Cairnfang, North Bank]
description: Still following the river, the trail begins to climb.  The cairns of stone that give the river its name appear infrequently here.

title: [Cairnfang, North Bank]
description: An expanse of cattails and open pockets of water spread westward from the river just south of here, forcing the trail to veer to the southwest to stay on dry ground.  To the north, the trail is able to keep close to the river atop its firm western bank.

title: [Cairnfang, North Bank]
description: Avoiding the cattails and marshgrass within the bend of the river, the trail drops away from the bank and sticks to higher ground.

title: [Cairnfang, North Bank]
description: Following the northern bank of the river as it heads east, the caravan trail quickly leaves the settled fields and pastures behind.  The trail and the ancient, piled stone markers that pierce the river's surface are soon the only signs that intelligent life has passed this way before.  To the west, the trail appears more used as it follows the Cairnfang towards the cliffs above Solhaven Bay.

title: [Cairnfang Crossing, North]
description: Black flies cover the dessicated remains of several criminals who ran afoul of the law one too many times.  The stench of death and decay, as well as the ghastly, slack-jawed visages of the eyeless corpses keeps passersby a healthy distance from the gibbets.  Bearing almost as much traffic as the road south across the bridge, although of a decidedly more squalid strain, a well-worn dirt road heads west.

title: [Hangman's Bridge]
[Hangman's Broken Bridge]
description: Named for the half-dozen gibbets that bear their hideous fruit just beyond its northern end, this bridge's heavy timbers stretch over the Cairnfang River as it flows west to the bay.

The gibbets for which the bridge is named are barely visible just beyond its northern end.  Heavy timbers that make up the bridge stretch out over the Cairnfang River as it flows west to the bay, but end in jagged splinters halfway across, preventing passage across to the southern side.

title: [Cairnfang Crossing, South]
description: The Hangman's Bridge spans the Cairnfang River, while a short distance to the east what appears to be a tavern or inn stands between the road and the riverbank.  The road continues to the east past the building, following the southern bank of the river.

title: [Vornavis Exterior]
description: Tilled fields and grazing lands for the city's flocks spread out north and south of the road.  The road is used by the locals headed to and from Vornavis' North Gate, so it is well-traveled and easy to follow.  Further east it veers closer to the Cairnfang River, where a timber bridge is barely visible.  To the west you can make out the low walls and canvas roofs of the caravansary.

title: [Vornavis Caravansary, Exterior]
description: Clouds of dust billow over the walls of the caravansary grounds.  Snorts and heavy sounds of stamping coming from the animal pens.

title: [Vornavis Caravansary, Exterior]
description: An old man, sitting against the low stone wall, grins toothlessly at travelers trudging down the pitted dirt trail between the caravansary and the Cairnfang River.

title: [Vornavis Cliffs, River Trail]
description: The narrow dirt path is strewn with rocks.  The distant roar of the Cairnfang tumbling down the cliffs into Solhaven Bay can be heard even this far away.

title: [Vornavis Caravansary, Exterior]
description: The bustle and noise inside the caravansary can barely be heard outside the rear wall.  The tumbling song of the Cairnfang echoes in the scrubby trees growing along the riverbank.

title: [Vornavis Cliffs, River Trail]
description: At the edge of the cliffs, Solhaven Bay stretches out towards the horizon.  At the foot of the cliff, the marshes lie spotted with buildings.  Below the cliffs to the southwest lies the Free Port of Solhaven.

title: [Vornavis Cliffs, City Walls]
description: The stone walls of Vornavis's Northwest Tower loom above as the cliffs fall away beneath.  The sensation is dizzying.  Just below, the first in many courses of Solhaven rooftops begins.  A strange contraption of ropes and pulleys is attached to the stone wall.  A metal track, newly set into the cobblestones, runs down the steep hillside.

title: [Solhaven, Tumbledown Lane]
description: Resembling a cobblestone footpath more than a street, Tumbledown Lane levels out for only a few feet.  The street dead ends at the door of a stone cottage sporting an incongruous onion-shaped dome, nestled close in the shadow of the Northwest Tower.  Behind the cottage, the metal track runs past, headed down the hillside.

title: [Solhaven, Tumbledown Lane]
description: The rough, uneven cobblestones are stacked like stairsteps here.  The view of the bay is breathtakingly distracting.  As you gingerly pick your way, a woman carefully balancing a basket of laundry climbs past hurriedly.

title: [Solhaven, Tumbledown Lane]
description: The tiny cottages here seem to have grown straight from the steep hillside.  From the top of the steps, you can see more of the Port stretching southward.  Farther in the distance, the dark stripe that is the Vornavis Canal slices the city in two.

title: [Solhaven, Tumbledown Lane]
description: The cobbled street twists southward, snaking its way down the cliffside.  Several stone cottages line the street to one side, while on the other lie the roofs of the next.  Two well-dressed merchants, deep in conversation, stand in front of the largest cottage.

title: [Solhaven, Tumbledown Lane]
description: Tumbledown Lane widens here, accommodating a number of brightly painted cottages.  The metal track runs across the southern end of the street, leaving little room for passage down.  Residents bustle past you in either direction, ignoring your presence.

title: [Solhaven, Tumbledown Lane]
description: The uneven, downward sloping cobblestones bring you into the looming shadow of Vornavis's Northwest Tower as you reach the top of the steps.  A single cottage, little more than a shack, sits nestled against the cliff wall.

title: [Solhaven, Tumbledown Lane]
description: Close to the bottom of the cliffs, the cobblestone street is somewhat level.  A tidy row of stone cottages faces the bay, moonlight glinting on their glaes window panes.  A well-dressed elven man walks by at a fast clip, his eyes glued to the pavement.

Close to the bottom of the cliffs, the cobblestone street is somewhat level.  A tidy row of stone cottages faces the bay, sunlight glinting on their glaes window panes.  A well-dressed elven man walks by at a fast clip, his eyes glued to the pavement.

title: [Solhaven, Tumbledown Lane]
description: A row of stone cottages lines the street, some washed in greens and blues.  A street peddler stands nearby, animatedly haggling with a dwarven woman over his wares.  Passersby simply walk around the pair, ignoring their animated discussion.

A row of stone cottages lines the street, some washed in greens and blues.  Clusters of gaudy jewels gleam beneath the garish awning of a street peddler's stall.  Nearby, a series of flagstone steps descend toward Bayside Road.

title: [Sylvarraend Road]
description: The fence continues to follow along the path as a horse lies down within the pasture.  A small gap in the eastern fence opens up to a path leading to the barn.
The fence continues to follow along the path as a horse can be seen standing in the field towards the west.  A small gap in the eastern fence opens up to a path leading to the barn.

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
description: The cobblestone street runs southwest, parallel to the Bay.  To the northeast, the road begins climbing the cliffs.  An oddly shaped structure stands nearby, a polished wooden plaque hanging over the door.  Well-dressed residents head purposefully in and out of the building.

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
description: The crowds thicken as they push deeper into town.  To the southwest, you notice the outline of a dock against the waters of the bay.  Eastward, you can see wagons trundling down the street towards the cliffs.  Nearby, a lone fisherman stands poised on the rocks, casting his line into the sea.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, south, southwest

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
description: A small wooden dock extends out into the bay, the barnacle-covered pilings driven down through the rocky shore.  The weathered planks run right up to the edge of the cobbled street.  Noisy crowds jostle past as townsfolk scurry about their errands.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, south, southwest

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
description: Bayside Road widens here, as throngs of people head southward into the North Market.  More than a few are drawn by the mouthwatering aroma of fresh-baked goods wafting from the doorway of the half-timber building opposite the bridge.  To the northwest, the Market Bridge spans the bay, heading towards Marshtown.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, south, southwest, northwest

title: [Solhaven, North Market]
description: The crush of the crowd is almost overwhelming here in the center of the market.  Peddlers wheeling small carts push their way through, shouting loudly.  Nearby, a group of dwarves argue heatedly with a local merchant.

The crush of the crowd is almost overwhelming here in the center of the market.  Peddlers wheeling small carts push their way through, shouting loudly.  Nearby, a group of dwarves argue heatedly with a local merchant.  Cracks splinter many of the cobblestones of the square.

The press of the crowd is little diminished by the late hour.  Peddlers wheel small carts, pushing their way through and splitting the air with their shouts.  Delectable scents of baked goods grace the air, drifting from the wrought iron oven of the Muffinsmith's stall at the corner of the market.  Before it, a blond thanot bench embellished with bas-relief pelican feathers glistens in the starlight thanks to a coat of varnish.  On the opposite end of the market, the Belts booth and the Small Blades stand laze beneath the night sky, still open for custom.

The crush of the crowd is almost overwhelming in the center of the sprawling marketplace.  Peddlers wheel small carts, pushing their way through and splitting the air with their shouts.  Delectable scents of baked goods grace the air, drifting from the wrought iron oven of the Muffinsmith's stall at the corner of the market.  Before it, a blond thanot bench embellished with bas-relief pelican feathers glistens in the sunlight thanks to a coat of varnish.  On the opposite end of the market, the Belts booth and the Small Blades stand battle for the throng's attention.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west

title: [Tanzania's Gems & Jewelry]
description: Soft amber-hued velvet curtains frame the shop's glaesine windows.  Thick garnet-colored carpeting muffles all sounds of footfalls as shoppers mill about the shop, buying and selling various pieces of jewelry and gems.  Sunlight streams in through the glaesine windowpanes, illuminating the jewels displayed in cases along the rear wall.

Soft amber-hued velvet curtains frame the shop's glaesine windows.  Thick garnet-colored carpeting muffles all sounds of footfalls as shoppers mill about the shop, buying and selling various pieces of jewelry and gems.  Moonlight streams in through the glaesine windowpanes, illuminating the jewels displayed in cases along the rear wall.

title: [Solhaven, Conch Street]
description: A small clapboard warehouse stands nearby, painted a drab grey.  Giantmen pull small wagons loaded with boxes eastward, towards the foot of the cliffs.  Guards trot alongside, eyeing the crowd for signs of trouble.

title: [Solhaven, Conch Street]
description: Clapboard warehouses sit on either side of the cobblestone street.  Wagons stand in long lines, the drivers leaning against them.  Burly guards keep a wary eye on passersby.

title: [Solhaven, Conch Street]
description: Here in the shadow of Vornavis' western wall, workers unload wagons and fill carts with boxed goods.  The carts are hauled up the cliffside on metal tracks with ropes pulled by still more laborers.  Guards are posted up the cliffs as far as you can see.

Here in the shadow of Vornavis' western wall, workers unload wagons and fill carts with boxed goods.  The carts are hauled up the cliffside on metal tracks with ropes pulled by still more laborers.  Vornavian guardsmen mingle with those in Solhaven blue and silver, gathered in squads along the cliffs as far as the eye can see.

title: [Solhaven, Triton Road]
description: Ivy climbs the walls of a stone cottage.  Smoke curls from the chimney, leaving the air heavy with the scent of burning modwir.  An old man sits on the doorstep, whittling a stick.

title: [Solhaven, Latirus Lane]
description: This lane is somewhat quieter, although quite a bit of traffic flows eastward.  A group of children plays hide-and-seek among the cozy, well-kept cottages lining the cobblestone street.  A halfling woman sits upon her doorstep, peeling apples into a small pot as she watches the children.

title: [Solhaven, Latirus Lane]
description: A charming ivy-covered cottage is built up against the hillside.  A small garden nestles beside the cottage, brimming with colorful roses.  A small number of townsfolk travel eastward, towards a cottage nestled at the end of Latirus Lane.

title: [Solhaven, Latirus Lane]
description: A large stone cottage rests at the end of the cobbled lane.  Wildflowers are scattered in bright clumps around the small yard, and window boxes burst with flowers.  A small brass plaque is tacked next to the door.  An old woman sits outside the door, rocking gently in her wooden chair.

title: [Solhaven, Triton Road]
description: The imposing facade of the Solhaven Library rises above the roadway.  Clad in soft white limestone, the building presents an elegant contrast to the surrounding stone cottages.  A knot of scholars argues on the limestone staircase leading to the entrance.

title: [Solhaven, North Market NE]
description: The northeast corner of the market is somewhat quieter than the bustling center.  A steady stream of customers flows through the door of an elegant stone building.  Windowboxes burst with bright red begonias.  A gleaming brass plaque is affixed to the bright blue front door.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, southwest, west

title: [Solhaven, Triton Road]
description: The cobbled street is awash with people traveling to and from the square.  A few small cottages line the road here, brightly painted in a rainbow of hues.

title: [Schoolhouse, Front Lawn]
description: Lush green grass spreads out around you, encompassing the white painted building that sits in the center of the lawn.  Wildflowers speckle the ground, adding a variety of colors to the scenery.  A small path cuts across the lawn to a small set of stairs leading up to the building's door.  Children run over the lawn as a few parents stand nearby with a keen eye.

Lush green grass spreads out around you, encompassing the white painted building that sits in the center of the lawn.  Wildflowers speckle the ground, adding a variety of colors to the scenery.  A small path cuts across the lawn to a small set of stairs leading up to the building's door.  Pale moonlight drifts lazily over the quiet courtyard as a few crickets chirrup nearby.

title: [Solhaven, Triton Road]
description: A large cottage rests in the shadow of the Vornavis Cliffs.  Well-dressed patrons wander past, carrying small boxes and packages.  Rose colored awnings cover the doors and windows, and a small silver sign is posted beside the entrance.

Stopping at the base of the Vornavian cliffs, the road ends in a small cul-de-sac.  A path lined with crystal lamps leads up to an elegant stone cottage.  Beds filled with beautiful flowers cover the lawn in front of the building.

title: [Old Ta'Faendryl, East]
description: The path moves past the crumbled remains of buildings that must have once been quite imposing in size.  At the point where the river passes between the ruins of the city wall is a wide stone platform, the base of what was most likely a stone bridge, jutting out a few feet over the edge of the river.

title: [Solhaven, North Market East]
description: A brown awning stretches across the front of the large stone building here.  Hanging above the entrance is a metal breastplate, rusted from exposure to the salty sea air.  Two giantmen, deeply engrossed in conversation, lean casually against the building.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Abalone Street]
description: Throngs of people travel westward towards the Market Square and the shouts of peddlers hawking their wares reach your ears.  The unmistakable scent of chocolate wafts from the doorway of a small, whitewashed shop on the north side of the street.  To the east you can see the hulking facade of the Solhaven Inn.

title: [Solhaven, Abalone and Chiton]
description: The elegant limestone facade of the Solhaven Inn and Restaurant dominates the street here.  Deep blue awnings hang above the glaes-paned windows and front walk.  A white-gloved doorman stands at the ready, ushering guests through the arched doors.

title: [Solhaven, Abalone and Cowrie]
description: One small cottage stands out among the other shops.  Climbing roses cover the exterior and a bright pink awning covers the front door.  An elegantly dressed elven man is just leaving the shop carrying a bouquet of roses.  A carved wooden sign swings from a post beside the door.

title: [Solhaven, Abalone Street]
description: The rough, cobblestone street dead-ends a the copper-faced doors of the Tradesman's Gates of the Solhaven-Vornavis wall.  Far to the west, you can hear the bustling sounds of the North Market.  A group of travelers mills about, drifting through the gates or off to the distant market, while a Vornavis Baronial guard converses with each of them one by one.

The rough, cobblestone street dead-ends here in the shadow of Vornavis' soaring west wall.  Far to the west, you can hear the bustling sounds of the North Market.  A group of travelers mills about, drifting westward one by one.

title: [Solhaven, Wentletrap and Cowrie]
description: A knot of merchants in their fur-trimmed doublets and cloaks stand in the middle of the intersection, engaged in an animated debate and oblivious to the glares of those who have to go around them.  The blue-grey of Vornavis' west wall forms a backdrop for the buildings to the east.  Filling the northeast corner of the intersection stands what appears to be a townhouse, but the dark grey brickwork and mortar the color of dried blood gives the building an ominous air.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Wentletrap and Chiton]
description: Shops ring the intersection except for the southeast corner, where a worn set of steps leads up to a raised courtyard.  A limestone keep that looks like it might have been carved from the natural rock of the bay shore rises behind the courtyard's crisp-cornered boxwood hedges.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, North Market SE]
description: Sooty smoke belches from a chimney precariously perched atop a stone building.  An old man leans against the outer wall, slowly sharpening his blade with a coarse whetstone.  An engraved imflass sign hangs from a metal bar mounted above the entrance.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, southeast, west, northwest

title: [Solhaven, Wentletrap Lane]
description: The crowds are thick here, travelling towards the Market Square.  Prosperous-looking merchants hurry in and out of the Bank of Solhaven, their coin purses jingling.  Two giantman guards flank the arched doors, carefully scrutinizing all who enter.

title: [Solhaven, Wentletrap Lane]
description: The buildings along this stretch of Wentletrap Lane are ornamented with a variety of sawtoothing, panelling and moldings, creating variety in a fairly conservative style.  A large, verdigrised brass quill hangs above the doorway of a small shop that occupies the northeast corner of the Scriveners' Hall.

title: [Solhaven, Wentletrap Lane]
description: The corbelled upper stories of the buildings loom over the street, reducing the sky to a narrow strip overhead and trapping the noise and the odors.  Vornavis' west wall forms an undeniable dead end to the lane, the eastern-most buildings leaning to within inches of the granite.

title: [Solhaven, Nerite and Cowrie]
description: The two-story facade of Solhaven's Town Hall looms above you.  Clad in elegantly carved limestone, the building stands out from other local architecture.  Townspeople scurry into and out of the structure at a fast clip.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Nerite and Chiton]
description: Whether out of agreement or competition, the shop fronts along this section of Nerite Lane have been painted red, blue or bright yellow, giving the area a festive appearance.

title: [Solhaven, Nerite and Eastbridge]
description: The flow of guildsmen, merchants, and shoppers is constant, moving northwest toward the North Market and south toward the East Bridge.  A bronze bow hangs above the entrance of a shop on the southeast corner of the intersection, and across from it a simple two story house occupies the intersection's northeast corner.
paths: Obvious paths: east, south, west, northwest

title: [Solhaven, Nerite Lane]
description: The long, gambrel-roofed bulk of the Scribners' Hall fills the north side of Nerite Lane, the gleam from its row of glaes-paned dormers lending brightness to an otherwise drab building.

title: [Solhaven, Nerite Lane]
description: The Solhaven Jail sits against Vornavis' west wall.  Curiously, the structure appears to be built into the wall, and there is no indication how far back it truly goes.  Two watchful, burly giantmen stand on either side of the entrance to the guardhouse.  A group of Vornavian guards stand nearby, conversing quietly.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Esplanade]
description: The tops of birch, oak, and yew trees as well as the peaked roof of a large temple rise above the myrtle hedge that runs along the south side of the esplanade.  Vornavis' Canal Gate is visible to the east, Jastev's Temple complex on the north side of the esplanade just west of here, and Solhaven's Town Hall is visible further along the street to the north.  An unassuming brick walkway leads south from a break in the tall hedge.

The tops of faewood trees enshroud the peaked roof of a small temple rising above the myrtle hedge running along the esplanade's southern edge.  Near a budding linden tree with a narrow crack in the ground at the base of the tree splitting the ground at its base, an unassuming shrouded walk proceeds through a break in the hedge.  Vornavis's Canal Gate is visible to the east, rising beyond a glaes-studded steel archway.
