Near a budding linden tree with a narrow crack splitting the ground at its base, an unassuming shrouded walk proceeds through a break in the hedge.  Vornavis's Canal Gate is visible to the east, rising beyond a glaes-studded steel archway.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Esplanade]
[Solhaven, Liabo and Eastbridge]
description: A polished ebon gate dominates the intersection, set into the tall, white marble walls that occupy the intersection's southeast corner.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Nerite Lane]
description: Amid the intermixed dwellings and storefronts, a well-maintained shop catches your eye.  From the trimly-painted frame of the generous doorway to the fresh whitewash of the half-timbered walls, the very appearance of the shop says - Quality -.

Amid the intermixed dwellings and storefronts, a well-maintained shop catches your eye.  From the trimly-painted frame of the generous doorway to the fresh whitewash of the half-timbered walls, the immaculate appearance of the shop alludes to the quality of its wares.

title: [Solhaven, North Market South]
description: A young lad in a tattered tunic sits begging in front of a half-timber store, fending off any that would encroach on his domain with a deadly glare.  To the north, the hawking of merchants, arguments of bargainers and shuffle of wares and boots combine to form an almost pleasant din.

title: [Solhaven, North Market SW]
description: Trappers, still dusty from traveling the caravan route, drift into and out of this small shop.  A velnalin pelt, stretched across a wooden frame, hangs above the narrow entrance.  An old man sits nearby, playing a merry tune on his cornet.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
description: Bayside Road borders the North Market, bustling with noise and activity.  The North Market Pier juts northwestward into the bay.  A street peddler has set up her cart nearby, doing a brisk trade with thirsty shoppers.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, south, southwest, northwest

title: [Solhaven, Nerite Lane]
description: The bustle of merchants, tradesmen, and sailors through the intersection is almost frantic.  More than a few of them appear to do business within a rather run-down corner shop that displays three brass spheres above the door.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
description: Grains of sand pried loose by the wind and rain form a tiny bank along the facade of the Captain's Rest.  The building's weathered sandstone walls and salt-flecked slate roof give it the honest appearance of being one of Solhaven's oldest structures.

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
description: A capacious, whitewashed warehouse faces North 'Haven Quay across Bayside Road.  The constant flow of longshoremen to and from the quay is often at odds with the traffic on Bayside.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, south, southwest, northwest

title: [Solhaven, Nerite Lane]
description: Achieving a trim, conservative air, the buildings in this area are all fronted with tiles in earthtones and pastels.  On the north side of the lane, a set of steps leads down to a modest tiled shop and its narrow entrance.  To the south, just beyond a high wall of white stone, a high-spired temple rises into the sky like a golden beacon.
Achieving a trim, conservative air, the buildings in this area are all fronted with tiles in earthtones and pastels.

Achieving a trim, conservative air, the buildings in this area are all fronted with tiles in earthtones and pastels.  To the south, just beyond a high wall of white stone, a high-spired temple rises into the sky like a golden beacon.

title: [Solhaven, Nerite Lane]
description: White-wimpled housewives in their mantles and gowns mingle with brightly-clad artisans and clerics sporting their deities' colors, each on some private mission among the shops and stalls of Solhaven.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Esplanade]
description: A wall built of the same golden-yellow bricks as the esplanade borders the southern side of the avenue.  To the west, the brick wall ends where a white granite wall begins.  Above the brick wall the red tiled roofs and stuccoed walls of several large, gabled buildings can be seen.  Near the compound's gate the paving takes on a fanciful appearance as crimson, white, green, cerulean, and black bricks take turns alternating with the ever-present golden-yellow ones.

A wall built of bricks that boast the same golden hue as the paving stones of the esplanade borders the southern side of the avenue.  To the west, the high span of brick segues into a wall of white granite.  Above the brick wall, the red-tiled roofs and stuccoed walls of several large, gabled buildings are visible.  Near the southern compound's gate the paving takes on a fanciful appearance as white, viridian, crimson, cerulean, and ebon bricks take alternating turns with the omnipresent golden ones.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Plaza]
description: Easily as large as the entire North Market, the plaza is paved with a spiral pattern of alternating terra-cotta and golden-yellow bricks.  On the eastern edge of the plaza stands an ornate, white limestone arch, and beyond it the brick-paved avenue stretches toward Vornavis' towering west wall.  A steady mix of merchants, artisans, and clerics pass through the arch in both directions.

Easily as large as the entire North Market, the plaza is paved with a spiral pattern of alternating terra-cotta and golden-yellow bricks.  On the eastern edge of the plaza stands an ornate, pale limestone arch, and beyond it the brick-paved avenue stretches toward Vornavis' towering west wall.  A steady mix of merchants, artisans, and clerics pass through the arch in both directions.

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
description: Tarred pilings and a stone block wall shore up Bayside Road and stand against the constant action of the waves.  This section of Bayside is windier than most, since nothing slows the winds from the west and the expanse of Liabo Plaza to the east provides no obstructions.  An old sailor sits on a wooden bench facing the bay, oblivious to the wind and to passersby.

title: [Solhaven, North 'Haven Quay]
description: Lighters and barges tie up along the north side of the quay, loading supplies and cargo for the larger carracks and cogs moored further out in the bay.  The south side of the quay descends in a broad stretch of steps to the water, providing easy boarding for the passengers of the many punts, gigs and skiffs plying the bay between the shore and the anchored vessels.

title: [Solhaven, North 'Haven Quay]
description: Stacks of barrels, crates, and bales leave little room to even walk, as a purser and his crew unload a caravel that is docked along the west end of the quay.

The stretch of grass tufts and jutting stone is littered with stacks of barrels, crates, and bales that leave little room to move, but that seems to little impede the flow of merchants and sailors swarming over the quay like garish ants.  A dark-painted cutter with crimson eyes on its prow is roped opposite a caravel with a shallow draft and swan-patterned green sails.

title: [Solhaven, Bayside Road]
[Solhaven, Bayside and Baron's]
description: Bayside Road either begins or ends here on the north bank of the Vornavis Canal, depending on whether you're heading northeast or south, and gulls hover constantly, scanning the pavement and the waters for anything edible.  South of here Baron's Bridge arcs over the canal, tying North 'Haven to South and rising high enough to let galleys and barges pass beneath on their way to and from the docks beneath Vornavis.  A deserted quay juts into the water of the bay to the northwest.

title: [Solhaven, Baron's Bridge]
description: Cargo ships and barges dock at Baron's Quay just to the west, the quay forming a breakwater that protects the canal and its shipping.  To the north beyond Bayside Road and Charl's Quay, the timbers of the Market Bridge stretch across the waters of the bay from North 'Haven to Marshtown.  South along the waterfront the South Market Pier is visible reaching out into the ocean, while beyond it the naked timbers of the shipyard and the stilted warehouses of the Bonding Pier can be made out.

Cargo ships and barges dock at Baron's Quay just to the west, the quay forming a breakwater that protects the canal and its shipping.  To the north beyond Bayside Road and Charl's Quay, the timbers of the Market Bridge stretch across the waters of the bay from North 'Haven to Marshtown.  South along the waterfront, piers and quays are visible reaching out into the ocean, while beyond them the naked timbers of the shipyard and the stilted warehouses nearby can be made out.

title: [Solhaven, Charl's Quay]
description: Piles of driftwood, obviously pieces of wrecked ships, litter the quay.  Several of the boards have names burned into them, proclaiming the ships lost to the fury of the ocean.  They do not seem to have been stacked here by humans looking to clean up the beach, but more appear to have been washed here at the will of the sea, or perhaps a greater force looking to clean up the blue waters.

title: [Solhaven, Charl's Quay]
description: A small altar has been constructed here, made of wood from destroyed ships and decorated with chips of coral and tiny pearls.  Breakers wash over the monument, as if in reminder of whom it belongs to.  Very few offerings have been placed here, and the area shows signs of disuse.  A large barnacle-covered trident has been driven into the sand just behind the altar.

title: [Solhaven, Baron's Bridge Road]
description: Just to the north, Baron's Bridge arches over the waters of the Vornavis Canal, connecting South 'Haven with North 'Haven and Marshtown.  A constant flow of townsfolk moves in both directions over the granite span, occasionally delayed by horse drawn wains hauling loads of sun dried marsh hay from the Marshtown haycribs to the South 'Haven mews.
Just to the north, the shattered ruins of the Baron's Bridge jab up through the waters of the Vornavis Canal, looking like nothing so much as accusing, fleshless fingers pointed at the heedless sky.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Court]
description: Alternating terra-cotta and black basalt bricks spiral outward from the center of the court, ending at the low, crenellated wall of basalt blocks that encircles it.  Dominating the expansive court on its eastern edge looms a massive crimson glaes arch of flames that illuminates the area with its wavering, lurid glow.

Alternating terra-cotta and black basalt bricks spiral outward from the center of the court, ending at the low, crenellated wall of basalt blocks that encircles it.  Dominating the expansive court on its eastern edge looms a massive crimson glaes arch of flames.

title: [Solhaven, Baron's Bridge Road]
description: The footfalls and rasp of wagon wheels on stone accompanying the traffic from the north suddenly take on a hollow undertones as solid ground and stone roadway are replaced by the timbers and planking of South 'Haven.  No less busy than Bayside Road north of the bridge, the smocks and leather aprons of tradesmen are more evident here.

The footfalls and rasp of wagon wheels on stone accompanying the traffic from the north suddenly take on hollow undertones as solid ground and stone roadway are replaced by the timbers and planking of South 'Haven.  No less busy than Bayside Road north of the bridge, the smocks and leather aprons of tradesmen are more evident here.

The rasping of wagon wheels and clunks of booted feet on stone accompanying the traffic from the north take on hollow undertones as solid ground and cobbled roadway surrender to the timbers and planking of South 'Haven.  A quiet tavern with a gated patio and smoked windows rules over one of the scant swathes of solid ground, though only the occasional customer slinks inside.

The occcasional rasping of wagon wheels and clunks of booted feet on stone accompanying the traffic from the north take on hollow undertones as solid ground and cobbled roadway surrender to the timbers and planking of South 'Haven.  A bustling tavern with a gated patio and smoked windows rules over one of the scant swathes of solid ground, its entryway clogged with grizzled tradesmen and overfed wenches.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, south, west
Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, west

title: [Solhaven, Baron's Bridge Road]
description: Tidewater Road intersects from the west, and the crenellated circle of Lornon Court, lit by the glowing arch of flame, lies just a few paces to the east.  Further to the north, lanterns along the arch of Baron's Bridge are visible, while braziers light a conical red and yellow building far to the south.

Tidewater Road intersects from the west, and the crenellated circle of Lornon Court, lit by the glowing arch of flame, lies just a few paces to the east.  Further to the north, lanterns along the arch of Baron's Bridge are visible.

Tidewater Road intersects from the west, and the crenellated circle of Lornon Court, with its towering glaes arch, lies just a few paces to the east.  Further to the north the arch of Baron's Bridge is visible.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Heron Lane]
description: Several fair-sized dwellings along the lane's north side have been stained in dark greys and browns, doubtless influenced by the nearness of the Lornon temples visible beyond them to the northeast.  The houses along the south side of the street, however, appear just as substantial, but have been whitewashed to preserve them against the salt sea air and are shingled and shuttered in reds and blues.

title: [Solhaven, Heron Lane]
description: Scaffolding embraces two of the townhouses on the south side of the lane, the buildings bearing partial coats of fresh whitewash, but with no painters around at this hour.  Across the street, a row of potted boxwood shrubs forming a hedge between two of the houses appears to be half trimmed.

Scaffolding embraces two of the townhouses on the south side of the lane, where workers perch at different levels to whitewash the buildings.  Paying more attention to the wisecracking of the painters than to her own work, a gardener trims a row of potted boxwood shrubs between two of the houses across the street.

title: [Solhaven, Heron and Eider]
description: Visible to the north between the wooden townhouses, the cut stone manors and stuccoed courtyard walls of the "on stone" portion of South 'Haven proclaim the wealth and status of their owners.  Extending to the southeast, Eider Run follows the edge of the wooden platform that supports all of the "on water" streets and buildings of South 'Haven.  The dwellings along this portion of Eider are constructed of fine woods and surrounded by large potted trees and ornamental shrubs.

title: [Solhaven, Eider and Murre]
description: Surprisingly, the courtyard wall facing the intersection with Murre Road is constructed of solid grey blocks, as is the manor that can be seen between the polished brass bars of the courtyard gate.  The tops of yew trees visible above the wall are undeniably similar to those of many other potted trees in South 'Haven, but the stone wall and manorhouse are remarkable in this platformed part of town.

title: [Solhaven, Grebe and Eider]
description: Pushing his handcart, a journeyman butcher trundles wearily westward over the timbers of Grebe Lane.  Along both streets, many windows stand open to the cool night breeze.

Standing at the intersection, a journyeman butcher hawks his wares to the open windows of the dwellings that line the two streets.  More than one white-capped head or aproned torso can be seen in an attentive pose, harkening to his call.

title: [Solhaven, Grebe and Eastending]
description: A crew of labourers, wearing grey Mercantylers' Guild tunics, work determinedly to replace the bevelled timber that mates South 'Haven's platform to the solid ground along its northeast edge.  West of them, the wooden manor houses along Grebe Lane strive to mimic their larger cousins to the northeast, but their high wooden fences stand mere feet from them.

title: [Solhaven, Eastbridge End]
description: Standing out because of its crisp, but darker lines, as well as its location, the high wall surrounding the estate at the southern corner of the intersection is constructed entirely of grey brick.  Wrought iron arabesques and spikes adorn the top of the wall and the felwood gates at the compound's entrance.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, southeast, southwest, west

title: [Solhaven, Eastbridge Lane]
[Solhaven, Eastbridge End]
description: The tapered top of a single yew tree peaks over the corner of the high stone wall surrounding the villa to the southeast, but no roof is visible beyond the wall, nor does the solid oak gate permit any glimpse of what lies within.  The rough stone wall forming the northeast corner of the intersection is not nearly as tall, and a copper-sheathed dome can be seen beyond it, gleaming in the starlight.

The tapered top of a single yew tree peaks over the corner of the high stone wall surrounding the villa to the southeast, but no roof is visible beyond, nor does the solid oak gate permit any glimpse of what lies within.  The rough stone rise forming the northeast corner of the intersection is not nearly as tall, and a copper-sheathed dome can be seen beyond it, gleaming in the starlight.

paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Lornon and Eastbridge]
description: A solid wall of evergreens fills the intersection's northeast corner, providing privacy and seclusion for whatever lies beyond.  In contrast, facing the trees from the other side of Eastbridge, a black iron fence -- its gate gaping wide at the corner -- does nothing to hide the brownstone crypt standing in the center of that plot.  Above the gate, a brown enamelled lozenge bears the image of a coiled, green snake.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Eastbridge Lane]
description: Eastbridge rises to span the Vornavis Canal to the north, and a dark-paved court parallels the canal as it runs toward Vornavis' West Wall.  South of the Lane, a low granite building stands well back from the road between paired conifers.

title: [Solhaven, East Bridge]
description: Barges and galleys ply the length of the canal, passing beneath the arch of the East Bridge on their way towards either the seagates below Vornavis or the docks at Baron's Quay.  To the north the roofs and spires of the temples of Liabo rise close at hand, while the northern cliffs beyond the Cascade of Tears provide a backdrop to the massed buildings of North 'Haven.  In the opposite direction, the tops of the Lornon temples stand in front of the plain of rooftops and warehouses that stretch southward.

title: [Solhaven, Eastbridge Lane]
[Eastbridge, Disaster Area]
description: Paired temple gates stand on either side of the street, the gate to the east bearing the silver clenched fist of Kai and the gate to the west bearing the silver sword of Ronan.  Flanking Eastbridge Lane, the two temples guard the roadway from the bridge and the temples of Lornon south of the canal.

Paired temples stand to either side of the street.  The gate to the east bears the silver clenched fist of Kai, while to the west, a ruined opening leads in to the ransacked grounds of Ronan's Temple.  Flanking Eastbridge Lane, the two temples guard the roadway from the temples of Lornon south of the canal.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Esplanade]
description: A waist-high black iron and golden glaes fence surrounds the grounds of Eonak's Temple to the north.  No gate or archway marks the entrance, yet a broad, flagstone road leads from the esplanade towards the stone bulk of the temple.  Columns of heat-distorted air rise from the squat domes of the charcoal furnaces and the forges ranged beyond the temple proper.

A tall black iron and white imflass fence encircles the grounds of Fasthr's Lance to the north.  Winding through a spade-topped stygian steel gate, a broad flagstone road leads from the esplanade toward the stone bulk of the tower.  Whitewashed and tall, the tower rises from a courtyard atop a green hillock.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Esplanade]
description: A utilitarian, grey stone wall of uneven courses surrounds a temple complex to the north.  In the center of the wall, opalescent grey spheres top the gateposts to either side of a high wooden gate.  The upper two-thirds of a tower, built in the same stone and style, and surrounded by scaffolding, is visible beyond the gate.

title: [Solhaven, Esplanade Gate]
description: A swan of white ora sits on the green copper gates, proclaiming them an entrance into Vornavis.  Around them stands a huge granite wall, protecting the inhabitants of the city from all intruders.  Citizens move through the gates under the careful eye of the Baronial guard standing in front of the portal.

A swan of white ora sits on the green copper gates, proclaiming them an entrance into Vornavis.  Around them stands a huge granite wall, protecting the inhabitants of the city from all intruders.  Citizens move through the gates under the careful eye of the guard standing in front of the portal.

title: [Empath Guild, Entrance]
[Empaths' Guild, Entrance]
description: A silver portcullis yawns widely between two red brick walls.  Ivy clambers haphazardly over the walls, wandering where it pleases except two places where it has been neatly trimmed back: the portcullis and a silver plaque mounted on the right hand wall.  The ground is strewn with a thick layer of crushed brick that crunches loudly underfoot, and a bright banner ripples in the brisk sea breeze as it clings to the top of a tall flagpole.  Torches attached to the flagpole brightly illuminate the area.

Torches attached to the flagpole await the onset of night.

Red brick walls choked by a lush blanket of climbing ivy give way to a yawning silver portcullis.  The thriving greenery has been cut back on one wall to reveal a lustrous silver plaque.  Where it is not home to rampant greenery and creepers with blossoms in riotous, prismatic hues, the ground is strewn with a thick layer of crushed brick that forms a spiraling trail centered upon a tall flagpole flying a bright acantha leaf banner.  Torches at the flagpole's base await the onset of night.

Red brick walls choked by a lush blanket of climbing ivy give way to a yawning silver portcullis.  The thriving greenery has been cut back on one wall to reveal a lustrous silver plaque.  Where it is not home to rampant greenery and creepers with blossoms in riotous, prismatic hues, the ground is strewn with a thick layer of crushed brick that forms a spiraling trail centered upon a tall flagpole flying a bright acantha leaf banner.  Torches at the flagpole's base brightly illuminate the area.

title: [Solhaven, Ebondrift Court]
description: A black slate walk borders the Vornavis Canal to the north, but only for a few dozen paces.  The walk ends opposite a freestanding ebonwood archway on the south side of the court, that pierces a wall of closely planted red cedars.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Avenue]
description: A scattering of terra-cotta bricks break up the black and dark grey ones that predominate along this stretch of the Avenue, augmenting the sense of harshness and gloom that the black wall of volcanic stone on the street's south side evokes.  Opposite it, close-planted red cedars form a living wall of greenery that is just as solid, but much less imposing on the street's north side.  Polished, black steel six-tentacled stars surmount the stylized piles of rubble that flank a gap in the black wall.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Avenue]
description: Red, white and black bricks alternate to form this portion of the Avenue.  Bordering the paving along the south is a white brick wall that would be waist height on most folk.  Fluted, white marble columns mark the garden's entrance, taking the place of gateposts -- both prominently hung with white shields bearing the image of a red heart transfixed by a vertical, black dagger.  On the north side of the Avenue, a small cul-de-sac reaches toward the canal, its paving bricks random in placement and color.

title: [Solhaven, Zelia's Court]
description: A low wall, constructed of various-sized stones, boards and odd pieces of refuse, surrounds a small plot of land between the end of the paved road and the canal.  A statue of a monkey, almost as tall as a halfling, squats in the middle of the lot, while a middle-aged woman dressed in drab, threadbare robes and an oversized horned helm putters tirelessly about the area, apparently unperturbed by the darkness.

A low wall, constructed of various-sized stones, boards and odd pieces of refuse, surrounds a small plot of land between the end of the paved road and the canal.  A statue of a monkey, almost as tall as a halfling, squats in the middle of the lot, while a middle-aged woman dressed in drab, threadbare robes and an oversized horned helm putters tirelessly about the area.  A half dozen or so brick-bordered patches of weeds show evidence of unskilled and even detrimental attention.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon and Shadow]
description: Set between two large gated residences, a low dark building is visible to the north, its dirtied windows and peeling coat of paint imparting a very dilapidated, abandoned look to the structure.  Faint shadows of movement shift within its dark interior, lending an ominous feeling that's supplemented by the silence pervading the area.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Gate]
description: A swan of white ora sits on the green copper gates, proclaiming them an entrance into Vornavis.  Above them looms the blue granite expanse of the West Wall, protecting the inhabitants of the city from all intruders.  Citizens move through the gates under the careful eye of the guard standing in front of the portal.

A swan of white ora sits on the green copper gates, proclaiming them an entrance into Vornavis.  Above them looms the blue granite expanse of the West Wall, protecting the inhabitants of the city from all intruders.  Citizens move through the gates in a near-constant flow.

title: [Solhaven, Scaup and Shadow]
description: The four high-walled estates filling the corners of this intersection are unremarkable, but for the constant din of deep-throated barking that rises from behind the gate of the southeast one--its owner evidently unwilling to rely upon inanimate barriers alone.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Scaup Road]
description: Tall, potted yews stand at regular intervals along both sides of the street, providing some small shade and aesthetic relief from the expanses of high stone wall on either hand.  A slate-roofed manor on the north side of the road faces its grey tiled counterpart behind its wall to the south.

title: [Solhaven, Scaup Road]
description: Demonstrating various shades of pale grey stucco, the courtyard walls along this stretch of Scaup Road are otherwise indistinguishable.  Perhaps the various greys are more attractive in daylight and are just too subtle for starlight and moonlight to do them justice.

Demonstrating the range of off-whites that stucco can attain, the courtyard walls along this stretch of Scaup Road are otherwise indistinguishable.  The north side of the road is an undisturbed expanse of first pale beige, then ivory, then dust-grey, while on the south side of the road are displayed alabaster, white with a hint of blue, followed by palest rose.

title: [Solhaven, Scaup Court]
description: Having seen better days, the courtyard walls of the villas ringing Scaup Court bear numerous cracks and even patches of missing plaster, exposing the stone and timbers beneath.  On the other hand, the iron spikes topping the walls all gleam with freshly filed edges and recent oiling.

title: [Solhaven, Limpet and Shadow]
description: Three of the four corners of the intersection are occupied by the dark stone walls of expansive estates, but the southwest corner contains tall, granite block town homes that are the hallmark of South 'Haven's aged heart.  This corner appears to be as far north as they were ever built.

Three of the four corners of the intersection are occupied by the dark stone walls of expansive estates, which stand like monuments to forgotten splendor and long-squandered wealth.  The southwest corner is dominated by the steepled roof of a dilapidated townhome, one of many littering the aged heart of South 'Haven.  A garland of vivid red roses hangs from the painted steel pole of a street lantern near the home's entrance.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Limpet Trail]
description: A solid wall of close-planted evergreens reaches well past the top of the courtyard wall of the manor nearest the corner.  In sharp contrast, the rest of the estates along here have limited themselves to a few widely separated trees growing taller than -- and well away from -- their protective walls.

title: [Solhaven, Limpet Trail]
description: The red tiled roof of a villa is visible beyond the vine-covered wall bordering the south side of Limpet Trail.  Although the vines may make the wall easily scalable, passersby give it a wide berth and test the air with hesitant sniffs as they pass.  Apparently, the vines' pale blossoms provide some form of deterrant to any who might harbor an inclination to trespass.

title: [Solhaven, Limpet Ending]
description: Bathing the lane in its soft glow, a series of polished crystal spheres creates an eye-catching embellishment to the spiked ironwork topping this section of the Vornavis wall.  Pulsing with harnessed mana, the objects suggest that their purpose is more than mere decorations for the small cul-de-sac.  Matching orbs, slightly smaller but no less vibrant and connected by corded chains, dangle over green copper gates recessed into the wall.

Polished crystal spheres add an eye-catching embellishment to the spiked ironwork topping the courtyard wall at the eastern end of the cul-de-sac.  The pulsing glow of harnessed mana suggests that their purpose is more than mere decoration.

title: [Solhaven, Short and Shadow]
description: The overhanging bulk of stone buildings reduces the sky overhead to a mere stripe, casting the street into a deeper gloom even on nights when the sky is moonlit.  Occasional street lamps cast too little light to drive back the shadows that fill South 'Haven's aged "on stone" sector after dark.  Those who need to be out at this hour hasten about their business with a constant eye on those who chance to pass near them.

The overhanging bulks of stone buildings reduce the sky to a mere star-spangled stripe.  This compounds the gloom cast by Vornavis's West Wall, which rises in a sheer stretch to the east and blocks out direct sunlight.  Beneath the haze of constant twilight, a perpetual flow of guildsmen, clerics, merchants, and servants fills the street, the sounds of their passing distorted by the unnatural tunnel.  A stone edifice with an ornate mansard roof watches the proceedings through baleful crimson-stained windows.

title: [Solhaven, Old Market Plaza]
description: In contrast to the smooth walls and estates to the north, the tall granite buildings crowding this section of South 'Haven look as though they existed long before the wooden platform that supports most of South 'Haven to the west.  Streets running to the east are barely wide enough for a single wagon, and narrow alleys separate the aged townhouses and residences fronting on the cobblestoned market plaza.

paths: Obvious paths: north, southeast, south, west, northwest
Obvious paths: north, southeast, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Eastrun and Snippet]
description: A wooden statue of a long-bearded guard leaning on a halberd stands in front of an imposing stone manor that faces Snippet Lane.  The peak of the building's roof is just visible beyond the crenellations that line its eaves, lending the place a more martial air than its neighbors.

title: [Solhaven, Snippet and Shadow]
description: Lancet arches of pale limestone above the doors and windows of a building near the intersection's northwest corner set it off from its neighbors.  One more facade in the walls of stone buildings facing the streets on all sides -- the lighter stone and graceful curves create a positive image in this canyon of gloom that is Shadow Street.

Lancet arches of pale limestone above the walls of an enclosure near the intersection's northwest corner set it off from neighboring walled estates.  While the arcs are routinely crafted of dark slate embellished with swirls of ebony, the limestone's lighter shade and graceful curves create a positive image in the canyon of gloom that is Shadow Street.  A carved thanot gate stands partially open in the face of the wall.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Short Court]
description: The sagging of overhanging upper stories has become such a problem in this small backwater that massive beams have been set in place to prevent their toppling.  The result is a cobblestoned court that resembles some kind of man-made grove of leaning, square cut trunks.  A single lantern illuminates a cracked and paintless wooden mushroom between the timbers on the north side of the court, hanging above a first floor doorway.

A cracked and paintless wooden mushroom is barely noticeable between the timbers on the north side of the court, hanging above a first floor doorway.

title: [Solhaven, Snippet Circle]
description: Flies buzz around a puddle of foul water trapped between the cobblestones at the circle's east end.  Beyond it, stacks of slate shingles surround the scaffolding that leads up to bared roof timbers and exposed sections of rotted wood on the narrow court's eastern-most residence.

title: [Solhaven, Eastrun and Shadow]
description: Large arched roofs accompanied by equally sharply-angled windows impart an almost ominous feel to the area, and the encroaching buildings do little to alleviate it.  The cobblestones lead off into different directions from here, brighter paths branching off to the west, while the distant manors huddle in the shadow of the wall of Vornavis to the east.

title: [Solhaven, Punkt Court]
description: Vornavis' West Wall looms just a few yards to the east, casting this tiny court in almost perpetual shadow.  As if seeking to mimic the Wall's height, the townhouses along the court are all three stories tall, but they have ended up leaning over the street as their timbers have sagged over the years.  In contrast, the east end of the court is occupied by a small, half-timber cottage with wooden shingles, a fieldstone chimney and a pair of blue-lensed lamps lighting its front door.

The silhouette of Vornavis's western wall looms to the east, casting much of the cultivated court in its shadow.  As if seeking to rival the wall's height, the townhouses bordering its stone bulk are all at least three stories tall.  Hoarding the sole patch of moonlight in the yard is a small but tidy manor house with a silver-inlaid pale mistwood door, its sloping roof wrought of diamond-shaped verdigris bronze shingles.

Vornavis's western wall looms to the east, casting the cultivated court in near-perpetual shadow.  As if seeking to rival the wall's height, the townhouses bordering its stone bulk are all at least three stories tall.  Hoarding the sole patch of sunlight in the yard is a small but tidy manor house with a silver-inlaid pale mistwood door, its sloping roof featuring diamond-shaped verdigris bronze shingles.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Circle North]
description: The paving stones of the Circle spread outward, covering the ground right up to the Beacon Ring's retaining wall that rises southwest of the road.  Helpfully, a low stone fence marks the boundaries of the blacksmith's yard, separating that domain from the roadway, but giving the impression that the space was fenced off long ago and the blacksmith's tenancy is a relatively recent occurrence.  The blacksmith's forge and anvil stand idle beneath the night sky.

A low stone fence marks the boundaries of the blacksmith's yard, separating her domain from the roadway, but giving the impression that the space was fenced off long ago and the blacksmith's tenancy is a relatively recent occurrence.  Working intently at her anvil, she hammers away at an andiron, carefully heating, hammering and then quenching the metal.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Circle North]
description: Townsfolk pass by on their way to or from the plaza to the east.  A large wagon stands in front of a closed workshop on the street's south side, where a pair of brawny Giantmen are loading up new barrels.

The ring of hammerfalls echoes along the cobblestoned length of the street between the cut stone residences.  In his open-fronted workshop, the barrelwright hammers an iron hoop closed -- glancing up from his work now and then to nod to a recognized passerby.  A stack of oaken barrels stand ready for pickup, while piles of curved staves line one wall of the shop.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Circle East]
description: Huddled along the ancient retaining wall that supports the Beacon Ring, numerous wooden shingled huts lean against the retaining wall and each other in varying stages of degeneration.  Here and there a fresh coat of whitewash, a peppering of unweathered shingles or a windowbox laden with bright blossoms attest to the existence of townsfolk who regard these sheds as their homes.

Huddled by a series of tiered steps leading up Beacon Ring's retaining wall, numerous wooden shingled huts lean against the retaining wall and one another in varying stages of degeneration.  Here and there a fresh coat of whitewash, a peppering of unweathered shingles, or a windowbox laden with bright blossoms attest to the existence of townsfolk who regard these sheds as their homes.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Circle South]
[Solhaven, Beacon Monument]
description: A few small houses line the street here, their quaint and plain architecture overshadowed by the large wall of the Beacon Tower looming north in the darkness.  Faint candlelight filters out from the a few of the curtained windows, though most appear to be dark.

A few small houses line the street here, their quaint and plain architecture overshadowed by the large wall of the Beacon Tower looming to the north.  Faint trails of smoke pour from the stunted little chimneys poking from underneath the building's wooden-shingled roofs, and the mild scent of cooking food drifts through the surroundings.

title: [Solhaven, Grebe Lane]
description: This far south of the Vornavis Canal, the manors and walled estates have given way to half-timbered townhouses competing for every bit of space on South 'Haven's platform.  Grebe Lane narrows visibly to the west as the structures have been built inch-by-inch further into the street.  Open sky diminishes also, the second stories of most of these buildings having been built to overhang the street rather than straight above their first floors.

title: [Solhaven, Murre Bending]
[Solhaven, Murre Court]
[Solhaven, Falcon's Nest]
description: Although of good construction and well-maintained, the half-timber townhomes lining both sides of the road are definitely a step down from the walled villas and manors to the east and north.  Huddled in a doorway, a trio of young boys chat quietly as they stoop to examine some object of vital interest.

The waves of the Sunderer's Glaive lap at the white sands surrounding Murre Court, where large piles of materials lie around the foundation of a nascent construction project.  Pastel paints stand out like ghostly lights over the dark walls that, but for a high archway, would seal the court completely off from the street.  Spades of emerald imflass protrude from tops of the walls, making the archway the only safe means of egress.

The waves of the Sunderer's Glaive lap at the white sands surrounding the multicolored tiles of the courtyard, the center of which is dominated by a red-banded alabaster spire surrounded by several levitating vessels.  Their low-pitched droning sound fills the air with a constant thrumming sound.  Pastel paints stand out like ghostly lights over the dark walls of the court.  Spades of red imflass protrude from the tops of the walls, making a carved archway the only safe means of egress.

title: [Solhaven, Baron's Bridge Road]
description: The double-layered planking of Baron's Bridge Road continues its north-south run amidst the wooden structures that are characteristic of South 'Haven.  Large, potted yews stand at the corners of the intersection, passable stand-ins for free-growing trees in this built-on-a-platform section of Solhaven.

title: [Solhaven, Tidewater Road]
description: Splitting off from Tidewater Road just short of where the solid ground ends and South 'Haven's supporting wooden platform begins, a narrow causeway extends out into the Bay.  Polished brass railings supported by grey marble dolphins run the length of the isthmus, ending at the doors of a gold-spired limestone temple that stands above the waves half a cable's length out in the Bay.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Tidewater Road]
description: A battlemented gatehouse on the west side of the road overarches the gateway to Baron's Quay.  Clearly a military fortification built to guard the mouth of the Vornavis Canal, a closed portcullis -- well-lit by lanterns -- and four guards prevent anyone not wearing Vornavis Guard livery from entering.  Tidewater Road turns inland to avoid the small backwater built in the lee of Baron's Quay.

title: [Solhaven, Tidewater Road]
description: Hanging nets, stacked lobster cages and large wicker maunds are ranged about the intersection, and small wooden stools stand amongst partially-mended nets.  In a circle of lantern light, an older fellow is busy wrapping a rusted chain around a ground rope, a pile of recently removed wooden bobbins at his feet.

paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Niima's Walk]
description: Midway between Solhaven's shoreline and Niima's temple to the west, the solidity of the balustraded causeway gives small reassurance when flanked on either hand by Charl's realm.  The worn stones of the walk and the polished rails speak of the reverence and devotion harbored by devotees of The Daughter of the Sea, and of the countless numbers who have trod this path before.

title: [Niima's Isle, Causeway]
description: Weathered flagstones stretch along the causeway, leading out from the mainland to this tiny isle set with an opal-like jewel of a temple, doors open and awaiting.  Close to the isle, sidings of openwork blued steel create an ornate lattice to keep visitors from falling into the water below.  Every few steps, a silver dolphin is set within a circle, above which sits a glaes-covered oil lamp lighting the way.

Every few steps, a silver dolphin is set within a circle, above which sits a dormant glaes-covered oil lamp, snuffed during daytime.

title: [Solhaven, No Name Road]
description: On the north side of the road, an open-walled barn gives shelter to a four-wheeled wagon and two large carts in different stages of construction.  All manner of tools have been safely locked away, but the floor is still littered with shaving, sawdust and several large smears of axle grease.

title: [Solhaven, Miller's Court]
description: Looking impressive in spite of its ungainly lines, a post-mill's vane turns slowly in the onshore breeze.  With lantern light streaming from the mill's doorways and windows, it is apparent that the miller works whenever the wind is blowing, be it day or night.

title: [Solhaven, No Name Road]
description: Low-built cottages shingled to the ground line the west side of the road, while a tall building with expansive glaes windows stands opposite them.  Dozens of oak-staved tuns are stacked along the front of the building, and polished metal surfaces distorted by the bevelled panes can be glimpsed through the windows.  For such a large building, there seems to be little activity around it.

title: [Solhaven, Tidewater Road]
description: A plank-walled warehouse faces the bay, its grey, weathered face telling a silent tale of years spent in the sun and salt sea air.  Clustered about its base are stacks of newly hewn boards and spools of cordage and cable half covered by canvas tarps.  Across the road, a gravel apron stretches from the edge of Tidewater's planking to a silver gate set in a limestone wall.

Heedless of the rushing waters beneath it, the road rises gently to form an arch over the neck of the Sunderer's Glaive.  The smell of salt is sharp in the air, its concentration great enough to peel the coat of fresh paint from the facade of a plank-walled warehouse facing the bay.  Clustered about the warehouse's base are stacks of fresh-hewn boards, accompanied by spools of cordage and cable half-covered by canvas tarps.

title: [Solhaven, Fisherman's Quay]
description: The well-traveled wooden planks of a small quay stretch out to the west into the bay's sparkling waters.  Small skiffs and other boats line the edges of the dock, each filled with fishing equipment.  Gulls circle overhead, their shrill cries echoing about the area.

title: [Solhaven, Fisherman's Quay]
description: Crates are piled high atop this end of the Quay, and the sloshing sounds of the bay against its thin supporting timbers mingle with the sounds of many travelers across its planks.  Many skiffs and other small vessels are moored further to the west toward the end of the small dock.  A small shack, its roof draped with numerous fishing nets and other odd implements of the trade, stands at the northern edge of the Quay.

title: [Solhaven, Tidewater Road]
description: A mix of boats from peapod and square-sterned skiffs to broad-beamed fishing cutters lie on either side of the road, most of them resting keel upward.  Although an aged wall encloses her workyard east of the thoroughfare, the boatwright has a portable workbench set up between Tidewater and the bay and is engrossed in repairing several sprung strakes in the hull of a small pinnace by the light of several lanterns.

title: [Sorcerer Guild, Entrance]
description: A limestone wall topped with driftwood carvings supports a silver gate.  A thick layer of crunchy yellow and white brick chips covers the area between the street and the gate.  Torches affixed to the wall on either side of the gate blaze brilliantly to light the surrounding area.

Mere feet from the dark waters that tug at every shore of the small island, a silver gate gleams from the surface of a limestone wall topped with driftwood carvings.  A thick layer of blue and black stone chips forms a path that extends from the gate to a short span of carved stone to the east that links the island to the mainland.  Torches affixed to the walls to either side of the gate blaze brilliantly, throwing the shadows back to the meeting of sand and sea.

A thick layer of blue and black stone chips forms a path that extends from the gate to a short span of carved stone to the east that links the island to the mainland.  Unlit torches affixed to the walls to either side of the gate await the onset of night.

title: [Solhaven, South Market NW]
description: Heavy-timbered stalls fill this corner of the South Market, where the Fishmarket Pier joins the market proper.  The offshore breeze thankfully carries most of the odor of the day's catch towards the bay.  Supporting stacked sacks of grains along with milled flours and amphorae of domestic and imported oils, the goods being hawked here appear to be of varieties less affected by the fishmarket's ubiquitous bouquet.  A catwalk extends to the southwest behind the Market's row of east-facing shops.

paths: Obvious paths: north, east, southeast, south, west

title: [Solhaven, South Market North]
description: A narrow storefront with a blue-shingled bay window occupies the center of the row of shops along this side of the market.  A variety of gadgets and navigational instruments fill the velvet lined display behind the window's many panes.

A storefront with a blue-shingled bay window occupies the center of the row of shops along this side of the market, a narrow lane tucked between it and the yellow-awninged shop to its east.  A variety of gadgets and navigational instruments fill the velvet lined display behind the window's many panes.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, South Market Court]
description: A trio of red tile roofed townhouses form the walls enclosing this tiny court.  Freshly whitewashed and bearing polished brass lanterns beside each door, the decor successfully counters the shadows and close confines of the little enclave.

Cradled by the salt-laden flow of the Sunderer's Glaive, the peninsula is lifted above the water by craggy banks of bone-white stone.  A trio of townhouses roofed in red tile are surrounded by mosaic walls of granite enclosing the tiny court.  Freshly whitewashed and bearing polished brass lanterns beside each door, their bright decor counters the shadows and close confines of the little enclave.

title: [Solhaven, South Market NE]
description: The eastern-most shop on the north side of the market bears a weathered thimble-and-needle sign above its polished haon door.  Rolls of cloth can be seen through the shop's windows, lined up to form aisles that fill the shop's brightly lit interior.

The eastern-most shop on the north side of the market bears a weathered thimble-and-needle sign above its polished haon door.  Rolls of cloth can be seen through the shop's windows, lined up to form aisles by fabric type and arranged in rainbows of the available hues.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, south, southwest, west
Obvious paths: northeast, east, south, southwest, west

title: [Solhaven, No Name Road]
description: Both sides of the road are filled with two-story, half-timbered buildings.  A few of the second floor windows stand open to the cool night air, but most are shuttered.  A large, wooden wedge of Mestanir Gold cheese hangs above one of the street level doors that appears to still be open at this time of night.

title: [Solhaven, Changeling Bending]
description: The flow of townsfolk along Changeling is a mix of merchants, craftsmen, servants and tradesmen, although more appear to be servants on specific errands at this time of night.  A two story building on the south side of the road at its bending is not a merchant's shop, judging by its tightly closed double-wide doors and neglected condition.  A faded sign above the door is barely readable in the lamplight.

The flow of townsfolk along Changeling is a motley mix of merchants, craftsmen, and tradesmen, although a hearty compliment of servants in muted garb skirt the moonlit streets.  A gentle grassy slope leads northward to a stand of trees, beyond which the dark waters of the Sunderer's Glaive ebb and flow over a stretch of beach.  Steepled roofs of temples, faintly aglow in the moonlight, reflect off of the Glaive's northern waters.

A gentle grassy slope leads northward to a stand of trees, beyond which the crystal waters of the Sunderer's Glaive ebb and flow over a stretch of sparkling sand.  Steepled roofs of temples, dark against the day's radiance, reflect off of the Glaive's northern waters.

title: [Solhaven, Changeling and Murre]
[Solhaven, Changeling Bending]
description: Flooding the intersection with the light streaming from its windows as well as the aroma of baked goods from its door, a modest-sized building stands on the northwest corner.  Customers enter in ones and twos and leave with cookies, muffins and small loaves in hand.

A modest-sized building stained a pale yellow with dark blue trim around the windows and powder blue awnings sits on the northwest corner, the mouthwatering aroma of fresh baked goods wafting from its open door.  A pair of pushcart vendors are loading up with golden brown loaves just outside, their efforts constantly impeded by the flow of customers in and out of the entrance.

title: [Solhaven, Murre and Grebe]
description: A large, wooden wine bottle hangs from the overhanging story of one of the town homes near the corner of Grebe Lane.  An inebriated giantman leans against the front of the building, but appears unaware of it other than as a convenient support.  The sounds of joviality and music from further west carry on the breeze.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Changeling Lane]
description: A pair of large, purple amphorae stand in bas-relief to either side of an open shop door on Changeling's north side.  The windows flanking the doorway contain ceramic and glass bottles of many shapes and sizes, but all recognizable as common containers for oils of various kinds, from olive oil to strongly scented bath oils.

title: [Solhaven, Changeling and Plover]
description: Tucked into the northeast corner where Changeling and Plover meet, a lavender-awninged shop stands with dried herbs and small barrels of peppercorns and dried peppers ranged about the entrance.  Providing the area with the mixed scents of a variety of spices, the shop appears to do a brisk business in spite of its unobtrusive location, and the customers leaving the shop appear to have consistently satisfied expressions on their faces.

Tucked into the bend where Changeling and Plover meet and bordered to the north by a broad span of beach, a large domed building stands between twin silver-twined poles of Cairnfang pine.  Occasionally, multicolored bubbles drift from its entrance, carried on husky breaths of air flavored with hints of rose, cinnamon, and other luxuriant scents.  The lapping waves of the Glaive whisper gently over the sea breeze.

title: [Solhaven, Kraken and Plover]
description: A brightly glowing lantern hangs from the lone umbrella modwir tree that stands at the center of the intersection, with four wooden benches forming a box around the large ceramic pot that contains it.  Becoming almost a plaza towards the east where the roads circling The Beacon come together, the west side of the intersection is bordered by tall town homes constructed of monir and maoral and roofed with tiles.

title: [Solhaven, Kraken Run]
description: A wooden representation of an oversized rolton steak swings gently in the night breeze beneath a shop's overhang on the south side of the Run.  The shop's windows and front door are open and a faint light filters out to the street.  Intent on their own business, only a few townsfolk are present on this section of the street, which looks like it sees more activity during the day.

Chops, steaks and strings of sausage cover the plank tables set out in front of a shop on the Run's south side.  Sides of rolton hang in a row beneath the building's overhang, forming a backdrop to the butcher's tabled wares and obscuring the storefront itself.  A sharpener wheels her stone down the street, nodding to well-known customers and calling out prices to those that show an interest.

title: [Solhaven, Kraken and Tentacle]
[Solhaven, Kraken Run]
description: Plank tables line the sides of both streets near the intersection, interspersed with barrels and bushel baskets, all of them laden with fruits and vegetables and attended by vendors claiming the greatest freshness and lowest prices.  Locally grown produce is easily distinguishable from what has arrived by ship or overland, but the variety is impressive.

title: [Solhaven, Kraken Run]
description: A long, open-sided shed stands alongside the Run's south side.  Within the shed's shelter, four rope-walks stand idle, their strands of hemp yarn running the length of the building, but pegged to sideboards above baskets of hemp fiber.

A long, open-sided shed stands along the south side of Kraken Run.  Within its shelter, craftsmen work tirelessly along rope-walks running the length of the building.  Carrying tremendous bundles of hemp, they slowly move down the walks in teams, feeding out fibers as others work to spin them into yarn.  In front of the residences on the street's north side, spools of cordage and cable are offered for sale by dark-skinned women in bright garb.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Ring]
description: Curving to the southeast and northeast as they climb, two broad roadways circle the base of an ancient shell of a tower that stands just east of here.  A small court lies to the north of this intersection, but to the south the road bends to the southeast, forming a second circle around The Beacon.  Lit by a hand lantern, a pair of youths play a game of knucklebones against the retaining wall where the roadways diverge.

paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, southeast, south, west

title: [Solhaven, Tucknotch Place]
description: Taking advantage of the solid ground surrounding the base of The Beacon to the southeast, a pristine cottage of wisteria-covered mistwood walls and bevelled window panes nestles at the north end of this cul-de-sac.  Twin gold oil lamps light the doorway, beckoning.

Taking advantage of the span of beachfront to the north of the Beacon, a pristine cottage of wisteria-covered mistwood walls and bevelled window panes nestles at the north end of this cul-de-sac.  Where the ground around it does not sparkle with diamond white sand, it is dotted with patches of bluish-green sweetgrass.  Twin gold oil lamps frame the door, beckoning.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Ring]
description: The road climbs as it circles the base of the tower.  The massive paving blocks and fitted stone walls obviously of earlier construction than any other visible structure, including Vornavis' West Wall that rises to the east.  Although small shops and dwellings cluster about the base below, none have encroached upon this roadway that leads up to the ancient structure.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Ring]
description: The circling roadways from the north and south meet here on a level with the rooftops of buildings to the north, east and south.  A steep ramp reaches upward to the west, ending at a jagged opening in the tower's base where a gateway must once have stood long ago.  Paired torches bracket the tower's entrance and light the ramp's summit.

The steep incline of the circling roadways from the north and south meet here on a level with the rooftops of the buildings directly north, east and south.  Rising to the west is a ramp that leads through the opening at the tower's base.  Noticeable repair is evident where white limestones replace the old, darker stones around a fitted steel portcullis.  Paired torches, in polished brass brackets, flank the refurbished tower entrance and illuminate the ramp's summit.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Ring]
description: The road slopes gently upwards as it hugs the wall of the ancient tower, the massive stone blocks gradually beginning to rise toward the rooftops to either side.  Two scruffy-looking boys whisper quietly to one another beneath a single torch higher up near the entrance of the tower, apparently engaged in a game of knucklebones.

The road slopes gently upwards as it hugs the wall of the ancient tower, the massive stone blocks gradually beginning to rise toward the rooftops to the south and east.  Ragged youths continually run back and forth as they chase an old barrel hoop up and down the slanted road, their laughter echoing across the sprawling roofscape of houses below.

title: [Solhaven, Beacon Circle South]
description: Glowing a dull red in the night, a row of brick kilns squat as close to The Beacon Ring's ancient retaining walls as their builders could manage.  Where the ground drops away and the windak platform takes its place, row upon row of brick molds and large mixing tubs lie between piles of sand and sacks of powdered clay.  The plank roadway that is Beacon Circle curves from the north to the southeast, dividing the brickmaker's lot from the small cottages opposite.

title: [Solhaven, South Market East]
description: Notable amidst the array of bright awnings and wide-windowed storefronts, the largest business on the eastern edge of the market is a blue-stained modwir building with only a few narrow windows set high in the wall.  An assortment of ceramic vases, jugs and pots are lined up along the wall under the watchful eye of a rather petulant-looking apprentice.

title: [Solhaven, South Market]
description: Crowded with booths, merchants hawking their wares and customers chatting and arguing under the glaes-lensed street lamps, the market is filled with an almost frantic air.  Even with the thinning of the crowds that nightfall brings, the market is still a noisy place.

title: [Solhaven, South Market SE]
description: Puffin Street, leading out of the market to the east, is torn up and impassable.  Piles of rotted planks alongside stacks of new ones lie beside the gaping hole that was once a roadway.  Dim light bathes the ground infront of the candle-laddened windows of a haon and fel shop.

Despite the disruption, a shop of alternating haon and fel planks, and windows filled with brightly colored and sculpted candles, has a regular stream of customers coming and going from its open doorway.

title: [Solhaven, South Market South]
description: Perched on the corner where Salters' Road enters the market from the south is a maoral-sided store with shallow steps leading up to its carved maoral door.  Light from the shop shines through the myriad of small crystal bottles resting on narrow shelves close behind the windows, setting each aglow with a different shade of red, yellow, green, blue or violet.

paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Solhaven, South Market SW]
description: Looking more like an oversized stall than a shop, the wooden wall panels of the western-most business have been swung open to allow customers to more easily enter and examine the wide variety of items for sale.  A silver-painted breastplate hangs from the second story of the storefront.  The bustle of the South Market continues to the west along a substantial pier, and a catwalk extends to the northwest behind the Market's row of east-facing shops.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, west

title: [Solhaven, South Market West]
description: A row of half a dozen colorfully painted shops form the western end of the South Market.  Although brightly lit by the Market's oil lamps, the insides of the shops are dark.  The doorways are boarded over and through the windows the partially plastered walls can be seen.

A row of half a dozen colorfully painted shops form the western end of the South Market.  Unfortunately, the doorways are boarded over and the windows are dark, the insides clearly being replastered and refinished.

title: [Solhaven, Fishmarket Pier]
description: A folded canvas umbrella leans against the side of this small seafood stand.  A large wooden table supports several ice trays, filled with a variety of specialty seafood.
A colorful canvas umbrella provides shade for a gaily painted seafood stand.  A large wooden table supports several ice trays, filled with a variety of specialty seafood.

title: [Solhaven, Fishmarket Pier]
description: A group of sailors wanders past, holding steaming fishcakes that they consume as they walk.  A small wooden shack rests on the quay, and through the open door comes the strong odor of frying fish.

title: [Dilapidated Shack]
description: A dilapidated shack sits proudly on the edge of the pier in all its gaudy splendor, having been cobbled together from mud, seashells, and the remains of abandoned shipping crates.  Rusted cages that house tiny paper lobsters hang precariously from chaotically draped old fishing nets that serve as a makeshift canopy.  Dangling from the crooked doorway, uneven strands of beads glint metallic red in the pale moonlight.

title: [Solhaven, Fishmarket Pier]
description: The smell of fresh fish fills the air on the quay.  A vendor's stand, comprised of barrels and casks filled with iced shellfish, is crammed into a small space between two other hawkers.  Moonlight gleams dully from the ice in the barrels.

The stench of fresh fish fills the air of the quay, which overlooks the jagged breakwater known as The Fang, its shape sullen and gnarled against the graceful expanse of the bay and its fathomless waters. title: [Solhaven, Salters' Road]

description: With a single gateway at the corner of Salters' Road and Trade Row, a plank walled workyard fills the northeast corner of the intersection.  A tin-roofed warehouse rises above the wall at the back of the yard.

Bordered to the west by the crushing surf of Solhaven Bay, the intersection of Salters' Road and Trade Row is an expansive street lined with even cobbles.  A plank-walled workyard fills the northeast corner of the intersection, festooned with garlands of rose and lily that do little to mask the briny smell cloaking it.  A tin-roofed warehouse rises above the wall at the back of the yard.

title: [Solhaven, South Market Pier]
[Solhaven, South Market Isle]
description: A row of compact shops line the pier's north side, extending the South Market out over the Bay.  Lit by a series of torches along the pier, a shop with an assortment of helms, hats and hoods is hard not to notice.

Solhaven's South Market Pier stretches to the west, guarded by shops fighting for space on an island severed from Solhaven proper by several feet of water.  Among the finest of the stores is a squat millinery situated near the meeting of the pier's planks and the paved stones of the isle.  Lit by a series of torches along the pier, the shop's assortment of helms, hats, and hoods displayed through its murky windows is difficult not to notice.  A stone bridge to the east joins the island with the South Market.

A stone bridge joins the island with the South Market.

title: [Solhaven, South Market Pier]
description: Festooned with brightly colored banners, pennants and flags, a weathered modwir shed, with very little else attractive about it, still manages to look appealing.  Further west, the row of shops becomes more sparse and the passersby appear to be more interested in simply taking in the Bay beneath the night sky than haggling over goods.

title: [Warehouse, First Floor]
description: Several smashed crates litter the floor here, apparently broken after having fallen a great distance from the top of one of the stacks.  The contents of the broken containers have long been removed, but the refuse remains.  The boxes and crates part to allow passage to the west and south from here.

title: [Solhaven, Trade Row]
description: An empty wagon stands outside a closed up warehouse on the Row's south side.  A small stack of tar-stained barrels stand outside the door, ready for loading or were perhaps unloaded after the warehouse was closed.

A crew of bare chested Giantmen roll tar-stained barrels out of a warehouse on the Row's south side, up a plank and into the back of a wagon.  Within the shaded interior of the low building, rows of barrels and hogsheads are stacked to the rafters, and the crew's leader discusses payment with the overseer of the warehouse.

title: [Solhaven, Trade Row]
description: A sawmill stands north of the road, the muted buzz of a mechanically-driven saw forming a constant backdrop to the periodical clatter of freshly-sawn planks being handled and stacked.  Through the workyard gate, the open interior of the mill can be seen by the light of well-placed lanterns, an old, dun mule plodding in an endless circle around the center pole and driving the large wooden gears that turn on the floors above.

title: [Solhaven, Salters' Road]
description: The high gabled roof and inmistakable odor would mark the stable east of the intersection as the South 'Haven Mews, even if the sign above the open doorway did not.  Dark stains and the crescent scoring from shod hooves have marred the surface of Salters' Road, and whinnying and neighs can be heard from the stable's dark interior.  Salters' Road ends just to the south, where the wooden platform ends and the close-built structures of a past era close in, leaving only an alleyway to the south.

title: [Solhaven, Murre Place]
description: Whether by chance or by design, this end of the street is filled with drinking revellers and a trio of bards engaged in an improptu performance.  A beer vendor has parked his cart to partially block the court from the intersection to the east, but whether he was the instigator of this little celebration or just an opportunist is unclear.

title: [Solhaven, Limpet Trail]
description: The courtyard walls along this section of the street are remarkably pale beneath the night sky, and the bladed ornamentations along their tops reflect whatever light chances to touch them.  Clearly the owners of these estates are proud enough of their wealth that they want passersby to know it.

title: [Solhaven, Limpet Bending]
description: The villa occupying the corner is surrounded by a lower wall than any of the other estates along this street, the entire second story of the manorhouse visible above the stuccoed wall.  Three small balconies grace the manor's west wall, and multi-paned doors stand open to the cool night breeze.

title: [Solhaven, Scaup and Limpet]
description: Built of-a-piece, a half-timber manor house peers over its protective half-timber wall at the end of Scaup Lane.  Clearly not the most secure, with the multiple handholds and footholds that the protruding timbers provide, the manor's gate, doors and shutters -- all with obvious locks -- appear to be ironbound oak by way of compensation.

title: [Solhaven, Scaup Road]
description: High, stuccoed walls line either side of the brick paved street, providing privacy and security to the lush gardens and impressive manors that can be glimpsed beyond the bars of the finely wrought gates.  Here and there, precisely-trimmed conifers reach above the confining walls or adorn spacious balconies.

title: [Solhaven, Scaup Road]
description: Polished iron spikes and razor-toothed ornamentations top the walls of the manors to either hand, attesting to the owners' unwillingness to entertain uninvited guests.  Steel-barred gates at the main entrances and servants' side doors do little to soften the area's stark character.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Avenue]
description: A high, red brick wall set with black mortar fills the lot on the avenue's south side, where Limpet Trail joins from the southeast.  Standing at the oblique corner, a pair of gateposts face the intersection, the gateway unobstructed by a gate of any kind.  Lit by torches set beneath them, black scimitars carved into the capitals of the gateposts proclaim the holding's owner.  On the north side of the avenue, the iron fence surrounding Eorgina's temple ends at the west wall of Andelas' temple.

On the north side of the avenue, the iron fence surrounding Eorgina's temple ends at the west wall of Andelas' temple.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Avenue]
description: Wide, shallow steps of polished black stone lead upward from the north side of the avenue, piercing the sandstone wall that runs west to the edge of Eorgina's compound.  The steps end at a pair of felwood doors, each bearing a crimson cat's head carved into its center.  Poised to each side of the steps is a tall, gold leaf covered feline statue, their amber metal gleaming in the starlight.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Avenue]
description: The paving changes from the red brick and black basalt blocks prevalent in front of Andelas' temple to the west to a mix of yellow brick and grey granite blocks in front of the matching wall now bordering the street's north side.  A birchwood gate bearing an enamelled grey shield with a glowing, slit-pupilled sunstone eye set in its center opens in the center of the wall.  A narrow alley opens to the north between Andelas' sandstone wall and the wall of Fash'lo'nae's compound.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Avenue]
description: This section of the avenue is paved with alternating red granite blocks and green-glazed bricks, and a low, red granite wall borders the street's south side.  Rising to twice the wall's height, twin gateposts bear green enamelled wisps of smoke, and a garden filled with pale blossoms and neatly-trimmed shrubs is visible beyond them.

title: [Solhaven, Lornon Avenue]
description: An overbearing triple-turreted fane rises up on the north side of the avenue and sits well back from the road on a small hillock, giving it a bit of elevation above the other buildings along this passage.  Surrounded by a tall ironwork fence, an opening at the foot of a path leads up to a darkened entry.  A massive crimson glaes arch of flames illuminates the area with its wavering, lurid glow.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Esplanade]
description: Moonlight softly illuminates the crowded flowerbeds forming the northern border of the avenue.  Saffron snapdragon compete with bright yellow daffodils and golden sunflowers, forming a wall of living color and greenery.  A pair of golden sandstone pegasi kneel to either side of a brick walkway that leads north beyond the flowerbeds.  Tall boxwood hedges line the south side of the esplanade, parted by a broad tiled path leading south.

[Solhaven, Zoo Approach]
description: Colorful rounded tiles curve through this grassy park in a serpentine fashion, the path guarded on both sides by a variety of large hedge animals.  Several children scurry along the path, most of them eagerly heading toward the Solindago Anox zoo grounds.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Esplanade]
description: A towering pair of rose quartz swans kiss, their heads and necks forming a heart-shaped archway leading into a temple on the north side of the esplanade.  To the east and west of the swans, a thick hedge of rose bushes bearing yellow, white, pink, and deep red roses forms a striking, if impenetrable, wall.  Small rose quartz blocks replace the terra cotta bricks in this part of the avenue.

title: [Solhaven, Liabo Esplanade]
description: The color of paving shifts to a pale gold as the terra cotta bricks are replaced by small blocks of white granite.  South of the avenue the view is blocked by a high, white granite wall, although a stonework structure is just visible beyond it.  A large wooden gate, painted with a golden crown atop a circle of white, fills the gateway in the center of the wall.  A sign hangs below the symbol.
