North of the avenue, the view is obscured by a high stone wall, although a towering golden fane rises into the skyline beyond it.  Twin columns of shining white stone split the wall, supporting an arc carved with a crown in detailed bas-relief.  Floral scents sugar the air, emanating from a gold-flecked white marble building across the way.

The color of paving stones shifts to pale gold as terra cotta bricks segue gently into small blocks of white granite.  North of the avenue, the view is obscured by a high stone wall, although a towering golden fane rises into the skyline beyond it.  Twin  of shining white stone split the wall, supporting an arc carved with a crown in detailed bas-relief.  Floral scents sugar the air, emanating from a gold-flecked white marble building across the way.

title: [Solindago Anox, Main Gates]
description: Flanking the opening in a tall, black, wrought iron fence that surrounds the perimeter of the park are massive twin griffin statues, placed to face each other.  The creatures have reared up on their hind legs, one clawed hand reaching out so that they touch talons high overhead.  Emblazoned upon the gates in gleaming golden plating are the letters "S" and "A."

title: [Solhaven, North Market Pier]
description: Wider than Bayside Road, the rock-solid pilings and smooth worn planks of the pier extend the marketplace out over the water.

title: [Solhaven, North Market Pier]
description: The aroma of cooking seafood mingles with the raw odors of the sea carried by the onshore breeze.  To the west the pier widens to support a low, net-shrouded building.  Little more than a stone's throw to the northeast, the tarred timbers of the Market Bridge parallel the pier's stretch to Bayside Road.  Tight against the southern edge of the pier, an old shed appears to have been refurbished, and a wooden sign bearing a sea chest picture hangs above the door.

title: [Solhaven, North Market Pier]
description: A squat building, hung about with old fishing nets fills the pier, with only a narrow gallery running south along its shoreward side and west along its northern side.  Mouth-watering aromas of cooking seafood waft through an arched doorway formed from the bleached jawbone of a mammoth sea troll.

title: [Market Bridge]
description: This section of bridge descends to the southeast to a stone pier, where it is anchored firmly in place at the edge of Solhaven.  To the northwest, the bridge rises above the Cairnfang delta and continues down into Marshtown.  The bridge is well maintained and very clean on this slope.

title: [Market Bridge]
description: Small board-and-plank shops wearing the odious whitewash of perching gulls line either side of the bridge.  Relying on the bridge's traffic for business, and taking advantage of the gentle incline from here to the peak of the bridge, the shops look to be an odd mix that might appeal to Marshtowner and 'Havener alike.  You notice a small, weathered cask hangs above the doorway of one of the shops.

title: [Masked Hills, Eroded Spires]
description: For a plateau the surface here is incredibly uneven.  Rocks jut into the air at wild angles, forcing you to pick your way carefully between them.  Most of the gaps and crevices have been packed with dried grass and pebbles by the constant wind.

title: [Masked Hills, Eroded Spires]
description: The wind makes an unearthly keening sound as it rushes past the stony spires.  The howling rises and fades at strange intervals, sometimes catching you off-guard.  A nearby rock is marred by a series of four deep gouges, their origin unclear.

title: [Masked Hills, Eroded Spires]
description: Looking at the western spire from this angle, you notice how much it resembles a stooped old man raising his staff to the heavens.  A whirlwind of dust forms at the hem of his robe, then soundlessly dissipates.

title: [Masked Hills, Eroded Spires]
description: In the lee of the eastern spire is a cozy niche.  Even this partial shelter from the neverending wind comes as a great relief.  You are not the first to pause here, however, and those who preceded you have carved their marks upon the ancient stone.

title: [Masked Hills, Eroded Spires]
description: Starting out as a thin line, a vein of nearly translucent pale pink quartz travels down a rocky outcropping, widens as it skates over the cracked and uneven ground, then finally disappears under a pair of large boulders.  Who knows what valuable untapped minerals might be concealed deep within this mountain?

title: [Masked Hills, Eroded Spires]
description: Fanned out across the face of a low shelf is an exquisite series of manganese dendrites.  Pale yellow rock makes up most of this part of the plateau, though in the southwest corner some greenish granite makes an appearance.

title: [Masked Hills, Eroded Spires]
description: Two wind-swept rock towers rise from the ground to the east.  The trail skirts their bases in one direction, and in the other strikes out along a narrow ridge to the northwest.  From your perch upon this plateau you are able to look out across the foothills to the south, so green in comparison to this stony desolation.

title: [Masked Hills, Hairline Ridge]
description: The ground drops away to either side of this razor-sharp ridge, leaving you with the sensation of being balanced on a tightrope.  Frequent rockslides have eaten away at the trail, giving it a scalloped edge right at the bend.

title: [Masked Hills, Hairline Ridge]
description: The plates of rock which form this section of the trail are cracked and tumbled, victims of some past upheaval.  Two paths lead down the steep slope to the west, and neither one looks easy.
paths: Obvious paths: north, south, southwest, west

title: [Gorget Trails, Overhang]
description: The sharp overhang up above makes this cliff face impossible to scale.  A greasewood shrub has carved out a small niche, taking advantage of the slight protection offered by the jutting rock.

title: [Gorget Trails, Overhang]
description: The air is cooler here in the shade of the protruding rock overhead.  Sheltered from the elements, two fragile rock paintings, one small and one large, are still visible despite the harsh conditions.  A flat-topped boulder pushed up against the cliff would be a comfortable place to rest if the pile of small rodent bones next to it didn't remind you of the everpresent dangers of this region.

title: [Gorget Trails, Overhang]
description: The cliff face leans out over the path, as though peering down at the forest far below.  Where the trail meets the rock wall, there are several small holes, probably home to some sort of burrowing mouse.

title: [Gorget Trails, Ledge]
description: A portion of this very shallow ledge has been washed away by a steady trickle of water running down the face of the cliff.  Flecks of smoky mica sparkle in shafts of silvery moonlight and a stink beetle parades slowly along the edge of the path.

A portion of this very shallow ledge has been washed away by a steady trickle of water running down the face of the cliff.  Flecks of smoky mica sparkle in the sun, and a stink beetle parades slowly along the edge of the path.

title: [Gorget Trails, Ledge]
description: Little more than a foot across, this path has been cut directly into the cliff and allows no room for error.  Forced into proximity with the rocky embankment, you notice an extended trail of ants, each carrying a tiny crumb of something in a westward direction.

title: [Gorget Trails, Fissure]
description: To the north the trail disappears into a dark gap between the weathered rock walls.  A tattered bird's nest sits atop a small shelf jutting out from the cliff face.  Though long abandoned, several pale grey feathers still flutter among the interwoven twigs and dried grass.

title: [Gorget Trails, Fissure]
description: Almost no moonlight reaches the bottom of this elbow-bend crevasse, and the rocks are quite cold to the touch.  A broad layer of pink rock travels sinuously along one wall, describing past deformations.  Wedged into the fissure high overhead is a massive boulder, arrested in its fall by the narrowing canyon.

Almost no light reaches the bottom of this elbow-bend crevasse, and the rocks are quite cold to the touch.  A broad layer of pink rock travels sinuously along one wall, describing past deformations.  Wedged into the fissure high overhead is a massive boulder, arrested in its fall by the narrowing canyon.

title: [Gorget Trails, Fissure]
description: Two rock walls converge here, with only a narrow fissure allowing passage to the west.  A scrawny blue oak stands to one side like a gatekeeper, branches outstretched to collect a toll.

title: [Gorget Trails, East Cliff Face]
description: The cliff here is composed of thin layers of blue and grey stone tilted sharply downward.  Ruddy iron oxide stains dapple the surface and darken a wide vertical fracture.  Broken shards of stone litter the base of the cliff, having tumbled from the treacherous rock faces.

title: [Gorget Trails, East Switchback]
description: From this overlook you can see all the way across the valley below, where darker lines of vegetation trace the paths of streams and the meadows are scraps of pale yellow-green.  Tiny acorn caps pepper the trail, material evidence of the scrub oaks which emerge improbably from a narrow shelf high above your head.

title: [Moonglae Inn, Cloister]
description: A covered walkway paved with dark blue slate is brightly lit by an eahnor oil lamp crafted in the shape of a crescent moon.  A row of tall, grey marble pillars separates the walkway from the skylit atrium beyond.  A large oil painting hangs on the dark greystone wall.

title: [Moonglae Inn, Cloister]
description: A covered walkway paved with dark blue slate is brightly lit by an eahnor oil lamp crafted in the shape of a crescent moon.  A row of tall, grey marble pillars separates the walkway from the skylit atrium beyond.  A white marble statue stands against the dark greystone wall.

title: [Moonglae Inn, Cloister]
description: A covered walkway paved with dark blue slate is brightly lit by an eahnor oil lamp crafted in the shape of a crescent moon.  A row of tall, grey marble pillars separates the walkway from the skylit atrium beyond.  A hemispherical ceramic planter hangs on the dark greystone wall.

title: [Moonglae Inn, Cloister]
description: A covered walkway paved with dark blue slate is brightly lit by an eahnor oil lamp crafted in the shape of a crescent moon.  A row of tall, grey marble pillars separates the walkway from the skylit atrium beyond.  An enormous glass tank has been set into the dark greystone wall.

title: [Moonglae Inn, Cloister]
description: A covered walkway paved with dark blue slate is brightly lit by an eahnor oil lamp crafted in the shape of a crescent moon.  A row of tall, grey marble pillars separates the walkway from the skylit atrium beyond.  A heavily embroidered tapestry covers the dark greystone wall.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Mossy Trail]
description: The dark, narrow, sloping trail wends its way through the tall coniferous forest.  Moss-covered stones line the trail.  Through the trees a narrow creek can be glimpsed at the bottom of the valley.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Mossy Trail]
description: The trail widens here as it proceeds over a large, uneven slab of stone.  Thick patches of brownish-red lichen grow here and there.  The bright moonlight casts a bluish glow over the stone, which retains some of the heat of the day.  From the north comes the sound of the creek.

The trail widens here as it proceeds over a large, uneven slab of stone.  Thick patches of brownish-red lichen grow here and there.  The bright sunlight glints on the exposed portions of the stone and makes it warm under foot.  From the north comes the sound of the creek.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Creek Trail]
description: The stone-filled creek rushes by, making a pleasant chuckling sound.  The path is barely illuminated by the moonlight filtering through the tall tanik trees.  Tanik needles line the path.
The stone-filled creek rushes by, making a pleasant chuckling sound.  The path is made cool by the tall tanik trees which filter the sunlight.  Tanik needles line the path.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Creek Trail]
description: The creek eddies here, forming a small pool.  The muddy creek bank reveals the footprints of various woodland creatures.  The massive tanik trees tower overhead, blocking much of the light.  To the south is a stubby boulder.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Stubby Boulder]
description: Although surrounded by giant taniks and pines the boulder give you the chance to look up and see the sky.  The stone is flecked with tiny facets of mica which reflect the moonlight, making it sparkle under your feet.  One side of the boulder is worn smooth from the many hands and feet which have clambered up and down its surface.

Although surrounded by giant taniks and pines the boulder give you the chance to look up and see the sky.  The stone is flecked with tiny facets of mica which reflect the sunlight, making it sparkle under your feet.  One side of the boulder is worn smooth from the many hands and feet which have clambered up and down its surface.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Stubby Boulder]
description: From the top of the boulder you can see much of Teorainn Valley.  The narrow creek widens as if flows east into a small lake.  Directly across the creek the terrain rises sharply among rocky escarpments.  Across the lake to the northeast a scattering of old wooden structures stand beside a field of tall yellow flowers.  To the south is a path that slopes downward through the woods.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Wooded Path]
description: A soft carpet of fallen tanik needles pads the sloping, circuitous path.  Tall taniks grow along each side.  Smaller scrub bushes and patches of briar are crowded among the tanik trunks.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Wooded Path]
description: The path follows the gently rolling contours of the valley floor.  Through the curtain of taniks the creek can occasionally be glimpsed.  Small boulders, covered in rust-colored lichens, are strewn among the trees.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Creek Trail]
description: The path dips down along the steep bank of the burbling creek.  A small, grassy hummock is dotted with tiny-petaled flowers.  A steep footpath leads up along the face of a wall of rock.  The sound of the water rushing along the stone-filled creek is almost musical.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Brambles]
description: The narrow footpath winds its tortuous way through wickedly sharp brambles which grow thickly on the rock.  The uneven surface of the rock is covered with patches of moss, making the footing unreliable.
paths: Obvious paths: east, south, southwest, down

title: [Teorainn Valley, Brambles]
description: The brambles are so tall and wild they almost form a tunnel.  The narrow aperture between the brambles overhead permits just enough moonlight to illuminate the stony path.  A passing breeze fails to penetrate to the path but makes the long, sharp spikes of the brambles rustle slightly.

The brambles are so tall and wild they almost form a tunnel.  The narrow aperture between the brambles overhead permits just enough sunlight to illuminate the stony path.  A passing breeze fails to penetrate to the path but makes the long, sharp spikes of the brambles rustle slightly.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Brambles]
description: The thick mass of brambles stands tall along both sides of the stony path.  The air is still and fusty.  Motes of dust hang in the air, illuminated by the moonlight.  The long, sharp spikes of the brambles loom menacingly.

The thick mass of brambles stands tall along both sides of the stony path.  The air is still and fusty.  Motes of dust hang in the air, illuminated by the sunlight.  The long, sharp spikes of the brambles loom menacingly.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Lake Tanai]
description: The trail bends around a stubby promontory which gives a wide view of the lake.  Moonlight sparkles off the water like pearls.  A gentle breeze caresses your cheek.  On the far bank of the lake, barely visible in the moonlight, is a small group of buildings standing beside a field of sunflowers.

The trail bends around a stubby promontory which gives a wide view of the lake.  Sunlight sparkles off the water like diamonds.  A gentle breeze caresses your cheek.  On the far bank of the lake, barely visible against the glare of the sun, is a small group of buildings standing beside a field of sunflowers.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Creek Trail]
description: The gently rolling trail follows the quick-flowing creek.  From this vantage you can see the creek gradually begin to widen into a narrow lake which stretches off to the east.  A faint scent of blackberries wafts from a thick mass of brambles to the south.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Brambles]
description: The footpath narrows and cuts back sharply in this small, bramble-filled hollow.  Scattered among the spiky brambles are ragged bits of cloth and tufts of fur, the evidence of people and creatures who have been less careful passing by.  A rather putrid stench suggests that some small, unfortunate creature has crawled under the brambles and died.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Creek Trail]
description: This small copse of yew trees is completely encircled by the tall tanik forest.  The swiftly-flowing creek is quite narrow here, rushing loudly among the stones.  A series of flat riverstones seem to have been deliberately placed in the creek to offer a way for the nimble adventurer to cross.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Creek Trail]
description: A narrow grassy trail passes between the swift creek to the south and the steep rock face to the north.  A pair of small thanot shrubs flank the first of a series of flat riverstones which cross the creek.  The sound of the swiftly flowing water is echoed by the rock face so that you are surrounded by the chuckling of the creek.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Creek Trail]
description: The narrow grassy trail follows the edge of the creek.  A low wall of striated rock on the northern side of the trail gradually becomes taller and steeper to the west.  Tanik trees and thanot shrubs line the trail, giving the area a pleasantly sharp odor.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Creek Trail]
description: The creek slows and widens, forming a narrow lake stretching off to the east.  The constant, gentle breeze stirs small whitecaps which make the lake seem to sparkle in the moonlight.  In the distance to the northeast, through the thin growth of tanik trees, you see a rather dilapidated house and shed standing in a field of sunflowers.  The sharp smell of tanik sap pervades the area.

The creek slows and widens, forming a narrow lake stretching off to the east.  The constant, gentle breeze stirs small whitecaps which make the lake seem to sparkle in the sunlight.  In the distance to the northeast, through the thin growth of tanik trees, you see a rather dilapidated house and shed standing in a field of sunflowers.  The sharp smell of tanik sap pervades the area.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Small Clearing]
description: Field grass grows thick in the clearing, bluish-green in the moonlight.  The terrain climbs steeply to the north, where a stand of yew trees grows.  The tanik trees to the south spread thinly around the clearing.  To the east is a ruined ornamental gate.

Field grass grows thick in the clearing, bright green in the sunlight.  The terrain climbs steeply to the north, where a stand of yew trees grows.  The tanik trees to the south spread thinly around the clearing.  To the east is a ruined ornamental gate.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Creek Trail]
description: The trail, barely wide enough for two people to walk abreast, wends its way between the creek and an enormous, kidney-shaped boulder.  Weeds and thistles grow along the bottom of the rock face.  A small rivulet of water trickles down the side of the boulder, joining the quick-flowing creek.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Creek Trail]
description: The trail slopes steeply, passing among a small copse of bayberry shrubs.  The scent of bayberry fills the area.  Along the south side of the trail the creek splashes musically over rounded stones.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ledge]
description: The trail follows a narrow rock ledge.  A wall of red-veined grey stone rises on the north.  To the south, some distance below, you can see the creek.  Small clumps of gorse grow on both sides of the trail.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ledge]
description: A small rivulet of brownish water trickles down the red-veined rock face.  Centuries of erosion have pockmarked the stone, making it possible to scrabble up.  The thin trickle of water worms its way over the edge of the ledge.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Rock Lip]
description: Stunted gorse bushes dot this knobby projection of rock and thin soil.  A muddy puddle, fed by a trickle of brown water from above, overflows and dribbles down the rock face.  A bulwark of red-veined grey stone sweeps around the rock lip, providing shelter from the wind.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Wide Ledge]
description: A thin layer of soil supports a few gorse bushes and a scrawny bayberry shrub.  A tiny trickle of reddish-brown water flows out of a crack in the grey stone.  At the back of the ledge, set beneath an overhang of stone, are the remnants of an old nest.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Exposed Ridge]
description: A small, dead tanik tree juts out from the ridge at a precarious angle, its scrawny roots exposed.  The wind blows in violent gusts, as if determined not to let anything stand on the ridge.  Much of Teorainn Dale and Valley can be seen from this vantage.  A rocky scrabble leads up.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Sloping Path]
description: The stony path slopes at an awkward angle, making your footing uncertain.  A narrow track leads up toward a stand of young yew trees.  Through the trees to the southeast you can see a very large boulder.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Boulder]
description: The huge, blunt stone juts up from the ground like a massive fist.  Flakes of mica catch and reflect the moonlight, making the hulking dark boulder sparkle.  Thorny scrub bushes surround the boulder.  A low, dark path leads north, dipping down under a jagged overhang of rock.

The huge, blunt stone juts up from the ground like a massive fist.  Flakes of mica catch and reflect the sunlight, making the hulking dark boulder sparkle.  Thorny scrub bushes surround the boulder.  A low, dark path leads north, dipping down under a jagged overhang of rock.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Boulder]
description: It's dark, damp and cool beneath the overhang of the boulder.  The air is still and ripe with the doughy smell of mold.  Cobwebs clutter the deepest recesses of the overhang.  An indentation in the soil suggests some beast or person has curled up here and slept.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Boulder]
description: The boulder looms overhead, casting you in a moonshadow.  Mosses and the spores of molds grows thick on the cool, dark stone.  A westward path dips down beneath a jagged overhang.
The boulder looms overhead, casting you in a shadow.  Mosses and the spores of molds grows thick on the cool, dark stone.  A westward path dips down beneath a jagged overhang.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Boulder]
description: A huge, dark boulder juts aggressively from the ground like an enormous stone fist.  A dense thicket of thorny scrub brush surrounds the massive rock.  A few small bird nests hang precariously from tiny crannies in the rock face.  A stand of young yew trees lies to the northeast.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Old Campsite]
description: Gnarled and stunted tanik trees are interspersed with scrubby thanot shrubs.  In the shelter of a pair of taniks are the remains of an old campfire--a circle of smoke-blackened stones surrounding a mound of ash and burnt wood.  A stand of yew trees lies off to the east.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Yew Wood]
description: The trail winds lazily through this pleasant copse of yew trees.  Tiny wildflowers, their petals tightly closed, are visible in the moonlight.  Although hidden by the underbrush a mild, nut-like scent informs you that mushrooms grow nearby.

The trail winds lazily through this pleasant copse of yew trees.  Tiny wildflowers turn their faces to the sun.  Although hidden by the underbrush a mild, nut-like scent informs you that mushrooms grow nearby.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Yew Wood]
description: A tall, rocky escarpment rises above you to the north.  The striated rock looks almost as if it had been gouged out by claws.  Yew trees and thanot grow thickly along the path.  Some of the trees lean against each other, the victims of some bygone storm.  One has toppled down the side of the hill.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Yew Wood]
description: The trail inclines steeply as it wends its way through this dense stand of young yew trees.  Sharp, jagged stones jut up through the fern-thick undergrowth.  Far below you is the sound of the rushing creek.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Yew Wood]
description: The ground rises steeply to the north.  The trail dips beneath the trunk of a large, dead yew tree which has toppled from above.  The inverted tree looks odd with its branches against the soil and its root ball in the air.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Yew Wood]
description: The trail follows the line of a long, oval declivity.  Mature yew trees grow along the rim.  Within the basin of the declivity the trees are much younger.  Scattered throughout the area are chunks of dark stone.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Yew Wood]
description: The ground slopes down radically to the east.  From this tall vantage point you can see the narrow lake and an old farmstead in a marshy plain.  The yew wood continues to the west.  The trail wends up to a ridge.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Yew Wood]
description: Young yew trees grow thickly along the paths.  Large shards of dark stone lie scattered among the ferns.  Through the trees to the southwest you catch a glimpse of a very large boulder.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: The trail follows the curve of a narrow ridge.  Scraggly shrubs and stunted sumacs line the stony trail.  A breeze from the northwest carries a mountain chill and the scent of juniper.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: The rocky trail rises and falls with the contours of the ridge.  To the east the original trail has collapsed into a narrow rockfall lined with dead and dying sumacs.  A new trail bends to the northeast around the rockfall.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: The ground is uneven on this recently cut section of trail.  To the south the old trail has collapsed, pulling down the tall sumacs and giving you a narrow view of the valley below.  The occasional clatter of stone skittering down the rockfall is evidence the ridge is still shifting.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: A rockfall to the west has destroyed the old trail.  A new trail, carved through the thick sumacs lining the ridge, winds around the loose, collapsing stones.  The wind causes the sumac leaves to rattle against each other, making a sound like the tapping of old bones.  A copse of birch trees stands to the northeast.  The ridge trail continues down.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Birch Copse]
description: The chalky white bark of the birch trees contrasts pleasantly with the bright green of their leaves.  In places the papery bark has separated into curling strips, revealing an orangish inner bark.  Moonlight dapples the grassy path.

The chalky white bark of the birch trees contrasts pleasantly with the bright green of their leaves.  In places the papery bark has separated into curling strips, revealing an orangish inner bark.  Sunlight dapples the grassy path.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Birch Copse]
description: The path curves through the pale, tranquil birch trees.  Wood sage and pink fireweed dot the undergrowth.  The scent of sage fills the air.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Birch Copse]
description: The sound of distant birdsong is carried by the cool breeze.  The white-barked birches sway gently.  The moon-dappled path rises and falls with the rolling terrain.
The sound of distant birdsong is carried by the cool breeze.  The white-barked birches sway gently.  The sun-dappled path rises and falls with the rolling terrain.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Birch Copse]
description: The path meanders through the dignified old birches.  Claw marks gouge the bark of one large tree.  Wood sage and pink fireweed grow thickly between the trees.  The air is redolent with the scent of wild sage.  Below, down a stony path, can be seen the distinctive blue-green of young tanik trees.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Juniper Point]
description: A lone tanik tree, stunted and gnarled by age and weather, stands in stark contrast to the cloud-dotted moonlit sky.  The tree is surrounded by a patch of low blue-green juniper shrubs.  The chilly breeze makes the junipers rustle.  An ancient wooden shield has been jammed into the prickly shrubs.

A lone tanik tree, stunted and gnarled by age and weather, stands in stark contrast to the cloud-dotted azure sky.  The tree is surrounded by a patch of low blue-green juniper shrubs.  The chilly breeze makes the junipers rustle.  An ancient wooden shield has been jammed into the prickly shrubs.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: A few small tufts of grey fur have been caught on the spiky-leaved thistles which line the stony path along the ridge.  Tall tanik trees grow along the ridge to the east.  The trail leading up and north is lined with bright sumacs.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: The trail wends its way through an old growth of majestic tanik trees.  A few younger trees struggle to survive in the shadows of the older ones.  Ferns and thistles grow thick along the trail.  An owl pellet lies at the bottom of one of the tanik trees.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: The trail loses all definition as it passes through the widely dispersed trees.  Older tanik trees are mixed with younger specimens.  The trunks of a few dead, old tanik trees lie among the undergrowth of ferns, slowly decomposing.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: Young tanik trees grow thickly along the ridge.  A few venerable trees, some showing signs of old damage, stand tall among them like adults among children.  Barely visible in the undergrowth are some charred and shattered stumps.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Ridge]
description: Scattered through the new growth of young tanik trees are the shattered trunks of older ones.  Massive stumps, charred and splintered, are visible among the young trees, mute evidence of some violent cataclysm.  A narrow trail around a scorched and cracked boulder leads up to a copse of birch trees.

title: [Teorainn Dale, Creek Trail]
description: A group of tall dark stones are gathered together in a rough half-circle among the tanik trees.  The stones, angular and covered with lichen, lean against each other precariously.  The pattern formed by the stones seems too consistent to be a matter of chance, but too irregular to have been placed by design.  Through the trees you can see the glitter of moonlight on the lake to the east.

A group of tall dark stones are gathered together in a rough half-circle among the tanik trees.  The stones, angular and covered with lichen, lean against each other precariously.  The pattern formed by the stones seems too consistent to be a matter of chance, but too irregular to have been placed by design.  Through the trees you can see the glitter of sunlight on the lake to the east.

title: [Abandoned Homestead]
description: The mountainous terrain provides a dramatic background to a derelict homestead.  The farm house, clearly abandoned, is flanked by a pair of dead trees.  To the south the creek has widened to become the narrow Lake Tanai.  Weeds and small saplings grow in the fields which once nourished crops.  Some bright yellow sunflowers grow tall to the east.

title: [Abandoned Homestead]
description: A small, ramshackle farm house, its door broken and hanging awkwardly by a single hinge, stands forlornly between a pair of dead apple trees.  A path to the east leads through a field of sunflowers.  To the south is a stone well and the northern bank of Lake Tanai.

title: [Abandoned Homestead, Sunflowers]
description: The path leads through a field of sunflowers.  The irregular spacing of the rows of sunflowers suggest they had once been planted for harvesting but have begun to grow wild.  The large heads of the flowers are closed in the moonlight.

The path leads through a field of sunflowers.  The irregular spacing of the rows of sunflowers suggest they had once been planted for harvesting but have begun to grow wild.  The large yellow heads of the flowers are all turned to face the sun.

title: [Abandoned Homestead, Sunflowers]
description: The path wends its way through the brightly colored flowers to an old shed made of daub and wattle.  Small birds flutter through the flowers, alighting on the large heads and eating the seeds.

title: [Old Shed]
description: The angled roof of the shed is covered with dusty cobwebs.  Empty hooks and bare shelves line the walls.  The air smells of loamy soil.  A few broken, rusted farm implements lean in the corners of the shed.

title: [Old Farm House ]
[Old Farm House]
description: The painted plaster walls have long since turned to yellow.  Cobwebs abound in the rafters.  The smell of mold and decay is somewhat alleviated by a soft breeze coming through a broken window.  Some words, faded with age, have been scratched in the wall by the door.

title: [Old Farm House]
description: Tattered scraps of rotten fabric, faded nearly white by the sun, flutter on each side of the broken kitchen window.  In one corner is a partially collapsed oven made from brick.  The soot-darkened rafters are covered in cobwebs.

title: [Old Farm House]
description: The plastered walls are cracked and yellowed with age.  The wide-planked floorboards creak under your feet.  One end of the steeply angled ceiling is thick with soot.  The air feels dank and the room smells of mold.

title: [Old Farm House]
description: Moonlight streaming through a hole in the steeply angled ceiling illuminates motes of dust and mold spore.  The plastered walls are chipped and peeling.  The wide-planked floorboards are warped and sag as you step on them.

Sunlight streaming through a hole in the steeply angled ceiling illuminates motes of dust and mold spore.  The plastered walls are chipped and peeling.  The wide-planked floorboards are warped and sag as you step on them.

title: [Abandoned Homestead, Well]
description: The stone well is placed only a few yards from the green waters of Lake Tanai.  Dragonflies dart restlessly among the reeds that line the bank.  The sound of lapping water is punctuated by the occasional croak of frog.  A tall oak tree is visible on the opposite shore of the narrow lake.

title: [Bottom of the Well]
description: The damp stone walls of the well rise steeply, ending in a dark circle of star-filled sky.  Water trickles down the stone walls and drips onto the muddy floor with a soft, repetitious plop.  On the southern wall is the entrance to a narrow tunnel.

The damp stone walls of the well rise steeply, ending in a bright blue circle of cloudless sky.  Water trickles down the stone walls and drips onto the muddy floor with a soft, repetitious plop.  On the southern wall is the entrance to a low tunnel.

title: [Tunnel]
description: The mud and muck of the tunnel oozes around your feet, sucking at them, gripping them, making slurping noises as you walk.  Cold water drips from the ceiling.  The tunnel has a primordial stink of slime and mold and decay.  An eerie moaning sound seems to come from the south.

title: [Bottom of the Well]
description: The wind blowing over the top of the well creates an odd, eerie moaning sound.  The moonlight slants into the well, illuminating the rope so that it looks like a bright strand of spidersilk.  The air at the bottom is rank, smelling of mud and mold.  A narrow tunnel in the wall leads north under the lake.

The air at the bottom is rank, smelling of mud and mold.  A narrow tunnel in the wall leads north under the lake.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Lake Tanai]
description: A gently sloping hillock forms the banks of Lake Tanai.  The narrow lake shimmers in the moonlight.  A few wooden structures and a field of sunflowers are visible on the opposite bank.  The branches of a tall, ancient oak tree form a canopy over the area.  An old, deteriorated stone well stands nearby.

The branches of a tall, ancient oak tree form a canopy over the area.  An old, deteriorated stone well stands nearby.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Grassy Hillock]
description: This grassy hillock is nestled between a sheer wall of red-veined rock to the south and an impenetrable hedge of brambles to the north.  A tall oak tree dominates the woods to the northeast.  Beyond the tree are the blue waters of Lake Tanai.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Lake Tanai]
description: The lake glistens in the moonlight.  To the east, barely visible through a tall, thick tangle of brambles, is some sort of wooden structure suspended in the branches of a tall oak tree.  To the south the terrain rises sharply, becoming a rocky escarpment dotted with thanot shrubs.

The lake glistens in the sunlight.  To the east, barely visible through a tall, thick tangle of brambles, is some sort of wooden structure suspended in the branches of a tall oak tree.  To the south the terrain rises sharply, becoming a rocky escarpment dotted with thanot shrubs.

title: [Teorainn Valley, Arboreal Haven]
description: This skeleton of a storm-battered treehouse no longer provides much shelter from the elements.  Only the flooring and sections of two walls remain relatively intact.  A small altar has been erected in one corner.  The branches sway gently in the breeze.  Through the thick, green leaves you can see the blue waters of Lake Tanai.

title: [Sabizki's Hut, Living Area]
description: Filtered moonlight shines through the window of the small, tidy hut, casting a silvery stripe across the woven rug in front of the blazing fireplace.  A wooden table and matching chairs sit below the window.  On the opposite wall is a neatly made bed covered by an earth-toned quilt.  At its foot, a wooden stand holds a tiny black-faced monkey securely attached to the stand by a leather harness and leash.

Filtered sunlight shines through the window of the small, tidy hut, illuminating idly mingling dust motes and casting a stripe of warmth across the woven rug in front of the unlit fireplace.  A wooden table and matching chairs sit below the window.  On the opposite wall is a neatly made bed covered by an earth-toned quilt.  At its foot, a wooden stand holds a tiny black-faced monkey securely attached to the stand by a leather harness and leash.

title: [Abandoned Shrine, Vestibule]
description: A thick coat of dust obscures a mosaic of a dagger-pierced heart inlaid in the floor.  Only a few sets of footprints testify to the fact that the shrine may not be completely abandoned.  Heavy swaths of white cloth line the walls, dampening all sound.

title: [Shrine, Meditation Chamber]
description: The smell of oiled leather and dust lingers in the air.  Three raised wooden beams cross the stone floor in parallel.  Each beam, intended for kneeling upon in contemplation, is topped with an assortment of small, razor sharp pieces of glass and metal.  Numerous whips and crops hang from a set of hooks on the eastern wall and a single torch provides light from its sconce next to the door.

title: [Abandoned Shrine, Altar]
description: Red and white bolts of silk hang in alternating columns around the periphery of this enormous sanctuary.  Skeletons lie in four rows on either side of a marbled aisle leading to a large dais centered on the northern wall.  Upon the dais is a simple golden altar supporting a small ceremonial dagger stand.

title: [Abandoned Shrine, Cells]
description: Neither decoration nor torch adorns the stone walls of this small chamber.  Two cells, each containing a granite bench, are divided by mithril bars.  Upon one bench is a small skull, while the remainder of the skeleton is scattered about on the floor.  Three heavy bolts, each with a slight tinge of rust, stand ready to secure the heavy door.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Trail]
description: The trail heads up a steep slope, the air growing noticeably colder as the climb continues.  The stand of pines, growing crookedly out of the sharply slanted hillside, grows thicker.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Rocky Trail]
description: The air grows ever colder as the trail ascends the mountainside.  Hand and footholds are difficult to come by as the rocks littering the path come loose and go tumbling downward.

title: [Whistler's Pass, Alpine Trail]
description: The conifers grow close and thick, leaving barely enough room for one person to pass between them.  The trail, now a barely visible worn spot winding amongst the underbrush, climbs higher up the mountainside.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: A tight, barely visible path squeezes between the towering pines and through the holly bush thickets.  The serrated edges of the holly leaves tear at clothing and skin to make passage painful as well as arduous.  Their presence so close against the trail indicates that neither adventurers nor creatures pass this way very often.  Here and again a scrap of clothing or something akin to dried blood appears on one of the leaves, indicating that at least some others do venture this direction.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: The snow blankets everything around...the tree branches, the holly bushes, the ground...to reflect the moon in a ghostly display of whiteness.  Although the wind is clearly heard in the treetops, closer to the ground the air is still, and nothing disturbs the tranquil forest except the soft crunching of feet upon the snowy trail and the occasional 'plop' of some snow escaping an overloaded tree branch.

Although the wind is clearly heard in the treetops, closer to the ground the air is still, and nothing disturbs the tranquil forest except the soft crunching of feet upon the snowy trail and the occasional 'plop' of some snow escaping an overloaded tree branch.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: To the west the ground rises sharply up a sparsely vegetated incline, while to the southeast it plunges into the thick conifer forest.  Further up the hill the trees regroup to become a thick forest again. The cloven hoof prints of some large herbivore or herbivores cross back and forth on the hillside as if the animals were unsure which way to go.  Perhaps some of their confusion can be attributed to the wolf-like paw prints intermingled with the hoof prints.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: The path, if it could even be called that, plunges down a hillside into the dense forest below.  Barely discernible traces of passage also lead off to the south, following a ridgeline that drops steeply on the eastern side of the forest.  The footing in both directions appears tricky, but it also looks much easier to navigate than plunging directly into several feet of powdery snow underneath the trees to the north and west.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: The conifer forest envelops the path, cutting off most of the light to create a patchwork of light and shade.  Firs and cedars compete with pines and spruces for light, water and nutrients, and an abundance of all three must exist judging from the closely spaced nature of the tree trunks.  A soft carpet of snow and needles coats the ground, releasing a soft crunching sound with each step.  The trail seems to rise slightly to the west.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: The forest butts up against the DragonSpine Mountains.  A faint path winds its way into the conifers to the east, but nothing really resembling a trail ventures up the incline toward the westerly peaks.  Even the forest appears to have given up hope of extending its influence up the rocky face of the mountainside and contents itself with occupying the flatter area just below.  There do appear to be handholds and footholds, though, and perhaps an ascent can be managed.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: The face of the mountain is steep, although the climb is not particularly difficult.  An abundance of protruding rocks provides ample handholds and footholds.  Occasionally a small shelf presents itself as a stopping place, but the harsh wind colliding with the mountainside makes for a rather chilly rest area.  Stones, dislodged by heavy feet, careen swiftly downward to smash noisily into the forest below.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: An eagle swoops close, keeping a keen eye on you, then floats away over the forest in search of a meal.  To the east the conifer forest of the Whistler's Pass area fills the floor between the peaks, and even further east another forest appears, although there is something strangely wrong about it.  From this distance details are not quite apparent, but the trees somehow seem misshapen and the forest's hue seems much too dark.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: A thick cloudbank, trapped by the wind against the mountain, envelops the area at this altitude.  The dense clouds limit vision to only a few feet, and their moisture coats the rocks with damp, slippery ice.  More time is spent moving laterally to find just the right hold than progressing either up or down.  The wind howls and gusts all around, seemingly intent on dislodging anything foolish enough to traverse this mountainside.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: The clouds open a bit, swirling about to reveal patches of starry sky, then run together to block the light and enclose the area in an eerie, gleaming whiteness.  Often the outcroppings appear to be made of pure ice, affixed to the mountainside by the numbing cold.  Dislodged rocks fall quickly out of sight.  From the perceived sounds, the rocks careen a few times off the mountain and then...nothing.  Perhaps it is too far down for the sound to travel back through the wind.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: A ledge underneath an outcropping presents a shelter from the wind.  Ice clings to the edges of the mountain all around, but the floor of the ledge is remarkably dry.  Here and there tiny piles of snow have collected, pushed about by small wind eddies, but the snow is sparse.  Most of the snow is probably released at the lower altitudes as the clouds are driven up the side of the mountain.  A trail, not very wide but fairly flat, moves off to the north to disappear in between two rising peaks.

title: [Trail Ascent]
description: A pass opens up to the northwest between two of the DragonSpine's loftier peaks while a narrow trail winds along the mountainside to the south.  There might be a spectacular view to the east, if it weren't for the clouds.  Instead the view is one of a fluffy, swirling, pillow-like surface of white stretching away into the distance.  Occasionally the clouds part briefly to give a glimpse of thick forest and rugged terrain below.

title: [Gossamer Pass]
description: Sheer rock walls rise several hundred feet on either side of this narrow cleft, and far above the sky is visible.  The walls cast the area into deep shadow, though, and near-invisible patches of ice make the going slow.  The wind whistles noisily through the passage, reverberating off the rock walls to produce a thunderous cacophony.  An icy chute curves steeply upward and out of sight to the southwest.

title: [Gossamer Pass]
description: The passage extends north and south.  It is flat and travel is easy but boring as the monotony of the walls around changes little.  The rock walls tower high enough that the positions of the stars are not readily discernible.  The wind obscures most sounds, but occasionally a howling unlike that of the wind's normal passage rises above the airflow's moaning only to subside slowly.  Faint markings are discernible on the eastern wall.

title: [Gossamer Pass]
description: Part of the eastern wall has collapsed into the passage, strewing rubble for several hundred feet in either direction and creating a sizeable mound that must be traversed.  Large, sharp chunks of hard, igneous rock protrude up through the pile of smaller pieces.  Although these chunks are boulder size, they do not succeed in blocking the entire passage, and it is relatively easy to circumvent them.  The break has exposed banded veins of dark stone within the mountainside.

title: [Gossamer Pass]
description: The passage slopes gently upward from northwest to southeast.  To the southeast the mountain faces loom ever closer to the path as if they would suddenly clap shut, crushing anyone within.  Northwestward, the mountains take the opposite tack, leaning away from the trail and forming a narrow valley.  Perhaps this is just a different sinister trap, allowing a tremendous amount of snow to collect on the slopes before sending it down in a thunderous avalanche on trapped adventurers below.

title: [Gossamer Pass]
description: Thin air in this high altitude takes its toll on body and mind.  Shadows resolve themselves into dark, sinister objects against the mountainside, while the moonlight dancing off patches of pristine snow makes the patches appear to pulsate and undulate with lives of their own.  Moist breath quickly coalesces into fine, icy particles that cling to faces, beards and hoods.  It is so cold that spit freezes with a crackling sound before it hits the ground.

title: [Gossamer Pass]
description: A canyon's delta rises to either side.  The canyon narrows gradually to the southeast, rising slowly and disappearing into the towering mountain peaks.  The passage does not appear difficult.  To the north, a wide, flat valley spreads out for several miles before the mountains hem it in once again.  The valley has the appearance of a bowl that has been filled in with centuries of ice, for its surface is level and smooth with only the occasional rock protruding through the snow.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: A tranquil sea of snow spreads out to the west, north and east to fill Gossamer Valley.  The protruding peaks of the DragonSpine Mountains hem in the valley on all sides, extremely close to the south and closer to the east and north than to the west.  The wind blows steadily, and the air is clear and crisp.  In places the snow layer seems rather thin, however, and, with a few kicks from a boot, quickly gives way to ice or permafrost underneath.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: Despite the harsh climate of the area, life does seem to take hold even here in the frigid heights of Gossamer Valley.  In a pocket of daytime warmth by a dark boulder, bunches of light grey sawgrass poke up tentatively from the exposed ground, waving slowly in the filtered wind.  The serrated blades stand no more than a couple feet high, and, judging from the pruning done to some of the plants, something has been grazing on them.

Despite the harsh climate of the area, life does seem to take hold even here in the frigid heights of Gossamer Valley.  In the reflected sunlight and sheltering warmth of a dark boulder, bunches of light green sawgrass poke up tentatively from the exposed ground, basking in nearly twice the sunlight of the surrounding area.  The serrated blades stand no more than a couple feet high, and, judging from the pruning done to some of the plants, something has been grazing on them.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: Jagged, dark peaks hem in the eastern edge of Gossamer Valley.  The dark rock absorbs the sunlight during the day, so even at night small, gurgling melt streams slide down the rock from the collected snow high above. The streams run down to the icy floor below and spread out to quickly freeze into ice deltas.  Near the stream, small holes in the mountainside with accumulated debris just outside indicate the presence of burrowing animals.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: In a small, sheltered depression in the uplifted rocks, groundsel flowers and the red stalks of fruiting mountain heather form a four-inch-high canopy.  The cold night air is undisturbed by the noises of insects, however.  The small patch of flowers seems so very out of place against the stark, grey sides of the mountains and the bright white surface of the valley's snow-covered floor.  Yet here and again, similar patches of life present themselves all along the valley.

Bumblebees flit noisily among the flowers, gathering sustenance to take back to their homes.  The small patch of color seems so very out of place against the stark, grey sides of the mountains and the bright white surface of the valley's snow-covered floor.  Yet here and again, similar patches of life present themselves all along the valley.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: Rounded boulders and huge, jagged rocks break through the valley's smooth snow floor in several places, thrusting up toward the sky.  Rabbit tracks skitter around and between these islands of stone, pock marking the snow with their padded impressions.  Something or things much larger have made indistinct impressions in the snow and left long trails across the glacier.  Bits of fur, scattered bones and frozen blood attest to violence where the tracks meet.

Bits of fur, scattered bones and frozen blood attest to violence where the tracks meet.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: A huge, rounded section of the DragonSpine Mountains impinges on the valley from the west, leaving three general directions of travel.  A wide, flat, snow-filled valley extends due east, its flatness punctuated by boulders here and there.  Northward, the vision is much the same, although in the distance the valley seems to rise somewhat and shed some of its snow covering.  A narrow leg of the glacier slips in between the mountains to the southwest.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: Small specks against the mountainside resolve themselves into the frozen carcasses of sparrows, thrushes and warblers.  The cause of their demise was most likely the cold, but why the birds came to be here in the first place is a mystery.  Perhaps they were forced down by storms or exhausted on their migratory flights.  Several of the carcasses have been torn open by predators.

Ravens flit among the carcasses, feeding on the icy flesh and keeping a watchful eye on your position through malignant yellow eyes.  Certainly they would like something a little meatier on which to feast.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: A wide crack yawns in the glacier, running in a jagged pattern west and northwest until it reaches the mountains.  The sides of the crack are sharp and solid.  Small rocks dropped into the crevice bounce against the sides and disappear into the darkness, never indicating when they hit bottom.  Much of the southeastern end is covered in snow, but a judicious circumvention of the area, walking near to the mountains, provides a safe path.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: The glacier floor ends at a huge cavern of glittering ice directly southwest.  The mountains pinch in tightly, suspending the ice in between them.  Strange rumblings followed by the sounds of explosions emanate from the south, shaking the ground slightly and making it difficult to stand.  The smaller animals seem to have abandoned this area entirely, although the sawgrass appears to flourish nearer to the ice cavern.  To the east the glacier widens out again in this canyon.

title: [Glitter Ice Caverns]
description: Tendrils of ice writhe overhead in a frozen dance.  Winding and weaving in a complex canopy, the ice forms an inverted bowl that descends to the ground on all sides except the northeast, where a large hole still allows egress.  The wind whistles musically through the ice strands, its speed changing along with its pitch as it courses through the unclosed holes in the roof.  The floor is a solid, smooth sheet of glassy ice.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: A canopy of starry sky arches over Gossamer Valley.  The few clouds brave enough to appear race across the sky from east to west, driven by the constant wind, only to be piled up against the western mountain face.  Forced upward, the clouds quickly drop their snow load and disappear, leaving the DragonSpine Mountains to the west heavy with snow while their counterparts to the east appear sparsely covered.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: The mountains just to the west rumble ominously under their weight of snow.  No trees grow on the mountainsides, and nothing appears to be positioned to block an onrushing avalanche.  Piles of snow hundreds of feet high spread out nearly as far from the base of the mountains, testimony to the sheer volume of frozen water that the peaks can unleash with little warning.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The icy, flat, glaciated surface spreads out to the east and south.  A long, wide spur of the Gossamer Valley extends to the north.  The ground rises slightly and sheds its snowy covering in many areas, exposing large expanses of permafrost.  It is soil, though, and not ice.  Yellow-brown moss and light green sawgrass attempt to grow in spots that receive extra daytime sun, but these are still relatively few compared to the totally barren sections.

Yellow-brown moss and light green sawgrass attempt to grow in some of the sunnier spots, but these are still relatively few compared to the totally barren sections.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The icy wind blasts over the flat, frozen ground, picking up whatever things it can find--snow, ice, dust, pebbles--and flinging them against anything that stands in its way.  The constant windy assault has rounded the edges of the boulders that stand in the area.  Their windward faces are smooth and curvaceous, while the leeward sides are sharp and well defined.  It is not surprising that the leeward side of these boulders is where small animal burrows can be found.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The stars move slowly across the clear sky, twinkling brilliantly, but providing no warmth.  The uncovered soil makes it much more difficult to note the tracks of predators and prey alike, as the frozen ground gives no indication of their passing.  Only occasionally, in the snow piled up against boulders or in sheltered flat patches, do the prints appear.  Sometimes one type is alone, sometimes two types are together, and sometimes one type suddenly ends entirely.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: A small patch of forget-me-nots bravely blooms in the shelter of a large nearby boulder.  The boulder cuts off the wind and snow on one side while reflecting the daytime sun down to the flowers on the other side.  A bit of a breeze manages to swirl around the boulder to gently rock the flowers back and forth.  Underneath, in small moss beds, insects busily rustle through the debris from the flowers, perhaps searching for food or nesting material.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The valley continues monotonously to the north and south, although with a slight cant to the northeast and southwest.  On either side the DragonSpine Mountains press up against the sky.  Their sharp, cold peaks rise steeply, giving no indication of a way to pass through them.  It is entirely plausible that they have stood this way for hundreds of centuries as protective sentinels hemming in this desolate valley.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The boulders and their shadows take on strange shapes in the moonlight.  One boulder in particular resembles a giant fish rising up from a surrounding lake of snow.  The wind's action has piled the snow up around the boulder, giving life to the impression that the fish is dragging the ocean's waters up with it as it leaps into the air.  The action is frozen in time and climate, its eventual splash back into the sea left to the imagination.

The boulders and their shadows take on strange shapes in the glare of the sun.  One boulder in particular resembles a giant fish rising up from a surrounding lake of snow.  The wind's action has piled the snow up around the boulder, giving life to the impression that the fish is dragging the ocean's waters up with it as it leaps into the air.  The action is frozen in time and climate, its eventual splash back into the sea left to the imagination.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The valley constricts to the southwest as the mountains appear to press in closer.  To the northeast it widens with the mountains giving the opposite impression.  They seem to move away, allowing the valley floor to spread out and giving one the choice of following the western slope or crossing over to the eastern slope.  Neither choice looks particularly appealing as both sides appear to have the same unexciting terrain.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: South and northwest, the western DragonSpine Mountains follow the valley's side.  Snow has piled up against the slopes, and it often extends well into the valley, making passage colder and crunchier.  The snow is very dry, though, and it doesn't tend to stick to clothing, so walking through it is relatively easy except for those rare times when it happens to cover a deep hole.  The snow gets deeper the farther northwest one travels and shallower in the southern direction.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: Heavy snow blankets the area and makes progress slow.  To the northeast low, heavy clouds cover a conifer forest, and every so often a tendril reaches out of the cloudbank and drops some snow in your area.  The snowfall does not last long as the tendril dissipates quickly in the frigid cold.  The wind adds more snow, driving it in from the east in lashing gusts then forcing it up the mountainside where it adds to the heavy weight already there.  Soon it will all come down at once.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The snow is nearly impassable, piling up several yards high around most of the large pines and firs in the area.  A thick, damp fog wraps itself around the trees, limiting vision to only a few yards.  To compound the sight problem, snow seems to constantly fall from the clouds.  The forceful wind is modified somewhat by the trees, but it still carries away quite a bit of snow.  If not for its action, it is possible that the entire forest would soon become one giant snow lump.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The lakeshore meets the mountainside just to the north, closing off travel in that direction entirely.  The snow pelts the area relentlessly, floating down thickly from the massed clouds and driven by the incessant wind.  The trees bend and sway, but their thick trunks have adapted to the constant motion, and they are in no danger of falling.  The sound of water lapping against a shore reaches your ears, but it's difficult to see much through the blizzard conditions.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: Sturdy pines and spreading spruces dominate this part of the forest.  Their branches hang heavily with the weight of accumulated snow, and clumps of snow drop constantly to the ground.  The snowfall is thick, and the wind swirls it around.  Southward, vision clears a bit, as does the forest.  The trees are massed closest to the lake, and their abundance drops off drastically in direct proportion to their distance from the lakeshore.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: Snow falls steadily on the conifer forest, but much of it is driven west by the prevailing wind, so the accumulation is nearly negligible.  The falling snow hides tracks quickly, though, and the forest appears to be a pristine wilderness, untouched by adventurers or creatures.  Several of the pines are ancient specimens, their age unknown, but their trunks so wide that a giantman could not wrap his arms halfway around them.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: A river flows out of the lake, moving eastward before disappearing underneath one of the mountains.  It is difficult to see exactly where it drains, though, because the surface ices over before it actually reaches the mountainside.  Although iced, the river's surface does not feel thick enough to allow travel to the north.  The conifer forest follows the lakeshore and the river's bank all the way to the mountains, providing a green strip in the midst of the valley's barren scenery.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: Snow covers the ground, although the snow is not very deep and seems well packed.  Clouds exude from a fog bank to the north, dropping snow flurries for a time before retracting again.  The wind rushing down the eastern slope of the mountains carries most of the snow westward, though, leaving only a small covering.  Occasionally, with the help of the wind, the fog bank rolls back enough to reveal a conifer forest standing to the north and northeast.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The trail, if there even is one, crosses the valley floor between the western and eastern mountain slopes.  The valley floor is flat and, for the most part, lifeless.  Long striations crisscross the tundra.  These are not deep or very wide, and snow has filled many of them in.  It is indiscernible as to whether these have a seismological origin or are the result of the constant passage of large animals, a passage that has perhaps followed the same path for centuries.

title: [Gossamer Valley, North Valley]
description: The eastern DragonSpine Mountains loom closely.  Their peaks march off to the south and northeast.  The peaks have very little snow cover, and the mountainsides are practically devoid of snow.  The wind's general direction is from east to west, and when a rare cloud does make an appearance it is quickly shuttled over to the western side of the valley.  To the northeast, though, the valley's floor is covered with a blanket of white.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: Archipelagos of rock jut out into the glaciated valley, causing the trail to swing westward around them.  Snowdrifts pile high up against the windward side of these outcroppings, and the tracks of small mammals are readily apparent across the snow.  Sawgrass thrives on the leeward side of these rocks, in the warmer areas, and occasionally a snowshoe rabbit peers out from the sawgrass, its long ears and button nose twitching inquisitively, before it hastily retreats again.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Glacier]
description: A canyon tumbles down from the mountains to the northeast into the glacial valley.  Perhaps at one time it was carved by the erosive action of flowing water.  Now it is a glacial tributary, a river of ice moving slowly downward toward the huge glacier locked in Gossamer Valley.  The canyon is several hundred feet wide, and the ice provides a fairly flat footing for those wishing to explore the canyon's origins.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Blind Canyon]
description: The canyon makes a sweeping turn as its ice load slowly descends from east to southwest.  The wind has driven most of the snow up against the northwestern side of the canyon, exposing the surface of the glacier.  It is not smooth and slick, but rather pitted and scarred by the effects of the wind driving both snow and dirt particles across its surface.  The ice is milky, with dirt, rocks and other debris trapped within its frigid grasp.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Blind Canyon]
description: The canyon twists and narrows, ascending to the northeast and descending to the west.  Nothing grows in the canyon, neither on the ice nor on the sheer mountainsides.  Perhaps the snow's constant downward slide scrapes the rocks clean of any moss or vegetation that might attempt to take hold there.  The moon reflects brightly off the snow on the southeastern wall, eliminating shadows and bathing the area in a solid, eerie glare.

The canyon twists and narrows, ascending to the northeast and descending to the west.  Nothing grows in the canyon, neither on the ice nor on the sheer mountainsides.  Perhaps the snow's constant downward slide scrapes the rocks clean of any moss or vegetation that might attempt to take hold there.  The sun reflects brightly off the snow on the southeastern wall, eliminating shadows and bathing the area in an almost painful glare.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Blind Canyon]
description: The glacier continues its relentless descent from northeast to southwest, fueled by the constant supply of snow from the mountainsides.  The snow slides down, piling high on top of the glacier and turning the lower levels of snow into ice.  This ice, in turn, becomes part of the glacier, and the combined weight forces the entire ice mass downward to the southwest in a slow, imperceptible, grinding movement.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Blind Canyon]
description: The rock walls close in tightly, constricting the space to a mere thirty yards or so as the canyon snakes up to the northeast and down to the southwest.  Several large boulders have fallen from the mountainsides, imbedding in the snow and providing excellent places for predators to hide.  Small pikas scramble over one of the boulders, chittering noisily at your approach, then racing down the side of the boulder to find safety in their burrows.

title: [Gossamer Valley, Blind Canyon]
description: A chasm crosses the glacier from wall to wall, cutting off movement to the north.  On the other side of the chasm a wide, sheltered cavern snuggles into the mountain face.  Many small bones, fur, and patches of frozen blood are scattered among the confused animal tracks in the snow, testimony to creatures that got trapped and killed by something much bigger.  The glacier descends to the southwest, narrowing as the mountains close in on it.

title: [Ta'Illistim, Alearyl Hall]
description: The floor is a highly polished dark grey granite and narrow runners make way between a multitude of shelves.  The racks fill the room, each loaded with a heap of valuable treasure.  A host of guards monitor the room's activity, one poised at either end of every single row.  A trio of oil lamps adequately illuminate the room's valuables and rewards.

title: [Temporal Rift]
description: You are trapped in a time rift!  You catch brief glimpses of events both past and future.  Beyond these strange and confusing visions extends a vast, ever-changing field of stars, pinpoints of light against unfathomable utter blackness.  It is very cold here.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest, up, down

title: [Old Ta'Faendryl, East Woods]
description: The ground rises in a gentle slope to the north, slowly flattening out as it works its way back to the south.  A large and ancient oak, having lost the strength of the roots that bound it to the earth, has toppled across the lower end of the path, creating a detour that leads a bit to the west.

title: [Sylvarraend Road]
description: A cracked support in the fence leans downwards as the fence begins to sag.  Insects rummage along the surface of the wood seeking to make a home.  Pale moonlight reflects off the surface of a lake in the distance to the southeast.

A cracked support in the fence leans downwards as the fence begins to sag.  Insects rummage along the surface of the wood seeking to make a home.  A clear blue lake can be seen in the distance to the southeast.

title: [Urylia's Doors]
description: An air of silence pervades this spacious shop, not even the squeak of a patron's shoe on the marble floors defying this stillness. Rows of assorted doors are set in the center of the large room, displayed on tall stands and arranged like a miniature labyrinth. An old and cantankerous elf leans against a counter in the back, keeping a close eye on those in her shop.

title: [Gawiel's Floor Coverings]
description: Upon entering this shop, the high beamed ceiling gives a false impression of ample space.  Maps of exotic rug-weaving regions where villagers create precious coverings are prominently displayed on the smooth sandstone walls.  On highly polished and slightly cluttered maoral shelves, an astounding array of color, intricate design and texture is exhibited for the perusal of would-be customers.

title: [Vund's Chairs]
description: Scattered about the shiny granite floor in seemingly no particular order are chairs, chairs, chairs!  Looks like the inventory was set out in a hurry, or maybe the owner does not have much imagination or need to impress the clientele.  From deeply carved and ornately detailed pieces to stark simple types, you get the impression that here there is, indeed, something for everyone.

title: [Sylvarraend Road]
description: Stern fences continue to line the path and, on one side, a small gopher lies curled up under the moonlit sky.  The light sound of waves lapping against the shore can be heard from this distance.
Stern fences continue to line the path and, on one side, a small gopher basks in the sun while nibbling a carrot.  The light sound of waves lapping against the shore can be heard from this distance.

title: [Adventurer's Guild, Lobby]
description: Airy and spacious, the lower half of the chamber's walls are trimmed with carved mahogany panels with matching floor tiles.  Raised murals depict various scenes of brave adventurers battling foes with their ladies fair in the background cheering them onward.  Scattered around the area are chairs which provide a little respite for the weary.

Raised murals depicting various scenes of brave adventurers battling foes with their ladies fair in the background cheering them onward.  Scattered around the area are chairs which provide a little respite for the weary.
