title: [Yander's Farm, Tool Storage]
description: A large selection of implements hangs from the walls and beams in this section of the barn.

A large selection of implements hangs from the walls and beams in this section of the barn.  Scythes and sickles, their long, curved blades honed to a gleaming sharpness, adorn one area of the walls, while picks and shovels in nearly new condition are affixed in another area.  A heavy spool of thick rope nestles into the southeast corner.  The chaff is heavily scuffed and disturbed as if something or someone has been traveling between the tools and the barn door with great regularity.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barn]
description: Bands of light and dark splay across the beams and floor in alternating bright moonlight stripes and darker shade stripes.

Bands of light and dark splay across the beams and floor in alternating bright moonlight stripes and darker shade stripes.  Fine particles of dust float lazily through the moonlit areas.  The air inside the barn moves only slightly, though the wind's whistling reverberates loudly at times from the openings in the roof overhead.  The wind's modulating whistle echoes eerily within the empty barn, and the darkness of the shadows in the corners adds to a feeling of uneasiness.

title: [Yander's Farm, Feed Storage]
description: Large wooden bins line the walls of this area of the barn.  Each bin has a heavy, hinged top that opens upward, and a smaller, hinged door on the front.  Small piles of dried corn litter the floor beneath the small door on each bin, spreading out to blend in with the chaff that covers the entire floor.  Two shiny metal buckets hang from hooks on the central beam.  Mice skitter through the area, frantically looking for little bits of sustenance that they can consume or take back to their nests.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barn]
description: The floor's chaff is damp toward the barn's northwest corner, and the walls display lines of dark discoloration.

The floor's chaff is damp toward the barn's northwest corner, and the walls display lines of dark discoloration.  The smell of mildew rises from the area, though it is faint and not overpowering at all.  Mice race about, searching for morsels of wheat that the threshers may have left behind.

title: [Yander's Farm, Threshing Floor]
description: Heavy granite slabs have been carefully butted together to form a wide, flat area in the northeast corner of the barn.  Chaff and grain are scattered across the floor, but for the most part it is clean.  A wide door on the north wall and a wide door on the east wall are both securely locked.

Heavy granite slabs have been carefully butted together to form a wide, flat area in the northeast corner of the barn.  Chaff and grain are scattered across the floor, but for the most part it is clean.  A wide door on the north wall and a wide door on the east wall are both securely locked.  It is easy to picture them both open, though, and the wind coursing through this corner of the barn, carrying the chaff outside as the heavier wheat falls to the granite floor in the threshing process.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barn]
description: Thick, tall weeds cover the ground on this side of the barn, making passage difficult.

Thick, tall weeds cover the ground on this side of the barn, making passage difficult.  The weeds spread out down an embankment to the east, and it is apparent that the soil is poor and useless for farming.  Wide rain gullies cut through the embankment, exposing rocks and stones.  The barn's east wall rises to a height of approximately twelve feet.  Its expanse is flat and unmarred except for a long wooden door set in the northern end.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barn]
description: The rear of the barn appears as new and sturdy as any of the other sides.  A sliding door is mounted on the west end of the wall.  Paths extend through the weeds in different directions.  The path to the southwest appears well traveled, as does the path to the west.  Those to the east and southeast are somewhat more overgrown with weeds and more difficult to follow.  A large mound rises to the east, and it appears to defy the weeds that cluster around it.
paths: Obvious paths: east, southeast, southwest, west

title: [Yander's Farm, Chaff Dump]
description: A huge mound of wheat chaff towers over the weeds that surround it like a huge golden altar before a crowd of worshipping green acolytes.

A huge mound of wheat chaff towers over the weeds that surround it like a huge golden altar before a crowd of worshipping green acolytes.  Thick, tall and prickly, the weeds attempt to prevent approach to the mound.  Mice skitter through the weeds, searching for any remaining wheat, however slight.  The mound's purity is contaminated by the remains of moldy feed corn, wheat stalks, barley plants and decomposing turnip greens.

title: [Yander's Farm, Well]
description: A round, brick well stands among the usual clusters of weeds.

A round, brick well stands among the usual clusters of weeds.  Twin cedar beams rise toward the sky to support an equally thick crossbeam.  Mounted on this crossbeam is a crank, and a thick rope coils over the crank's mechanism to dangle a bucket into the well.  Though the weeds insidiously crowd the well and attempt to possess the entire area, someone has cleared a small area around the well and planted some petunias.

title: [Yander's Farm, Farmland Road]
description: A wide, rutted road runs southwest between two culverts.  The road also continues to the southeast.

A wide, rutted road runs southwest between two culverts.  The road displays indentations from the passage of wheels, and few weeds attempt to grow in these indentations.  The road also continues to the southeast, though the ground appears harder there and the indentations are not nearly as noticeable.  A circular brick well sits to the east, surrounded by weeds and petunias.  A flowing wheat field extends to the northwest, and rocks are stacked in the culvert to allow access to the field.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barn]
description: Wheat fields, their golden tassels waving gently in the soft wind, spread out to the northwest.  To the southwest, rows of turnip plants extend their green shoots toward the sunlight, and near the turnip patch two fenced pens sit with open gates.  Directly eastward, the wide, sturdy side of a well-built barn rises into the air.  Weeds cluster against the barn's side and spread out toward the fields, though foot traffic has cleared the weeds from paths in four directions.
Directly eastward, the wide, sturdy side of a well-built barn rises into the air.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, southeast, southwest, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Rolton Pens]
description: Two circular pens stand, one to the northwest and one to the southwest.  Farther to the west, a turnip patch spreads out, the tops of the vegetables forming curving rows.

Two circular pens stand, one to the northwest and one to the southwest.  Long cedar planks intersect within holes cut in vertical cedar beams.  The planks stack up four high, with the width of a plank between each.  This is easily adequate to contain animals that do not tend to jump, such as roltons.  Farther to the west, a turnip patch spreads out, the tops of the vegetables forming curving rows.  Paths also lead northeast, east, and southeast through the scrubby weeds.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: The rounded tops of turnip roots protrude slightly from the loam in this garden area.

The rounded tops of turnip roots protrude slightly from the loam in this garden area.  Though the area is littered with large rocks, the sandy consistency of the soil creates an excellent location for growing root crops.  The turnips are planted in long rows, with a foot or so between the rows.  In each row, the plants are spaced only a few inches apart.  Unfortunately, the weeds also find this sort of soil to be particularly inviting.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: The rows of turnip wind about the landscape, avoiding large rocks and finding the best patches of soil.

The rows of turnips wind about the landscape, avoiding large rocks and finding the best patches of soil.  To the west, a long, deep culvert defines the western end of the turnip patch.  The culvert carries a slight bit of water southward, keeping the turnip patch well drained so that the turnip roots do not become soggy and rotten.  Thus it can rain often in the area, but the porous soil and the flanking culvert keep the soil moisture at a level conducive to growing turnips.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: Long rows of turnips run northeast and southwest, except when they have to detour around large rocks.

Long rows of turnips run northeast and southwest, except when they have to detour around large rocks.  A long, deep culvert parallels the rows on the northwest side, carrying drainage from the northeast to the southwest.  The ground has slumped into the culvert, perhaps because the soil was too waterlogged after recent rains, and many plants in the westernmost rows have been lost to the collapse while the next closest row has many roots exposed.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: The soil in the north end of the turnip patch is not in the best of shape.  Rocks abundantly poke through the surface, and a plethora of weeds encroaches on the planting area despite the indications of heavy hoeing.

The soil in the north end of the turnip patch is not in the best of shape.  Rocks abundantly poke through the surface, and a plethora of weeds encroaches on the planting area despite the indications of heavy hoeing.  The soil has lost much of its dark color, indicating that the nutrients it might have once held are either now in possession of the weeds or have washed down the culvert that flanks the area to the northwest.  The turnips are stunted and don't appear happy about the situation at all.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: The long rows of turnips course off to the northeast, southwest and southeast like dark grey ribbons laid over a mottled, light grey quilt.

The long rows of turnips course off to the northeast, southwest and southeast like dark grey ribbons laid over a mottled, light grey quilt.  Something seems to be amiss with many of the turnips in the nearby rows, though.  Something has taken large bites of out some of them.  Others are completely missing their leaves.  Some are merely uprooted, while others appear to have completely disappeared.  Rolton tracks are evident in the soft soil.

The long rows of turnips course off to the northeast, southwest and southeast like dark green ribbons laid over a mottled green and brown quilt.  Something seems to be amiss with many of the turnips in the nearby rows, though.  Something has taken large bites of out some of them.  Others are completely missing their leaves.  Some are merely uprooted, while others appear to have completely disappeared.  Rolton tracks are evident in the soft soil.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: A wide, deep culvert cuts between the turnip patch on the east side and a corn field on the west side.

A wide, deep culvert cuts between the turnip patch on the east side and a corn field on the west side.  Muddy water in the culvert flows slowly southward, carrying silt from the farmlands to the north.  The turnips in this area have been trampled, and their leaves are smashed and torn.  Rolton tracks are abundantly evident in the moist soil.  The tracks lead off in all directions, though, giving no clear indication of the perpetrators' whereabouts.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: The battle between farmer and nature is quite evident in this portion of the turnip patch.

The battle between farmer and nature is quite evident in this portion of the turnip patch.  Weeds grow abundantly among the turnips near the boulder to the southeast, clustering around the outnumbered turnip plants.  Just to the northwest, someone has taken a hoe to the weeds that infested several of the turnip rows.  These weeds are now dead, their roots exposed and their stems and leaves shriveled.  It is a constant battle to see if the hoe will be faster than the weed.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: To the west, a stately oak tree spreads its branches over the culvert and part of the turnip patch.

To the west, a stately oak tree spreads its branches over the culvert and part of the turnip patch.  The oak's roots spread throughout the culvert to draw up the moisture that resides there, and the oak appears healthy and well nourished.  The oak's branches allow plenty of light to reach the turnips during the day, and the plants grow well despite the presence of their larger cousin.  For reasons unknown, the farmer has allowed this tree to remain.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: Turnips grow abundantly, their leaves spreading out in small canopies above the widening root crowns.

Turnips grow abundantly, their leaves spreading out in small canopies above the widening root crowns.  As evidenced by the dead weeds and disturbed soil between the turnip rows, this section has recently seen the passing of the hoe.  Live weeds still crowd the edges of the patch, looking over their fallen comrades expressionlessly, but they are unable to do anything about the uprooted weeds' plights.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: A wide slough spreads out to the west.  The marshy area has been created by the runoff from the upper sections of the farmlands to the north, northwest and northeast, and the blocking action of the stone wall that runs along the farmlands' south border.  The soil becomes too wet for turnip plants at the edge of the slough, and the cattails and bulrushes make certain that any turnips valiantly attempting to survive get choked off mercilessly.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: The ground slopes downward to the southwest and becomes soggier in that direction.

The ground slopes downward to the southwest and becomes soggier in that direction.  Rainwater cascading from the huge boulder has furrowed the soil as it rushed southwestward, carrying dirt particles with it and leaving small channels of gravel and exposed stones.  For the time being the erosion is minor, but more rains could easily undermine the entire section and destroy all the turnips planted here.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: To the southeast, the turnip patch runs up against a long stone wall.

To the southeast, the turnip patch runs up against a long stone wall.  The wall stands three feet high and is formed of the same type of stones that appear scattered throughout the turnip patch.  The wall's stones are smaller than those found in the patch, though.  No mortar holds the stones together, and in places the stones look as though they have just been unceremoniously heaped with no attempt at fitting them together at all.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: The cedar planks and beams of a rolton pen stand to the northeast.  To the southwest, a huge boulder rises from the soil to tower over the turnip patch.

The cedar planks and beams of a rolton pen stand to the northeast, barely visible through a thick screen of tall weeds.  To the southwest, a huge boulder rises from the soil to tower over the turnip patch.  The granite boulder is at least three times as tall as a giantman and twice as wide as tall.  No handholds or other climbing aids appear on the lower surfaces of the boulder, though small birds have made a few nests in the upper crevices.

title: [Yander's Farm, Turnip Patch]
description: In some areas, such as this one, it seems as if there are more rocks than turnips.

In some areas, such as this one, it seems as if there are more rocks than turnips.  Large chunks of granite, slightly smoothed and rounded from the wind's erosive action, litter the area.  Their presence causes the turnip rows to twist and turn in order to use the maximum soil area possible.  The rocks are large enough that they defy easy removal, so the farmer has adapted.  If the rocks provide any benefit at all to the area, it is in the form of a low windbreak.

title: [Yander's Farm, Farmland Road]
description: The farmland road bends west and northeast on its way between the fields.

The farmland road bends west and northeast on its way between the fields.  The culvert on the northern side of the road turns and crosses the road to join with the culvert on the southern side of the road, and together they meander off to the southwest.  Wide cedar planks form a flat bridge spanning the northern culvert's change of course.  A spacious wheat field waves in the wind to the north, while a wide, rocky patch of ground harbors a turnip patch to the southeast.

title: [Yander's Farm, Farmland Road]
description: A juncture of three roads occurs amidst four different crop fields.  Culverts and ridges keep the fields from being accessible from this point.

A juncture of three roads occurs amidst four different crop fields.  Wheat grows directly to the north.  The even heights of the plants give the area the appearance of a long, flat sea of light and dark grey grain.  To the west a wide spiral of barley grows toward the heavens, while to the southwest long rows of corn, not yet tasseled, wave in the distance.  A turnip patch displays ribbons of turnip plants to the southeast.  Culverts and ridges keep the fields from being accessible from this point.

A turnip patch displays ribbons of turnip plants to the southeast.  Culverts and ridges keep the fields from being accessible from this point.

title: [Yander's Farm, Farmland Road]
description: The farmland road makes a right-angle turn, moving off to the north and west.  A small area of the shoulder allows a gentle climb down in the field of corn.

The farmland road makes a right-angle turn, moving off to the north and west.  The culvert paralleling the road on the east side, however, continues to the south, emptying out into a wide slough where the water pools among the thick weeds.  Just to the southwest the road's shoulder plunges down a steep embankment and into a corn field.  A small area of the shoulder, perhaps no more than ten feet wide, allows a gentler climb down in the field of corn.

title: [Yander's Farm, Farmland Road]
description: The farmland road ends at the western edge of the farmland.  The embankment separating the field and the road levels, allowing access to the corn field.

The farmland road ends at the western edge of the farmland.  To the west the weeds cluster thickly, and beyond them the forest presents an impenetrable barrier to travel.  The corn field that parallels the road to the south also ends, the corn stalks competing with the encroaching forest shrubs and vines.  Many of these wild interlopers have been intercepted as evidenced by the large piles of cut brush and wood.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: Tightly spaced corn stalks sweep southwest and southeast like dark green soldiers standing at attention.

Tightly spaced corn stalks sweep southwest and southeast like dark green soldiers standing at attention.  Their long, ribbed leaves wave slowly in the warm breeze, flapping against each other to produce a quick fluttering sound whenever a sudden gust of wind blows through.  The soil is dark and crumbly, and the corn stalks appear healthy despite the presence of thousands of weeds that enjoy the two feet of unplanted soil between the rows.
paths: Obvious paths: southeast, south, southwest, out

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: The forest to the west and the sweeping corn fields practically collide, with only a small amount of weed-infested space between them.

The forest to the west and the sweeping corn fields practically collide, with only a small amount of weed-infested space between them.  Dark spots on the trunks of nearby trees suggest that the forest was partially burned away just recently in order to reclaim farming land.  The corn stalks do not appear to be flourishing on the recently cleared land, but rather are surviving adequately.  Many of them have chewed leaves, but that is to be expected being so close to the herbivores' safe cover.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: Here at the far southwest corner of the corn fields, the soil is poor and yields little in the way of nutrients.

Here at the far southwest corner of the corn fields, the soil is poor and yields little in the way of nutrients.  The nearby forest trees and bushes have sapped the available nutrients over the years, and even though the closest trees have been cleared away, the soil has not yet had time to recover.  The corn stalks are barely a foot high, and more light grey than dark grey.  Even the weeds do not seem to like the soil here, evidenced by the large patches of totally barren ground.

Here at the far southwest corner of the corn fields, the soil is poor and yields little in the way of nutrients.  The nearby forest trees and bushes have sapped the available nutrients over the years, and even though the closest trees have been cleared away, the soil has not yet had time to recover.  The corn stalks are barely a foot high, and more yellow than green.  Even the weeds do not seem to like the soil here, evidenced by the large patches of totally barren ground.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: Something is not right with the corn stalks here.  Dark brown growths protrude from the stalks just above the leaves, and the leaves themselves are shot with yellow veins.

Something is not right with the corn stalks here.  Dark brown growths protrude from the stalks just above the leaves, and the leaves themselves are shot with yellow veins.  The tops of the corn stalks are stunted and twisted.  A few of the growths have broken open to exhibit a black, powdery discharge.  Whatever it is appears to be confined to a few dozen stalks or so, but these must be quickly destroyed before the infection spreads.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: A large corn crib stands just to the south, awaiting the harvest that is yet to come.

A large corn crib stands just to the south, awaiting the harvest that is yet to come.  Long cedar slats are nailed to tall cedar beams, with just enough space in between the slats to allow air circulation to dry the feed corn.  The cribs are only three feet deep but ten feet high and fifteen feet wide.  A large, hinged door in the top allows corn to be poured in from above, while a small door at the bottom center of each crib allows the dried feed corn to be removed.  No corn occupies the crib.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: The rows of corn stalks sweep northwest and east, following the best soil.

The rows of corn stalks sweep northwest and east, following the best soil.  To the south, weeds occupy a large plot of fallow ground.  The ground is flat, and appears to once have been turned over by the plow.  Now it rests, acquiring nutrients and awaiting another planting season.  It will then be of better use to the farmer.  Beyond the fallow ground, farther south, a long stone wall extends northeast and southwest, most likely paralleling the Victory Road.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: The tracks of some large herbivore run up and down the area between the rows of corn stalks.

The tracks of some large herbivore run up and down the area between the rows of corn stalks.  The tracks indicate that the herbivore or herbivores traveled in both directions, and the sheer number of tracks would lead one to believe that there were many of these creatures.  Interestingly, none of the corn stalks appear to be eaten at all.  Perhaps the herbivores were just on their way to tastier fare somewhere else on the farm.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: The wind, combined with heavy rains, has wreaked some havoc among the corn stalks in this area of the field.

The wind, combined with heavy rains, has wreaked some havoc among the corn stalks in this area of the field.  Dozens of stalks have been blown over to block the areas between the rows.  Caution must be used to step over and between them when proceeding.  Some are already raising themselves back toward an upright position, while others have compensated by sending new growth upward from the main stalk's reclining position.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: The southeast end of the corn field meets the northwest corner of the slough.

The southeast end of the corn field meets the northwest corner of the slough.  The result is a messy conglomeration of mud, cattails, and corn stalks.  The mud and cattails intrude upon the neatly arranged corn area, causing the corn stalks to only grow to half their normal size in the soggy ground.  If less rain occurs, though, the mud will dry out, leaving the cattails to wither and the corn stalks to grow healthier and taller.  One never knows about the weather.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: Parallel rows of tall corn stalks march off to the west.  Their glossy, dark leaves wave lazily in the warm breeze, and their tops bend back and forth only slightly.  No ears yet adorn the stalks, and only a few of the stalks extend grainy tassels toward the sky.  The corn stalks are spaced only half a foot apart in the rows, creating a dense grey curtain when viewed from the north.  Each row is two feet from the next, giving the effect of parallel vegetation channels when viewed from the east.

No ears yet adorn the stalks, and only a few of the stalks extend grainy tassels toward the sky.  The corn stalks are spaced only half a foot apart in the rows, creating a dense green curtain when viewed from the north. title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: Though the wind blowing across the corn field is cool and somewhat dry, the moisture rising from the wet ground in between the rows creates pockets of still, clammy air.

Though the wind blowing across the corn field is cool and somewhat dry, the moisture rising from the wet ground in between the rows creates pockets of still, clammy air.  Droplets of condensation cling to skin, clothing, armor, and most anything on which they can collect.  Then they combine with other droplets, running in sticky rivulets in between skin and clothing to drip back again on the damp soil underfoot.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: Smaller nuisance animals can be trapped or poisoned.  Larger nuisance animals can be fenced out.  Nuisance weeds, however, never seem to be driven away entirely.  Weeds of various shapes and sizes insinuate themselves among the corn stalk and cover the soil in the areas between the rows.  Hoeing removes the larger ones, but new weeds soon spring up in their place.  It would be so much easier to just grow weeds.
Weeds of various shapes and sizes insinuate themselves among the corn stalk and cover the soil in the areas between the rows.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: The corn stalks sweep southward to avoid a cluster of large rocks.

The corn stalks sweep southward to avoid a cluster of large rocks.  A huge boulder, twenty feet wide and equally high, holds sway in the soft soil and weeds.  Around it cluster eight smaller boulders, large in their own right, but dwarfed by the giant they surround.  They wait patiently, as they have probably waited for hundreds, even thousands of years, for a word of advice from the larger, obviously more successful boulder.

title: [Yander's Farm, Corn Fields]
description: A headless scarecrow hangs from a cedar pole amidst the corn stalks.

A headless scarecrow hangs from a cedar pole amidst the corn stalks.  A brown canvas shirt, tightly stuffed with dried wheat sheaves, sits atop a pair of blue canvas pants, equally stuffed with the same material.  The shirt's sleeves have been stuffed in such a manner that they protrude outward at right angles to the body of the shirt, as if the scarecrow is waiting to catch something large or about to flap its arms.  From the liberal amount of bird droppings on the shirt, the birds are unimpressed.

title: [Yander's Farm, Farmland Road]
description: The road disappears into the scrub weeds as it approaches a spiral field of barley.

The road disappears into the weeds as it approaches a spiral field of barley.  The weeds clamber over the road and insinuate themselves in the wheel ruts, unaware that the crushing wheels may very well return again to evict the squatters from their new-found homes.  Barley, planted in a wide, tight row, spirals toward a center point to the southwest.  The spiral takes advantage of the flat, marshy terrain of the field, allowing a trench to follow the spiral on both sides and drain off excess water.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: Rows of barley, tightly bunched, form a long, dark ribbon that spirals through the field to the southwest.

Rows of barley, tightly bunched, form a long, dark ribbon that spirals through the field to the southwest.  The spiral begins with a wide loop that encompasses the ends of the field, then revolves inward until it runs out of room in the middle of the field and comes to a halt.  Two small trenches, one on either side of the spiral, drain water away from the barley plants and keep their roots dry.  The trenches themselves are too muddy to traverse.

Rows of barley, tightly bunched, form a long, green ribbon that spirals through the field to the southwest.  The spiral begins with a wide loop that encompasses the ends of the field, then revolves inward until it runs out of room in the middle of the field and comes to a halt.  Two small trenches, one on either side of the spiral, drain water away from the barley plants and keep their roots dry.  The trenches themselves are too muddy to traverse.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The barley plants march east and west in a slow arc, keeping their spacing consistent.

The barley plants march east and west in a slow arc, keeping their spacing consistent.  When the rows encounter a rock too large to be removed, they merely stop and continue along on the other side of the rock.  Occasionally weeds insinuate themselves in between the barley plants, but for the most part the barley seems to hold its own, keeping out the unwanted interlopers and maintaining the purity of their ranks.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: Several tall sycamore trees loom close to the barley plants.

Several tall sycamore trees loom close to the barley plants.  The sycamore roots heave up the ground all around the trees, disturbing the barley plants nearby and sucking water and nutrients from the soil.  However, the sycamores make up for this by providing a windbreak.  The trees' spreading branches and wide leaves act like natural baffles, intercepting the wind gusts and calming them into soft, gentle breezes.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The thick, deciduous forest looms close to the barley field at the western edge of the spiral.

The thick, deciduous forest looms close to the barley field at the western edge of the spiral.  Tall birches, walnuts, and elms peer out from their lofty places as if eyeing the farmlands and waiting to reclaim what should be rightfully theirs.  Underneath, prickly, twisting brambles press toward the barley, moving inch by inch and reclaiming small bits of land until driven back by the saw or the flame.  Weeds, the vanguards of the forest's flora troops, already raid the fields in various places.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The ground is very moist, and water seeps up around boots and feet.

The ground is very moist, and water seeps up around boots and feet.  The tracks of hoofed animals are plainly evident in the wet clay soil.  Lower than most of the areas around it, this portion of the barley fields collects much of the runoff from the rains.  The barley plants here seem to be surviving well despite the increased amount of soil moisture. To the east, though, the plants appear to be suffering from an overabundance of water.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: A thin sheen of water covers the ground in the southern portion of the barley fields.

A thin sheen of water covers the ground in the southern portion of the barley fields.  Cloying mud sticks to shoes and feet as if the soil is filled with glue. Bad drainage apparently has backed up the rainwater, and the barley plants here are definitely not happy about it.  The plants are much shorter than those in the fields to the north and lack the dark coloration prevalent in healthy plants.  The area could definitely benefit from the digging of a drainage ditch.

Bad drainage apparently has backed up the rainwater, and the barley plants here are definitely not happy about it.  The plants are much shorter than those in the fields to the north and lack the dark green coloration prevalent in healthy plants.  The area could definitely benefit from the digging of a drainage ditch.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The barley spiral sweeps from west to north in a wide arc, tightening its angle just slightly as it proceeds northward.

Water squishes up from the soil to cover boots and feet with a wet layer of silt, and the barley plants lean precariously as one steps in between them.  The plants appear to be tolerating the moist conditions well, especially compared to their cousins to the west.  To the north, the soil appears to be much drier and the footing much firmer.  The barley spiral sweeps from west to north in a wide arc, tightening its angle just slightly as it proceeds northward.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The tight lines of barley plants arc to the northwest and south.

The tight lines of barley plants arc to the northwest and south.  A large number of heavy rocks infest the area, and the number of barley plants is reduced proportionally.  The rocks stick up from the soil at odd angles.  Some are long and thin, protruding more horizontal than vertical.  Others are just strangely shaped, as if some rock-eating creature had come along and taken big bites out of them.  Still others are just normal, everyday, run-of-the-mill, round boulders.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The barley field is a buzz of activity--literally.  Gnats, flies, and other small flying insects wing their way over the green plants, alighting here and there.

The barley field is a buzz of activity--literally.  Gnats, flies, and other small flying insects wing their way over the green plants, alighting here and there with no apparent sense of purpose or direction.  Spiders weave their webs between and within the plants in hopes of intercepting some of these airborne insects.  Snails and slugs crawl slowly underneath the plants, searching for decaying matter to consume, while lines of ants industriously move food into their conical mound.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The wide ribbon of barley continues its slow spiral, like following the curvature of a ram's horn or a snail shell.  Unlike these examples from nature, the ribbon does not become any narrower as it moves toward the center.  The plants retain their same spacing, both between plants within a row and between rows.  The farmer's consistency is also displayed in the trenches that flank the barley ribbon.  These also do not vary in their width.

The wide green ribbon of barley continues its slow spiral, like following the curvature of a ram's horn or a snail shell.  Unlike these examples from nature, the ribbon does not become any narrower as it moves toward the center.  The plants retain their same spacing, both between plants within a row and between rows.  The farmer's consistency is also displayed in the trenches that flank the barley ribbon.  These also do not vary in their width.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: Something has decided to dine on the barley plants here.  Hoofed tracks in the flanking trench show that a heavy beast came through the barley traveling south.

Something has decided to dine on the barley plants here.  Hoofed tracks in the flanking trench show that a heavy beast came through the barley traveling south.  From the chewed appearance of the plants, it took its time filling its belly.  Many of the plants have been consumed right down to the soil level, while many others display ripped and torn leaves.  Crushed plants indicate the beast moved off to the southeast, perhaps to the turnip fields for an after-dinner dessert.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The rows of barley plants make a sharp turn from the west to the northwest, or vice versa, depending upon which way one is traveling.

The rows of barley plants make a sharp turn from the west to the northwest, or vice versa, depending upon which way one is traveling.  It appears as though the farmer has taken a little time recently to drag the hoe between these rows of plants.  Only a few weeds cautiously extend their stalks or leaves above the level of the barley plants, and the dirt between has been recently turned over.  The barley plants appear healthy and vigorous, appreciative of the weeding efforts.

title: [Yander's Farm, Barley Fields]
description: The wide ribbon of barley plants finally reaches a dead-end in the middle of the spiral.

The wide ribbon of barley plants finally reaches a dead-end in the middle of the spiral.  The farmer displays a slight bit of design sense here.  The rows do not just end, though.  Instead the inside rows connect to each other.  Then the next row on each side makes a curve to connect.  This occurs again and again until finally the outside rows arc around and join, giving the end of the ribbon a symmetrical, rounded appearance.

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: A sea of mottled grey wheat stretches out to the northwest, west, and southwest, its surface only a few feet high.

A sea of mottled grey wheat stretches out to the northwest, west, and southwest, its surface only a few feet high.  The stalks, heavy with their nearly ripened kernels, wave slowly back and forth in the warm, gentle wind.  The ground underfoot is soft, springy and just a little moist.  To the southeast, the farmland road runs between fields, while in the northwest distance a line of birch trees blocks the horizon.

A sea of brown-and-green wheat stretches out to the northwest, west, and southwest, its surface only a few feet high.  The stalks, heavy with their nearly ripened kernels, wave slowly back and forth in the warm, gentle wind.  The ground underfoot is soft, springy and just a little moist.  To the southeast, the farmland road runs between fields, while in the northwest distance a line of birch trees blocks the horizon.

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: The wheat field has a sea-like appearance.  Almost all the wheat stalks are the same length, presenting their kernels at nearly the same height to give a smooth, level look to the surrounding wheat.  As the wind blows, the stalks ripple.  Since the air moves in small gusts, though, the rippling is not all over the field all at once, but proceeds in waves from one end to the other, much like swells move across a large body of water.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: A deep culvert runs northeast and southwest, marking the southeast border of the wheat fields.

A deep culvert runs northeast and southwest, marking the southeast border of the wheat fields.  A small amount of water trickles toward the southwest, carrying a bit of silt downstream with it.  Rocks line the culvert's sides, but these appear to be more stones that have been unearthed by the passing water rather than those purposely brought to shore up the embankments.  The farmland road runs along the other side.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: Here, farthest from the birch tree windbreak at the wheat fields's northern border, the wind picks up speed again, forcing the wheat stalks to bend heavily under the faster gusts.

Here, farthest from the birch tree windbreak at the wheat fields's northern border, the wind picks up speed again, forcing the wheat stalks to bend heavily under the faster gusts.  The stalks curve with the wind, and when the wind abates for a few seconds, they do not spring back to a vertical alignment.  The stalks also have fewer kernels, as the wind has interfered with the initial growth, causing dried kernels to fall and leaving the gaps in the lines.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, west, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: Small mounds of dirt can be seen here and there under the wheat.  Fire ants emerge from the mounds to collect food, returning to the mounds to deposit their bounty and go out once again.

Small mounds of dirt can be seen here and there under the wheat.  Fire ants emerge from the mounds and tread preset paths to collect food, returning to the mounds to deposit their bounty and go out once again.  The ants seem unperturbed by the presence of anything around them until their mounds are disturbed, and then they boil from the ground in a frenzy of military activity.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: Weeds insinuate themselves among the wheat stalks, digging in and taking over wherever they can find an opening.

Weeds insinuate themselves among the wheat stalks, digging in and taking over wherever they can find an opening.  The height of the wheat discourages or kills many of the low-growing types of weeds, but the taller weeds grow as fast or faster than the wheat, shooting up to drink in the available light.  These weeds will be cut down with the wheat, separated at the threshing floor, and burned or discarded.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: The fields of wheat stretch off in every direction.  Here and there boulders protrude up through the wheat, like whales breaching through the ocean of grain.  To the north, past the grain, a long line of birch treess presents a rustling grey curtain against the darkened sky.  The trees and the grain sway almost in unison with the passing of the soft breeze.

The fields of wheat stretch off in every direction.  Here and there boulders protrude up through the wheat, like whales breaching through the ocean of grain.  To the north, past the golden grain, a long line of birch trees presents a rustling green curtain against the blue sky.  The trees and the grain sway almost in unison with the passing of the soft breeze.

The fields of wheat stretch off in every direction.  Here and there boulders protrude up through the wheat, like whales breaching through the ocean of grain.  To the north, past the grain, a long line of birch trees presents a rustling grey curtain against the darkened sky.  The trees and the grain sway almost in unison with the passing of the soft breeze.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: A particularly large boulder rests in the soil.  Wheat surrounds it on all sides, pressing up close to the boulder's granite sides.  Small tunnels extend underneath the boulder, leading away quickly into darkness.  The tunnels are no more than a few inches across, and small squeakings and chitterings emanate from the holes.  Occasionally a rustling sound comes from somewhere just out of sight in the wheat, but no creatures ever pop out of the holes.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: The land dips slightly, creating a low spot in the wheat fields and collecting more moisture than the surrounding areas.

The land dips slightly, creating a low spot in the wheat fields and collecting more moisture than the surrounding areas.  Mushy ground sucks at feet and boots, attempting to trap anyone moving through the area.  The wheat appears healthy enough, though a little shorter than the wheat in the surrounding areas.  Unseen bullfrogs voice their opinions in deep croaks all around the area.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: Long, jagged furrows start out thin and shallow near the center of this part of the wheat field then widen and deepen until they plunge over the side of the culvert that skirts the field's southwestern edge.

Long, jagged furrows start out thin and shallow near the center of this part of the wheat field then widen and deepen until they plunge over the side of the culvert that skirts the field's southwestern edge.  Apparently heavy rains combined with the slight cant of the field caused the water to drain from the field faster than anticipated, and the result is a loss of wheat to the rocky bottom of the culvert and further downstream.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: The stone wall that defines the farmlands' northern border stops at a twisted, tight thicket to the west.

The stone wall that defines the farmlands' northern border stops at a twisted, tight thicket to the west.  Long, sharp thorns protrude dangerously from the woody plants that cover the slightly marshy ground.  The cheeping of small birds, the croaking of frogs, and the chirping of crickets pour happily out of the dark depths of the thicket.  There appears to be no way into the mass of pointed needles, but there also appears to be no reason for anyone to want to go in there, either.

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: Several rocks have been pushed off the top of the stone wall.  The rocks have rolled into the wheat field, rolling over and smashing down the wheat in their path before finally coming to a stop.
paths: Obvious paths: east, southeast, south, southwest, west

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: A long line of tall tall birch trees stands slightly into the grasslands just behind the stone wall.

A long line of tall tall birch trees stands slightly into the grasslands just behind the stone wall.  Planted closely together, the narrow, leafy trees slow down the air currents, turning them from brisk winds into gentle breezes that merely caress the tops of the stalks.  The line of trees marches west and east, and the trees are positioned well to filter the prevailing winds that sweep down from the north.  All the birches are upright, straight, and appear to be in excellent health.
paths: Obvious paths: east, southeast, south, southwest, west

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: A stone wall varying between three and four feet high trudges west and east, separating the farmlands and fields from the grasslands to the north.

A stone wall varying between three and four feet high trudges west and east, separating the farmlands and fields from the grasslands to the north.  Large granite rocks, sometimes carefully piled, sometimes haphazardly piled, form the wall.  The wall appears to be built from rocks cleared from the fields, probably to serve the purpose of keeping large foraging animals out of the wheat.
paths: Obvious paths: southeast, south, southwest, west

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: Rocks occasionally protrude from the wheat field.  Some are tall enough to easily see above the stalks, and some are low enough to be only found by bumping into them.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: Some unknown creatures have crushed the wheat down and formed narrow paths in several directions.

Some unknown creatures have crushed the wheat down and formed narrow paths in several directions.  No wheat or weeds grow on the compacted trail of barren soil.  Wheat next to the trails is broken and beaten down, as if some of the creatures were not so good at staying on the straight and narrow.  However, the wheat in the fields is so thick overall that these trails are not discernible until you are nearly right on top of them.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest

title: [Yander's Farm, Wheat Fields]
description: The wheat stands mostly at the same height, and here and there holes appear where granite boulders occupy the growing area.  The rocks are few and far between, and the wheat is thick and abundant.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, northwest

title: [Barefoot Hill, Corner]
description: A huge pile of wheat chaff to the west spills through a thick patch of weeds at the western boundary of the field, the overflow of dusty material drifting into the muddy furrows to form a sticky, blackened muck between the rows.  The wind from that direction carries a faint smell of rotting turnips.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Abandoned Field]
description: A clump of brush nearby has been half charred, most of it lying on the ground in a pile of ash.  To the south, a sparse woodland edge is visible beyond a crumbling stone wall that borders the overgrown field.

Deep furrows can be glimpsed between the thin, tall grasses, the small trenches pooled with thick, inky-black water.  A clump of brush nearby has been half charred, most of it lying on the ground in a pile of ash.  To the south, a sparse woodland edge is visible beyond a crumbling stone wall that borders the overgrown field.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, west, northwest

title: [Barefoot Hill, Abandoned Field]
description: A large patch of wheat grows throughout the area, nearly blocking out the soft light of the moon with its tall stalks.  Some of the wheat appears to be matted, as if something had simply walked over it on their way through.  The flattened vegetation seems to follow some sort of curvy, winding trail, leading toward a towering dirt mound visible to the southeast.

A large patch of wheat grows throughout the area, nearly blocking out the harsh glare of the sun with its tall stalks.  Some of the wheat appears to be matted, as if something had simply walked over it on their way through.  The flattened vegetation seems to follow some sort of curvy, winding trail, leading toward a towering dirt mound visible to the southeast.
A large patch of wheat grows throughout the area.  Some of the wheat appears to be matted.  The flattened vegetation seems to follow some sort trail leading toward a towering dirt mound.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Field]
description: Fallen chunks of crumbling dirt and dried mud have fallen from the huge mound into a pile that nearly conceals the opening of a narrow tunnel leading into the towering structure.

Fallen chunks of crumbling dirt and dried mud have fallen from the huge mound into a pile that nearly conceals the opening of a narrow tunnel leading into the towering structure.  A crumbling stone wall separates the overgrown field from the sparse forest and the road beyond, and an acrid, burnt smell of charred vegetation and something fouler wafts through the cool night air.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Field]
description: Ancient oaks bound the southern edge of the field, shading the crumbling stone wall that marks the boundary between the weed-choked grassland and the road beyond.  Streaks of black ash and burnt grasses mar the vegetation in places, as if someone had scorched the ground and plants with many tiny fires.
Ancient oaks bound the southern edge of the field.  Streaks of black ash and burnt grasses mar the vegetation in places.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Abandoned Field]
description: Pale flecks of soot drift through the air here and there, dusting the ground with a light coating of grey.  The red dirt mound that towers above you is covered in places with ash.

Pale flecks of soot drift through the air here and there, dusting the ground with a light coating of grey.  The red dirt mound that towers above you is covered in places with ash, parts of its craggy, misshapen surface almost resembling the snow-covered slopes of a large mountain.  That illusion is quickly broken by sinuous waves of heat that occasionally blur and distort its outline as they rise upwards.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Outside Mound]
description: Smoldering piles of what may have been vegetation lie at the base of the large dirt mound, lending their foul, burnt smell to the dry air.  Small cracks riddle the structure's surface, scars from the intense heat that constantly bathes the area.  Several trenches in the dark red earth can be glimpsed at the borders of the towering hill, though black ash is the only thing that fills them.
Smoldering piles of what may have been vegetation lie at the base of the large dirt mound.  Several trenches in the dark red earth can be seen.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Outside Mound]
description: A faint, constant chittering sound seems to emanate from the huge mound of reddish earth and dried mud that towers above you, and now and then a small rock or clump of dried mud tumbles down the side of the steep slope as if something moving above has knocked it down.  The scrub brush and wild stalks of wheat grow more sparsely here, half-buried in piles of dirt and stones, and a sour, burnt odor fills the air.
A faint, constant chittering sound seems to emanate from the huge mound of reddish earth and dried mud that towers above you.  The scrub brush and wild stalks of wheat grow more sparsely here.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Outside Mound]
description: Thick patches of hardy underbrush and weeds grow against the side of the massive mound, their older and drier leaves and branches charred and falling to ash.  A low, dark tunnel leads into the side of the huge mound, the brush near its opening almost completely burned away.

Thick patches of hardy underbrush and weeds grow against the side of the massive mound, their older and drier leaves and branches charred and falling to ash.  An odd layer of blackened, burnt vegetation mixes with the reddish earth, sticking to your feet and clothing.  A low, dark tunnel leads into the side of the huge mound, the brush near its opening almost completely burned away.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Abandoned Field]
description: A huge, uneven mound of earth rises in the center of the weed-choked field just southwest of here, as tall as a three-story building.  The mound is too crude by far to have been built by the elves, its reddish-brown spires of dried mud rough and half-crumbled by the ravages of the weather, and skittering dark forms the size of large cats seem to be moving across its tortuous surface.

A huge, uneven mound of earth rises in the center of the weed-choked field just southwest of here.  The mound is too crude by far to have been built by the elves, its reddish-brown spires of dried mud rough and half-crumbled by the ravages of the weather.

title: [Barefoot Hill, Trail]
description: A grassy trail leads across the sparsely wooded hills to the northeast, nearly concealed by a patch of half-charred brush.

A grassy trail leads across the sparsely wooded hills to the northeast, nearly concealed by a patch of half-charred brush.  A spacious field stretches out to the southwest, its wild covering of weeds and scrub and neglected patches of wheat indicating that it has not been farmed in many years.

title: [Fearling Pass, Cobbled Road]
description: The surrounding wold is dotted with plenty of trees, mostly in clusters or small stands no where near as thick as the dark forest to the northwest.  Gently rolling hills are divided by a wide winding road, making it difficult to glimpse much of a view.  From time to time as the pass shifts, a bridge and what appears to be an island can be seen towards the south.

title: [Cleric Guild, Courtyard]
description: A limestone walkway crosses briefly with a tiny rivulet as it winds its way towards a mist-shrouded stone temple.  Rows of slender limbed trees nearly obscure the high seashell-inset walls that enclose this courtyard.  As the sea breeze propels the leafy foliage into motion, a shady bower reveals a darkened tunnel leading into the earth.

title: [Ta'Vaalor, Amaranth Bridge]
description: The thick limestone blocks of the bridge arc across the river, arching higher as they approach the center of the Mistydeep's breadth.  Few travellers cross the bridge at this late hour.  Those who do hurry along the way, heads down and fleet of foot.

The thick limestone blocks of the bridge arc across the river, sweeping higher as they approach the center of the Mistydeep's breadth.  Throngs of travelers and merchants push across the bridge, many carrying boxes and trundling small wagons loaded with goods in their wake.

title: [Ta'Vaalor, Amaranth Bridge]
description: The slope of the bridge runs downward towards the city gate, its polished limestone cobbles gleaming softly in the moonlight.  Several city guardsmen stand outside the gate, casually inspecting the passersby as they enter and exit the city.

The slope of the bridge runs downward towards the city gate, its polished limestone cobbles gleaming softly in the light.  Glittering ruby-hued pennants edged in golden thread flutter atop the massive city walls.  Several city guardsmen stand along the bridge's thick limestone walls, casually inspecting the passersby as they enter and exit the city.

title: [Cleric Guild, Tunnel]
description: Cramped walls of cavernous earth stretch out before you, a natural incline leading deeper down into the darkness.  Small bits of colorful coral are placed decoratively on ledges of rock, adding splashes of color to the rather mute grey surroundings.  The air is thick with the pungent smell of sea-salt, and small drops of condensation trail softly along the walls giving them a glistening sheen.

title: [White Marble Table]
description: The square marble table's top matches perfectly with the marble in the second tier of the huge fountain that looms to the northeast.  Thin golden strands course through the white marble, causing the surface to sparkle in the light.  The table's top has been buffed to a fine sheen, and the edges and supports are exactly chiseled.  An umbrella with a grey-and-white awning spreads out over the table in an attempt to shade the occupants from the sun.  A freestanding torch occupies a place near the table.

The square marble table's top matches perfectly with the marble in the second tier of the huge fountain that looms to the northeast.  Thin golden strands course through the white marble, causing the surface to sparkle in the light.  The table's top has been buffed to a fine sheen, and the edges and supports are exactly chiseled.  The table's grey-and-white umbrella is closed, allowing a breathtaking view of the constellation-filled night sky.  A freestanding torch flickers brightly nearby.

title: [Upper Dragonsclaw, Slopes]
description: The path ends at this point, replaced by a rugged trail that winds through high rock walls.  There is little in the way of vegetation here, and a cold wind from the southeast whips at your clothing.  In that direction, you see the faint beginnings of a mountain pass.

title: [Upper Dragonsclaw, Slopes]
description: The mountain pass here is narrow and the slope becomes more and more difficult to climb.  The way south is completely blocked by stones, boulders, and loose dirt, the rubble from an avalanche.  Just past the rubble you can barely see the beginnings of a rough trail.

title: [A Mountain Trail]
description: The trail here is barely passable, probably due to the avalanche that occurred here many years ago.

title: [Twin Canyons, Rocky Pass]
description: Jagged outcrops of craggy rocks split the valley into twin canyons.  Small rocks skitter down the steep walls of the canyon and form small wisps of dust that look like rising steam.  Cold air flows steadily north out of both canyons as the night cools the rock faces to near freezing temperatures.  Very faint chattering sounds can be heard coming from large cracks in the rock outcrop to the south.

Jagged outcrops of craggy rocks split the valley into twin canyons.  Small rocks skitter down the steep walls of the canyon creating small wisps of dust that look like rising steam while the cool rock of the canyon floor creates a stream of cool air that flows steadily north out of both canyons.  Very faint chattering sounds can be heard coming from large cracks in the rock outcrop to the south.

title: [Twin Canyons, Eastern Canyon]
description: Crisp air swirls here, carrying little chattering sounds that echo around the canyon.  The wind has frozen the surfaces of small puddles of water that have collected in weatherworn divots on the canyon floor.  Small patches of lichen are the only signs of vegetation within the canyon, though the thickly wooded northern slope of The Krag is visible above the canyon rim.  In the southwestern wall a small crack can barely be made out in the shadows of the canyon.

Crisp air swirls here, carrying little chattering sounds that echo around the canyon.  The wind disturbs the surfaces of small puddles of water that have collected in weatherworn divots on the canyon floor.  Small patches of lichen are the only signs of vegetation within the canyon, though the thickly wooded northern slope of The Krag is visible above the canyon rim.  In the southwestern wall a small crack about three feet high and a foot wide can be seen.

title: [Twin Canyons, Eastern Canyon]
description: Jutting up like a knife, a rift in the rock floor rises two feet, forming a large step.  The canyon widens here allowing large portions of the silvery night sky to be seen.  Resting along the northeast wall of the canyon, piles of rubble show signs of recent additions.  Echoing sounds can be heard from all directions while a chattering noise can be heard from the south, coming from wide cracks in the rock outcrop.

Jutting up like a knife, a rift in the rock floor rises two feet, forming a large step.  The canyon widens here allowing sunlight to illuminate the area.  Resting along the northeast wall of the canyon, piles of rubble show signs of recent additions.  Echoing sounds can be heard from all directions while a chattering noise can be heard from the south, coming from wide cracks in the rock outcrop.

title: [Twin Canyons, Eastern Canyon]
description: Turning to the south, the canyon follows the outcrop that separates it from its western twin.  Visible in the distance is the southern junction of the canyons at the base of the southern canyon wall.  Rubble piles along the eastern wall show signs of very recent additions and join with a huge pile of rubble further south in the canyon.  Barely visible above the rim of the canyon, The Krag's snow-covered peak appears like a pointed diamond set in the silvery night sky.

Turning to the south, the canyon follows the outcrop that separates it from its western twin.  Visible in the distance is the southern junction of the canyons at the base of the southern canyon wall.  Rubble piles along the eastern wall show signs of very recent additions and join with a huge pile of rubble further south in the canyon.  Barely visible above the rim of the canyon, The Krag's snow-covered peak can be seen scraping the sky.

title: [Twin Canyons, Canyon Junction]
description: Rubble from the collapsed eastern wall litters the ground while the rockslide rises over two hundred feet up the eastern end of the canyon.  The wall beyond the rubble is extremely jagged and appears to be unstable as small rocks are constantly falling free and joining their predecessors on the rockslide.  To the north the eastern branch of the twin canyons works its way around the rock outcrop that splits the pair, while to the west jagged rocks jut up amidst a covering of eerily dancing mist and steam.

The wall beyond the rubble is extremely jagged and appears to be unstable as small rocks are constantly falling free and joining their predecessors on the rockslide.  To the north the eastern branch of the twin canyons works its way around the rock outcrop that splits the pair, while to the west jagged rocks jut up amidst a covering of mist and steam.

title: [Twin Canyons, Western Canyon]
description: Jagged rocks protrude from the floor as wisps of steam dance in the swirling air.  The cold night air causes the steam to crystallize, making the air shimmer with dancing sparkles as the ice reflects the silvery night sky.  The floor is pitted and cracked and extremely hot causing the water dripping off the southern wall to hiss as it evaporates on impact.  The sounds of hissing steam overwhelm all others and deafen the echoes present in the rest of the canyon.

Jagged rocks protrude from the floor as wisps of steam dance in the swirling air.  The floor is pitted and cracked and extremely hot, causing the water dripping off the southern wall to hiss as it evaporates on impact.  The sound of hissing steam overwhelms all others and deafens the echoes present in the rest of the canyon.  To the east the junction of the canyons can be seen at the base of a collapsed canyon wall while to the west, a tree can be seen growing on a ledge, high on the western wall.

title: [Twin Canyons, Western Canyon]
description: Towering over five hundred feet, the southern wall of the canyon stands like a void against the silvery night sky.  Rubble forms a ramp up to the western canyon wall where a ledge can barely be discerned high above.  The canyon junction can be seen to the distant east as the canyon turns again, around the central rock outcrop.  Heat wafts up from the canyon floor here, where it is almost uncomfortably warm, while small puddles of glowing yellowish water bubble to the surface.

Towering over five hundred feet, the southern wall of the canyon blocks out half the sky.  Rubble forms a ramp up to the western canyon wall where a ledge can be seen about two hundred and fifty feet high.  The canyon junction can be seen to the distant east as the canyon turns again, around the central rock outcrop.  Heat wafts up from the canyon floor here, where it is almost uncomfortably warm, while small puddles of yellowish water bubble to the surface.
paths: Obvious paths: northeast, east, northwest, up

title: [Twin Canyons, Western Canyon]
description: Rising higher and higher, the walls of the canyon leave only a small sliver of the night sky visible overhead.  Falling pebbles create a constant background of echoes that disrupt a continuous chattering noise emanating from cracks in the northeast face of the rock outcrop.  To the south, the steep southern wall of the canyon can be seen as a towering black void against the silver night sky.

Rising higher and higher, the walls of the canyon leave only a small sliver of daylight visible overhead.  Falling pebbles create a constant background of echoes that disrupt a continuous chattering noise emanating from cracks in the northeast face of the rock outcrop.  To the south, the steep southern wall of the canyon can be seen towering several hundred feet into the sky.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, southeast, northwest

title: [Twin Canyons, Western Canyon]
description: Making a slight bend here, the canyon winds its way around the rock outcrop.  Deep shadows permeate the canyon as it narrows, making the darkness of night seem almost an ink black void.  Chattering noises can be distinctly heard from a large crack in the rockface to the east while water slowly drips from icicles that hang from smaller cracks in the southern canyon wall.

Making a slight bend here, the canyon winds its way around the rock outcrop.  Deep shadows hug the southern wall as the canyon narrows, forcing the sunlight to diffuse higher on the walls.  Chattering noises can be distinctly heard from a large crack in the rockface to the east, while water slowly drips from smaller cracks in the southern canyon wall.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: Poised on the very edge of a canyon wall, you look upon the brink of a seemingly bottomless pit, your feet threatening to slip out from beneath you and plunge you into the dark depths below.  The distance across the chasm is not too great, and you ponder the wisdom of trying to cross it.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: A worn mountain trail climbs up the side of the slope.  Sparse patches of vegetation testify to the harsh conditions of this rocky mountainside.  A deep chasm yawns to the north, its depths lost in the darkness as it seems to swallow the dim light that manages its way past the towering heights to the south.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The mountain trail wanders up the side of the slope becoming readily steeper.  Just off the side of the path, a darkened recess in the face of the slope draws your attention.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The slope grows even steeper as the mountain trail gives way to little more than an uneven path.  A blanket of gloom permeates the surrounding dark rock that is obviously the result of volcanic activity.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The trees and foliage are becoming sparser, their roots finding it difficult to gain purchase in the mountainside as the soil gives way to rockier terrain.  The dark adit of a cave can be seen just up the side of the slope.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: Standing upright becomes more difficult as the path becomes less discernible among the barren rocks.  What manner of creature could endure living in such a hostile environment?

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: A crushed skull and a few scattered bones lie just outside a deep breach in the wall facing.  Perhaps the looming darkness of the breach offers some blessed relief from the biting cold and sharp wind.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The bitterly cold wind screeches endlessly as it batters against the barren, blackened rocks.  No sign of life can be found in this desolate place.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The almost nonexistent trail wanders onward past a gaping aperture at the base of a sheer wall of rock.  The biting wind and penetrating dampness combine into an onslaught of misery for any hapless traveler of this region.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: A scraggly modwir tree cants to one side as it struggles to maintain a lifehold in this desolate place.  It is difficult to actually see the trail as it climbs higher, flanked on either side by steep lava rock.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: Movement over the rough, uneven terrain is slow and very taxing, allowing more time for the frigid air to penetrate clothing and set teeth chattering.  The deadly combination of severe cold and increased exertion is sure to dull the senses of the unwary hunter.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: A tremendous landslide has tumbled rocks and boulders over much of the miniscule track, all but barring passage.  Beyond the rubble, a grotesque pile of rotting bodies lies outside a narrow crack in the crumbling wall ahead.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The biting winds that echo through this narrow passage sound like screeching banshees after they have sighted fresh prey.  Rising abruptly from the lava bed is a giant-sized rock, topped by a slack-jawed human skull.  Was the skull placed here as a warning?

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The fierce wind sends low-lying clouds scudding across the path, almost obscuring the fact that one side of the rock has fallen away and the way forward becomes a narrow ledge.  A long fissure has been gouged in the dark rock, barely visible in the covering darkness.

The fierce wind sends low-lying clouds scudding across the path, almost obscuring the fact that one side of the rock has fallen away and the way forward becomes a narrow ledge.  A long fissure has been gouged in the dark rock, barely visible in the deep shadows that linger there.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The misting clouds that blanket the ground separate intermittently to reveal a tiny path more fitting for a mountain rolton to use than a hunter with only two legs!  The howling wind is persistent in its attempts to toss unsuspecting wayfarers from their precarious perch and send them plummeting over the precipice to certain death.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The incline of the mountainside has become steeper, and finding purchase on the barren rocks is even more difficult.  Strangely, it sounds as if the wind is whistling through an opening, but none is in sight.

title: [Krag Slopes]
description: The shrieking wind races across the frozen ground and slams against the rugged wall which rises sharply to the south.  To one side a sizeable stone chest lies on its side, firmly imbedded in the lava that spilled over it years ago.
