Access to windows is blocked by the various shelf that line the walls, though the floor is largely free of debris.

title: [Woodcutter's Shed]
description: Sawdust and woodchips cover the rough, uneven floor of the small shed.  Pale sunlight filters through the dirty panes of a crooked, narrow window, illuminating bits of dust floating through the beams.  An old board balanced over two crates is placed in the center of the small space.  Leaning against one wall is a neatly stacked pile of wood.  Hanging above an old wooden toolbox are several totes and satchels.

title: [Hollowlair, Demon Roost]
description: Crimson-flamed torches in coiled tentacle brackets line the walls of this chamber, their flickering light dancing over a hoard that has been secreted away here for an unfathomable amount of time.  While less blood and flesh adorns the floor, cobwebs stretch from corner to corner near the ceiling, and even still, the sense of being watched persists.  Across from a barbed stone door is a wavering exit.

title: [Huckleberry Room]
description: The floor is tiled with gray granite, veined in shining huckleberry red.  Marble statues of halflings in various stances line the walls, giving the room a friendly atmosphere.  One statue in particular seems a focal point of attention, either by design or chance, as it stands somewhat apart from the others in the room.

title: [Name of Thrones, Front]
description: In desperate need of repair, this modest, one-room cottage appears to have all of a home's amenities in a single area.  Food preparation and storage is on one side of the room, indicated by the iron hearth and porcelain basin, while a cedar bed and matching chest of drawers occupies the other and is suggestive of the sleeping area.  To the side of a cracked window and below a wooden sign is a dangling shelf, broken glass and tiny labels strewn along the floor.

title: [Name of Thrones, Porch]
description: Slanted and unkempt, this meager porch is covered in a maze of cobwebs, and an invasive weed has hijacked the space between the splintering pine boards.  Monopolizing more than half of the floor space is a double-scooped rocking chair with a knitted blanket draped over the crest rail.  Next to the back door are two pottery bowls, one etched with the name "Clarice" and the other one "Hannibal".

title: [Huckleberry Room Cubbyhole]
description: The small room ends in a dark leather curtain which is drawn shut.  Remnants of old advertising slogans are painted onto the curtain.

title: [Huckleberry Room Locker]
description: The grey stone walls are bare, except for brass wall sconces with candles burning cheerfully.  A woolly, rolton fur rug stretches out on the floor of this small room.

title: [Caeruil City School, Gallery]
description: Tall lancet windows valanced in silvery organza swag grace the front of the exhibition area on either side of some mistwood doors paneled with ornate floriation.  Pristine white floors of decoratively misshapen tile give way to sapphire-padded chairs in rows before a lacquered mahogany lectern facing the entry.  Artwork decorates the whitewashed side walls and nearby floorspace, each socle guarded by gilt stanchions with cobalt velvet ropes that match the draped partitions.  At the far end, a white linen-draped buffet stands near the eastern archway leading toward a rotunda.
location: Caeruil City School, inside the elven city of Ta'Illistim

title: [Caeruil City School, Rotunda]
description: Artwork decorates the whitewashed walls, each guarded by gilt stanchions with cobalt velvet ropes, while several displays are strategically spaced around the rotunda.  Low beechwood wainscotting meets recessed exits scattered around the area, each leading in a different direction.  Sunlight casts a warm glow upon a three-tiered silvery marble fountain with cardinal-facing features that dominates the otherwise rounded room.
location: Caeruil City School, inside the elven city of Ta'Illistim

title: [Caeruil City School, Workshop]
description: Wide glass panels lead to an open-air workspace, where racks of tools and piles of materials are stowed neatly under the terracotta portico.  Pottery wheels and a brown brick kiln on a squat firebox are positioned on the northern side of the yard, and tidy trundle-style workstations for sculpting and other large craft take up the central area.  Arborvitae peek above the alabaster privacy walls, where low terracing in ruddy slate features a quaint garden, set with faded leather curule chairs along the southern side.
location: Caeruil City School, inside the elven city of Ta'Illistim

title: [Caeruil City School, Studio]
description: Rolls of painted backdrops hang from the ceiling, suspended by chains from sturdy oaken rods.  Airy windows stand on either side of a wood-framed dark slate chalkboard, laid open to catch the breeze, while tilted tables on casters and neatly spaced wooden easels encircle a plush plum divan in the center.  The wooden floor is splotched with a plethora of paint in every shade and hue, creating a mosaic of its own.  Slat-doored shelves line the periphery and the studio's rear wall is plastered with drawings between a marquetry faewood door and a gated passageway terminating in a spiral staircase.
location: Caeruil City School, inside the elven city of Ta'Illistim

title: [Caeruil City School, Study]
description: Contrasting pale marble floors, six blue-grey pillars support the crescent-shaped room's domed ceiling off the rotunda.  The center of the study contains a large granadillo desk and a plush plum divan set upon a round crimson rug just beyond.  Wheeled haon ladders set on either side of a bronze peacock-faced fireplace afford access to the room's tiered art displays and bookshelves.  Smooth white marble ledges afford a view of the gently gurgling fountain in the gallery below, following the crescented wall toward a rounded wrought-iron door in the corner.
location: Caeruil City School, inside the elven city of Ta'Illistim

title: [Talondown Arena, Stands]
description: Beyond a weathered wooden gate, a ring of oak bleachers is festooned from above with multicolored pennants.  Some flags are vivid and new, while others are as frayed and tatterdemain as the members of the hoarse-voiced crowd.  Poles topped with sharp spaded tips protect the arena floor below.  The pits are a flurry of commotion: cleaners bustling; guards standing in fractious watch over matches.  Beneath the commotion, the smell of blood lingers on the air, subtle as a snake.

title: [Olbin Strath, Ridge]
description: The wide, sloping strath cradling the rushing waters of the Olbin is shielded from the worst of the wind and cold by the smallest sisters of the Sleeping Lady mountains in the north and high hills in the south.  Here and there, hardy greens peek from amidst the snowbanks, with even a few wildflowers brightly announcing their presence.  A roadway has been worn into the cold earth, beginning at an ice-slicked ridge climbing toward a pair of hillocks and lazing westward through the valley's meadows and farmland.
tags: meta:mapname:Icemule Trace - Moonsedge Road & Crawling Shore

title: [Olbin Strath, Roadway]
description: The roadway cuts between small banks of fresh snow, the diamond powder glowing faintly in the moonlight.  Here and there, banks of resting poppy poke pink, periwinkle, and purple heads out of the glinting snowfall, their leaves a bluer shade of green than the needles of the Olbin spruces growing further from the roadside.  A patch of wintersbite has grown across the road, the intrusive little creeper's vines stretching delicately over the hardpack.

title: [Olbin Strath, Roadway]
description: The roadway splits around a vast granite boulder, the full size of which is concealed by a white blanket of fresh-fallen snow.  As it descends toward the northwest, the path is flanked by hardy scrub that gives way to stony banks.  The main road veers sharply southwest, the hardpack permanently marred by the crisscross of wagon wheels and the even punctuation of mule prints.

title: [Olbin Strath, River's Edge]
description: Frothing and roiling on its way toward the sea, the Olbin River splashes at the stony shores of the strath.  Heavy white rocks, some near as large as a full-grown dwarf, have been heaped upon the shores.  Across the wide blue waters, farms and dwellings dot the foothills of the Sleeping Lady Mountains, whose peaks are lost in puffy grey clouds.

title: [Olbin Strath, Farm Road]
description: Two paths, one northern and the other southern, converge to from a wide dirt road that plunges between two hills as it descends toward the west.  Here and there are signs of old habitation: patches of gravel and cobblestone that have been lost over the years, leaving behind only denuded dirt.  The hillocks are crowned with patches of blue iceblossom, and the gold-tipped flowers sway gently in the breeze coming off the river.

title: [Olbin Strath, Farm Road]
description: Far from the road, farms cling to the rolling land to the south, thinning in number as hillocks grow into proper hills.  A few have tended fields, but just as many are overgrown, the wilds racing to reclaim land that cultivation stole.  The closest field is choked by wild crallisberries, their fruits white as bone amid the verdant greenery.

title: [Olbin Strath, Farm Road]
description: The road births a smaller trail that meanders southeast through a small plot of untended farmland.  A scarecrow, his shoulders stained white with droppings, marks the fork.  Crows have left glittering prizes--red and blue glass, silver tinsel, and even a few pieces of obsidian--at the base of the mannequin as if in tribute to his ineffectiveness.

title: [Olbin Strath, Farm Road]
description: The road grows thin and tenuous, red grasses sprouting from the scarce-trodden dirt.  It coils through a strand of white-clad elm and spruce, the trees' boles teal and silver with the growth of iseya lichen.  Their leaves occlude the path entirely in places as it bends away from the banks of the Olbin.

title: [Olbin Strath, Farm Road]
description: Near a fork in the road sits a broken mule cart, abandoned and askew.  One of its wheels is missing, but another is sunken into the earth.  The metal of it is spotted heavily with rust and has corroded through in places, as if it has been there for some time.  Mulefoot fungus has flourished in the shadow of the abandoned vehicle, fleshy, green, and shaped like a mule's hooves.

title: [Olbin Strath, Covered Bridge]
description: A shallow, rock-strewn fork of the Olbin cuts through the roadway, whispering through the high red and green grasses clinging to the banks.  A bridge of stone, sharp edges worn down by long years of hard wind and snowfall, spans the river.  Grotesques are perched along its rooftop, but the same wear has dwindled them down to mere suggestions of figures that have more in common with melted candles than statues.

title: [Olbin Delta, Covered Bridge]
description: Moss flourishes in the cracks of a covered stone bridge spanning a shallow distributary of the river that gives the valley its name.  Fish thrive in the clear waters below, gleaming with scales in colors reminiscent of coins: brazen golds, dusky silvers, and ruddy coppers.  Above the entrance to the bridge is a carved effigy that looks like a bramble branch silhouetted against a moon.

title: [Olbin Strath, Farm]
description: Framed by hardy apple trees that sag under a weight of unharvested fruit, a dirt path leads up to an old painted modwir farmhouse.  Staring accusatorily down at the yard, a broken window looks into a bedroom on the top floor.  The quiet is a palpable thing, as if bird and beast and even the wind shun the place.  Even so, the door creaks now and then on rusty hinges.

title: [Deserted Farmhouse, Entry]
description: The cramped interior of the farmhouse is made less navigable by an overturned table blocking the way into a ransacked kitchen.  Despite the cold, the smells of spoilage and rot commingle into a revolting melange that hangs on the air like a rancid oil slick.  Some rickety wooden stairs climb past the wreckage, guarded by an unwieldy looking bannister as they ascend to the house's second story.

title: [Deserted Farmhouse, Upstairs]
description: Smashed pottery litters the upstairs landing of the small farmhouse, the low ceiling of which leaves the raw timber eaves crowding down upon the passage.  What remains of a rug cushions the hardwood floor in places, but exposure to the elements has left it a threadbare ruin.  The air is cold, and occasional breezes solicit rusty creaks from a rounded wooden door at the end of the hall.

title: [Deserted Farmhouse, Bedroom]
description: Torn open to spill its downy guts on the hardwood floor, a small bed dominates the ransacked bedroom.  Goose feathers twitch warily on the wind whistling through a broken bay window on the northern wall, through which trickles icy starlight.  A crooked armoire stands open, one of its doors hanging on twisted hinges, revealing moldering clothing too long exposed to the elements to be salvageable.

title: [Olbin Strath, Ruined Stead]
description: Framed by overgrown fields dotted here and there with drifts of snow, the old farmhouse waiting at the end of the path has succumbed to decay.  The paint on the wooden siding has started to peel, revealing age-silvered spruce underneath.  Several of the windows are broken, giving glimpses of a dark interior full of warped wood and deep shadows.  The ceiling has collapsed in, barring entry through the red-limned front door, the knob of which is missing.

title: [Olbin Strath, Farm Road]
description: Half-concealed by a stand of young hoarbeams, an old pinewood sign leans crookedly away from the road.  The trees have shed a gentle blanket of needles onto the road.  Dark purple cones amongst the greenery present an added hazard on the way, which is slick with ice in places.

title: [Olbin Delta, Meadow]
description: A distributary of the Olbin laps at the shores of a small meadow that is dusted with snowfall.  Ice clings to the high grasses and glitters like a scattering of jewels over the wildflowers that have somehow managed to thrive in the strath's limited protection from the cold.  The ground is sodden rather than frozen, as if the river is occasionally discontent to stay within its appointed bounds.

title: [Olbin Delta, Meadow]
description: The meadow stretches over an expanse of hilly terrain that seems to grow less flat to the north and west as the land rises away from one of the river's smaller forks.  Wildflowers are plentiful, colluding with the abundant grasses, verdant green and vibrantly red, to clash with the greys and whites in the distance.  Far to the northeast, the Sleeping Ladies are clad in snows and crowned with clouds.

title: [Olbin Delta, Barrow]
description: A barrow has been cut into the face of a high hill that disturbs the flatlands of the delta.  Heavy stones, some nearly the size of boulders, have been piled in front of the entrance.  Great furrows in the ground lead to the west, hinting at how the stones were moved.  They have been in place long enough to boast a filigree of iseya lichen, the brightly colored flora blanketing the rocks in teal and silver colonies.

title: [Olbin Delta, Broken Statue]
description: Atop the high hill stands a statue of black volcanic stone, its features corroded by the ocean air and eroded by the snow and storms.  Broken in half, the statue's lower legs strike a heroic posture, oriented toward the ice-dotted sea to the northwest.  The remains are scattered amidst the snowy grasses covering the hilltop.  Only a faint hint of salt seasons the air, which is otherwise crisp and clear.

title: [Moonsedge, Grand Pavilion]
description: Dark silk walls ripple in the keening mountain breeze, but cold finds no purchase within the richly appointed pavilion.  At its center has been erected a wide stone fire pit that fills the interior with the sharpness of resin and woodsmoke, though the latter is channeled up through a cut in the high ceiling.  Carpets embroidered with a briar sprig against a charcoal grey moon soften the ground.  There is a plenitude of finely upholstered seats around a great table of interlocking rosewood and ebony set near the fire's warmth.

title: [Moonsedge, Briar Gate]
description: Walls twice the height of a giantman loom over the cobblestone road as it winds toward the city.  Ornamental etchings of thorny briars adorn the stone faces, which are hewn from vast cubes of dark basalt.  The wall is unbroken save for a black gate of wrought iron that is adorned with countless wild roses fashioned of dark metal.  From within come none of the sounds of a thriving city, not wagons squeaking, nor the din of a throng.

title: [Olbin Delta, Highland Ridge]
description: The ridge overlooks an unforgiving shoreline of black sand that stretches a long way before it is devoured by the frigid waters of the ocean.  Between the ridge and the shore is a steep cliff face scattered with jagged rocks and gravel, a switchback trail cutting across it to allow access to old docks stretching out into the water.  A rise to the east flows gracefully down toward an expanse of highland dotted with clumps of snow and alpine wildlfowers.

title: [Olbin Delta, Highland Ridge]
description: Wind whips the highland ridge overlooking the black beaches verging on the steel-colored waters of the Frostmain.  Great icebergs breach out of the waters, some the size of cities, the remnants of glaciers that have finished their long migration to the sea.  The cries of seabirds fill the air and the scent of brine is on every cutting breeze.

title: [Olbin Delta, Highland Ridge]
description: The ridge begins to curve westward as it slopes down toward the Frostmain and its long beaches of black sand.  At the same time, the trailway narrows, crowded to either side by sharp, dark-colored boulders.  Lying in a nook between two great stones is a small stuffed doll.

title: [Olbin Delta, Highland Ridge]
description: The gravel and rocks scattering the ridge side give way to a rocky shoreline trail that, while steep, seems safely traversible.  Down the trail, glimpses of habitation beckon in the form of small, huddled buildings of wood and grass thatching.  Despite the hour, no firelights are visible from the village.  It is shrouded thickly in mists coming off of the water.

title: [Olbin Delta, Old Road]
description: Woods crowd in on the highland ridge, but the old hoarbeams and Ossian pines do not grow thick enough to conceal an ancient roadway that glides southward toward the hills bordering the southernmost reaches of the delta.  Despite the proximity of the ocean, nary a seabird cry can be heard.  A splintered signpost gestures in the road's direction, but whatever writing once graced its face is long gone.

title: [Olbin Delta, Old Road]
description: Climbing into the hills that mark the southern end of the river valley, the pathway is a balding stretch of cobblestone being devoured by mosses and grass, but it widens into a full road as it climbs southward.  Through the elms crowding in from the northwest, the waters of the Frostmain are visible, choked heavily with silvery mist transformed into glowing clouds by the starlight.

title: [Moonsedge, Old Road]
description: A forest of elm and birch and pine closes in upon the road as it climbs away from the strath below toward a walled city in the hills.  Carved wooden poles etched with fanciful briar motifs hoist lanterns aloft, but the lights are dark and cold despite the late hour.  Weeds and moss cling to the cobblestones of the roadway as if it has seen too few visitors to keep the encroaching vegetation at bay.

title: [Moonsedge, Old Road]
description: Through a break in the snow-dusted boughs of a great spruce, the silhouette of a castle at the top of the hills is black against a halo of moonlight.  Old and grim, the fortress looks down on a small city from its lofty perch.  Atop the walls of the city, faded crimson pennants fly, bearing the sigil of a briar sprig against a rising charcoal moon.

title: [Olbin Delta, Glade]
description: Sunlight filters, cold and pale, through the colorful leaves of the surrounding trees, cold white rime tracing the jewel-toned foliage like diamond filigree.  The woods give wide berth to a respectably sized inn, its sturdy stone construction and freshly thatched roof both welcome glimpses of civilization in the untamed woodland.  Several carriages, too fine by half for the rustic setting, occupy the cobblestone yard.

title: [The Snowcat's Den, Foyer]
description: Left open, the inn's stone-framed maple double doors allow in starlight and the susurrus of leaves from the glade outside.  The scents of birch and pine from without mingle pleasantly with the sharpness of woodsmoke and leather from within.  Well-appointed without being ostentatious, the establishment's entryway boasts a dark suede couch and a cathedral ceiling of raw pine.  Standing guard from a nook in the opposite wall, a stuffed snowcat gazes watchfully down at the entryway with gleaming glass eyes.

title: [The Snowcat's Den, Common Room]
description: Guarded by a long counter of dark-stained pine, the common room's bar boasts an impressive array of spirits in pristine bottles that come in all of the colors of the rainbow.  Several leather-upholstered stools sit along the counter's outer edge.  A half wall behind the bar provides a glimpse of the inn's kitchen and its hearths, above which game birds and other meats roast on wooden spits.  Nearby, a carved white pine stairway ascends to the second story.

title: [The Snowcat's Den, Parlor]
description: Light filters intimately through windows of smoky stained glass bearing scenes of the hunt, vivid reds commingling with the glistening golds and silvers of bright weaponry adorning the panes.  A capacious suede couch faces the translucent artwork, framed to either side by a burled maple endtable.  The sweet pungence of pipe smoke has permeated the walls and furnishings, and is a not unpleasant undertone to the aroma of roasting meat wafting from the kitchens.

title: [The Snowcat's Den, Landing]
description: Looking down upon the common room of the inn, the landing is framed by a raw pine bannister scored with stylized claw marks.  Mounted on the walls are trophies of past hunts, ranging from an elk head to the scaled blue wings of a reptilian beast, each as wide as a man is tall.  Two doors, one of spruce and one of honey oak, break the trophy wall.

title: [The Snowcat's Den, Fang Room]
description: A stylized fang in opalescent inlay shines from the face of the honey oak door.  The motif is repeated in the carvings on the posts of a huge four-poster bed draped in supple amber curtains.  Opposite a trio of bay windows that overlook the glade is a dark stone fireplace.  Several porcelain statues of wolves prowl along the mantel.

title: [The Snowcat's Den, Claw Room]
description: A stylized claw in gilt adorns the arched spruce door that is the primary means of egress from the room.  The hearth opposite the window is framed in rough-hewn stone that is flecked with glimmers of pyrite and looks to provide ample warmth should the bed, with its high-piled fur blankets, fail to do so.  A stuffed lynx stands by the window, amber eyes narrowed as if carefully keeping watch.

title: [The Frostmain, Shore]
description: Frigid winds whip the black sand shoreline as it clings to sheer, dark bluffs of basalt as if pinned between the stone and sea.  Salt is heavy on the icy breeze.  Leading up to an old dock of time-silvered wood, the stone-strewn sands are spattered with white droppings.  A switchback trail climbs to the lip of a ridge crowning the bluffs.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Shoreline]
[Frostmain, Docks]
description: Sprouting from a shore of black sand and sharp stone, the docks are an aging trident of planks that stretch out into the forbidding waters of the Frostmain.  Chunks of ice born from the vast white icebergs not far offshore bob in the dark water to the seaward side of the walk.  Despite the cold, silvery fish dart in the dark waters, little bothered by the frigid tides in which they swim.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Crab Pier]
[Frostmain, Main Pier]
description: A sign with a blue crab on it hangs askew from one of the pilings, the paint having flaked away in places.  Its inspiration seems to be the bright blue crabs that skitter around on the rocks near to the shore.  They are evidently the only creatures hardy enough to thrive near the warmthless shores of the main.

The thoroughfare of the main pier is wide and largely clear of debris.  Rotting barrels crowd to the sides of the dock, sprouting from heaps of netting, lines, and twine that have been similarly abandoned.  The cold has glazed all surfaces with a glistening coat of rime.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Crawling Pier]
[Frostmain, Main Pier]
description: Barnacles, black and unlovely, cling thick to the pilings near the water line and hold there miraculously despite the constant pounding of the frothing main.  Bright blue crabs dwell amidst the tenacious life, skittering and crawling here and there.  They are like jewels against the tenebrous grey of the sun-battered wood.

The thoroughfare of the main pier is wide and largely clear of debris.  Rotting barrels crowd to the sides of the dock, sprouting from heaps of netting, lines, and twine that have been similarly abandoned.  The cold has glazed all surfaces with a glistening coat of rime.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Shadowed Pier]
[Frostmain, Main Pier]
description: The pilings to either side of the pier rise high like defiant fingers pointing toward the uncaring sky.  They cast cruel shadows over the planks.  Below, the waters are angry and cold, black depths holding unknowable secrets.

The thoroughfare of the main pier is wide and largely clear of debris.  Rotting barrels crowd to the sides of the dock, sprouting from heaps of netting, lines, and twine that have been similarly abandoned.  The cold has glazed all surfaces with a glistening coat of rime.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Moon Pier]
[Frostmain, Main Pier]
description: Though the planks are badly damaged by time and the ravages of the waves, an inscribed moon adorns them, haloed by a twine of stylized brambles.  Several barrels, cracked and long since robbed of their contents by exposure, huddle by one of the pilings.  They may have once been painted with bright symbols, but now their destinations and origins are a mystery lost to the past.

The thoroughfare of the main pier is wide and largely clear of debris.  Rotting barrels crowd to the sides of the dock, sprouting from heaps of netting, lines, and twine that have been similarly abandoned.  The cold has glazed all surfaces with a glistening coat of rime.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Highland Pier]
[Frostmain, Main Pier]
description: A tiny scratched image of two figures fighting with swords decorates one of the pilings, a crooked timber that looks ready to fall at any moment.  The piling is somehow more intact than most of the planks, which are cracked, broken, or rotted depending on their proximity to the crashing surf.  Icy waves throw up spray like cold needles as they crash mercilessly against the pier.  In the battle between water and wood, there can be only one victor.

The thoroughfare of the main pier is wide and largely clear of debris.  Rotting barrels crowd to the sides of the dock, sprouting from heaps of netting, lines, and twine that have been similarly abandoned.  The cold has glazed all surfaces with a glistening coat of rime.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Barrow Pier]
[Frostmain, Main Pier]
description: An ancient wheelbarrow sits crookedly on one leg, left to be devoured by the salty gale.  It has been scoured down to rust and ruin, much like the pier on which it stands.  The planks and black with rot or silver from exposure where snow has not obscured them.

The thoroughfare of the main pier is wide and largely clear of debris.  Rotting barrels crowd to the sides of the dock, sprouting from heaps of netting, lines, and twine that have been similarly abandoned.  The cold has glazed all surfaces with a glistening coat of rime.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Albatross Pier]
[Frostmain, Main Pier]
description: A spread-winged albatross of carved wood stands guard from one of the nearby pilings.  They flaying of the wind has stripped all but the last hints of painted color from its wings.  Heaped at the bottom of the pilings is a coil of hempen line that is stained and useless, too frayed for any purpose.

The thoroughfare of the main pier is wide and largely clear of debris.  Rotting barrels crowd to the sides of the dock, sprouting from heaps of netting, lines, and twine that have been similarly abandoned.  The cold has glazed all surfaces with a glistening coat of rime.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Greying Pier]
[Frostmain, Docks]
description: The skeletal remains of a waterfowl hang in a rusted cage that is suspended from a nearby post.  To the north, the starboard tine of the trident-shaped docks thrusts into the cruel waters of the main.  Set rocking by the breeze, the cage's grating creaks are the only sounds approximating birdsong.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Gelid Pier]
[Frostmain, Starboard Pier]
description: So cold are the waters of the main that rings of ice have formed near the water line, putting out protrusions like jagged fangs.  The air is bitter cold and has an unsavory tang of too much brine upon it.  Hoarfrost climbs the pilings with silvery, grasping claws.

The easternmost of the trio of piers is a mess of creaky planks spotted heavily with the droppings of seafowl.  Waters to either side are deep, black, and cold.  Stinging salt is so thick on the air as to have left cakes of gleaming grit on the nearby pylons.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Snowy Pier]
[Frostmain, Starboard Pier]
description: Snow occludes most of the pier's planking, making the expanse of wood difficult to navigate.  Glimpses of the planks between drifts of snow suggest that there are cracks and treacherous gaps waiting beneath the white blanket.  One of the pilings to the east of the pier has collapsed into the water, finally having lost its battle with the waves.

The easternmost of the trio of piers is a mess of creaky planks spotted heavily with the droppings of seafowl.  Waters to either side are deep, black, and cold.  Stinging salt is so thick on the air as to have left cakes of gleaming grit on the nearby pylons.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Broken Pier]
[Frostmain, Starboard Pier]
description: Clad heavily in hardy barnacles, black and rotting struts support the portmost of the docks' three tines as it stretches out into the water.  Droppings spatter the walkway, white against the grey and black of the wood, but not a gull's cry stirs the air.  The waters near the dock are shallow and grant glimpses of bright blue crabs scuttling around on the seafloor.

The easternmost of the trio of piers is a mess of creaky planks spotted heavily with the droppings of seafowl.  Waters to either side are deep, black, and cold.  Stinging salt is so thick on the air as to have left cakes of gleaming grit on the nearby pylons.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Starboard Pier]
[Frostmain, Starboard Pier]
description: The easternmost of the trio of piers is a mess of creaky planks spotted heavily with the droppings of seafowl.  Waters to either side are deep, black, and cold.  Stinging salt is so thick on the air as to have left cakes of gleaming grit on the nearby pylons.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Salty Pier]
[Frostmain, Starboard Pier]
description: Salt cakes, deposited by the waters over the years, have turned the planks of the pier into a crunchy mess.  The salt is stained red and orange by the rust coming off of the nails that hold the planks together.  Brine stings sharply in the air.

The easternmost of the trio of piers is a mess of creaky planks spotted heavily with the droppings of seafowl.  Waters to either side are deep, black, and cold.  Stinging salt is so thick on the air as to have left cakes of gleaming grit on the nearby pylons.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Rimy Pier]
[Frostmain, Starboard Pier]
description: The thoroughfare of the starboard pier is wide and largely clear of debris.  Rotting barrels crowd to the sides of the dock, sprouting from heaps of netting, lines, and twine that have been similarly abandoned.  The cold has glazed all surfaces with a glistening coat of rime.

The easternmost of the trio of piers is a mess of creaky planks spotted heavily with the droppings of seafowl.  Waters to either side are deep, black, and cold.  Stinging salt is so thick on the air as to have left cakes of gleaming grit on the nearby pylons.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Briar Pier]
[Frostmain, Docks]
description: Two great pilings stand at the end of the pier.  Each is deeply engraved with ornate briars, the work done by a master's hand.  Salt has caked the recesses and glints brightly where there ought to be shadows in the carvings.

Clad heavily in hardy barnacles, black and rotting struts support the portmost of the docks' three tines as it stretches out into the water.  Droppings spatter the walkway, white against the grey and black of the wood, but not a gull's cry stirs the air.  The waters near the dock are shallow and grant glimpses of bright blue crabs scuttling around on the seafloor.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Decaying Pier]
[Frostmain, Port Pier]
description: The dusty odor of decaying wood commingles with the bitterness of brine on the cruel gale.  Pilings breach up from the water like rotting teeth in a crooked grin, broken and blackened.  A nearby pile heaped on the planks is more mildew than canvas.

The wood of the westernmost pier has silvered unevenly, leaving a strange stripe pattern in the warped planks as they alternate between grey and black.  The nails securing the planks are spotted with rust that makes each look as if it sits in a pool of old dried blood.  Traceries of rime glisten from the wood, lending a glint of natural beauty to the manmade decay.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Old Pier]
[Frostmain, Port Pier]
description: A sense of great age pervades the wood and steel working desperately to hold the pier together against the restless thrashing of the cold tide.  The visible nails are pocked with corrosion where they have not surrendered to rust.  Creaking and groaning, the pilings sway with the ebb and flow of the water.

The wood of the westernmost pier has silvered unevenly, leaving a strange stripe pattern in the warped planks as they alternate between grey and black.  The nails securing the planks are spotted with rust that makes each look as if it sits in a pool of old dried blood.  Traceries of rime glisten from the wood, lending a glint of natural beauty to the manmade decay.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Port Pier]
[Frostmain, Port Pier]
description: The wood of the westernmost pier has silvered unevenly, leaving a strange stripe pattern in the warped planks as they alternate between grey and black.  The nails securing the planks are spotted with rust that makes each look as if it sits in a pool of old dried blood.  Traceries of rime glisten from the wood, lending a glint of natural beauty to the manmade decay.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Weathered Pier]
[Frostmain, Port Pier]
description: Grey and black planks fray into splintered ends as they stretch toward the frigid waters, resembling grasping skeletal talons.  Old nails barely hold the pier together, but have bled dark red rust onto the surrounding wood.  Gleaming ice crystals cling to the wood, their loveliness making the docks' disrepair all the more ugly.

The wood of the westernmost pier has silvered unevenly, leaving a strange stripe pattern in the warped planks as they alternate between grey and black.  The nails securing the planks are spotted with rust that makes each look as if it sits in a pool of old dried blood.  Traceries of rime glisten from the wood, lending a glint of natural beauty to the manmade decay.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Cracked Pier]
[Frostmain, Port Pier]
description: As they have aged, the planks of the pier have curved away from one another to form a wide fissure.  The waters of the Frostmain surge up and through in crashes of white froth and icy water, leaving behind cakes of salt to decorate the wood.  Between surges, the waters are deep and black and foreboding.

The wood of the westernmost pier has silvered unevenly, leaving a strange stripe pattern in the warped planks as they alternate between grey and black.  The nails securing the planks are spotted with rust that makes each look as if it sits in a pool of old dried blood.  Traceries of rime glisten from the wood, lending a glint of natural beauty to the manmade decay.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Crumbling Pier]
[Frostmain, Port Pier]
description: Crumbling wooden planks hang broken and askew, pounded relentlessly by the frosty surf.  The sun-silvered wood is caked with rime and clusters of salt crystals that have built up over long years of disuse.  A frayed line dangles like a noose from one of the pilings, flapping ominously in the whipping wind.

The wood of the westernmost pier has silvered unevenly, leaving a strange stripe pattern in the warped planks as they alternate between grey and black.  The nails securing the planks are spotted with rust that makes each look as if it sits in a pool of old dried blood.  Traceries of rime glisten from the wood, lending a glint of natural beauty to the manmade decay.

title: [Silvergate, Chaddeaux's Lair]
description: The room is dimly lit by a chandelier fashioned from frayed rope nooses and carved ivory skulls, the hollow eyes glowing from candles hidden within.  Blood red walls stretch from the night black ceiling to the lush black carpet.  A small four poster bed, draped with silver satin curtains, occupies one corner.  A round table sits next to the bed, holding a decanter of dwarven whiskey.  One wall is dominated by a black marble fireplace.

title: [The Snowcat's Den, Cellar]
description: Barrels crowd the walls of the cellar, redolent with odors of brine.  Pitch seals most of them to protect the pickled contents.  Roots breach through the foundations of the inn toward the further verges of the cellar, having worked their inexorable way through the old stone.

title: [Lair of the Hunter, Antechamber]
description: Blazing torches light a tunnel with a high ceiling as it delves down into the cold earth.  Walls of carved rock have been worn smooth by centuries of use, and their natural striations are accompanied by paintings of man and beast engaged in bloodsport.  To the east, the tunnel dead ends into a foundation wall that is being dismantled by the encroachment of roots, which have partially dislodged a crooked stone.

title: [Lair of the Hunter, Statuary]
description: Ancient statues carve from the same stone as the surrounding rock loom over the walkway, stained by primitive paints.  The carvings take the shapes of bobcats and lynxes, and despite the crudeness of the old craftsmanship, they have a predatory grace to their postures.  More paintings adorn the walls, depicting masses of humanoids engaged in acts both carnal and savage.

title: [Lair of the Hunter, Altar]
description: Steps hewn out of the natural rock underfoot rise toward a cylindrical chamber with a high ceiling shot through with veins of pyrite.  A heavily gilded triptych painted with laquer adorns the wall behind an ornate altar of tawny marble.  Lithe golden figures support the altar, wrought musculatures bunching as if beneath its weight.

title: [Moot Hall, Pukk's Office]
description: The pale grey walls of the office appear almost white when bathed in the moonlight that streams in through a large window overlooking the street below.  Two weapon racks stretch out above a heavy oak desk which fills the space before a huge, red bearskin rug.  A plush, large-backed couch is situated between a slate-topped bar and a wide, fur-lined dog bed.

title: [Yander's Farm, Stables]
description: Several stalls line the outer wall of this small stable.  Stray bits of straw and scattered oats cover the hard-packed dirt floor, giving silent testament to the area's inhabitants.  A small metal pail sits quietly near a pitchfork, patiently awaiting use.

title: [Grey Wind Manor, Porch]
description: Shadows drip from the eaves, and a light coating of mist covers the floorboards of the porch.  The manor sports no visible windows, just a massive set of double doors of engraved ebon oak.

title: [Grey Wind Manor, Foyer]
description: Niches in the walls house candles that gently flicker, radiating a warm glow that barely penetrates the heavy shadows lurking about the manor.  A woven rug embroidered with complex knotwork in varying shades of blue covers the floor, and a double staircase leads up to a darkened landing.  In the middle of the room, towering nearly one story tall, is an engraved crystal tablet.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Gleaming Pier]
description: Spared by some trick of the winds and waters the ravages visited upon much of the area, the pier is mostly intact.  Rime gleams in ornate traceries from the pilings, punctuated here and there by clusters of ice crystals that shine like gemstones.  There are even some nails that have not yet been bitten down to rusting nubs by the salt and water.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Shivering Pier]
description: Shivering timbers quake and quaver with each assault of the waves as if the entire ragged structure of old nails and older wood might collapse with the next blow.  The pilings are crooked, either from poor craftsmanship or because the tide has shifted them in whatever moors them down below.  The answer to that question is a futile one, as the waters are as lightless as they are deep.

title: [Frostmain Docks, Cold Pier]
description: Wailing and biting, the gale shrieking down off of the icebergs in the distance carries a cruel chill.  In concert with the seaspray, it has coated the pier in ice crystals that gleam and glisten, distracting from the rotting wood beneath.  Some of the planks, clad in icy skin, shine like polished glass.

title: [Moonsedge, Bramble Market]
description: A sprawling market forms a crescent around the vast black iron gate leading out of the city.  Stalls and wagons crowd the marketplace, huddling beneath maples that have been planted in earthen beds along its borders.  Discarded wares, from tattered remnants of silks to shattered potion bottles, are scattered in disarray across the pale white stones that form the crescent-shaped plaza and not a seller can be seen.

title: [Crawling Shore, Incline]
description: Gravel-clad and jagged, an incline climbs away from the shore toward a highland ridge that overlooks the water.  Gulls and other sea birds have stained the rocks with their leavings, but otherwise the shale is unrelieved and tenebrous.  The desolate expanse of black stone is mostly impassible, but a rocky shoreline trail connects the shore with a low point in the ridgeway.

title: [Crawling Shore, Lowlands]
description: Sand and stone meet in a clash of blacks and greys, the volcanic grit darker by several shades than the sharp bits of shale that have tumbled down the incline to the east.  Though whipped by winds wailing off of the Frostmain's frigid waters, the area is graced by patches of scraggly vegetation, mostly tenacious weeds that have found purchase in crags and furrows in the earth.

title: [Crawling Shore, Lowlands]
description: Fresh snow shines in patches atop the rock and sand that defines the unforgiving lowlands near to the shore, mostly occluding a wispy trail that winds aimlessly westward.  Abandoned in a nearby drift, a carved maple sled sits at the side of the road.  The way does not appear to be well traveled, as tundra grasses have grown over the path in places.

title: [Crawling Shore, Lowlands]
description: Crisp is the breeze, brined heavily with the salt of the ocean, as it scours the lowlands.  The trailway ascends through a patch of ruddy scrub toward a small slope.  Rudimentary attempts to line the path with gravel seem to have ended in defeat, leaving behind loose, skittering stones that hinder progress more than help it.

title: [Crawling Shore, Totem]
description: Its base secured by a trio of flat boulders that are covered with the remains of spent tallow candles, a totem of carved driftwood rises out of the ground.  The boulders' faces are carved with leaping dolphins and swirling patterns that are repeated in bright paint on the totem alongside a stern, bearded face and the repeated image of a golden trident.  Beads, bits of seaglass, and other offerings have been heaped at the totem's base.

title: [Crawling Shore, Barrow]
description: One of the few hills of substantive size this near to the shoreline has a wide open mouth framed by an arch of cut stone.  The barrow is clad in downy seaside mosses, sparse but vividly blue-green in hue.  Footsteps have worn a grim furrow into the space before the aperture.

title: [Crawling Shore, Ebon Sands]
description: Gleaming mica and bits of quartz wink from the black sands that consume the path toward the shoreline.  The powdery grit rolls in low, wave-like dunes and is strewn here and there with bits of bone and whole shells.  To the northwest, on a low bluff above the bleakness of the beach, a quiet village shelters beneath an uncaring sky.

title: [Crawling Shore, Ebon Sands]
description: A walrus skeleton has been heaped onto the sand as if by an exceptionally high tide.  Though crabs and other scavengers have picked every last scrap of flesh away, they have left the bones remarkably intact.  The splintered remains of a spear shaft lie nearby, its head a shattered piece of obsidian with jagged edges.

title: [Crawling Shore, Tidepool]
description: Despite the bitter cold of the windswept shores, life flourishes in a shallow tidepool near the water's edge.  Framed by jagged blocks of banded shale, the pool is clear, its water occasionally refreshed by the onslaught of the tide at its height.  Beneath the surface, jewel-toned blue crabs shuffle about on beds of algae, accompanied by pale white clams and black mussels.

title: [Crawling Shore, Sinkhole]
description: Seawater swirls slowly on the ground, carrying bits of muck toward a deep sucking sinkhole near the water's edge.  Up above, on a bluff with steeply cragged sides, rest signs of civilization in the rooftops and palisade walls of a small village.  Despite the buildings' presence, the breeze carries only the cries of gulls and the roar of the crashing waves.

title: [Crawling Shore, Sinkhole]
description: Swirling muck and sucking goo covers the bottom of the sinkhole, fed by a constant trickle of frigid seawater and sandy mud from above.  A rope ladder dangles from the sinkhole's aperture, which occupies a good third of its crumbling ceiling.  Nearby, a silver stake lies mostly submerged in the water.

title: [Crawling Shore, Ebon Sands]
description: The cold tide laps at both sides of a bridge of black sand leading out toward a rocky promontory.  Ravenous, the waves look to be on the verge of eroding the tenuous bridge, leaving its stony destination an island.  Bitter brine sprays frequently through the air, icy cold and endless.

title: [Crawling Shore, Promontory]
description: Waves rage against the jagged stones of the promontory, sending up explosions of icy saltwater.  Crabs scuttle in the dark places between the stones, bright blue bodies starkly colorful against the monochrome of the black rock.  High tides have trapped kelp and other, more ambulatory sources of sustenance for the little crustaceans.  The finger of stone stretches defiantly out into the water, looking out onto a phalanx of vast icebergs.

title: [Crawling Shore, Village Path]
description: A path strewn with fragments of shale climbs toward the simple wooden gate of a village perched atop a bluff overlooking the beach.  The gate is the sole opening in a wooden palisade of sharpened stakes that surrounds the holdfast.  A faint, sickly sweetness lingers on the air despite the howling ocean breeze.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: Though the surrounding palisade wall does little to mute the cries of gulls or the whistling of the western wind, the holdfast swathed in eerie silence.  Not a child's cry stirs the air, and the surrounding huts, with their pine-and-tar construction and rooftops thatched with tundra grass, have a hollowness to them that betrays a lack of habitation.  Near the gate that is the sole means of egress from the hold, a net full of skeletal fish lies forgotten.

title: [Crawling Shore, Village Circle]
description: A circle of stones too flat and rounded to be natural sits at the intersection of several dirt roads.  There is a wide firepit at the center, though its flames and the stories that were doubtless told by their side are but ghosts of the past.  Gull droppings now stain the flats of the rocks.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: Standing atop the highest point in the holdfast, the remains of a charred wooden hut stand amid a patch of burnt brush.  Crumbling, blackened logs are heaped at the base of the hut.  There are boards across the door, but whatever was securing them lost its purchase in the blaze.

title: [Crawling Shore, Burnt Hut]
description: A pyroclasm consumed the interior of the hut, gutting it and leaving behind only a barely standing frame of wood.  What remains of the door squeaks in the breeze, swaying on charred hinges.  Five skeletons lie amidst the ruins, blackened beoynd recognition, but next to them is a man-shaped space where the floor is clear of char.  No sign of the space's occupant remains.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: Graves mar a patch of land to one side of the street.  A sturdy shovel is driven into the heart of one of the graves, but it has been there long enough for the briny air to devour much of the exposed metal.  Another, strewn with dried flower petals, is open, the dirt filling it thrown aside as if by great force.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: A lone tree stands over the roadway, the sole tree in the holdfast.  The white bark is flaking and has a pleasantly effervescent smell.  Ribbons festoon the trunk, knotted from a variety of materials from coarse wool to fine silk, but they are old and bleached by the sun.

title: [Crawling Shore, Shrine]
description: Dolphins painstakingly awakened from dark rock flank the entrance to a blue seastone shrine at the end of the winding road.  Iseya lichen has found purchase between the stones of the walls, the sharp silvers and teals of the flora brighter than the muted blue of the seastone.  A few half-spent tallow candles sit to either side of the entrance, their blackened wicks sodden from the sea air.

title: [Crawling Shore, Storm Shrine]
description: Moonlight beckons through chinks in the stones of the shrine's rounded ceiling.  Shafts of pale radiance bathe a glistening seaglass statue of a powerfully built half-krolvin with a heavy beard, a trident held aloft in one blunt hand.  Offerings of strange golden coins and carved whalebone charms are heaped before the figure.  The air is redolent with the odor of the spent tallow candles that fill niches along the walls.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: Choked with weeds and blanketed with fallen snow, an herb garden stretches from the side of the road to the border of the palisade.  Several gardening tools, including a spade with a handle of carved bone and a bent shovel, lie scattered across the earth.  The garden's perimeter is demarcated by dark chunks of shale harvested from the beaches below.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: A huge carved richly adorned with scrimshaw hangs from the entryway of a large wooden hut with a pine plank deck.  Earthen beds to either side of the walkway leading toward it hold the dried husks of iceblossoms.  The road curves away from the home as if avoiding the splintered remains of a door that once secured the home.

title: [Crawling Shore, Hut]
description: The interior of the hut was once a sizeable single room with an earthen hearth and a curtain delineating a bedchamber with a frame and overstuffed mattress full of goat wool stuffing.  The curtain has been slashed, and the copper cookwares are scattered across the ground, twisted into unrecognizable shapes.  The smell of dried iceblossoms, sweetly herbal, lingers amid the destruction.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: Ruined huts, their walls collapsing and their windows smashed, crowd in on the road.  Near one, a sled is loaded with sodden bundles of clothing and other belongings.  The crimson edge of a sweater peeks from one bundle, the spot of color jarring in the greying landscape.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: The road begins a gently decline near a corner dominated by the remains of a tanner's hut.  Though the interior is ruined and choked with debris from the collapsing thatch of its roof, the smell of tanning agents and dyes is still acrid on the air.  A walrus skull, its eye sockets empty, stares from one of the intact windows, dispassionately watching the village's decay.

title: [Crawling Shore, Holdfast]
description: The pathway between houses descends steeply toward a finger of land protruding from the palisade out into the unforgiving waters of the Frostmain.  To one side of the road stands a wooden hut with a thatched roof of long-dried grass that has caved in, undone by the weight of snowfall.  Blankets and clothing are strewn before the steps of the hut, unmoving save when they are tugged by an errant breeze.

title: [Crawling Shore, Hut]
description: Snow swathes the wood plank floor of the hut, strewn with bits of grass thatching from a ragged hole in the roofing.  A bed that is scarcely more than a wool-stuffed mattress on the ground lies half-buried under the snow, spotted with the unsavory darkness of mold.  Oddly undisturbed, a carved whalebone figurine sits atop the hearth of a fireplace in the eastern wall.

title: [Crawling Shore, Dockside]
description: To the west, at the lowest point of the holdfast, a dock of time-silvered wood stretches out over the waters of the sea, shaking each time the waves pound against its aging timbers.  Woven baskets crowd the nearby shoreline, most empty and several pulverized and rent apart.  Up on the bluff above, huts stare outward with empty, lightless windows.

title: [Crawling Shore, Dock]
description: Small fishing vessels are moored to the dock by brittle lengths of rope that creak with the rise and fall of the waves.  Devoured by salt and and compromised by neglect, they have begun to take on water, and several silver fish dart around in the lower third of the nearest.  Some woven baskets cram the uneven planks of the dock near where it meets the shore, emitting a horrific, sour stench.

title: [Moonsedge, Bramble and Dirge]
description: A tall black iron lamppost sits at the intersection of Bramble Street and Dirge Row.  A weathered sign once hung from chains beneath the post's outstretched arm, but rust has eaten through them.  The sign lies in a dying bed of ornamental brambles, devoured by rot.  Tall, greying buildings with broken windows like gouged eyes stare down on the crossing blindly, not a hint of light within.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Moonsedge, Dirge Row]
description: Hay lies in scattered piles near the entrance to the city's stables.  Although the telltale odors of horse lend their tang to the cold breeze, the smells are as faint as a memory.  Watering troughs along the outside of the building stand unused, their vessels dry and heaped with leaves and other detritus.

title: [Moonsedge, Stables]
description: Mold has overwhelmed the straw of the stables, pervading the air with a stale funk that smells like the work of long years of decay.  Once, the stable would have comfortably housed several dozen horses, judging from the stalls proceeding into the unlit dimness.  The building is still and quiet, and now it houses only unsettling creaks and groans.

title: [Moonsedge, Wildrose and Dirge]
description: Beneath the shelter of the walls flourish banks of sweetbriar, their petals like rubies in the dimness.  The perfume of the resplendent blossoms lingers on the air, heavy and saccharine.  At a join in the walls, a basalt guard tower climbs high into the air, gargoyles and grotesques lending their hideous grace to perches up its dark stone facade.

title: [Moonsedge, Guard Tower]
description: Racks of weapons, rusted to the point of uselessness, occupy the lower story of the watchtower.  Though blunted by corrosion, the deteriorating blades were obviously once of impressive make.  Stone steps climb in a spiral toward the tower's top, proceeding behind a curved wall adorned with a large crimson banner embroidered with a rising charcoal crescent moon with a briar sprig before it.

title: [Moonsedge, Wildrose Court]
description: Banks of wild rose framing the court have gone neglected long enough for them to overgrow their beds.  Their petals are a crimson flood on the dark cobblestones.  Beyond the boundaries of the courtyard, down long paths that wind beneath thornwood trees, are spacious homes of shadowy stone.  They look abandoned and their yards have fallen into ruin and overgrowth.

title: [Moonsedge, Wildrose Way]
description: The remains of a fine mirror are scattered across the roadway, the silver-backed fragments commingled with more mundane glass.  The source of both appears to be a broken window two stories above in the facade of a high basalt edifice.  Through the cracked aperture is visible the decomposing husk of a handsome apartment, silken hangings and gilded furnishings spotted with mold and rot.

title: [Moonsedge, Wildrose and Scarlet]
description: A toymaker's shop along the streetside is boarded up, doors and windows secured by sturdy lengths of hoarbeam and nails thicker than a finger.  The broad display window is cracked at the center, the damage radiating outward from the point of impact in a spiderweb pattern.  Though obstructive, the damage and boards do not entirely obscure the phalanx of painted, smiling toys standing attentively on the other side of the window, their lifeless eyes watching the street.

title: [Moonsedge, Scarlet Road]
description: Gilt flakes glint from the street in front of a capacious bathhouse.  Their source is its arched sign, which has been flayed by the elements until the letters are unreadable.  A barricade of overturned wagons, splintered furniture, and heavy barrels has been shoved up against the doors.  The business's facade is otherwise windowless, and there appears no other means of egress.

title: [Moonsedge, Bramble Street]
description: A trio of gibbets stands along the roadside, suspending rusty metal cages.  Though two are empty, one cage holds charred bones, the skeleton fused together by combustion.  The ghoulish instruments of execution were set up with little regard for the windows of the bordering businesses, including a tailor shop with boarded windows and a padlock securing its door.

title: [Moonsedge, Bramble Square]
description: Bramble topiaries frame a raised city square, urged by their gardeners' dereliction into an overgrown tangle that holds little resemblance to the cultivated shapes they once held.  The brambles cast their gnarled shadows on steps leading down to the streets feeding the square, stretching as far as the foundations of once-prosperous businesses nearby.  Most of the buildings are boarded and barricaded, but a dim countinghouse to the northwest has had its doors torn away, leaving only deformed hinges behind.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Moonsedge, Countinghouse]
description: The countinghouse is a spacious business.  Dozens of desks line the walls, protected by metal grates that are smothered by rust, leaving an unpleasant coppery tang in the air.  Tarnished, a silver emblem in the form of a currency scale is inlaid into the stone face of the northern wall.

title: [Moonsedge, Blade Court]
description: Empty weapon racks outside of an old stone smithy have begun to warp and splinter, the nails holding them together rusted to the point of uselessness.  Char rims the open windows, making them look like sunken sockets that stare out at the court.  Beds of briars once meant to decorate the court's landscape are overgrown, thorny heaps that stretch threateningly out onto the roadside, snatching thorns aggressively displayed.

title: [Moonsedge, Smithy]
description: A cadaver hangs from the soot-blackened rafters of the smithy, his flesh ravaged with claw-marks and bites as if wild animals have been at the body.  The forge has been cold long enough to have a silvery coating of dust over it, and the leather of the nearby bellows is torn to shreds.  Weapon blades of iron and steel lie in a pile on the ground, fused together by rust.

title: [Moonsedge, Bramble Street]
description: All that remains of a once-prosperous alchemist's shop is a pile of charred wreckage.  A gleaming steel sign protrudes from the ruins, its edges catching the sunlight.  The glass of broken vials and beakers litters the destruction, glittering threateningly in in the bright glow of day.

title: [Moonsedge, Bramble and Umbral]
description: To the south, the ground rises precipitously toward high hills whose black shadows stretch over the road, casting the area in darkness.  Flower beds full of night-blooming jasmine thrive in the gloom, filling the air with their cloying sweetness.  Sprawling across the highest hilltop is a castle of dark basalt.  Its soaring towers and vaulting walls are cut a severe silhouette against the blue of the sky.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Moonsedge, Umbral Road]
description: A cemetery stretches along the side of the road, banks of rolling green grass concealing crooked headstones and plinths.  The largest of the memorials is a mausoleum of alabaster etched with a bas-relief of a surpassingly beautiful woman in a flowing gown.  Businesses seem to give the cemetery wide berth, though from the look of their shuttered windows and boarded doors, they are as dead as the graveyard's occupants.

title: [Moonsedge, Bridge Approach]
description: A vast, deep ravine severs the highlands on which the city sits from the high hills dominated by the castle.  Joining them is a sinuous bridge of pale stone, a masterwork of architecture and stonecraft.  Flecks of mica in the stonework glint sharply in the moonlight, twinkling like stars against the dark silhouette of the bridge.

A vast, deep ravine severs the highlands on which the city sits from the high hills dominated by the castle.  Joining them is a sinuous bridge of pale stone, a masterwork of architecture and stonecraft.  Flecks of mica in the stonework gleam brightly in the daylight, engulfing the bridge in a nimbus of reflected light.

title: [Moonsedge, Nimbus Bridge]
description: The bridge is a wide span of pale stone that winds gently upward toward the castle.  To either side is a drop of hundreds of feet into a hungry black ravine that plunges between the highlands and their neighboring hills.  Patterns of inlay form intertwining branches of sweetbrier that spiral along the bridge's inner wall.

title: [Moonsedge, Ash and Umbral]
description: Vibrantly colorful to the point of being lurid, the collapsed remnant of a fortuneteller's tent drape over the cobblestones of the intersection.  Sitting upright before the spill of fabric and broken furnishings and oddly untouched, a crystal ball is aglow with refracted daylight.  Several embossed fortune cards flap in the stiff breeze, painted with elaborate figures and scenes.

title: [Moonsedge, Ash and Scarlet]
description: Mountain ash trees lean over the roadside, heavy with clusters of bright red berries.  They shadow the wreckage of a cleric's shop set back from the street, protected from prying eyes by high hedges.  Heavy doors of elm bear the scars of axe blows and the windows are shattered, but a barricade on the other side blocks entry.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west

title: [Moonsedge, Ash Row]
description: Dried leaves whisper a dry susurrus as they skitter trepidatiously past shuttered businesses and boarded homes to either side of the street.  The shadows of the ash trees planted in loamy beds along the center of the row stretch long and strange in the sunlight.  Their leaves have almost filled the bed of a wagon that sits unattended in the middle of the roadway, forlornly dangling broken leather straps that ought to be attached to horses or mules.
paths: Obvious paths: north, southeast, south, west

title: [Moonsedge, Ash and Dirge]
description: A retaining wall along the intersection holds back the earthen beds of several overgrown mountain ash trees that loom over the road.  The trees' branches are denuded of leaves but heavy with snow and clusters of berries, each as rich a red as a droplet of freshly spilled blood.  Graven into the retaining wall is a bas-relief of robed figures leading a procession.  The sign of a nearby inn creaks in the breeze.

title: [The Ram and Raven, Taproom]
description: Windows of stained glass gleam in the sunlight, casting jewel-bright shards of radiance on the dusty tables flanking the common room.  The light illuminates a capacious central bar, behind which kegs of ale have been left to go stale and sour.  An ebony carving hangs above the bar, depicting a raven purchase on the shoulders of a ram.

title: [Moonsedge, Ash Row]
description: Stirred by the breeze, a thin skim of sludge swirls sluggishly in the basin of a black marble fountain.  The spouts of the fountain, hoisted aloft by nubile maidens and supple young men adorned with gilt, are choked with opportunistic flora that has dried in time with the water.  Across the street, the rear wall of a large manor house is draped in vines that are almost obscenely lush, garish with a growth of crimson flowers.

title: [Moonsedge, Scarlet Road]
description: Beneath flapping scarlet banners, a decrepit jeweler's shop stands at an intersection choked with empty carriages and wagons.  Beds of black velvet near the windows of the shop have been stripped of their valuables and the door hangs open.  Outside, the vehicles are abandoned, whatever wares or baggage they carried either taken or ruined by the elements.
paths: Obvious paths: east, south, west, northwest

title: [Moonsedge, Gem Shop]
description: Paintings of fanciful trinkets and ostentatious adornments line the walls of the store, likely a mirror to the jewelry that once lined beds of black velvet near to the windows.  Not a trace of gold glistens within the looted shop.  Even the inlay on the counter has been pried free.  A sturdy modwir door in the rear of the shop is hacked and clawed, but stands fast, a testament to its sturdy wood.

title: [Moonsedge, Dirge Row]
description: Hooded figures stand along the streetside, carved beautifully from lustrous dark grey stone.  One statue is taller than the rest, robes draping her oddly elongated limbs.  The facades of the surrounding buildings are ostentatiously ornate, featuring bas-relief thorns and grotesque faces, each more comedically hideous than the last.  Dirge Row bends away from the encroaching walls of the city, turning toward the southeast.

title: [The Ram and Raven, Suites]
description: Near the eastern edge of the common room is a raised dais where a visiting bard or performer might sit.  Only spiders entertain there now, weaving silvery webs that catch the dim light of the abandoned inn.  Just past the dais, an arch heralds a long hallway lined with suites.  The doors are boarded over from the outside.

title: [Moonsedge, Dirge Bend]
description: The menacing shadow of a guard tower looms over Dirge Row as it bends toward Scarlet Road.  Four stone perches adorn the tower's rounded walls toward its upper reaches.  Three are occupied by hideous grotesques of carved rock, the statues winged and horned.  The fourth is cracked and empty, but there is no sign of its missing occupant on the paving stones below.

title: [Moonsedge, Scarlet Road]
description: At the bend of the road sits a shrine in an overgrown bed of wolfsbane, the purple blossoms drooping mournfully over the stone carving.  The effigy, a half-dome of white marble encasing a woman with wild locks and an athletic build, has tokens and offerings heaped before it, from ribbons to golden coins.  Overhead, a gargoyle on the walls watches the offerings with dispassionate eyes.

title: [Moonsedge, Scarlet Court]
description: Flapping like thunder in the cold wind, an abundance of bright crimson banners enliven the austere courtyard.  Black cobblestones ripple out from a central statue in concentric circles, stretching out toward gated homes whose rolling lots stretch out toward the city's western wall.  One manor, closer than the rest, is the very picture of genteel decay behind a wrought iron gate secured by a heavy padlock.

title: [Moonsedge, Guard Tower]
description: Partially open to the air, the watchtower looks out over the rolling woodland.  Its broad, open windows provide sightlines that stretch as far as the inhabited cove far across the Olbin's river delta.  The buildings of the port city there are diminished to specks by distance, and the fleet of merchant vessels bobbing in the bay are but a suggestion of bobbing sails.

title: [Moonsedge, Nimbus Bridge]
description: Grotesques stand on parapets along the walls of the bridge, wings outstretched.  Their horned heads are lifted in an alert posture, and their stony eyes glare outward as if watching for threats to the bridge.  One of the stone carvings has crashed down onto the bridge and lies in craggy chunks.  Its unoccupied parapet is a jagged ruin.

title: [Moonsedge, Nimbus Bridge]
description: Near the zenith of the bridge, a black covered coach stands abandoned, the leads cut and one of its wheels badly bent.  The vehicle's windows are shattered, and the doors are savaged with claw marks.  One of the coach's doors is open toward the bridge's safety wall, where a pile of moldy luggage lies.

title: [Moonsedge, Castle Approach]
description: Winding down from the castle's high hilltop, a pale stone bridge stretches, long and serpentine, over a treacherous ravine.  Spread-winged grotesques stand on parapets along the bridge, guarding its length.  The bridge is carved from exquisite white stone aglitter with countless flecks of prismatic mica.

title: [Moonsedge, Widow's Bluff]
description: Stretching out over the deep ravine, the finger of land teeters precipitously over a drop of hundreds of feet.  Grasses grow doggedly up to and over the land's edge, their roots poking out of the underside of the thin lip of stone and earth.  A single boulder sits atop the bluff like a rocky crown.

title: [Moonsedge, Castle Approach]
description: The walls of the castle are high and crenellated, vaulting far overhead.  Cut and carved from dark basalt, they are etched with a bas-relief moon and briar emblem over a heavy steel portcullis that appears to be the primary means of entering the castle grounds.  Banners in scarlet and charcoal fabric bear the same device, flapping forlornly overhead on the cold highland breeze.

title: [Moonsedge Castle, Ward]
description: Guarded by unyielding walls of dark basalt and a heavy steel portcullis, the castle yard is shielded from the sounds of the outside world and the highland gale.  A flagstone path proceeds eastward, cut from the same material as the walls.  It winds past empty horse troughs and several disused hitching posts that are green with a thick coating of moss.

title: [Moonsedge Castle, Ward]
description: An imposing statue of white marble stands to the side of the flagstone path proceeding through the castle ward.  It depicts a man of powerful build, armored in chainmail, as he menaces a huge striking serpent with a blade.  The eyes of the man have been gouged out, and chunks of white stone litter the surrounding grasses.  Nearby lies a bent pickaxe that appears to have been the vandal's weapon of choice.

title: [Moonsedge Castle, Well]
description: A covered well sits at the intersection of two flagstone paths, one winding toward the castle entrance in the east and the other dwindling as it meanders northward.  The sounds of flowing water echo up from below, crisply musical.  A number of pottery jugs rest next to the well, consumed by the high grasses during the flora's unfettered growth.

title: [Moonsedge Castle, Ward]
description: The flagstones split into two distinct paths, one bending north toward the mouth of a small training yard sheltered by the castle walls.  Overgrown with grasses and weeds, the pathway is uncertain.  A clearer trail toward the castle's entrance leads past a dark tower stationed along the curtain wall.

title: [Moonsedge Castle, Raven Loft]
description: Old droppings stain the stairs and coops of the rookery but have mostly been washed clean by rain and snow in the intervening years since the tower's abandonment.  They still lend a chalky white patina to the stone perches along the walls, which spiral up in a clockwise pattern toward the tower's ruined crown.  The collapsed ceiling leaves the zenith of the tower open to the moonlight and the forbidding shine of the stars.
